positiveFlows.title: BRINGING SMALL PRIVATE LANDOWNERS OF THE MID-GULF REGION BACK INTO THE MIX

WE PROPOSE DEVELOPING A NEW MOBILE APP TOOL, HEALTHYWOODS, TO HELP LANDOWNERS ASSESS AND MANAGE THEIR WOODLANDS, MEETING THE RREA PRIORITY ISSUE OF INVASIVE SPECIES. INVASIVE SPECIES PRESENT MAJOR ECONOMIC AND ECOLOGICAL CHALLENGES FOR LANDOWNERS TRYING TO DEVELOP AND MAINTAIN HEALTHY AND PRODUCTIVE WOODLANDS. THIS IS ESPECIALLY TRUE FOR NEWER LANDOWNERS WHO ARE NOT ENGAGED IN ONGOING EXTENSION PROGRAMS AND ARE LARGELY UNFAMILIAR WITH INVASIVE THREATS, MANAGEMENT OPTIONS, AND AVAILABLE RESOURCES. WE PROPOSE A NEW APPROACH TO EXTENSION PROGRAM DELIVERY IN THE FORM OF HEALTHYWOODS, AN EXPANSION OF THE TREESNAP CITIZEN SCIENCE MOBILE APP. HEALTHYWOODS WILL GUIDE USERS IN A WOODLAND HEALTH ASSESSMENT, PROVIDING PHOTO AND VIDEO-BASED EDUCATIONAL INFORMATION WITH A FOCUS ON INVASIVE SPECIES AND OTHER HEALTH THREATS. USERS WILL RECEIVE A PERSONALIZED REPORT BASED ON THEIR ASSESSMENT WITH TAILORED RECOMMENDATIONS AND WILL BE ABLE TO SHARE THIS REPORT WITH LOCAL EXTENSION SPECIALISTS AND OTHERRELEVANT PROFESSIONALS TO CONTINUE THE CONVERSATION ABOUT WOODLAND HEALTH OUTSIDE OF THE TOOL. LANDOWNERS WILL HAVE ACCESS TO INFORMATION ABOUT THEIR WOODLANDS VIA THE APP AND WEBSITE BUT THE WEBSITE WILL ALSO ALLOW EXTENSION AGENTS TO VIEW REPORTS FROM THEIR AREA AND PRIORITIZE COMMON ISSUES IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF OUTREACH PROGRAMMING. BY WORKING WITH A TEAM OF EXTENSION SPECIALISTS ACROSS THE EASTERN UNITED STATES, HEALTHYWOODS WILL BE RELEVANT FOR A BROAD RANGE OF LANDOWNERS, WITH DIFFERENT GOALS AND IN DIFFERENT REGIONS. THIS TOOL WILL PROVIDE AN INNOVATIVE RESOURCE FOR EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS NATIONALLY TO BETTER ENGAGE NEW AUDIENCES ABOUT INVASIVE SPECIES AND FOREST HEALTH.

positiveFlows.title: A REGIONAL BLENDED LEARNING MODEL TO UNDERSTAND FOREST CARBON MANAGEMENT

IN-PERSON WORKSHOPS, SEMINARS, SITE VISITS, AND NEWSLETTERS ARE ALL TRADITIONAL FORMS OF ADULT EDUCATION USED BY EXTENSION EDUCATORS, AND THEY CONTINUE BE EFFECTIVE FOR MANY AUDIENCES. HOWEVER, WE AGREE WITH A STATEMENT IN THE RREA STRATEGIC PLAN "ALTHOUGH TRADITIONAL MODES OF CONTENT DELIVERY ARE THE MOST WIDELY USED, THE DATA SUGGESTS THERE IS INTEREST IN ADOPTING ALTERNATIVE METHODS FOR DELIVERING PROGRAMS." NEW FORMS OF PROGRAM DELIVERY THAT UTILIZE WEB AND SMART-PHONE TECHNOLOGIES WILL REACH ENTIRELY NEW AUDIENCES AND EXPAND THE REACH OF NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT EXTENSION PROGRAMMING AND ENSURE THE CONTINUED RELEVANCE OF THOSE EFFORTS INTO THE 21ST CENTURY.A RELATIVELY NOVEL FORM OF COMMUNICATION THAT IS POPULAR AMONG A WIDE RANGE OF AUDIENCES IS THE PODCAST. THE TERM PODCAST, A COMBINATION OF THE WORDS "IPOD" AND "BROADCAST", IS "DEFINED AS A DIGITAL AUDIO FILE CREATED AND THEN UPLOADED TO AN ONLINE PLATFORM TO SHARE WITH OTHERS". A MAJOR ADVANTAGE OF PODCASTS IS THAT THEY ALLOW AUDIENCES TO LISTEN TO EDUCATIONAL CONTENT WHILE COMPLETING OTHER DUTIES, SUCH AS DRIVING, EXERCISING, OR COOKING A MEAL. WITH MORE THAN 700,000 ACTIVE PODCASTS IN 2019, THIS NEW FORM OF COMMUNICATION APPEARS TO BE A VIABLE INSTRUMENT FOR ADULT EDUCATION. IN 2018 ALONE, THERE WERE 50 BILLION PODCAST DOWNLOADS. ALONG WITH THE CONVENIENCE OF LISTENING "ON THE GO" PODCASTS ARE POPULAR BECAUSE THEY CAN BE EXPERIENCED &AGRAVE; LA CARTE BY CONNECTING A SPECIFIC AUDIENCE WITH A SPECIFIC TOPIC. A SALIENT OPPORTUNITY AND CHALLENGE WITH THIS PLATFORM, AND MANY MODERN COMMUNICATION CHANNELS, IS THAT ANYONE WITH A CONNECTION TO THE INTERNET AND A MICROPHONE CAN EARN AN AUDIENCE TO SHARE THEIR IDEAS AND PERSPECTIVES. WHEN THESE IDEAS AND PERSPECTIVES ARE SCIENCE-BASED, THE PLATFORM REACHES NEW AUDIENCES AND CAN HAVE IMPORTANT IMPACTS IN SOCIETY. WHEN THE VOICES ELEVATED THROUGH THE PLATFORM ARE NOT SCIENCE-BASED, THE PLATFORM PRESENTS CHALLENGES OF MISINFORMATION. OUR WORK WILL SEEK TO ENGAGE THIS AUDIENCE AND MEDIA WITH SCIENCE-BASED EDUCATIONAL CONTENT RELATED TO RREA CRITICAL ISSUES THAT EXTENDS THE TRADITIONAL EXTENSION MODEL TO MODERN COMMUNICATION CHANNELS AND PROVIDES A RELIABLE AND TRUSTWORTHY VOICE ON NATURAL RESOURCE ISSUES IN THE PODCAST UNIVERSE.

FAMILY FOREST OWNERS (FFOS) CONTROL 263 MILLION ACRES (OR 35%) OF U.S. FORESTS. IN THE EASTERN U.S, FFOS CONTROL MORE THAN 50% OF THE FORESTS (BUTLER, 2008). THE AVERAGE AGE OF FFOS IS OVER 60 YEARS OLD. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT OVER 75% OF FAMILY FOREST LAND IS OWNED BY PEOPLE OVER THE AGE OF 55 AND NEARLY 50% IS OWNED BY PEOPLE OVER THE AGE OF 65 (BUTLER, ET AL. 2016). TIMBER PRODUCTION, IN THE U.S., RELIES HEAVILY ON PRIVATE LANDS, WHERE CLOSE TO 90% OF TIMBER PRODUCT OUTPUT COMES FROM THESE PROPERTIES (MORGAN, 2009). PARCELIZATION CONTINUES TO BE A CONCERN FOR THE ABILITY TO MANAGE WOODLANDS, AND ESTATE AND SUCCESSION PLANS CAN BE ONE WAY TO REDUCE THE POTENTIAL FOR THIS TO HAPPEN (CATANZARO ET AL, 2014; TYSON ET AL, 1999). THIS GRANT WILL BUILD UPON PREVIOUS NIFA GRANTS BY CATANZARO (2015) AND MUTH (2015), WHICH PROVIDED RESEARCH FROM WOODLAND OWNER INTERVIEWS AND MATERIALS TO IMPRESS THE IMPORTANCE OF LEGACY PLANNING TO WOODLAND OWNERS. THIS GRANT WOULD PROVIDE THE OPPORTUNITY TOTAKE LEGACY PLANNING TO THE NEXT LEVEL BY 1) GAINING A REGIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF THE SUCCESSES AND LESSONS LEARNED BY EDUCATORS CURRENTLY ENGAGING LEGACY PROGRAMMING, 2) PROVIDING AN ORGANIZED TOOLKIT OF TESTED MATERIALS TO SUPPORT MODIFICATIONS TO AND NEW PROGRAMMING FOR IN-STATE PROGRAMS, AND 3) PROVIDING TIME AND FUNDING FOR EACH PARTICIPATING STATE TO PLAN AND TEST AN OUTREACH PROGRAM, WITH PARTNERS, FOR PILOT IMPLEMENTATION.

positiveFlows.title: EASTERN WHITE PINE (EWP) IS A MAJOR COMPONENT OF EASTERN FOREST WITH OVER 186 MILLION MBF (15 BILLION FT3) IN 25 STATES. THE SPECIES IS A COMMERCIALLY IMPORTANT LUMBER SPECIES AND IS AN IMPORTANT PART OF THE URBAN/RURAL INTERFACE WHERE DEVELOPMENTS OCCUR WITHIN EXISTING FORESTS WITH EWP. EWP RESPONDS EXTREMELY WELL TO MANAGEMENT WHICH CAN AMELIORATE LOSSES DUE TO INCREASING THREATS FROM DROUGHT, FUNGAL PATHOGENS, AND INSECT PESTS. UNMANAGED TREES CAN SUFFER MORTALITY OVER 50%.OUR OBJECTIVES ARE:1. DEVELOP NEW AND INNOVATIVE OUTREACH PRODUCTS AND DELIVERY APPROACHES FOR ENGAGING LANDOWNERS TO UNDERSTAND EWP HEALTH ISSUES AND HOW TO MINIMIZE RISKS.2. INVOLVE STAKEHOLDERS FROM RURAL COMMUNITIES AND THE FROM URBAN/RURAL INTERFACE TO DEMONSTRATE COMMON CONCERNS AND THE NEED TO MANAGE THE HEALTH OF EWP TO BENEFIT BOTH COMMUNITIES.A SYMPOSIUM WILL BE HELD IN THE FIRST YEAR TO DOCUMENT CURRENT KNOWLEDGE ON THE HEALTH AND MANAGEMENT OF EWP, AND TO DEVELOP STAKEHOLDER PRIORITIES FOR OUTREACH EFFORTS TO RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS (CONSULTING FORESTERS, ARBORISTS, OTHER NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS) IN NATURAL SYSTEMS AND IN THE URBAN/RURAL INTERFACE. THE PRIORITIES WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP A EASTERN WHITE PINE MANAGEMENT INSTITUTE (EWPMI) WITH WEBSITE, FACT SHEETS, FIELD MANUALS, FIELD WORKSHOPS, WEBINARS, AND VIDEOS. THE OUTCOME WILL RESULT IN RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS HAVING THE NEEDED KNOWLEDGE TO ENGAGE LANDOWNERS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH, VALUE, AND SUSTAINABILITY OF EWP. THE EWPMI WILL INITIALLY FOCUS ON NEW ENGLAND, AND THE EXPERIENCE WILL PROVIDE THE BASIS TO EXPAND THE EWPMI TO RESOURCE MANAGERS THROUGHOUT THE RANGE OF EWP.

THE SOUTHEASTERN U.S. LEADS THE NATION IN BOTH ACRES OWNED BY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS AND BURNEDANNUALLY BY PRESCRIBED FIRE. FREQUENT FIRES ARE NEEDED IN SOUTHEASTERN FORESTS TO INCREASE ECOSYSTEMFUNCTION, IMPROVE FOREST HEALTH, AND REDUCE WILDFIRE RISK. HOWEVER, CLIMATE CHANGE, INCREASINGHUMAN POPULATIONS, AND LACK OF ADEQUATE TRAINING AND RESOURCES ARE INCREASINGLY RESTRICTING THE USEOF PRESCRIBED FIRE. SURVEYS OF COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS AND PRIVATE LANDOWNERS INDICATEA NEED FOR MORE ACCESSIBLE WILDLAND FIRE INFORMATION, ESPECIALLY PERTAINING TO PRESCRIBED FIREPLANNING AND MANAGEMENT. COMMUNITY-BASED APPROACHES SUCH AS PRESCRIBED BURN ASSOCIATIONS(PBAS) CAN INCREASE THE CAPACITY TO CONDUCT PRESCRIBED BURNS. PBAS ARE COLLABORATIVE GROUPS OFPRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND OTHER COMMUNITY MEMBERS WHO SHARE KNOWLEDGE AND RESOURCES TOCOLLECTIVELY INCREASE THE USE OF PRESCRIBED FIRE ON THEIR LANDS. EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS ARE THE IDEALCONDUIT FOR DISSEMINATING FIRE SCIENCE RESOURCES AND BRINGING LANDOWNERS TOGETHER TO FORM PBASBECAUSE OF THEIR RELATIONSHIP WITH THEIR LOCAL COMMUNITY. BASED ON A NEEDS ASSESSMENT OF EXTENSIONPROFESSIONALS AND INTERVIEWS WITH EXISTING PBA MEMBERS, WE WILL DEVELOP EDUCATIONAL MATERIALSFOCUSED ON BASIC WILDLAND FIRE KNOWLEDGE GAPS. ALSO, WE WILL FOSTER NETWORKING BETWEEN EXTENSIONPROFESSIONALS AND PBA LEADERS TO REINFORCE CONCEPTS RELATED TO WILDLAND FIRE AND FACILITATEESTABLISHMENT OF SUCCESSFUL PBAS. FOLLOWING THE TRAINING, EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS SHOULD HAVEBASIC KNOWLEDGE OF WILDLAND FIRE AND THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE AND UNDERSTAND HOW TO FACILITATE APBA IN THEIR LOCAL COMMUNITY. SINCE THE NEED FOR EXTENSION TO ADDRESS WILDLAND FIRE ISSUES SPANSTHE NATION, THIS PROJECT WILL BE REPLICABLE NATIONWIDE.

positiveFlows.title: MANAGERS AND DECISION MAKERS ARE OFTEN TASKED WITH ACCOMPLISHING LARGE LANDSCAPE-SCALE GOALS WITH LIMITED RESOURCES. THIS IS ESPECIALLY TRUE WHEN CONCEPTUALIZING FOREST PRODUCT HARVESTING AS PART OF A FOREST MANAGEMENT STRATEGY. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL USE ECONOMIC MODELING TO CREATE A WOODSHED MAP OF THE GREAT LAKES FORESTED REGION BASED ON USER GROUP NEEDS ASSESSMENTS AND CREATE EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS AROUND THIS MAP FOR THREE BROAD END USER GROUPS: FOREST LANDOWNERS, INDUSTRY, AND FORESTRY AND EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO MAP PROCUREMENT ZONES AND A COMPETITIVENESS INDEX IN SPATIAL FORM, THAT WILL ALLOW END USERS TO DETERMINE IF THEIR FORESTED REGION IS SUITABLE FOR DIFFERENT TYPES OF FOREST PRODUCT MARKETS. THERE ARE EXISTING SPATIAL TOOLS FOR LANDOWNERS, BUT MANY SIMPLY DISPLAY THE RESOURCES AND OWNERSHIP PATTERNS, WITHOUT OFFERING A MODEL OF WOODSHEDS AND MARKET OPPORTUNITIES. TO SHOW THE MARKET EXTENT FOR WOOD PRODUCTS IN THIS TRI-STATE (MICHIGAN, WISCONSIN, MINNESOTA) REGION, WE WILL UTILIZE EXISTING AND POTENTIAL MILLS LOCATIONS COUPLED WITH A ROAD NETWORK DATABASE TO DETERMINE THE GEOGRAPHICAL EXTENT OF EACH FACILITY'S POTENTIAL PROCUREMENT ZONE OR WOODSHED. WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE VIDEO DEMONSTRATIONS AND WEBINARS OF THE TOOL FOR THE THREE USER GROUPS. FINALLY, WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER OR NOT TOOL USE LEADS TO MANAGEMENT ACTIONS AMONG LANDOWNERS AND IS USEFUL FOR GENERAL DECISION SUPPORT AMONG INDUSTRY AND FOREST MANAGEMENT AGENCY USERS.

THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CREATE A SPATIALLY-EXPLICIT, WEB-BASED DECISION SUPPORT TOOL TO INFORM LANDOWNERS' AND MANAGERS' SUSTAINABLE GRAZING MANAGEMENT DECISIONS; THE TOOL WILL COMBINE REMOTELY-SENSED RANGELAND PRODUCTION DATA WITH USER-DEFINED, PLACE-BASED KNOWLEDGE, AND THE TEAM WILL ENGAGE LAND MANAGERS IN TOOL DEVELOPMENT SO THAT THE TOOL MEETS THEIR MANAGEMENT-RELEVANT NEEDS AND CAN BE USED TO HELP CONSERVE HEALTHY RANGELANDS AND THE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES THEY PROVIDE. RANGELANDS ACROSS THE WESTERN UNITED STATES SUPPORT THE PROVISION OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND ARE A KEY RENEWABLE RESOURCE SUPPORTING LIVELIHOODS OF RANCHERS AND THE ASSOCIATED LIVESTOCK INDUSTRY. RANGELAND-BASED LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION MAINTAINS NATURALLY-OCCURRING PLANT COMMUNITIES, PROVIDING ECOSYSTEM SERVICES ALONGSIDE FOOD AND FIBER PRODUCTION. GRAZING MANAGEMENT DECISIONS THAT DETERMINE WHEN, WHERE, AND HOW MUCH OF THE RANGELAND VEGETATION'S ANNUAL ABOVEGROUND NET PRIMARY PRODUCTIVITY (ANPP) IS CONSUMED BY LIVESTOCK ARE KEY DETERMINANTS OF RANGELAND HEALTH AND THE FUTURE SUSTAINABILITY OF LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION. HOWEVER, PARTICULARLY IN WESTERN U.S. RANGELANDS, ANPP IS HIGHLY VARIABLE ACROSS THE LANDSCAPE, FROM YEAR TO YEAR, AND WITHIN A GROWING SEASON. LANDOWNERS MUST THEREFORE UNDERSTAND THE EXTENT OF THIS VARIABILITY AND MAKE GRAZING MANAGEMENT DECISIONS THAT ACCOUNT FOR THESE DYNAMICS. IN ADDITION, CLIMATE CHANGE IS INCREASING VARIABILITY IN ANPP, MAKING IT IMPERATIVE TO FULLY UNDERSTAND THE PATTERNS AND TRENDS IN FORAGE AVAILABILITY WHEN MAKING GRAZING MANAGEMENT DECISIONS.MANY IN THE RANGE MANAGEMENT PROFESSION CONSIDER THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN LAND AREA AND NUMBER OF GRAZING ANIMALS--THE STOCKING RATE--TO BE A PRIMARY FACTOR THAT CAN BE CONTROLLED TO ACHIEVE BOTH RANGELAND HEALTH AND RANCH ECONOMIC GOALS. MANY FACTORS ALSO DETERMINE THE EFFECTS OF GRAZING ON A PLANT COMMUNITY, AND OTHER METRICS ARE ALSO IMPORTANT IN DECIDING WHEN, WHERE, AND HOW TO GRAZE. NEVERTHELESS, STOCKING RATEREMAINS A SIGNIFICANT DECISION, AND ESTIMATES OF FORAGE AVAILABILITY AND ITS SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL VARIABILITY UNDERLIE STOCKING RATE DECISIONS. YET MANAGERS' ACCESS TO DATA ON AVAILABLE FORAGE AND ITS SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL VARIABILITY IS LIMITED. FIELD ESTIMATES BASED ON CLIPPING VEGETATION ARE PRONE TO ERROR AND BIAS, AND LARGE ENOUGH SAMPLES TO CAPTURE VARIATIONS IN SPACE AND TIME ARE ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TO OBTAIN. AND THOUGH REMOTE SENSING DATA ON ANPP EXIST, OBTAINING, INTERPRETING, AND USING DATA SPECIFIC TO THE LANDS ONE MANAGES IS NOT STRAIGHTFORWARD. SUCH LIMITATIONS LEAD TO CHALLENGES IN LANDOWNERS' AND MANAGERS' EFFORTS TO ACCURATELY ESTIMATE GRAZING CAPACITY ON RANGELANDS UNDER THEIR CONTROL, TO TRACK AND MONITOR CHANGES IN THE VEGETATION UNDER A PARTICULAR SET OF MANAGEMENT DECISIONS, AND TO PREPARE FOR AND ADJUST THEIR MANAGEMENT AS FORAGE AVAILABILITY CHANGES WITH CLIMATE CHANGE. WE PROPOSE TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL THROUGH THREE OBJECTIVES: 1) DEVELOP A SPATIALLY-EXPLICIT, WEB-BASED DECISION SUPPORT TOOL (DST) THAT IMPORTS MULTIPLE SOURCES OF RANGELAND FORAGE PRODUCTION DATA FOR AN AREA OF INTEREST, ALLOWS THE USER TO DEFINE KEY FACTORS THAT DETERMINE RANGELAND ACCESSIBILITY, AND PRODUCES MAPS OF STOCKING RATE AND OTHER SYNTHETIC METRICS SHOWING VARIATION THROUGH THE GROWING SEASON AND FROM YEAR-TO-YEAR. 2) CONVENE AN ADVISORY GROUP OF RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS TO PROVIDE ACTIONABLE INPUT AND REAL-LIFE PILOT CASES TO TEST THE TOOL ON, ENSURING THAT THE DST PROVIDES RELEVANT AND ACTIONABLE INFORMATION NEEDED FOR IMPROVED GRAZING MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. 3) ENGAGE WITH EXTENSION AGENTS AND SPECIALISTS, PUBLIC LAND MANAGERS, AND OTHER RANGELAND ADVISORS THROUGH EXISTING COMMUNICATION NETWORKS TO BUILD AWARENESS, COLLECT VALUABLE FEEDBACK, AND ENCOURAGE EARLY ADOPTERS TO USE THE DST. THE ACCESS TO DATA CHARACTERIZING VARIATIONS IN FORAGE AVAILABILITY AND OTHER KEY FACTORS WILL IMPROVE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS' AND PUBLIC LAND MANAGERS' ABILITY TO (A) ENHANCE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE NATION'S FORESTS AND RANGELANDS, (B) PROVIDE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND MARKET GOODS, (C) IMPROVE ECOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE TO CLIMATE CHANGE, AND (D) SUPPORT RURAL LIVELIHOODS.

TO MEET THE CHALLENGE OF DELIVERING ACCURATE, RELEVANT, TIMELY, AND PRACTICAL INFORMATION TO EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS AND OTHER ADVISORS AND STAKEHOLDERS, A NEW APPROACH IS NEEDED FOR EFFICIENTLY DISCOVERING, LOCATING, AND SAVING SPECIFIC INFORMATION LOCATED IN HANDBOOKS, TECHNICAL NOTES, AND OTHER REFERENCE MATERIALS.THIS PROJECT WILL BUILD ON A PREVIOUS PROJECT FUNDED BY NRCS BY PROVIDING DIRECT ACCESS TO LOCALLY- AND REGIONALLY-PRODUCED RANGELAND SCIENCE WITHIN EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS FOR EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS, AND PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAND MANAGERS. SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS ARE OFTEN LONG AND DENSE AND CAN TAKE CONSIDERABLE TIME TO REVIEW AND SYNTHESIZE. GIVEN THE PLETHORA OF ELECTRONIC INFORMATION AVAILABLE, THIS CAN BE AN OVERWHELMING PROCESS. A NEW AND INNOVATED SEARCH TOOL HAS BEEN CREATED TO ADDRESS THIS PERSISTENT ISSUE THROUGH A NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION SERVICE (NRCS) CONSERVATION INNOVATION GRANT. RANGEDOCS (HTTPS://DOCS.RANGELANDSGATEWAY.ORG/) ALLOWS EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS AND OTHER LAND MANAGERS TO SEARCH RANGELAND TERMS AND PINPOINT PARAGRAPHS OF APPLICABLE INFORMATION FROM KEY NATIONAL RANGELAND RESOURCES (I.E. NRCS TECHNICAL REFERENCES, INTERAGENCY TECHNICAL REFERENCES, AND NATIONALLY-FOCUSED OPEN ACCESS PUBLICATIONS AND EXPERIMENTAL STATION BULLETINS). ALL RESOURCES IN RANGEDOCS HAVE BEEN ANNOTATED BY RANGELAND EXPERTS SO THAT SEARCH RESULTS ARE EFFICIENT AND POINT TO HIGHLY RELEVANT INFORMATION. ADDITIONALLY, RANGEDOCS FEATURES CURATED THEME COLLECTIONS (E.G. MONITORING, TARGETED GRAZING) TO DELIVER SELECTED PASSAGES OF RANGELAND LITERATURE AS WELL AS ALLOWS USERS TO SAVE CRUCIAL EXCERPTS IN PRIVATE THEME COLLECTIONS BASED ON GEOGRAPHIC REGIONS, TOPICS, OR AUDIENCES. THUS, RANGEDOCS OFFERS THE OPPORTUNITY TO IDENTIFY RELEVANT, HIGHLY CUSTOMIZABLE INFORMATION ON EACH CRITICAL ISSUE QUICKLY AND EFFICIENTLY AND TO ORGANIZE IT FOR INDIVIDUAL NEEDS.

THIS PROJECT WILL UTILIZE A NATIONAL PANEL OF EXPERTS TO DEVELOP ONLINE LEARNING MATERIALS THROUGH WHICH KNOWLEDGE OF FOREST EFFECTS ON FOREST CARBON, CLIMATE CHANGE RELATED IMPACTS ON FOREST STRUCTURE, AND RELATED APPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT WILL BE CREATED. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE NEEDS ASSESSMENTS CONDUCTED THROUGH ITERATIVE STAKEHOLDER ENGAGMENT PROCESSES, WITH THE END GOAL OF CREATING MATERIAL THAT WILL BE ACCESSIBLE TO STAKEHOLDERS ACROSS THE FOREST SECTOR.

INTEREST IN FOREST CARBON AMONG POLICY, DECISION-MAKERS, AND INVESTORS TO EXTEND FOREST CARBON PAYMENT PROGRAMS TO FOREST LANDOWNERS HAS INCREASED. HOWEVER, LANDOWNERS ARE EITHER UNAWARE OF FOREST CARBON MARKETS OR DO NOT KNOW THE RIGHT PROGRAM TO GET INTO. THERE ARE ALSO GAPS IN UNDERSTANDING CARBON MARKETS AMONG EDUCATORS AND FORESTERS WORKING DIRECTLY WITH LANDOWNERS. THE PROJECT'S LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO SUPPORT LANDOWNERS IN UNDERSTANDING AND ACCESSING FOREST CARBON MARKETS BASED ON THEIR NEEDS. WE WILL DEVELOP A WEB TOOL TO CONDUCT A COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS OF DELAYING HARVESTS FOR CARBON OR OTHER ECOLOGICAL GOALS AND DEVELOP WEBINARS AND WORKSHOPS TO BUILD CAPACITY ON FOREST CARBON MARKET OPPORTUNITIES AMONG EDUCATORS, LANDOWNERS, AND FORESTERS. THE TOOL WILL ANALYZE THE COST AND BENEFIT OF DELAYING HARVEST USING USER-PROVIDED DBH, HEIGHT, FOREST TYPE, AND WOOD PRICE. LANDOWNERS COULD COLLECT THESE WITHOUT PROFESSIONAL HELP. WE WILL PROVIDE VIDEO DEMONSTRATIONS AND INSTRUCTIONS ON COLLECTING AND PREPARING DATA FOR THE TOOL, A PANEL DISCUSSION OF FOREST CARBON PAYMENT PROGRAM MARKETERS, INFORMATION ON THE PROS AND CONS OF VARIOUS CARBON MARKETS, AND FINANCIAL OPPORTUNITIES ASSOCIATED WITH FOREST CARBON. WORKSHOPS AND ON-DEMAND WEBINARS WILL BUILD CAPACITY ON FOREST CARBON TO SUPPORT LANDOWNERS AMONG EXTENSION EDUCATORS, LANDOWNERS, FORESTERS, INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS, AND OTHERS. FINALLY, WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER TOOL USES LEAD TO A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF CARBON MARKET OPPORTUNITIES AMONG LANDOWNERS AND IS HELPFUL FOR GENERAL DECISION SUPPORT FOR USERS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE THREAT OF TREE FAILURE DAMAGE TO COASTAL COMMUNITIES IS RELATED TO INCREASING FREQUENCY AND INTENSITY OF STORMS. PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT INSURANCE COMPANIES ARE IMPLEMENTING POLICIES THAT COULD INFLUENCE COMMUNITY FOREST MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. THESE POLICIES INCLUDE INCREASING PREMIUMS, DENYING COVERAGE, OR SUGGESTING THE REMOVAL OF TREES, ALL OF WHICH REPRESENT A NEGATIVE ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE BECAUSE NOT ALL TREES ARE VULNERABLE TO STORMS. PROPER MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES SUCH AS APPROPRIATE SPECIES SELECTION AND PLACEMENT, PRUNING AND TREE HEALTH CARE CAN MITIGATE RISK. IN TURN, A HEALTHY AND ABUNDANT TREE CANOPY IS A CRITICAL STEP TOWARDS CLIMATE CHANGE RESILIENCE. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROMOTE ADOPTION OF CLIMATE SMART PRACTICES THROUGH APPROPRIATE MITIGATION OF RISKS IN URBAN AND PERI-URBAN FORESTS. TO THIS END, WE AIM TO PROMOTE CONSERVATION, PROTECTION, AND MARKET DEVELOPMENT THROUGH EFFECTIVE EXTENSION EDUCATIONAL DESIGN, CORRESPONDING TO GOAL 2 OF THE 2023 NATIONAL FOCUS FUNDS PROGRAM. WE WILL BUILD NETWORKS, UNDERSTANDING, AND COMMUNICATION AMONG PROPERTY OWNERS, TREE CARE WORKERS (INCLUDING PRIVATE AND PUBLIC TREE ARBORISTS), AND THE INSURANCE INDUSTRY. THIS WILL, IN TURN, SHAPE THE FUTURE OF FORESTS WITHIN AND SURROUNDING COASTAL COMMUNITIES. CURRENTLY, THERE IS VERY LITTLE INTERACTION BETWEEN THE TREE CARE AND INSURANCE INDUSTRIES. THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY THE POLICIES AND PRACTICES USED BY THE INSURANCE INDUSTRY TO MITIGATE THEIR RISK AND DEVELOP OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE INSURANCE AND TREE CARE INDUSTRIES TO INCREASE THEIR KNOWLEDGE ABOUT TREE RISK AND MANAGEMENT AS WELL AS IMPROVE WORKING RELATIONSHIPS.

PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS ARE UNDER INCREASING PRESSURE TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO FOREST RESOURCES WHILE MAINTAINING PUBLIC BENEFITS SUCH AS FISHAND WILDLIFE HABITAT, WATER AND WETLAND RESOURCES AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES BUT OFTEN LACK OPPORTUNITIES TO ACCESS THE MOST CURRENT INFORMATION. (2) ECOSYSTEM SERVICES: ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS IN ACTIVELY MANAGING THEIR LANDS WITH KNOWLEDGE OF FOREST ANDRANGELAND ECOSYSTEM PROCESSES AND HOW SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES PRODUCE DIFFERENT COMBINATIONS OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; AND ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND USERS IN UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE DIFFERENT ECOSYSTEM SERVICES HAVE ON COMMUNITY WELL-BEING. (3) FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT: ENSURING THAT PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS HAVE THE BEST AVAILABLE INFORMATION ABOUT FISH AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT HABITAT MANAGEMENT IN FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS. (4) GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION AND OTHER LANDOWNERSHIP CHANGES: ENHANCING THE DECISION-MAKING ABILITY OF RANCH AND FOREST LANDOWNER FAMILIES FOR GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION BY PROVIDING INFORMATION ON AND FACILITATING COMMUNICATION ABOUT SUCH PLANNING OPTIONS AS CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, COMMUNITY-BASED NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT OR OTHER NON-TRADITIONAL SUCCESSION MODELS; TRAINING AND LINKING INTERESTED PARTIES IN COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS THAT WILL AUGMENT GENERATIONAL TRANSFER OF FOREST AND RANGELAND ENTERPRISES. (5) INVASIVE SPECIES: INCREASING THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO ASSESS THE THREAT OF INVASIVE SPECIES; DEVELOPING INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT PLANS; IMPLEMENTING EFFECTIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL STRATEGIES TO PROTECT FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS; PROVIDING MEANS FOR THE GENERAL PUBLIC (INCLUDING ABSENTEE LANDOWNERS), YOUTH, AND COMMUNITY GROUPS FOR THEIR INTERACTION AND PARTICIPATION IN MONITORING AND CONTROLLING INVASIVE SPECIES. (6) RURAL COMMUNITIES: WORKING WITH RURAL COMMUNITIES TO ASSESS NEEDS AND DETERMINE HOW TO SUSTAINABLY ENHANCE LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT THROUGH A FOCUS ON FOREST AND RANGELAND INDUSTRIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, AND EXPERTISE; CREATING A STRONGER RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HEALTHY FORESTS AND RANGELANDS AND THE SOCIAL AND SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC BASES OF RURAL COMMUNITIES; ASSESSING NEEDS AND DETERMINING HOW TO ENHANCE LOCAL LANDSCAPE ECONOMICS. (7) WATER AND WETLANDS: ENCOURAGING MANAGEMENT OF FORESTS AND RANGELANDS TO IMPROVE WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY. (8) WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT: ENGAGING FOREST AND RANGELAND COMMUNITIES WITH RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION ON WILDFIRE RISK-MANAGEMENT AND POST-FIRE RECOVERY STRATEGIES; INCREASING THE CAPACITY OF COMMUNITY, COUNTY, AND STATE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS/CIVIL DEFENSE AUTHORITIES TO COMMUNICATE COMMUNITY NEEDS AND INFORM COMMUNITY-DEVELOPMENT POLICIES, CODES, AND ORDINANCES THAT PROTECT COMMUNITIES FROM WILDFIRE; DEVELOPING OUTREACH EFFORTS THAT INCLUDE CURRENT AND EMERGING RESEARCH ON IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE ON FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOLOGY AND ECONOMICS, FUELS MANAGEMENT, AND PRESCRIBED FIRE TO CREATE APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES; INCREASING CAPACITY FOR COMMUNITY ACTION, EMPOWER LANDOWNERS TO ENGAGE IN PRESCRIBED FIRE, AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR TRAINING AND CAPACITY IN FUELS REDUCTION.

positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT FUNDING RECEIVED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA WARNELL SCHOOL OF FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES IS TO SUPPORT THE OUTREACH EFFORTS OF OUR EXTENSION FACULTY. WE BRING SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION TO OUR TARGET AUDIENCES, SUCH AS GEORGIA FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, TO HELP THEM MAKE CRITICAL MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. WE EDUCATE GEORGIA CITIZENS ABOUT HOW AND WHY NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES ARE PRESCRIBED AND CONDUCTED. WE PROVIDE CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDIT COURSES REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN PROFESSIONAL CREDENTIALS. THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM WILL APPROACH OUR EFFORTS LIKE WE ALWAYS DO: 1) DETERMINE NEEDS WITH INPUT FROM OUR TARGET AUDIENCES AND KEY STAKEHOLDERS; 2) DEVELOP MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES (TEMPORAL AND SPECIAL); 3) CREATE APPROPRIATE PRODUCT(S) THAT ADDRESS IDENTIFIED NEEDS; 4) EVALUATE IMPACT/EFFECTIVENESS; AND 5) REPEAT PROCESS UNTIL NEEDS ARE SATISFIED. THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED IN THE COMING YEAR INCLUDE: 1) WORKSHOPS; 2) APPLIED RESEARCH; 3) PEER REVIEWED AND EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS; 4) PRESENTATIONS; 5) PARTNER COLLABORATION; AND 6) WEB-BASED PRODUCTS. THE DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE: 1. WORKSHOPS: THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM WILL PLAN, ORGANIZE AND DELIVER WORKSHOPS COVERING TOPICS THAT INCLUDE THE DISTRIBUTION AND CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES, FIRESCAPING, TIMBER TAXATION, INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT, FOREST HEALTH, URBAN WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION CERTIFICATION, AND MANAGING FISHPONDS. WORKSHOPS WILL BE PLANNED AND DELIVERED THAT ARE BOTH PROACTIVE AND REACTIVE. ALL WORKSHOPS WILL BE DESIGNED AND CONDUCTED WITH THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES THAT PARTICIPANTS WILL INCREASE THEIR WORKING KNOWLEDGE, CHANGE THEIR ATTITUDE TOWARD ADOPTION OF NEW MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES OR REMOVAL OF AN INVASIVE SPECIES, AND DEVELOP NEW BEHAVIORS THAT SATISFIES A PERSONAL INTEREST OR HELPS THEM MEET THEIR OBJECTIVES. OUR ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION SPECIALISTSWILL OFFER EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EVENTS FOR STUDENTS AND TEACHERS USING INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED CURRICULA (PROJECT LEARNING TREE, PROJECT WILD, AND PROJECT WET). AS TEACHERS GAIN MORE FREEDOM TO PLAN AND CARRY-OUT FIELD TRIPS, WE HOPE TO SEE AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF CLASSES COMING TO OUR EDUCATION FOREST FACILITIES. 2. APPLIED RESEARCH: ACTIVITIES WILL INVOLVE MAINTAINING EXISTING AND DEVELOPING NEW SITES TO EVALUATE AND SERVE AS DEMONSTRATIONS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. THESE EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON SITE PREPARATION TECHNIQUES, FOREST HERBICIDE TRIALS, AND HERBICIDE APPLICATION TIMING. THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF APPLIED RESEARCH EFFORTS IS TO STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION WITH STATE/FEDERAL AGENCY PARTNERS AND PRIVATE INDUSTRY SPONSORS, AND AS DATA CONTINUES TO BE GATHERED AND ANALYZED, AN INCREASED USE OF THESE SITES AS EFFECTIVE DEMONSTRATION SITES FOR FIELD DAYS AND WORKSHOPS. 3. PUBLICATIONS: WE WILL CONTINUE TO PRODUCE PEER-REVIEWED JOURNAL MANUSCRIPTS AND EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS. TOPICS TO BE COVERED INCLUDE FIRESCAPING, WILD HARVESTING PRACTICES, WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES (HERBICIDE APPLICATION AND SITE PREPARATION). ALL PUBLICATIONS WILL BE PRODUCED WITH THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF SPREADING TRUSTED INFORMATION AND INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PUBLICATIONS POSTED ON OUR NEW WARNELL OUTREACH WEBSITE WHERE WE CAN TRACK THE NUMBER OF VIEWS AND DOWNLOADS. 4. PRESENTATIONS: OUR TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO DELIVER PRESENTATIONS IN-PERSON AND UTILIZING THE AFFORDANCES OF VIRTUAL DELIVERY SUCH AS ZOOM AND WEBINARS. WE HAVE PLANS TO COVER MANY TOPICS INCLUDING URBAN WILDLIFE ISSUES, FIRESCAPING, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, FOREST MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, AQUATIC RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, WOOD PLANT ID, AND OTHER TOPICS AS IDENTIFIED. THE OUTCOME OF OUR EFFORTS IS TO SHARE QUALITY UP-TO-DATE INFORMATION WITH GEORGIA CITIZENS THAT HELP THEM MAKE INFORMED NATURAL RESOURCE RELATED DECISIONS. 5. PARTNER COLLABORATION: OUR TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO NURTURE EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, EDUCATORS (K-16), AND INDUSTRY. WE ANTICIPATE THE OUTCOME OF THESE PARTNERSHIPS TO BE SUSTAINED SUPPORT AND COLLABORATION. WE ARE VERY AWARE OF THE IMPORTANCE OF PARTNERSHIPS WHEN IT COMES TO LENDING VALIDITY TO OUR WORK. FOR EXAMPLE, WHEN WE COLLABORATE WITH A STATE AGENCY OR A NATIONAL TREE FARMER OF THE YEAR THAT HOSTS A WORKSHOP OR FIELD DAY ON THEIR PROPERTY, OUR EFFORTS ARE REWARDED WITH A STRONG TURNOUT OF PARTICIPANTS AND THE TECHNICAL CONTENT WE DELIVER IS BACKED WITH EXAMPLES IN THE FIELD. 6. WEB BASED PRODUCTS: WE WILL CONTINUE TO REVIEW, UPDATE AND MODIFY OUR NEWLY CREATED WARNELL OUTREACH WEB PAGE. OUR WEB DEVELOPMENT TEAM WILL EVALUATE AND RETIRE SMARTPHONE APPS AND WEBSITES THAT HAVE LIMITED DOWNLOADS/HITS OR LIMITED FUNDING TO MAINTAIN. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF OUR EFFORT WILL BE TO OFFER WEB-BASED TOOLS THAT INCREASE INFORMATION SHARING AND DATA COLLECTION, AND PROVIDE EXPERIENCES THAT BUILD NEW SKILLS AND BENEFIT OUR TARGET AUDIENCES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS, PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, PRIVATE CONSULTANTS, COUNTY EXTENSION ANR AGENTS, CITY/COUNTY GOVERNMENT STAFF, K-12 TEACHERS AND STUDENTS, SPECIAL INTEREST GROUPS, ASSOCIATIONS, NGOS AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, AND ALL CITIZENS OF GEORGIA. THERE ARE NO SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES PLANNED AT THE TIME OF THIS AWARD.

RREA  AUBURN UNIVERSITY BACKGROUND: FOREST RESILIENCY, ESPECIALLY AS IT RELATES TO FOREST HEALTH IS A TOPIC OF GROWING CONCERN ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST. ALREADY POSING SIGNIFICANT THREATS TO FORESTED ECOSYSTEMS, THE IMPACTS OF INVASIVE SPECIES ARE EXPECTED TO INCREASE WITH CLIMATE VARIATION AND MORE FREQUENT EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS. POSITIONING LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS TO MINIMIZE THE IMPACTS OF INVASIVE SPECIES IS CRUCIAL. MANAGED FORESTS, NATURAL AREAS, URBAN GREEN SPACES, PASTURES, WATERWAYS, ROADSIDES AND RIGHT OF WAYS ARE ALL IMPACTED BY INVASIVE SPECIES. SPECIFICALLY, INVASIVE PLANTS DISPLACE NATIVE PLANT SPECIES AND THE WILDLIFE AND INSECTS THAT DEPEND ON THEM. FIRE REGIMES, WATER CYCLES, NUTRIENT CYCLES, AND FOREST REGENERATION ARE NEGATIVELY IMPACTED BY INVASIVE SPECIES. THREATS ARE COMPOUNDED WITH DISTURBANCES CREATED BY EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS. CONSEQUENTLY, INVASIVE SPECIES POSE AN INCREASING THREAT TO FOREST PRODUCTIVITY, FOREST MANAGEMENT OPTIONS, WILDLIFE HABITAT, OUTDOOR RECREATION, AND OVERALL ECOSYSTEM HEALTH. IN ADDITION TO THE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH HARM TO THE ENVIRONMENT AND REDUCED PRODUCTIVITY, INVASIVE PLANT CONTROL IS EXPENSIVE. ACROSS THE COUNTRY COSTS MOUNT TO BILLIONS OF DOLLARS EACH YEAR. PREVENTING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF INVASIVE PLANTS AND FINDING AND TREATING INFESTATIONS WHEN STILL SMALL ARE THE MOST COSTEFFECTIVE WAYS TO SLOW THE SPREAD AND REDUCE THE IMPACT OF INVASIVE PLANTS ACROSS THE LANDSCAPE. PREVENTION, EARLY DETECTION AND ADVANCE TREATMENT ARE ALSO IMPORTANT TOOLS FOR MINIMIZING IMPACTS OF INVASIVE SPECIES FOLLOWING EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS AND OTHER LANDSCAPE DISTURBANCES. STAKEHOLDERS CONSISTENTLY IDENTIFY INVASIVE SPECIES AS A TOP NATURAL RESOURCE ISSUE OF CONCERN. OBJECTIVES: LANDOWNER EDUCATION AND CONTINUING EDUCATION FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS ARE KEY TO REDUCING THE IMPACTS OF INVASIVE PLANTS AND IMPROVING THE HEALTH OF ALABAMA FORESTS. OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO EXPAND AWARENESS OF INVASIVE SPECIES, INCREASING KNOWLEDGE OF INVASIVE PLANT IDENTIFICATION, IMPACTS, AND CONTROL OPTIONS. A SECONDARY, BUT CLOSELY ALIGNED OBJECTIVE IS TO MAINTAIN STATE AND REGIONAL PARTNERSHIPS WITH RELEVANT PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR ORGANIZATIONS ADDRESSING ISSUES RELATED TO ASSESSMENT, MAPPING, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL, RESEARCH, AND EDUCATION. INVASIVE PLANTS WILL BE OUR MAIN FOCUS, BUT EMERGING INVASIVE INSECT AND ANIMAL PESTS MAY ALSO BE ADDRESSED. TARGET AUDIENCE: THE PRIMARY TARGET AUDIENCES ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS (E.G., FORESTERS, LOGGERS, WILDLIFE BIOLOGISTS) AND STUDENTS OF NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT. BECAUSE NONNATIVE PLANTS USED IN LANDSCAPING ARE A MAJOR SOURCE OF THE INVASIVE PLANTS THAT INVADE FORESTS, A SECONDARY AUDIENCE IS HOMEOWNERS, MASTER GARDENERS, THE GENERAL PUBLIC, AND K12 EDUCATORS. DELIVERABLES COMMUNICATION PRODUCTS: PRIMARY COMMUNICATION PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS ADDRESSING INVASIVE PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL; FREQUENT POSTS TO THE ALABAMA EXTENSION INVASIVE PLANT FACEBOOK PAGE THAT WE ADMINISTER; BLOGS AND SHORT ARTICLES FOR POPULAR PRESS AND THE TEAM NEWSLETTER; CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE ALABAMA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION SYSTEM (ACES) FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE WEBPAGE; AND CONTRIBUTIONS OF HIGH DEFINITION PHOTOGRAPHS OF INVASIVE PLANTS FOR USE IN EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS AND OTHER OUTREACH NEEDS. EVENTS: OUTREACH EVENTS WILL INCLUDE COCHAIRING THE STATEWIDE ANNUAL ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL CONFERENCE; ORGANIZING AND PARTICIPATING IN ACES WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DAYS; PROVIDING SEMINARS AND WEBINARS FOR FOREST INDUSTRY, FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AGENCIES, MASTER GARDENERS, CIVIC GROUPS AND OTHERS AS REQUESTED (TYPICALLY ABOUT 20 EVENTS A YEAR.) MANY OF THESE EVENTS PROVIDE CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDITS FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS. SERVICES AND ASSOCIATED ACTIVITIES: QUESTIONS FROM LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, EXTENSION AGENTS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC ARE FIELDED EACH YEAR. MOSTINVOLVEPLANT IDENTIFICATION AND TREATMENT OPTIONS FOR INVASIVE PLANTS. WELL OVER ONE HUNDRED QUESTIONS ARE ADDRESSED EACH YEAR VIA PHONE, EMAIL, TEXT AND SOCIAL MEDIA. WE ALSO TEACH A SECTION ON INVASIVE PLANTS TO AUBURN UNIVERSITY FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE STUDENTS, LEAD THE EFFORT TO UPDATE THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL (ALIPC) INVASIVE PLANT LIST (A NONREGULATORY STATE LIST), AND PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE TO LOCAL INVASIVE PLANT CONTROL EFFORTS. BUILDING CAPACITY: COLLABORATING WITH STATE AND LOCAL AGENCIES AND OTHER STAKEHOLDER PARTNERS STRENGTHENS EDUCATION AND OUTREACH EFFORTS. SERVING ON STATEWIDE INVASIVE PLANT TASK FORCES AND COMMITTEES AND MAINTAINING A LEADERSHIP ROLE WITHIN THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL ARE IMPORTANT AVENUES FOR EFFECTIVE COLLABORATION. REGIONAL PUBLICATIONS AND EVENTS ARE PERIODICALLY ORGANIZED THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH SOUTHERN REGION EXTENSION FORESTRY AND OTHER COLLEAGUES IN THE REGION. INVOLVEMENT IN ONE REGIONAL EFFORT IS LEADING TODEATE BENEFIT IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH THROUGH REDUCED SPREAD AND IMPACTS OF INVASIVE PLANTS. A CHANGE IN KNOWLEDGE WILL BE REFLECTED THROUGH AN INCREASED NUMBER OF LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS WHO KNOW HOW TO IDENTIFY INVASIVE PLANTS AND KNOW WHERE TO ACCESS SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION AND RESOURCES; INCREASED NUMBER OF LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS WITH KNOWLEDGE OF EFFECTIVE OPTIONS FOR INVASIVE PLANT PREVENTION AND CONTROL; AND INCREASED AWARENESS OF EDDMAPS. A CHANGE IN ACTION WILL BE REFLECTED THROUGH AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS WHO MONITOR FOR, AND INITIATE OR CONTINUE INVASIVE PLANT MONITORING AND CONTROL EFFORTS, LEADING TO AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF ACRES TREATED; A REDUCTION IN BEHAVIORS THAT SPREAD INVASIVE PLANTS; FEWER HOMEOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS USING RISKY NON-NATIVE PLANTS IN LANDSCAPING AND WILDLIFE PLANTINGS; AND AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE WHO USE EDDMAPS TO REPORT INVASIVE PLANTS. ULTIMATELY, THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH AND RESILIENCY THROUGH REDUCED USE OF NON-NATIVE PLANTS IN LANDSCAPING AND WILDLIFE PLANTINGS; REDUCTIONS IN BEHAVIORS THAT SPREAD INVASIVE PLANTS; AND EARLIER AND MORE EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OF INVASIVE PLANTS. EFFORTS TO IMPROVE INVASIVE PLANT LISTING AND MAPPING WILL IMPROVE THE ACCURACY OF DISTRIBUTION MAPS TO BETTER REFLECT OF INVASIVE PLANT POPULATIONS ACROSS THE STATE, BETTER INFORMING MANAGEMENT DECISIONS.

PROJECT ABSTRACT OUR PORTFOLIOS OF SOLUTIONDRIVEN, CUTTINGEDGE RESEARCH IS CREATING NEW KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY WHICH IS THEN EXTENDED TO ALL NORTH CAROLINIANS THROUGH NC COOPERATIVE EXTENSION. WE ARE TRANSFORMING SCIENCE INTO EVERYDAY SOLUTIONS THAT IMPROVE LIVES AND ALLOW NORTH CAROLINIANS TO LEAD PROSPEROUS, HEALTHY LIVES. A STATEWIDE NETWORK OF EXTENSION AGENTS SERVES AS THE CONDUIT THROUGH WHICH THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY ARE COMMUNICATED TO UNIVERSITY RESEARCHERS WHO THEN CONDUCT RESEARCH AND FORMULATE SOLUTIONS. EXTENSION AGENTS THEN DELIVER ESSENTIAL INFORMATION INTO THE HANDS OF GROWERS, INDUSTRY, AND MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS AT NC STATE FOCUS ON ADDRESSING FOUR IDENTIFIED STATEWIDE CRITICAL ISSUES: IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; PROTECTING ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES, ENRICHING YOUTH, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY WELLBEING; AND ENHANCING FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH. THROUGH INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, NC STATE IS SOLVING CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF BOTH LARGE AND SMALL SCALE FARMS. RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE LANDSCAPING AND GARDENING. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND METHODS FOR ANIMAL BREEDING, REPRODUCTION, NUTRITION, GENETICS AND GENOMICS, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND HEALTH AND WELLBEING. THESE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS ALSO AIM TO TACKLE THE CRITICAL ISSUES IMPACTING THE QUALITY OF OUR SOIL, WATER AND AIR BY PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC SOLUTIONS FOR ANIMAL WASTE MANAGEMENT, WASTEWATER TREATMENT, NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, SOIL PROPERTIES, AND FISHERY AND POND MANAGEMENT. NC STATE EXTENSION CONTINUES TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES TO ENRICH YOUTH, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY WELL BEING THROUGH THE 4H YOUTH DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM. 4H PROGRAMS INCREASE OPPORTUNITIES FOR YOUTH TO DEVELOP LIFE SKILLS, GROW CONFIDENCE, INDEPENDENCE, RESILIENCE, AND STEM SKILLS THROUGH FUN HANDS ON LEARNING IN SAFE, HEALTHY, AND ENRICHING ENVIRONMENTS. EXTENSION PROGRAMS ALSO ADDRESS CRITICAL CHALLENGES AFFECTING CONSUMER AND FAMILY WELLBEING. IN ADDITION TO YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, OTHER FOCUS AREAS INCLUDE PARENTING, CHILDCARE, FAMILY RELATIONSHIPS, FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT, AGING, HEALTHY HOMES, AND DISASTER READINESS, RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY. AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL, EXTENSION WORKS WITH INDIVIDUALS, COMMUNITY GROUPS AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS ON LEADERSHIP SKILLS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, CIVIC ENGAGEMENT, VOLUNTEERISM, COMMUNITY PLANNING, AND DISASTER PREPAREDNESS NC STATES RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH AND TO KEEP AMERICANS HEALTHY AND FREE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESS NECESSITATE A FOCUS ON PREVENTING FOOD SAFETY PROBLEMS RATHER THAN TAKING A REACTIONARY APPROACH. NC STATES INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS FOCUS ON PROTECTING THE SAFETY OF FOODS ALONG THE ENTIRE SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM PRODUCTION TO CONSUMPTION. TO MEET THE GROWING NEED FOR HEALTHY FOOD, RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS THAT PROMOTE HEALTH AND PREVENT DISEASE. AT THE SAME TIME, EXTENSION PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO ENSURE THAT INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE THEY NEED TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES ABOUT FOOD AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSSCUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEM, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGRO ECONOMICS. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITS WORK WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, PLACING SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON LIMITED RESOURCES, SMALL SCALE MINORITY FARMERS. THE FARM PAVILION WILL FOCUS ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND LOCAL AND COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, HOUSING ITS APPLIED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROGRAMS STAFF AND PROVIDING SPACE FOR MEETINGS, FORUMS AND CONFERENCES. ENHANCING FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH: WITHIN THIS AREA BOTH RESEARCH AND EXTENSION WILL WORK TO ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF HUMAN HEALTH, FOOD SAFETY AND HEALTHY LIVING HABITS. THE RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON WHOLE GRAIN CEREALS, HUMAN HEALTH AND HUMAN NUTRITION, PROBIOTICS STRAINS, FOOD ALLERGY, FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESS, BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS OF FOOD, POSTHARVEST TECHNOLOGY AND FOOD SECURITY. COOPERATIVE EXTENSION AND RESEARCHERS AT NCA<(>&<)>T WILL WORK TOGETHER IN A CONCERTED EFFORT TO INCREASE INFORMATION AND RESOURCES FOR AFRICAN AMERICAN FAMILIES AND CHILDREN IN RURAL COMMUNITIES WHO ARE OFTEN POOR AND DISPROPORNCIALLY VULNERABLE ARE WELL EQUIPPED TO MAKE SOUND FINANCIAL DECISIONS FOR THEMSELVES AND THEIR FAMILIES. 4-H PROGRAMMING WILL FOCUS ON AREAS SUCH AS STEM (SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATH), LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT, AND AGRISCIENCE. INNOVATION STATION, THE CUTTING-EDGE MOBILE LEARNING EXPERIENCE, WILL CONTINUE TRAVELING TO COUNTIES THROUGHOUT NORTH CAROLINA, PROVIDING INTRODUCTORY AND ADVANCED STEM CURRICULA FOR CHILDREN IN GRADES K-12. ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES: IN THIS AREA WE WILL WORK TO PROTECT THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, PROVIDE THE SOLUTION FOR WASTE MA NAGEMENT AND CONVENTIONAL ENERGY. CAES RESEARCHERS WILL INVESTIGATE AN ADVANCED BIOLOGICAL SYSTEM TO PRODUCE ALTERNATIVE ENERGY, TREAT THE AGRICULTURAL AND INDUSTRIAL WASTE, AND PROTECT AND IMPROVE WATER QUALITY. CAES RESEARCHERS WILL BE INVOLVED IN MULTISTATE CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECT TO STUDY THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE IN SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS AND COMMUNITY OF COLOR. RESEARCHERS WILL BE DEVELOPING THE ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION SOLUTION TO IMPROVE AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND WILL BE PROPOSING POLICIES TO ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND CLIMATE CHANGE. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT SMALL SCALE PRODUCERS AND LANDOWNERS IN THEIR EFFORT TO DEVELOP WOODLOT MANAGEMENT PLANS WHILE ALSO INTEGRATING TECHNIQUES AND PRACTICES SUCH AS SILVOPASTURE PRODUCTION AND RIPARIAN BUFFERS

MSU RREA ABSTRACT MISSISSIPPI CONTAINS OVER 19.5 MILLION ACRES OF FOREST LAND, WHICH ACCOUNTS FOR 65% OF THE STATE'S TOTAL LAND AREA, AND 81% OF MISSI SSIPPI'S FOREST LAND IS PRIVATELY OWNED BY NONINDUSTRIAL LANDOWNERS. OVER 80% OF PRIVATE FOREST OWNERSHIP IS IN PARCELS OF 100 ACRES OR LESS. EDUCATING PRIVATE FAMILY FOREST OWNERS ABOUT FOREST MANAGEMENT, HARVESTING, AND MARKETING PRACTICES AND TECHNIQUES IS ESSE NTIAL TO THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE FOREST RESOURCE. THESE FAMILY FOREST LANDS ARE NOT ALWAYS MANAGED IN A WAY THAT MAXIMIZES PRIVATE AND ASSOCIATED PUBLIC BENEFITS THAT CAN INCLUDE TIMBER PRODUCTS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES, RECREATION AND WATER QUALITY BENEFITS. MANY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS DO NOT HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE OR SKILLS TO MANAGE FORESTS TO MEET THEIR OWN OBJECTIVES. THE RREA PROGRAM ALLOWS MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SERVICE TO GIVE SPECIAL ATTENTION TO HELPING FAMILY FOREST OWNERS MANAGE THEIR FORESTLANDS FOR MAXIMUM BENEFIT. THUS, THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECTIS TO INCREASE AND IMPROVE THE LEVELS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES BEING CONDUCTED ON MISSISSIPPI FORESTLAND SO AS TO ENHANCE ALL THE BENEFITS SOCIETY RECEIVES FROM WELL MANAGED FORESTS. THE CORE GOALS OF THE FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAM AS SUPPORTED BY RREA ARE TO INCREASE THE PRODUCTIVITY, EFFECTIVENESS, EFFICIENCY, AND PROFITABILITY OF OUR CLIENTELE, AS WELL AS AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE MANY VALUES OF THEIR FORESTS. NEW RESEARCH AND TECHNOLOGIES ARE DISSEMINATED TO CLIENTELE STATEWIDE THROUGH FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAMS AND MATERIALS.

MUCH OF OREGON IS FORESTLAND AND RANGELAND, AND MUCH OF THIS ACREAGE IS MANAGED BY PRIVATE OWNERS OF NON-INDUSTRIAL OPERATIONS. RREA FUNDS PROVIDED TO OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY (OSU) ARE USED TO SUPPORT EFFORTS OF OSU EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF TO ASSIST THESE LANDOWNERS IN THEIR RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS, AND TO ASSIST OTHERS IN UNDERSTANDING HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE ECONOMIC AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES THESE LANDS PROVIDE. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION TO OREGONIANS THAT ASSISTS THEM IN UNDERSTANDING HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE HEALTH, PRODUCTIVITY, AND RESILIENCY OF THESE LANDS. OUR AIM IS TO ENSURE HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS, INCREASE ECONOMIC BENEFITS, BUILD CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS, AND IN THE LONG TERM ENSURE SUSTAINABLE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THIS PROJECT HAS SEVERAL OBJECTIVES. OBJECTIVE ONE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF OWNERS AND MANAGERS OF PRIVATE NON- INDUSTRIAL FOREST AND RANGELAND OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES SO AS TO ENABLE THEM TO MEET THEIR MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES WHILE ENSURING HEALTHY FOREST AND RANGELANDS. OBJECTIVE TWO IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW LAND USE AND LAND MANAGEMENT DECISIO NS INFLUENCE HABITAT FOR A VARIETY OF FISH AND WILDLIFE SPECIES TO ENSURE PRODUCTIVE POPULATIONS AND HIGH LEVELS OF BIODIVERSITY ACROSS ECOSYSTEMS. OBJECTIVE THREE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW CLIMATE CHANGE IS LIKELY TO INFLUENCE FOREST AND R ANGELAND RESOURCES (E.G., INCREASED SUMMER TEMPERATURES, PROLONGED DROUGHT, WIDESPREAD INSECT AND DISEASE OUTBREAKS, LARGER WILDFIRES), TO FOSTER EFFORTS THAT REDUCE THE THREATS IMPOSED BY THESE CHANGES. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS; NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS SUCH AS FORESTERS, FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE BIOLOGISTS, RESTORATION SPECIALISTS, AND RANGELAND MANAGERS; FOREST WORKERS SUCH AS LOGGERS, TREE PLANTERS, FIREFIGHTERS; RANCHERS AND FARMERS; FORMAL AND INFORMAL EDUCATORS; POLICYMAKERS; AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. EDUCATIONAL EFFORTS SUPPORTED BY RREA FUNDS ARE GUIDED BY NEEDS ASSESSMENTS AND ARE TAILORED TO BEST MEET THE NEEDS OF THE SPECIFIC AUDIENCES AND SITUATIONS THEY ARE INTENDED TO ADDRESS. STANDARDIZED CURRICULUM AND EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS ARE DEVELOPED AND DELIVERED TO IMPROVE FOREST AND RANGELAND HEALTH, ENSURE HABITAT FOR A VARIETY OF FISH AND WILDLIFE, REDUCE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH CHANGING CLIMATE, AND EDUCATE COMMUNITIES AND POLICYMAKERS OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC CONTRIBUTIONS AND VALUE OF OUR WORKING FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES. SOME EDUCATIONAL EFFORTS ARE REPEATED REGULARLY ACROSS YEARS, WHILE OTHERS ARE CONDUCTED ONLY ONCE AND ONLY IN A SINGLE REGION TO MEET ACUTE NEEDS. SOME USE STANDARDIZED CURRICULUM (ADAPTED TO LOCAL AUDIENCES), WHILE OTHERS ARE DESIGNED TO MEET URGENT, IMMEDIATE NEEDS. SOME ARE LED DIRECTLY BY EXTENSION FACULTY OR STAFF, WHILE OTHERS USE A TRAIN-THE-TRAINER APPROACH TO ACHIEVE MORE WIDESPREAD IMPACTS THROUGH NETWORKS OF TRAINED VOLUNTEERS. EDUCATION EFFORTS ENCOMPASS A WIDE VARIETY OF MODALITIES. WRITTEN MATERIALS INCLUDE PUBLICATIONS AND NEWSLETTERS. ONLINE MATERIALS INCLUDE WEBSITES, BLOGS, WEBINARS, VIDEOS, AND PRE-RECORDED LEARNING MODULES. IN-PERSON EVENTS INCLUDE SITE VISITS, FIELD DAYS, TOURS, SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND SHORT-COURSES. OTHER DELIVERY METHODS INCLUDE HYBRID (PARTIALLY ONLINE AND PARTIALLY IN-PERSON) AND PODCASTS. MANY EDUCATIONAL EFFORTS THAT TRADITIONALLY OCCURRED SOLELY IN PERSON WERE ADAPTED TO A FULLY REMOTE FORMAT TO ENSURE HUMAN HEALTH DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC AND EXPECT TO EVOLVE FURTHER IN THE FUTURE TO BEST MEET THE INTERESTS AND NEEDS OF CLIENTELE. EXTENSION PERSONNEL FROM FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES, RANGELAND RESOURCES ECOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT, AND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES RECEIVE BASE PROGRAM SUPPORT THROUGH RREA FUNDING. IN ADDITION, ALLOCATIONS ARE PROVIDED TO SUB-PROJECTS THAT ADDRESS A VARIETY OF STAKEHOLDER NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELANDS ACROSS THE STATE. RREA FUNDS ARE LEVERAGED WITH BOTH EXTERNAL GRANT FUNDS AND UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SUPPORT. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A WIDE VARIETY OF EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS AND TRAININGS THAT RESULT IN GAINS IN AWARENESS, GAINS IN KNOWLEDGE, INC REASES IN ACREAGE OVER WHICH RECOMMENDED PRACTICES ARE IMPLEMENTED, AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. ALL EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF REPORT ON THE ACTIVITIES PERFORMED AND OUTCOMES ACHIEVED ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

NON-TECHNICAL SUMMARY 8,000 CHARACTERS CUCE RREA PLAN OF WORK 2022-2024 SUSTAINING THE PRODUCTIVITY OF NY'S PRIVATE WOODLANDS RREA AT CORNELL HAS SUFFICIENT STAFF AND RESOURCES TO FOCUS ON THREE PRIMARY ISSUES: FOREST MANAGEMENT FOR DIVERSE OUTPUTS, WILDLIFE RESOURCES, AND FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY PARTICULARLY AS RELATES TO AGROFORESTRY ENTERPRISES OF FOREST FARMING AND SILVOPASTURE. NEW YORK IS APPROXIMATELY 63 PERCENT FORESTED AND HALF OF THE STATE IS IN PRIVATE WOODLAND OWNERSHIP. THE AVERAGE PARCEL SIZE IS LESS THAN 30 ACRES, AND THE MAJORITY OF ACREAGE IS LESS THAN 50 ACRES. THE CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES DEPENDS ON MANY WOODLAND OWNERS MAKING INFORMED DECISIONS THAT SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE OUTCOMES. THE DECISIONS ARE MADE ON SMALL PARCELS BUT AGGREGATE FOR AN ACCUMULATED IMPACT. PRIVATE OWNERS LACK AWARENESS AND KNOWLEDGE TO INTEGRATE BEST PRACTICES. SPECIALISTS AND PRACTITIONERS IDENTIFY KNOWLEDGE GAPS OR SEEK TECHNICAL SUPPORT. EXTENSION EDUCATORS SEEK SUPPORT WITH COMPLEXPROBLEMS AT COUNTY AND MULTI-COUNTY SCALES. PRIVATE WOODLANDS ARE CENTRAL TO MULTIPLE DESIRED OUTCOMES THAT SUPPORT THE MATERIAL NEEDS OF FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY, PRIVATE OWNER TANGIBLE AND INTANGIBLE OUTPUTS, RESILIENCE AGAINST STRESSORS OF THE FOREST, LOCALLY PRODUCED FOOD, AND MOST RECENTLY AN EXPECTATION FOR INCREASED AND SUSTAINED SEQUESTRATION AND STORAGE OF CARBON AS AN OFFSET TO THE STATE’S GREENHOUSE GAS MITIGATION TARGETS. WHILE MANY OF THESE OUTPUTS ARE COMPLEMENTARY, THEIR MUTUAL SUCCESS DEPENDS ON CONSIDERATION OF MULTIPLE CRITERIA AND REFINED MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES. THE GOAL FOR THE FOREST ISSUE IS TO ENSURE THAT FORESTS ARE SUSTAINABLY MANAGED FOR OPTIMAL OUTPUTS OF DESIRED GOODS AND SERVICES. THE OBJECTIVES TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL ARE TO INCREASE OWNER AWARENESS OF INFORMATION, GAIN ACCESS TO TECHNICAL SPECIALISTS THAT SUPPORT THEIR INFORMED DECISION MAKING, AND PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO TECHNICAL SPECIALISTS AND PRACTITIONERS BASED ON APPLIED RESEARCH. THE GOAL FOR WILDLIFE RESOURCES IS TO SUSTAIN AND ENHANCE THE BIODIVERSITY AND HEALTH OF NATIVE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS IN BALANCE WITH THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE IN THEIR ECOSYSTEMS. THE OBJECTIVE FOR THIS GOAL IS TO USE APPLIED RESEARCH TO INFORM THE DECISION MAKING OF WOODLAND OWNERS, WILDLIFE SPECIALISTS AND PRACTITIONERS. THE GOAL FOR FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY IS TO EXPAND THE AVAILABILITY OF LOCALLY PRODUCED FOREST-BASED FOODS, AND TO ENSURE THAT THE PRODUCERS ARE FINANCIALLY AND ECOLOGICALLY SUSTAINABLE. THE OBJECTIVE FOR THIS GOAL IS TO DEMONSTRATE BEST PRACTICES, ACCESS APPLIED RESEARCH ON PRIMARY FOODS (E.G., MAPLE SYRUP) AND RELATED FOOD DERIVATIVES, AND PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THAT SUPPORT NEW AND ESTABLISHED FOREST-FOOD BASED ENTERPRISES. THE ACTIVITIES DESCRIBED IN THE METHODS SECTION REFLECT A STRATEGY THAT RECOGNIZES STAKEHOLDERS ARRIVE AT DIFFERENT LEVELS OF AWARENESS, HAVE PREFERRED AND SOMETIMES ESSENTIAL MODES OF LEARNING, AND BENEFIT FROM MULTIPLE EXPOSURES TO SIMILAR INFORMATION,OPTIMALLY DEMONSTRATED TO ALLOW THEM TO VISUALIZE THE OUTCOME. IN RESPONSE TO DIFFERENT LEVELS OF AWARENESS, OUR PROGRAM MATERIALS RANGE FROM INTRODUCTORY TO MODERATELY COMPLEX. HIGHLY COMPLEX MATERIAL IS PROVIDED AS PEER REVIEWED SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS OR TECHNICAL REPORTS AND LARGELY OUTSIDE THE SCOPE OF RREA. WE ADDRESS PREFERRED LEARNING MODES BY CREATING MULTIPLE OUTLETS AND FORMATS THAT RANGE FROM SOCIAL MEDIA TO FACT SHEETS TO YOUTUBE TO FIELD TOURS AND DEMONSTRATION SITES. THE POWER OF VISUALIZATION IS REMARKABLE IN ITS CAPACITY TO CONVEY THE OPPORTUNITIES OF A PARTICULAR ACTION. THAT POWER, HOWEVER, CARRIES THE OBLIGATION TO ENSURE THAT THE ASSUMPTIONS OF WHAT’S DEMONSTRATED ARE CLEARLY DEFINED RELATIVE TO FACTORS THAT MIGHT BE DIFFERENT ELSEWHERE AND RESULT IN A DIFFERENT OUTCOME. DEMONSTRATIONS ARE CREATED TO ALLOW FOR DIRECT ENGAGEMENT, BUT ALSO THROUGH VIDEO, PICTURES, AND ILLUSTRATIONS. METHODOLOGY 8,000 CHARACTERS 1. ONLINE: A VARIETY OF ONLINE MEDIA WILL BE USED. WEBINARS WILL BE OFFERED MONTHLY, WITH ADDITIONAL SPECIAL FEATURE WEBINARS ON AN AS NEEDED BASIS. THE BASE PAGE FOR THE PROGRAM, WWW.FORESTCONNECT.INFO WILL INCLUDE ALL PROGRAM-RELEVANT EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS. VIDEO WILL BE UPLOADED TO YOUTUBE AND DISTRIBUTED THROUGH THE SOCIAL NETWORK. FACEBOOK PAGES WILL BE USED TO SUPPORT A COMMUNITY OF INTEREST. THE SOCIAL NETWORK SITE HTTP://CORNELLFORESTCONNECT.NING.COM AND HTTP://SILVOPASTURE.NING.COM WILL BE FURTHER DEVELOPED FOR INTERACTIONS AMONG STAKEHOLDERS AND TO SHARE RESOURCES. RREA FUNDS AS NECESSARY WILL ENSURE ADEQUATE COMPUTER HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE. 2. PEER-VOLUNTEERS: MASTER FOREST OWNER VOLUNTEERS WILL CONTINUE TO CONNECT WITH PRIVATE WOODLAND OWNERS. MASTER NATURALISTS WILL WORK IN THEIR COMMUNITIES THROUGH A VARIETY OF NETWORKS. ANNUALLY THERE WILL BE A NEW VOLUNTEER TRAINING, REGIONAL REFRESHERS, AND/OR OPPORTUNITIES FOR THESE TRAINED PARTICIPANTS TO CONTINUE TO DEVELOP PROFESSIONALLY. SELECT CCE EDUCATORS WILL SERVE AS REGIONAL DIRECTORS, AND THEY WILL ASSIST WITH PROGRAM MANAGEMENT. 3. DEMONSTRATION SITES: UNIVERSITY AND PRIVATE WOODLANDS WILL BE USED, AND MAY DEMONSTRATE PRACTICES SUCH AS, MANAGEMENT OF INTERFERING VEGETATION, MAPLE SYRUP PRODUCTION, SILVOPASTURE, WOODY BIOMASS HARVESTS, DEER IMPACTS, AND SILVICULTURAL PRACTICES. AREAS WHERE TEAMS OF MASTER NATURALIST VOLUNTEERS COMPLETE PROJECTS WILL BE INCLUDED ON SOCIAL MEDIA. 4. APPLIED RESEARCH: APPLIED RESEARCH WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF DIRECT SUPPORT OF EXTENSION EDUCATION WILL ADDRESS ISSUES AND QUESTIONS THAT LACK AN ADEQUATE RESEARCH BASIS. RREA FUNDS WILL AT MOST PROVIDE A MINIMAL SUPPLEMENT TO APPLIED RESEARCH FUNDS. TOPICS MAY INCLUDE VEGETATION MANAGEMENT, CONTROLLING DEER IMPACTS, FOREST CARBON MANAGEMENT, AND SILVICULTURAL MANIPULATIONS. 5. WORKSHOPS, TOURS AND FIELD DAYS: FIELD-BASED EVENTS WILL BE HELD WITH CCE EDUCATORS ON CORNELL AND PRIVATE LANDS TO DESCRIBE, DEMONSTRATE AND ILLUSTRATE SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES. 6. CONFERENCES AND SEMINARS: INDOOR EVENTS WILL PROVIDE AUDIENCES WITH SEMINAR STYLE LEARNING ON A VARIETY OF TOPICS. 7. MASS MEDIA: A MARKETING CAMPAIGN WILL DRAW ATTENTION TO EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM RESOURCES. 8. EDUCATOR IN-SERVICE: AN ANNUAL FORESTRY-MAPLE TRAINING FOR CCE EDUCATORS WILL PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY TO SHARE PROGRAM STRATEGIES, AND INTERACT WITH CAMPUS SPECIALISTS. 9. WRITTEN MATERIALS: STAFF AND SPECIALISTS, WITH COLLEAGUES, WILL DEVELOP FACT SHEETS, BULLETINS, AND ARTICLE SERIES ON RREA TOPICS. WRITTEN MATERIALS WILL TYPICALLY BE AVAILABLE ONLINE. 10. ORGANIZATIONAL SUPPORT: STAFF WILL WORK WITH PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, FOR EXAMPLE THE NEW YORK FOREST OWNERS ASSOCIATION AND THE STATE FORESTRY AGENCY, ON PROJECTS OF MUTUAL INTEREST AND THAT ENHANCE WORKING FOREST CONDITIONS. 11. EVALUATION OF PROGRAM ACTIVITIES WILL HAPPEN THROUGH INFORMAL EXIT SURVEYS, DOCUMENTATION OF PARTICIPATION AT EVENTS, WEB-BASED ANALYTICAL SOFTWARE, AND CALCULATIONS THAT PROJECT BEHAVIOR CHANGES. WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT FORMAL SURVEYS OF PEOPLE WHO USE PROGRAMS TO UNDERSTAND THEIR RESPONSE, AND TO HELP ADJUST OUR ESTIMATES OF CHANGES FROM NON-SURVEYED PROGRAM ACTIVITIES.

UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA LEVERAGES RREA FUNDS WITH OTHER SOURCES OF FUNDING, PRIMARILY SALARY AND PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (UF/IFAS), TO PROVIDE EXTENSION SUPPORT TO TWELVE EXTENSION FACULTY AND THREE TECHNICAL STAFF IN THE SCHOOL OF FOREST, FISHERIES AND GEOMATICS SCIENCES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF WILDLIFE ECOLOGY AND CONSERVATION. THE PURPOSE OF THESE EXTENSION PROGRAMS IS TO ADDRESS MULTIPLE STAKEHOLDERS NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES IN FLORIDA; PROMOTE INFORMATION TRANSFER REGARDING THE ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES; AND PROVIDE INFORMATION ON LAND USE OPTIONS AND STRATEGIES FOR WORKING LANDSCAPES AND URBAN FORESTS. SPECIFIC AREAS PRIORITIZED IN UF/IFAS EXTENSION PROGRAMS INCLUDE PROVIDING INFORMATION ON MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT INCREASE FOREST HEALTH AND MANAGEMENT; IDENTIFY AND CONTROL FOREST INSECT PESTS, PASTURE WEEDS AND INVASIVE PLANTS AND ANIMALS; AND PROVIDE EDUCATION ON THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC CONTRIBUTIONS AND VALUE OF OUR WORKING FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES IN FLORIDA, INCLUDING THE URBAN FOREST LANDSCAPE. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE FORMAL EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS SUCH AS COURSES, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS; INFORMAL INTERACTIONS TOA ADDRESS INDIVIDUAL PROBLEMS THROUGH PHONE CALLS, EMAIL CORRESPONDENCE, AND SITE VISITS; AND PASSIVE EDUCATION SUCH AS ONLINE WEBSITES AND EXTENSION FACT SHEETS THROUGH THE UF/IFD EDIS (ELECTRONIC DATA INFORMATION SOURCE) SYSTEM. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL DELIVER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS BOTH IN‐PERSON VIA WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING PROGRAMS THAT INCLUDE CLASSROOM, LAB, AND/OR FIELD EXPERIENCES; ONLINE TOOLS INCLUDING WEBINARS, WEBSITES, AND VIDEOS; AND SOCIAL MEDIA SUCH AS TWITTER, BLOGS, AND APPS. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE EVENTS AND PRODUCTS. EVENTS WILL INCLUDE FACILITATION AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL RESOURCES LEADERSHIP INSTITUTE (NRLI), EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS ADDRESSING FOREST AND RANGELAND MANAGEMENT, NATURAL HISTORY, AND CONSERVATION THROUGH FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS SUCH AS THE FLORIDA FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND THE MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAMS; FOREST AND RANGE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL AREAS TRAINING ACADEMY (NATA); WORKSHOPS ON THE MANAGEMENT OF INVASIVE PLATS AND ANIMALS, FOREST INSECT PESTS, AND RANGELAND WEEDS VIA WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DAYS THROUGH REGIONAL WORKSHOPS AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS INCLUDING THE FOREST STEWARDSHIP PROGRAM, BARK BEETLE ACADEMY, AND THE INVASIVE SPECIES COUNCIL AND THE COOPERATIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AREAS TEAMS. PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION FACT SHEETS, PUBLISHED ONLINE IN THE UF/IFAS EDIS SYSTEM ON MULTIPLE TOPICS INCLUDING FOREST AND RANGELAND WILDLIFE, FOREST AND RANGELAND HEALTH AND MANAGEMENT, INVASIVE SPECIES AND THEIR CONTROL, AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL MAINTAIN, UPDATE, AND EXPAND (E.G., INVASIVE SPECIES WEBSITE PORTAL) WEBSITES IN FORESTRY, WILDLIFE, INVASIVE SPECIES, AND RELATED EXTENSION PROGRAMS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE CHANGE IN KNOWLEDGE, CHANGE IN ACTION, AND CHANGE IN CONDITION. WE EXPECT OUR TRAINING PROGRAMS, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS TO INCREASE PARTICIPANT KNOWLEDGE. WE EXPECT THAT PARTICIPANTS IN TRAINING PROGRAMS AND WORKSHOPS/FIELD DAYS WILL INDICATE THE INTENTION OF IMPLEMENTING AT LEAST ONE MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATION OR OTHER ACTION. WE ALSO EXPECT THAT PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT OR OTHER ACTIONS THAT WILL AFFECT 25% OF THE FLORIDA ACREAGE MANAGEMENT BY PARTICIPANTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF OUR ACTIVITIES AND DELIVERABLES INCLUDE FLORIDA PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, FOREST, AND RANGELAND MANAGERS; PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, BIOLOGISTS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTANTS; EDUCATORS; ELECTED OFFICIALS AND STAFF, NON‐GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND INTERESTED CITIZENS; AND ECO/AGRITOURISM AND OTHER SMALL BUSINESS/RECREATIONAL OPERATIONS ON PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LANDS.

FEDERAL PURPOSE THE PURPOSE OF OUR RREA PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE EXTENSION PROGRAMMING DESIGNED TO ASSIST FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS AND MANAGERS IN MAKING SCIENCE-BASED RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS TO MEET THE FOREST AND RANGELAND SAFETY, PRODUCTION, PROTECTION, AND SUSTAINABILITY NEEDS OF THE OWNER AND SOCIETY. TOPICAL ISSUES INCLUDE: LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT; PUBLIC AWARENESS AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT; INVASIVE SPECIES; WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT; RURAL COMMUNITIES; WATER AND WETLANDS; GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION AND OTHER LAND-OWNERSHIP CHANGES; FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT; AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. WSUS RREA PROGRAM IS ALIGNED WITH THE USDA STRATEGIC GOAL #1, TO “COMBAT CLIMATE CHANGE TO SUPPORT AMERICA’S WORKING LANDS, NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMUNITIES.” OF THE TOPICS WE ADDRESS, WE FOCUS ON THE RREA GOAL ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. OUR ISSUES AREAS ARE 1) FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH, AND 2) RANGELAND STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH. OUR FOCUS IS WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF FOREST AND RANGE FIRES, AND THE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOREST AND RANGE RESOURCES. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED THE WSU EXTENSION FORESTRY <(>&<)> RANGE TEAM WILL PROVIDE THE UNBIASED, RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES TO MEET THE NEEDS OF LANDOWNERS AND SOCIETY. THROUGH FACE-TO-FACE AND ONLINE DELIVERIES OF CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, SEMINARS, CONFERENCES, PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, SHORT COURSES, RECRUITMENT, TRAININGS, CONSULTATIONS, MEDIA WORK, AND EDUCATIONAL COUNSELING AND FACILITATION, LANDOWNERS WILL IMPROVE LEARNING AND APPLICATION OF NEW IDEAS THAT WILL LEAD TO DESIRABLE FUTURE CONDITIONS. THESE PROGRAMS WILL BE PROVIDED BOTH LIVE AND PRE-RECORDED, TO SUIT PREFERENCE AND CONVENIENCE FOR LANDOWNERS TO ACCESS NEEDED INFORMATION. WHEN NECESSARY, INFORMATION WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN SPANISH FOR THOSE WITH ENGLISH AS A SECOND LANGUAGE. PHYSICAL ACCESS AND DISABILITIES WILL BE INQUIRED ABOUT FOLLOWED BY ADA STANDARDS. DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES WSU EXPECTS TO DELIVER 100 ACTIVITIES (DESCRIBED ABOVE) REACHING 10,000 OWNERS AND MANAGERS AND POSITIVELY IMPACTING THE CONDITION OF ½-MILLION ACRES OF FOREST AND RANGELAND. COMPREHENSIVE ACHIEVEMENTS WILL 1) TO ENHANCE FOREST AND RANGE SUSTAINABILITY BY DEVELOPING OWNER/ MANAGER CAPACITIES TO IMPROVE VIGOR AND PRODUCTIVITY; 2) PROMOTE FOREST AND RANGE LAND RESILIENCE BY PREPARING OWNER/ MANAGER CAPACITIES TO RESPOND TO THE ABIOTIC AND BIOTIC IMPACTS CAUSED BY WILDFIRE, DROUGHT, WILDLIFE DAMAGE, INVASIVE SPECIES, HARMFUL INSECTS AND DISEASE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS PERPETUATED BY CLIMATE CHANGE; AND 3) DIVERSITY FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS/ MANAGERS STEWARDSHIP OPPORTUNITIES THAT LEAD TO MULTIPLE-USE BENEFITS. WE BASE THESE EXPECTATIONS ON ACCOMPLISHMENTS DERIVED BY THE PAST 15 YEARS OF PROGRAM EVALUATION DATA. THESE DATA REVEALED THAT LANDOWNERS AND MANAGERS ENGAGED IN IN LEARNING-- CREATING AWARENESS AND CHANGES IN ATTITUDE, IMPROVED KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS, AND MOTIVATED THE APPLICATION AND/OR THE TRANSFER OF TECHNOLOGY TO PRACTICES  ON THE GROUND. WE EXPECT BEST PRACTICE DECISIONS AND BEHAVIORS EXECUTED WILL LEAD TO COMPREHENSIVE ACHIEVEMENTS AND IMPROVE THE ECONOMIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND ADD VALUE TO NATURAL RESOURCE CONDITIONS AND PRODUCTS. NOTEWORTHY IMPACTS WE EXPECT WILL: 1) IMPROVED FOREST <(>&<)> RANGELAND HEALTH; 2) DECREASE RISK FROM WILDFIRE; 3) IMPROVE HABITAT; 4) DECREASE RISKS FROM INSECT OR DISEASE; 5) IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY FOR GROWING TREES AND FORAGE; 6) DECREASE RISK OF EROSION; 7) INCREASE FORAGE AND TREE COVER; 8) IMPROVE WOOD QUALITY; 9) IMPROVE INCOME OPPORTUNITY; 10) IMPROVE IDENTIFICATION AND PROTECTION OF CULTURAL RESOURCES AND SPECIAL SITES; 11) IMPROVE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES; AND 12) DECREASE NOXIOUS WEEDS/ INVASIVE SPECIES. INDICATORS OF LEARNING (SHORT-TERM CHANGES) WILL BE ASSESSMENTS OF AWARENESS, KNOWLEDGE, AND SKILLS. WE WILL NOT SEEK INFORMATION REGARDING MANAGEMENT OPINIONS, ASPIRATIONS,OR MOTIVATIONS, THOUGH WE RECOGNIZE THAT THESE ARE SOMETIMES USED FOR EVALUATION METRICS. INSTEAD, WE SEEK TO MEASURE CHANGES IN OWNER/MANAGER BEHAVIORS, PRACTICES, AND WHEN APPROPRIATE, DECISIONS (FOR EXAMPLE, ASKING FOR A FORESTER VISIT, OR, APPLYING FOR COST-SHARE ASSISTANCE TO IMPLEMENT A PLANNING CONTRACT). WSU WILL DISSEMINATE INFORMATION VIA PERSONAL CONNECTIONS AND AFFILIATIONS, PARTNER NETWORKS, AND THROUGH STAFF EMAIL LISTS. WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE NATIVE AMERICAN AGROFORESTRY ROUNDTABLE AND OTHER FORUMS THAT ENGAGE WSU WITH TRIBAL CONNECTIONS THROUGH THE EXTENSION SERVICE AND THROUGH TRIBAL NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS. WE WILL CREATE ONLINE VIDEO CONTENT, CREATE POPULAR NEWSLETTERS AND RELEVANT MEDIA, AND WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE UNIVERSITY PRESS. MANY VIDEOS WILL BE HOSTED ON YOUTUBE AND INDEXED ON OUR WEBSITE. OTHER VECTORS OF DISSEMINATION WILL INCLUDE SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS (TWITTER, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM). PROGRAMS AND PUBLICATIONS WILL BE IDENTIFIABLE FOR BOTH ACCESSIBILITIES, AND FOR BILINGUAL AVAILABILITY WHERE WE SEE MOST FIT (SPANISH VERSION WHERE USER IS EXPECTED TO SPEAK SPANISH AS A FIRST LANGUAGE). WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR OUTREACH BY UTILIZING PARTNERSHIPS SUCH AS THE WA ASSOCIATION OF CONSERVATION ASSOCIATIONS, WA FARM FORESTRY ASSOCIATION, WA SOCIETY OF AMERICAN FORESTERS, INLAND EMPIRE SOCIETY OF AMERICAN FORESTERS, FORESTRY COLLABORATIVES, AND COUNTY PARTNERSHIPS. WE WILL CONTRIBUTE TO NGO PURPOSES THAT HOLD COMMON CONSERVATION GOALS FOR INFORMING THEIR MEMBERSHIP AND THE PUBLIC, SUCH AS THE NATURE CONSERVANCY, AMERICAN TREE FARM SYSTEM, AMERICAN FOREST FOUNDATIONS, ROCKY MOUNTAIN ELK FOUNDATION, AND VARIOUS LAND TRUSTS. WE WILL CAPTURE BOTH DIRECT AND INDIRECT CONTACTS FOR EVALUATION AND IMPACT ASSESSMENT. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OUR RREA PROGRAM TARGETS NON-INDUSTRIAL PRIVATE LANDOWNERS (NIPF) AND PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS (PRACTICING FORESTERS, LOGGERS, RANCHERS, SILVICULTURAL CONTRACTORS, AND TRIBAL NATURAL RESOURCE EMPLOYEES). WASHINGTON HAS 215,000 NIPF OWNERS THAT CONTROL 5.8 MILLION ACRES OF FORESTLAND, MAKING THIS THE LARGEST RURAL LAND USE GROUP IN THE STATE. ANOTHER 4.0 MILLION ACRES OF PRIVATE LAND IS GRAZED AS EITHER OPEN AND FORESTED OR TRANSITORY GRASS/ CROPLAND. MOST LANDOWNERS MANAGE FOR MULTIPLE OBJECTIVES, SUCH AS PRODUCTIVE TIMBER AND RANGE LAND, WILDLIFE HABITAT, AND RECREATION. HOWEVER, MOST NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS AGREE THAT MOST LANDOWNERS LACK THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILL TO ACCOMPLISH THEIR PERSONAL OBJECTIVES. THIS JEOPARDIZES THE HEALTH AND SAFETY OF THE LAND, THE ECONOMIC WELL-BEING OF THE LANDOWNER, AND THE PROTECTION OF PUBLIC RESOURCES SUCH AS WATER, AIR, AND WILDLIFE. MOST LANDOWNERS LACK A WRITTEN MANAGEMENT PLAN WHICH PROVIDES THE BIOLOGICAL, PHYSICAL, AND POLITICAL INFORMATION NECESSARY TO MAKE SOUND DECISIONS TO EXECUTE BEST PRACTICES IN A LOGICAL AND FEASIBLE MANNER. FOREST AND RANGE OWNERS NEED A SURROUND-SOUND APPROACH OF EDUCATIONAL DELIVERIES OF MANAGEMENT INFORMATIONTO PROTECT THEIR VALUES WITHOUT COMPROMISING THOSE AMENITY AND COMMODITY FOREST AND RANGE VALUES FOR THEMSELVES, SOCIETY, AND FUTURE FOR GENERATIONS.

PROJECT ABSTRACT ARKANSAS FORESTS AND NATURAL RESOURCES ARE CRITICAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY AND WELL-BEING OF ITS CITIZENS; THE STATE IS KNOWN AS "THE NATURAL STATE". MUCH OF THE STATE (54%) IS FORESTED, WITH THE MOST PREVALENT FOREST TYPES BEING OAK-HICKORY (40%) AND LOBLOLLY AND SHORTLEAF PINE (32%). THESE DIVERSE FORESTS PROVIDE HABITAT TO DIVERSE WILDLIFE SPECIES. THESE RANGE FROM GAME SPECIES, SUCH AS DEER, TURKEY, AND DUCKS, TO SONGBIRDS FOR WILDLIFE VIEWING, AND MANY REPTILES AND AMPHIBIANS. ARKANSAS FORESTS ALSO PROVIDE CLEAN DRINKING WATER TO METROPOLITAN AREAS AND PROTECT OTHER IMPORTANT WATERSHEDS. RAW MATERIALS FROM ARKANSAS FORESTS SUPPORT A VIBRANT FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY THAT CONTRIBUTED $6 BILLION TO THE STATE’S ECONOMY IN 2021. NON-INDUSTRIAL PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS OWN 69% OF ARKANSAS’S FORESTLANDS. THIS LANDOWNER GROUP IS EXTREMELY DIVERSE AND INCLUDES FARMERS, RANCHERS, HOMEOWNERS, TEACHERS, FACTORY WORKERS, PROFESSIONALS, AND RETIREES. THE DEMAND FOR BENEFITS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS, INCLUDING WILDLIFE HABITAT AND FOREST PRODUCTS, MUST INCREASINGLY BE MET BY THESE PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS. HOWEVER, MANY OF THESE LANDOWNERS ARE UNFAMILIAR WITH SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, TIMBER MARKETING, HABITAT RESTORATION, REFORESTATION INCENTIVES, AND OTHER VITAL INFORMATION CRITICAL TO SUSTAINING FORESTLANDS. MOST OF THEM ALSO HOLD THEIR FORESTLANDS FOR REASONS OTHER THAN TIMBER MANAGEMENT. AS SUCH, THE SECURITY OF FUTURE TIMBER SUPPLIES AND FOREST HEALTH IS COMPROMISED BY LACK OF LANDOWNER KNOWLEDGE OF THESE ISSUES. SEVERAL ISSUES ARE THREATENING ARKANSAS FORESTS, HOWEVER. INVASIVE PESTS INCLUDING FERAL HOGS, EMERALD ASH BORER, AND LAUREL WILT DISEASE ARE BUT A FEW OF THE DIRECT FACTORS AFFECTING FOREST HEALTH IN RURAL AND URBAN FORESTS. FORESTERS ARE ALSO CONCERNED ABOUT A POTENTIAL INCREASE IN PINE BARK BEETLES INCLUDING SOUTHERN PINE BEETLE RESULTING FROM STRESS FROM OVER-CROWDING AND DROUGHT. OTHER LESS DIRECT FACTORS ARE FOREST FRAGMENTATION, FOREST DENSIFICATION, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND A WEAK FOREST PRODUCTS MARKET. WEAK MARKETS CREATE CONSTRAINTS TO SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. NEW FOREST-BASED PRODUCTS, INCLUDING BIO-ENERGY, WOOD PELLETS, ARE STILL IN THE DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE BUT WILL HOPEFULLY AUGMENT AND INCREASE DEMAND FOR WOOD PRODUCTS. OUR GOAL THEN, IS TO INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO MANAGE AND SUSTAIN HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS THAT MEET HUMAN AND ECOL OGICAL NEEDS. ASSOCIATED WITH THIS GOAL, OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO IMPROVE FORESTRY STAKEHOLDER AWARENESS OF FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES BY: (1) HOSTING IN-PERSON EVENTS (WORKSHOPS, FIELD TOURS), (2) HOSTING VIRTUAL EVENTS (WEBINARS), (3) CONDUCTING DEMON STRATION PROJECTS, (4) DEVELOPING WEB-BASED MANAGEMENT TOOLS AND (5) PUBLISHING RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION THROUGH DIVERSE MEDIA (BULLETINS, POPULAR PRESS, MEDIA RELEASES, INTERNET ARTICLES).
