positiveFlows.title: PROJECT ABSTRACT – MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY: RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION HELPS IMPROVE PEOPLE’S LIVES THROUGH AN EDUCATIONAL PROCESS THAT APPLIES KNOWLEDGE TO CRITICAL ISSUES, NEEDS, AND OPPORTUNITIES. FOR MORE THAN 100 YEARS, MSU EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF MEMBERS HAVE BEEN ACTIVELY REACHING PEOPLE WHERE THEY ARE – IN THEIR HOMES, FARMS, BUSINESSES, AND COMMUNITIES – WITH RESEARCH DRIVEN EDUCATION. WE HELP PEOPLE PERFORM THEIR JOBS BETTER, RAISE HEALTHY AND SAFE FAMILIES, BUILD STRONGER COMMUNITIES, AND EMPOWER CHILDREN TO DREAM OF BRIGHTER FUTURES. WITH RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM (RREA) FUNDING, MSU EXTENSION FOSTERS ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE, A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, AND A PLENTIFUL AND SECURE FOOD SUPPLY FOR MICHIGAN RESIDENTS. MICHIGAN’S NATURAL RESOURCES ARE A FUNDAMENTAL ASSET FOR THE STATE’S FUTURE ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES. CHALLENGES CONCERN HOW RESIDENTS OF THE STATE CAN BEST BENEFIT FROM ITS RICH NATURAL HERITAGE WITHOUT OVERBURDENING THE CARRYING CAPACITY OF ITS NATURAL SYSTEMS AND REDUCING OPPORTUNITIES FOR RESIDENTS AND VISITORS ALIKE. OUR NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS IMPROVE PUBLIC UNDERSTANDING, HELP LANDOWNERS AND COMMUNITIES USE THOSE ASSETS FOR SUSTAINABLE LONG‐TERM SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. WE WILL DEVELOP TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY TO HELP MICHIGAN'S NATURAL RESOURCE‐BASED TOURISM INDUSTRY GROW BY MEETING CONSUMER DEMANDS AND DETERMINE HOW WILDLIFE, FISHERIES, FOREST AND NATURAL RESOURCES AREAS RESPOND TO HABITAT MANAGEMENT TO ENCOURAGE MANAGEMENT FOR SUSTAINABLE BENEFITS.

PURPOSE THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AT PENN STATE WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT TO PENNSYLVANIA RESIDENTS THROUGH THE PENNSYLVANIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND PENN STATE EXTENSION (PSE) ACTIVITIES. WE WILL BE RESPONSIVE TO STAKEHOLDER NEEDS THROUGH TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH AND DELIVERY OF SCIENCE‐BASED PROGRAMS TO CLIENTELE. WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT INTERNATIONALLY RELEVANT FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH THAT GENERATES BASELINE DATA TO SOLVE FUTURE PROBLEMS AND ACTIVELY SEEK NEW AND BETTER WAYS TO COMMUNICATE OUR PROGRAMS TO NEW AUDIENCES. OUR FACULTY AND STAFF, SUPPORTED BY FEDERAL BASE FUNDING, WILL EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE THIS INVESTMENT AGAINST MANY OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO CONDUCT PROGRAMS OF THE HIGHEST CALIBER. WE ARE COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE IN RESEARCH, EDUCATING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS AND CITIZENS, AND PROMOTING LIFE‐LONG LEARNING AMONG THE CITIZENS OF PENNSYLVANIA. OUR COLLEGE'S MISSION IS CLEAR: "THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES IS TO DISCOVER, INTEGRATE, TRANSLATE, AND DISSEMINATE KNOWLEDGE TO ENHANCE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM, NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP, AND ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL WELL‐BEING, THEREBY IMPROVING THE LIVES OF PEOPLE IN PENNSYLVANIA, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD." AGRICULTURE FACES CHALLENGES OF RISING ENERGY COSTS, WEATHER EXTREMES, AN EXPANDING HUMAN POPULATION, ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, AND LABOR SHORTAGES. THE COVID‐19 PANDEMIC ADDED TO THE CHALLENGES: DISRUPTIONS TO FOOD CHAINS, WORKFORCE CHALLENGES, IMPACTS ON YOUTH EDUCATION, AND BUSINESS INTERRUPTIONS. WE MUST ADDRESS THESE ISSUES TO MITIGATE FUTURE WIDESPREAD DISRUPTIONS THAT IMPACT ALL OF SOCIETY. ACTIVITIES TO HELP MEET THESE CHALLENGES, WE ARE DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK BASED ON THE SCIENCE OF AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY‐‐DEFINED AS THE INTEGRATION OF NATURAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO INFORM PRACTICE AND POLICY FOR PRODUCTIVE, WORKING LANDSCAPES, HEALTHY WATERSHEDS, AND RESILIENT ECONOMIES. THIS INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH, ENGAGEMENT, AND EDUCATION CENTERS ON THE IMPACTS AND SYNERGIES OF CONTIGUOUS RURAL AND URBAN LANDSCAPES. PENN STATE EXTENSION PROVIDES ACCESS TO FACE‐TO‐FACE AND ONLINE SCIENCE‐BASED EDUCATION TO OUR CUSTOMERS TO HELP THEM ADDRESS PROBLEMS AND TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVEMENT AND INNOVATION. WE MAKE A DIFFERENCE LOCALLY THROUGH FOCUSED ENGAGEMENT AND, MORE WIDELY, TO CUSTOMERS CONNECTING IN THE DIGITAL LANDSCAPE. INITIATIVES ENSURE THE STABILITY OF THE FOOD SYSTEM IN THE COMMONWEALTH AND OUR EFFORTS TO PROVIDE A BROAD‐BASED ONLINE LEARNING PLATFORM FOR NONCREDIT PROGRAMMING AND DIGITAL EDUCATION. THE WORK OF AES AND PSE IN OUR COLLEGE IS BUILT ON THE THREE INTEGRATED PILLARS OF INTENSIFICATION, RESILIENCE, AND REGENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AS SOLUTIONS TO SOME OF THE MOST VEXING PROBLEMS CONFRONTING PENNSYLVANIA AND SIMILAR MOSAIC LANDSCAPES WORLDWIDE. OUR CRITICAL ISSUES CAPTURE THE SYSTEMS APPROACH WE IDENTIFIED AS ESSENTIAL FOR GENERATING IMPACT. THEY CUT ACROSS DISCIPLINES, UNITING OUR RESEARCH EFFORTS WITH OUR EXTENSION EDUCATION CAPACITY. THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY PHILOSOPHY HAS REINFORCED THE NATURAL TENDENCY OF OUR FACULTY AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS TO WORK COOPERATIVELY TO SOLVE PROBLEMS. COUPLED WITH THE JOINT RESEARCH‐EXTENSION APPOINTMENTS OF MANY OF OUR COLLEGE FACULTY, OUR WORK, AS REPRESENTED IN OUR PLAN OF WORK, WILL EFFECTIVELY UNITE FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE WITH PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS DELIVERED TO STAKEHOLDERS, EMPOWERING THEM TO ADDRESS IMPORTANT AND EMERGING ISSUES USING RELEVANT SCIENCE‐BASED RESOURCES. THE NET RESULT WILL BE A TANGIBLE BENEFIT IN ECONOMIC PROSPERITY AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR PENNSYLVANIA CITIZENS.

PROJECT ABSTRACT WISCONSIN IS A LARGELY FORESTED LANDSCAPE COVERING 16 MILLION ACRES, ABOUT 46% OF THE STATE'S LAND AREA. OVERALL, 57% OF THE FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES, TOTALING 360,000 OWNERS. FOREST INDUSTRY IS VITAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY; THE STATE CONTINUES TO BE THE NUMBER ONE PAPER PRODUCING STATE IN THE COUNTRY, AND FOREST PRODUCT INDUSTRIES ARE SCATTERED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. THIS INDUSTRY RELIES HEAVILY ON FAMILY OWNED FORESTLAND. THE WDNR ESTIMATES THAT 10% OF THE 9.1 MILLION FORESTED ACRES, HELD BY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS, WILL BE SOLD, SUBDIVIDED OR CONVERTED TO NON‐FOREST USE IN THE NEXT 5 YEARS. IN A SIMILAR STUDY, THE SUSTAINING FAMILY FORESTS INITIATIVE (SFFI) FOUND THE HIGHEST CONCERN REPORTED BY 56% OF ALL LANDOWNERS WAS "KEEPING LAND INTACT FOR CHILDREN/HEIRS". INCIDENTALLY, THE SECOND HIGHEST CONCERN WAS "HIGH PROPERTY TAXES". A THIRD STUDY, BY GOBSTER AND RICKENBACH (2004) LOOKED AT PERCEPTIONS OF PARCELIZATION. THE PRIMARY DRIVERS INCLUDED ECONOMIC, DEMOGRAPHIC, VALUES <(>&<)> MOTIVATIONS, GLOBALIZATION <(>&<)> TECHNOLOGY, NATURAL CAPITAL, AND POLICIES. THUS EDUCATING LANDOWNERS ON RECOGNIZING THE BEST ECONOMIC RETURN ON TIMBER HARVESTS, UNDERSTANDING HOW DIVIDING PROPERTY AFFECTS THE ECOSYSTEM, AND WHAT POLICIES EXISTS TO ASSIST WITH MANAGEMENT WILL ASSIST WITH THESE ISSUES. OUR COMPREHENSIVE FORESTRY OUTREACH PROGRAM ZEROS IN ON THESE CONCERNS. DURING FFY2023, WISCONSIN RREA PROGRAMMING WILL ADDRESS RENEWABLE RESOURCES IN A VARIETY OF PROGRAMS AND PARTNERSHIPS TO ADDRESS STRATEGIC AND CROSS‐CUTTING NATIONAL ISSUES RELATING TO GOALS IDENTIFIED IN THE NIFA RREA STRATEGIC PLAN. GOAL 1‐ ENSURING HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND GOAL 3 ‐ ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THE PRIMARY CROSS‐CUTTING ISSUES WE WILL FOCUS ON INCLUDE FISH AND WILDLIFE R ESOURCES, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND INTERGENERATIONAL LAND AND OTHER LAND OWNERSHIP CHANGES. THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO HELP LANDOWNERS DEVELOP FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AROUND WOODLAND ECOLOGY, HEALTHY FORESTS, TIMBER HARVEST PRACTICES AND SALES, HABITAT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT BENEFIT WILDLIFE, STRATEGIES FOR THREATS SUCH AS INVASIVE SPECIES AND CLIMATE VARIABILITY, LAND OWNERSHIP AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRANSFERS, AND TO IMPLEMENT PRACTICES TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINABLE FOREST RESOURCES AND TO MEET PERSONAL MANAGEMENT GOALS. THROUGH IN‐PERSON CLASSES, DISTANCE CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WE ARE EXPECTING TO INCREASE LANDOWNERS' AND RESOURCES PROFESSIONALS' SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE TO AFFECT LONG‐TERM CHANGES IN ACTIVE MANAGEMENT BY WOODLAND OWNERS THAT WILL SUPPORT SUCCESSION TO FAMILY MEMBERS, REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF PARCELIZATION THROUGH STABLE LAND OWNERSHIP, AND RETAIN FOREST COVER AND CONTRIBUTE SUSTAINABLY TO THE WOOD FUEL CYCLE THROUGH REGULAR PLANNED TIMBER SALES.

RREA PROJECT ABSTRACT - MISSOURI WHILE 94 PERCENT OF THE STATE'S LAND BASE (41+MILLION ACRES) IS PRIVATELY OWNED, LESS THAN 10 PERCENT OF THESE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AC TIVELY MANAGE THEIR FORESTS, WOODLANDS, AND NON-AGRICULTURAL FIELDS. THIS TRANSLATES DIRECTLY INTO LOST, VALUE-ADDED FOREST PRODUCTS AND INDIRECTLY INTO DIMINISHED ABILITY OF OUR FOREST AND WOODLANDS IN PROVIDING VALUABLE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, SUCH AS CLEAN AIR AND WATER. THIS LACK OF MANAGEMENT IS ALSO RESULTING IN LOST WILDLIFE HABITAT IN OUR WOODLANDS, ON OUR FARMS, AND IN OUR COMMUNITIES. THUS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR EXPANDED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT WILL ENABLE ALL MISSOURI CITIZENS TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS REGARDING THE WISE STEWARDSHIP AND CONSERVATION OF THE STATE'S FORESTS AND WOODLANDS, GRASSLANDS AND FIELDS, AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AND THE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS WHICH DEPEND UPON THESE ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS SO THAT A GREATER NUMBER OF CLIENTELE WILL RECONNECT WITH MISSOURI'S NATURAL RESOURCES, INCLUDING THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESOURCE, BECOME ACTIVE LAND STEWARDS SUPPORTING CONSERVATION GOALS AND OBJECTIVES. PROJECT GOALS AND OBJECTIVES GOALS: A. INCREASE AND ENHANCE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING ON PRIVATE LANDS FEATURING WORKING FORESTS, WOODLANDS, GRASSLANDS AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION WITHIN MISSOURI AND B. BUILDING CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS. ISSUE: FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH ACTION: DEVELOP AND DELIVER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE FOREST AND WOODLAND MANAGEMENT BY MISSOURI’S FAMILY FOREST LANDOWNERS. PRODUCTS: 1.CONDUCT A MINIMUM OF 10 FOREST-RELATED EDUCATIONAL EVENTS UNDER THE “MISSOURI WOODLAND STEWARD” AND “WOMEN OWNING WOODLANDS” PROGRAMS. 2.CREATE AND/OR REVISE A MINIMUM OF 5 PEER-REVIEWED, MU EXTENSION GUIDES AND 12NEWSLETTERS. 3.DEVELOP A MINIMUM OF FOUR, 10- TO 15-MINUTE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RELATED VIDEO SEGMENTS. ISSUE: ENHANCING FOREST AND RANGELAND WILDLIFE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES ON PRIVATE LANDS ACTION: DEVELOP AND DELIVER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT SERVE TO INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES CONDUCTED BY MISSOURI'S PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. PRODUCTS: 1.CREATE 6 NEW MISSOURI MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAM VOLUNTEER COHORTS EITHER THROUGH EXISTING CHAPTERS OR THE CREATION OF NEW CHAPTERS. OVER 150 MU EXTENSION MASTER NATURALIST VOLUNTEERS WILL BE TRAINED AND CERTIFIED AND CONDUCT VOLUNTEER SERVICE PROJECTS FEATURING NATURAL RESOURCES. 2.CONDUCT 10 WILDLIFE-RELATED EDUCATIONAL EVENTS UNDER THEMES IDENTIFIED WITHIN THE“METHODOLOGY” SECTION OF THE FY22-24 RREA PLAN OF WORK AND 3 MASTER POLLINATOR STEWARD PROGRAMS. 3.CREATE/REVISE A MINIMUM OF 6 PEER-REVIEWED, MU EXTENSION GUIDES FEATURING WILDLIFE AND HABITAT MANAGEMENT THEMES, TARGETING PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND DEVELOP VIDEO SEGMENTS FOR USE. ISSUE: EXPAND, CREATE AND SUSTAIN EFFECTIVE PROGRAM COLLABORATIONS AND PARTNERSHIPS. TARGET AUDIENCES: PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, BOTH RESIDENT AND ABSENTEE, WISHING TO IMPROVE THE NATURAL RESOURCE BASE ON THEIR PROPERTY; EDUCATORS WISHING TO INCORPORATE SCIENCE-BASED FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES INTO THEIR CURRICULUM AND WITH NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS REPRESENTING STATE, FEDERAL AND NON-PROFIT CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS WISHING TO COLLABORATE IN DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS WITH A DIVERSE CLIENTELE ACROSS THE STATE.

PROJECT ABSTRACT EXECUTIVE SUMMARY TENNESSEES TWO LANDGRANT INSTITUTIONS COMPRISE THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SYSTEM. THEY WORK INDEPENDENTLY AND COLLABORATIVELY TO CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ALL 95 COUNTIES AND TO SERVE THE STATES 6.9 MILLION PEOPLE. THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE IS BASED IN KNOXVILLE AND SERVES AS THE STATES 1862 INSTITUTION. IT INCLUDES THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE EXTENSION (UT EXTENSION) AND THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (UT AGRESEARCH). BASED IN NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY (TSU) IS THE STATES 1890 INSTITUTION; IT INCLUDES THE TSU COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM AND THE TSU INSTITUTE FOR FOOD, AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH. THIS PLAN OF WORK REPRESENTS THE COMBINED EFFORTS OF UT EXTENSION, UT AGRESEARCH, TSU COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM, AND THE TSU INSTITUTE FOR FOOD, AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH. AGRICULTURE IS INTEGRAL TO TENNESSEES ECONOMY AND CULTURE. IN-PERSON WORKSHOPS, SEMINARS, SITE VISITS, AND NEWSLETTERS ARE ALL TRADITIONAL FORMS OF ADULT EDUCATION USED BY EXTENSION EDUCATORS, AND THEY CONTINUE BE EFFECTIVE FOR MANY AUDIENCES. HOWEVER, WE AGREE WITH A STATEMENT IN THE RREA STRATEGIC PLAN "ALTHOUGH TRADITIONAL MODES OF CONTENT DELIVERY ARE THE MOST WIDELY USED, THE DATA SUGGESTS THERE IS INTEREST IN ADOPTING ALTERNATIVE METHODS FOR DELIVERING PROGRAMS." NEW FORMS OF PROGRAM DELIVERY THAT UTILIZE WEB AND SMART-PHONE TECHNOLOGIES WILL REACH ENTIRELY NEW AUDIENCES AND EXPAND THE REACH OF NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT EXTENSION PROGRAMMING AND ENSURE THE CONTINUED RELEVANCE OF THOSE EFFORTS INTO THE 21ST CENTURY.A RELATIVELY NOVEL FORM OF COMMUNICATION THAT IS POPULAR AMONG A WIDE RANGE OF AUDIENCES IS THE PODCAST. THE TERM PODCAST, A COMBINATION OF THE WORDS "IPOD" AND "BROADCAST", IS "DEFINED AS A DIGITAL AUDIO FILE CREATED AND THEN UPLOADED TO AN ONLINE PLATFORM TO SHARE WITH OTHERS". A MAJOR ADVANTAGE OF PODCASTS IS THAT THEY ALLOW AUDIENCES TO LISTEN TO EDUCATIONAL CONTENT WHILE COMPLETING OTHER DUTIES, SUCH AS DRIVING, EXERCISING, OR COOKING A MEAL. WITH MORE THAN 700,000 ACTIVE PODCASTS IN 2019, THIS NEW FORM OF COMMUNICATION APPEARS TO BE A VIABLE INSTRUMENT FOR ADULT EDUCATION. IN 2018 ALONE, THERE WERE 50 BILLION PODCAST DOWNLOADS. ALONG WITH THE CONVENIENCE OF LISTENING "ON THE GO" PODCASTS ARE POPULAR BECAUSE THEY CAN BE EXPERIENCED &AGRAVE; LA CARTE BY CONNECTING A SPECIFIC AUDIENCE WITH A SPECIFIC TOPIC. A SALIENT OPPORTUNITY AND CHALLENGE WITH THIS PLATFORM, AND MANY MODERN COMMUNICATION CHANNELS, IS THAT ANYONE WITH A CONNECTION TO THE INTERNET AND A MICROPHONE CAN EARN AN AUDIENCE TO SHARE THEIR IDEAS AND PERSPECTIVES. WHEN THESE IDEAS AND PERSPECTIVES ARE SCIENCE-BASED, THE PLATFORM REACHES NEW AUDIENCES AND CAN HAVE IMPORTANT IMPACTS IN SOCIETY. WHEN THE VOICES ELEVATED THROUGH THE PLATFORM ARE NOT SCIENCE-BASED, THE PLATFORM PRESENTS CHALLENGES OF MISINFORMATION. OUR WORK WILL SEEK TO ENGAGE THIS AUDIENCE AND MEDIA WITH SCIENCE-BASED EDUCATIONAL CONTENT RELATED TO RREA CRITICAL ISSUES THAT EXTENDS THE TRADITIONAL EXTENSION MODEL TO MODERN COMMUNICATION CHANNELS AND PROVIDES A RELIABLE AND TRUSTWORTHY VOICE ON NATURAL RESOURCE ISSUES IN THE PODCAST UNIVERSE.

SHRUB ENCROACHMENT AND THE INTERVENTIONS TAKEN TO REDUCE SHRUB COVER ('BRUSH MANAGEMENT') ARE CRITICAL AREAS OF CONCERN FOR LAND MANAGERS AND PRODUCERS IN RANGELANDS ACROSS THE GREAT PLAINS AND THE WESTERN US. WE PROPOSE TO BRING TOGETHER RESEARCH AND OUTREACH TO BEGIN CONSTRUCTION OF A PRACTICAL, USER-GUIDED, WEB-BASED 'TOOLKIT' FOR DETERMINING BEST OPTIONS AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR MANAGING UNDESIRABLE WOODY WEEDS. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE EXISTING DROUGHTVIEWWEB APPLICATION TO TAKE THE FIRST STEPS IN DESIGNING A DECISION SUPPORT TOOL WHILE FORMULATING NEW BRUSH MANAGEMENT DECISION-MAKING RESOURCES, COLLECTIVELY CALLED THE 'TOOLKIT'. OUR DEVELOPMENT PROCESS WILL INCORPORATE GUIDANCE FROM STAKEHOLDERS WITH PAST AND ON-GOING RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT IDENTIFY CLIMATE-PLANT-SOIL-TREATMENT FACTORS DETERMINING SHRUB INVASION RISK AND OPTIONS FOR CONTAINMENT. THESE FACTORS WILL BE COMPILED INTO DESCRIPTIONS AND MANAGEMENT DECISION-TREES. AN ITERATIVE, PHASED DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT APPROACH WILL PACKAGE RESEARCH INFORMATION INTO AN ONLINE, USER-FRIENDLY INTERFACE AND REPOSITORY TO PROVIDE STEP-BY-STEP GUIDES FOR DECISION-MAKING. PRIMARY PROJECT OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: (1) SYNTHESIZING RESEARCH ON CONTROLS OVER AND CONSTRAINTS TO SHRUB ENCROACHMENT AND THE EFFICACY OF BRUSH MANAGEMENT; (2) COMPILING LOCAL/REGIONAL STAKEHOLDER KNOWLEDGE AND INPUT FOR USE IN TOOLKIT DESIGN THROUGH ITERATIVE FEEDBACK; (3) BROADENING EXISTING BRUSH MANAGEMENT ONLINE RESOURCESTO BUILD THE PROTOTYPIC TOOLKIT WITH RESEARCH/MANAGEMENT INFORMATION FOR OPEN STAKEHOLDER ACCESS; AND (4) DEVELOPING A FRAMEWORK FOR LAND MANAGERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS TO GUIDE AND ENHANCE FUTURE TOOLKIT FUNCTIONALITY, RELEVANCE AND USABILITY. THE WEB-BASED TOOLKIT WILL SUBSTANTIVELY EXPAND THE ONLINE PRESENCE OF LAND GRANT UNIVERSITY EXTENSION, WHILE PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT.

YET, AS THE GLOBAL HUMAN POPULATION BECOMES MORE MODERNIZED, PEOPLE IN URBAN CENTERS ARE OFTEN DISCONNECTED FROM RANGELANDS AND THEIR IMPORTANCE TO CLIMATE CHANGE, CONSERVATION PRACTICES, ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, AND ECONOMIC WELL-BEING. THE INTERNATIONAL YEAR OF RANGELANDS AND PASTORALISTS (IYRP2026 - HTTPS://IYRP.INFO)' S MISSION IS TO PROMOTE AN UNDERSTANDING AND APPRECIATION OF RANGELANDS AROUND THE WORLD, THE PEOPLE WHO USE THEM, AND THE CONTRIBUTIONS THEY MAKE TO THE HEALTH OF ALL COMMUNITIES.THIS EXTENSION OUTREACH PROJECT IS THE PRODUCTION OF A FEATURE-LENGTH DOCUMENTARY FILM ABOUT NORTH AMERICA'S RANGELANDS AND HOW THEY HOLD PROMISE FOR REDUCING THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE. THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH STORYTELLING THAT HIGHLIGHTS MISCONCEPTIONS ABOUT THESE LANDS AND THAT DEMONSTRATES THEIR IMPORTANCE FOR MEETING 21ST CENTURY ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL CHALLENGES. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO CHANGE PERCEPTIONS OF THE PUBLIC, PARTICULARLY NEW AUDIENCES SUCH AS YOUTH AND URBAN POPULATIONS AS WELL AS POLICYMAKERS, REGARDING THE VALUE OF THESE LANDS AS CLIMATE SOLUTIONS AND THE NEED TO CONSERVE THEM. BY PRESENTING REAL-LIFE STORIES ABOUT THE PEOPLE WHOSE LIVELIHOODS DEPEND ON THESE LANDS AND THE NATURE OF THEIR STEWARDSHIP, VIEWERS WILL LEARN ABOUT INNOVATIVE NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR LAND MANAGEMENT, COLLABORATIVE CONSERVATION EFFORTS, AND THE MANY ECOSYSTEM SERVICES PROVIDED BY NORTH AMERICA'S RANGELANDS INCLUDING CLEAN WATER, WILDLIFE HABITAT, WILDFIRE CONTROL, RENEWABLE ENERGY, AND RECREATION.IN ADDITION, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY TO SHOW HOW INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE CAN CONTRIBUTE TO CLIMATE SOLUTIONS ON NORTH AMERICA'S RANGELANDS.

TEXAS HAS EXPERIENCED A 40% INCREASE IN POPULATION SINCE 2002, AND IT NOW EXCEEDS 28M PEOPLE - A CHALLENGE ON MANY FRONTS, BUT A SIGNIFICANT ONE FOR RURAL WORKING LANDS. UNCHECKED GROWTH LEADS TO DIFFICULTIES FOR LOCAL ECONOMIES, OPEN-SPACE LANDS, WILDLIFE, AND WATER. OUR OBJECTIVES CENTER ON HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND PUBLIC BENEFIT OF PRIVATE LAND STEWARDSHIP FOR FOOD AND FIBER PRODUCTION AND ENHANCEMENT OF OUR NATURAL RESOURCES. WE WORK IN PRIORITY AREAS TO ADDRESS: 1) FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT, 2) GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION, 3) WILDFIRE PREVENTION, 4) LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT, AND 5) PUBLIC AWARENESS/YOUTH ENGAGEMENT. EXTENSION SPECIALISTS DEVELOP FLAGSHIP PROGRAMS IN THEIR AREA OF EXPERTISE TO MAXIMIZE REACH AND IMPACT FOR EACH. PROGRAMS LIKE PLANT PARTY, GENERATION NEXT, OUR TURN TO RANCH, PRESCRIBED BURN SCHOOL, TEXAS LAND TRENDS, AND LEOPOLD LIVE!, SHOW OUR ATTENTION TO EACH OF THESE PRIORITIES, RESPECTIVELY. OUR METHODS BLEND TRADITIONAL FACE-TO-FACE PROGRAMS, BUT WE ALSO DEVELOP ELECTRONIC RESOURCES, LIKE ON-LINE COURSES THAT ALLOW FOR EDUCATIONAL EXPLORATION, RATHER THAN JUST LINEAR LESSONS, ALLOWING FOR AN EDUCATIONAL JOURNEY. WE MAXIMIZE THE REACH OF OUR EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THROUGH IN-HOUSE SOCIAL MEDIA OUTLETS AND DEVELOP RELATIONSHIPS WITH CONSERVATION PARTNERS TO AMPLIFY THEIR DISTRIBUTION. WE STRUCTURE OUR MATERIALS IN A WAY THAT CURIOUS PEOPLE CAN FIND THEM ON THE INTERNET AND WE ACTIVELY TARGET TEACHING AND TRAINING TO SPECIFIC GROUPS LIKE LANDOWNERS, COUNTY OFFICIALS, STATE, AND FEDERAL AGENCY EMPLOYEES. COLLECTIVELY, OUR WORK KEEPS WORKING LANDS INTACT, AND WE KEEP THE NATION'S MOST IMPORTANT INFRASTRUCTURE - LAND - IN THE CENTER OF OUR THINKING.

ALASKA'S FORESTS ARE IMPORTANT FOR THEIR TIMBER, BIOMASS, SUBSISTENCE, FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT AND ECOSYSTEMS SERVICES RESOURCES. APPROXIMATELY 126 MILLION ACRES IN ALASKA ARE FORESTED, AND MOST ALASKANS LIVE IN OR NEXT TO A FOREST. CLIMATE VARIABILITY IMPACTS, CONTINUED DEMAND FOR TIMBER AND BIOMASS RESOURCES AND INCREASED USE FROM CONSUMPTIVE AND NON-CONSUMPTIVE USER GROUPS ARE PLACING MORE PRESSURES ON ALASKA'S FORESTS AND THE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND PROFESSIONALS MANAGING THOSE RESOURCES. IN ORDER TO SUSTAIN PRODUCTIVE FOREST RESOURCES AND FUNCTIONS ACROSS MULTIPLE LAND OWNERSHIP, INCLUDING FEDERAL, STATE, LOCAL, NATIVE AND PRIVATE, LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, USER GROUPS AND THE PUBLIC NEED ACCESS TO SCIENTIFICALLY SOUND AND RELEVANT INFORMATION ABOUT HOW FORESTS FUNCTION AND THE ROLE OF FOREST MANAGEMENT. PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS ARE UNDER INCREASING PRESSURE TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO FOREST RESOURCES WHILE MAINTAINING PUBLIC BENEFITS SUCH AS FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT, WATER AND WETLAND RESOURCES AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES BUT OFTEN LACK OPPORTUNITIES TO ACCESS THE MOST CURRENT INFORMATION. THIS PROJECT WILL USE A VARIETY OF METHODS, INCLUDING WEB-BASED PLATFORMS, PRINTED MATERIALS, SHORT WORKSHOPS AND PRESENTATIONS TO PROVIDE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS (INCLUDING NATIVE LANDOWNERS) AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS THE RESOURCES ALLOWING THEM TO MAKE GOOD MANAGEMENT DECISIONS FOR THEIR LANDS. THE GENERAL PUBLIC IS ALSO AN IMPORTANT AUDIENCE BECAUSE THEY CAN INFLUENCE POLICIES AFFECTING FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND MANAGEMENT ON PRIVATE AND PUBLIC FORESTED LANDS. THE GROWTH OF BIOMASS MARKETS OR OTHER WOOD USES IS ALSO INFLUENCED THROUGH PUBLIC OPINION IN THEIR LOCAL COMMUNITIES. EFFECTIVE AUDIENCE OUTREACH WILL INCLUDE EDUCATOR AND YOUTH PROGRAMMING ALONG WITH SOCIAL AND TRADITIONAL MEDIA RELEASES, WEB-BASED APPLICATIONS AND RADIO PROGRAMMING. THIS PROJECT WILL ENABLE PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS TO MAKE SOUND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS BASED ON THE LATEST AND MOST RELEVANT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH ON ALASKA'S FOREST RESOURCES AND IT WILL SUPPORT THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF ALASKA'S PUBLIC FORESTS LANDS BY INCREASING THE AWARENESS OF HOW FORESTS FUNCTION AND THE ROLE OF FOREST MANAGEMENT.

THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT OF 1978 (RREA) SUPPORTS AN EXPANDED AND COMPREHENSIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM FOR FOREST AND RANGELAND RENEWABLE RESOURCES. RREA SUPPORTS FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS IN THE SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF WOOD PRODUCTS, FORAGE AND LIVESTOCK, FISH AND WILDLIFE POPULATIONS AND DEVELOPING OUTDOOR RECREATION OPPORTUNITIES. UC AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES OVERSEES THE UC RREA PROGRAM WHICH FOCUSES ON EIGHT ISSUE AREAS. PUBLIC AWARENESS AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT: ENGAGING YOUTH AND ADULTS ABOUT THE IMPORTANCE OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES, PARTICULARLY HOW FOREST LANDS AND RANGELANDS AFFECT RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES AND THE NEED TO USE SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION WHEN MAKING DECISIONS ABOUT THESE RESOURCES. ECOSYSTEM SERVICES: ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS IN ACTIVELY MANAGING THEIR LANDS WITH KNOWLEDGE OF FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM PROCESSES AND HOW SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES PRODUCE DIFFERENT COMBINATIONS OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; AND ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND USERS IN UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE DIFFERENT ECOSYSTEM SERVICES HAVE ON COMMUNITY WELL-BEING. FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT: ENSURING THAT PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS HAVE THE BEST AVAILABLE INFORMATION ABOUT FISH AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT HABITAT MANAGEMENT IN FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS. GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION AND OTHER LANDOWNERSHIP CHANGES: ENHANCING THE DECISION-MAKING ABILITY OF RANCH AND FOREST LANDOWNER FAMILIES FOR GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION BY PROVIDING INFORMATION ON AND FACILITATING COMMUNICATION ABOUT SUCH PLANNING OPTIONS AS CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, COMMUNITY-BASED NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT OR OTHER NON-TRADITIONAL SUCCESSION MODELS; TRAINING AND LINKING INTERESTED PARTIES IN COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS THAT WILL AUGMENT GENERATIONAL TRANSFER OF FOREST AND RANGELAND ENTERPRISES. INVASIVE SPECIES: INCREASING THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO ASSESS THE THREAT OF INVASIVE SPECIES; DEVELOPING INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT PLANS; IMPLEMENTING EFFECTIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL STRATEGIES TO PROTECT FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS; PROVIDING MEANS FOR THE GENERAL PUBLIC (INCLUDING ABSENTEE LANDOWNERS), YOUTH, AND COMMUNITY GROUPS FOR THEIR INTERACTION AND PARTICIPATION IN MONITORING AND CONTROLLING INVASIVE SPECIES. RURAL COMMUNITIES: WORKING WITH RURAL COMMUNITIES TO ASSESS NEEDS AND DETERMINE HOW TO SUSTAINABLY ENHANCE LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT THROUGH A FOCUS ON FOREST AND RANGELAND INDUSTRIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, AND EXPERTISE; CREATING A STRONGER RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HEALTHY FORESTS AND RANGELANDS AND THE SOCIAL AND SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC BASES OF RURAL COMMUNITIES; ASSESSING NEEDS AND DETERMINING HOW TO ENHANCE LOCAL LANDSCAPE ECONOMICS. WATER AND WETLANDS: ENCOURAGING MANAGEMENT OF FORESTS AND RANGELANDS TO IMPROVE WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY. WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT: ENGAGING FOREST AND RANGELAND COMMUNITIES WITH RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION ON WILD FIRE RISK-MANAGEMENT AND POST-FIRE RECOVERY STRATEGIES; INCREASING THE CAPACITY OF COMMUNITY, COUNTY, AND STATE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS/CIVIL DEFENSE AUTHORITIES TO COMMUNICATE COMMUNITY NEEDS AND INFORM COMMUNITY-DEVELOPMENT POLICIES, CODES, AND ORDINANCES THAT PR OTECT COMMUNITIES FROM WILDFIRE; DEVELOPING OUTREACH EFFORTS THAT INCLUDE CURRENT AND EMERGING RESEARCH ON IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE ON FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOLOGY AND ECONOMICS, FUELS MANAGEMENT, AND PRESCRIBED FIRE TO CREATE APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES; INCREASING CAPACITY FOR COMMUNITY ACTION, EMPOWER LANDOWNERS TO ENGAGE IN PRESCRIBED FIRE, AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR TRAINING AND CAPACITY IN FUELS REDUCTION.

positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT FUNDING RECEIVED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA WARNELL SCHOOL OF FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES IS TO SUPPORT THE OUTREACH EFFORTS OF OUR EXTENSION FACULTY AND BRING SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION TO OUR TARGET AUDIENCES, SUCH AS GEORGIA FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, TO HELP THEM MAKE CRITICAL MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. WE EDUCATE GEORGIA CITIZENS ABOUT HOW AND WHY NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES ARE PRESCRIBED AND CONDUCTED. WE PROVIDE CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDIT COURSES REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN PROFESSIONAL CREDENTIALS. THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED IN THE COMING YEAR INCLUDE: 1) WORKSHOPS; 2) APPLIED RESEARCH; 3) PEER REVIEWED AND EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS; 4) PRESENTATIONS; AND 5) FOSTER PARTNER COLLABORATIONS. THE DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE: WORKSHOPS: THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM WILL PLAN, ORGANIZE AND DELIVER WORKSHOPS COVERING TOPICS THAT INCLUDE THE IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES, TIMBER TAXATION, INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT, FOREST HEALTH, URBAN WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION CERTIFICATION, AND AQUATIC RESOURCE MANAGEMENT. WORKSHOPS WILL BE PLANNED TO BE BOTH PROACTIVE AND REACTIVE. OUR ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION SPECIALISTS WILL OFFER EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EVENTS FOR STUDENTS AND TEACHERS USING INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED CURRICULA (PROJECT LEARNING TREE, PROJECT WILD, AND PROJECT WET). APPLIED RESEARCH: ACTIVITIES WILL INVOLVE MAINTAINING EXISTING AND DEVELOPING NEW SITES TO EVALUATE AND SERVE AS DEMONSTRATIONS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF APPLIED RESEARCH EFFORTS IS TO STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION WITH STATE/FEDERAL AGENCY PARTNERS AND PRIVATE INDUSTRY SPONSORS, AND AS DATA CONTINUES TO BE GATHERED AND ANALYZED, AN INCREASED USE OF THESE SITES AS EFFECTIVE DEMONSTRATION SITES FOR FIELD DAYS AND WORKSHOPS. PUBLICATIONS: TOPICS TO BE COVERED INCLUDE FIRESCAPING, WILD HARVESTING PRACTICES, WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES (HERBICIDE APPLICATION AND SITE PREPARATION). ALL PUBLICATIONS WILL BE PRODUCED WITH THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF SPREADING TRUSTED INFORMATION AND INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PUBLICATIONS POSTED ON OUR WARNELL OUTREACH WEBSITE WHERE WE CAN TRACK THE NUMBER OF VIEWS AND DOWNLOADS. PRESENTATIONS: WE HAVE PLANS TO COVER MANY TOPICS INCLUDING URBAN WILDLIFE ISSUES, FIRESCAPING, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, FOREST MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, AQUATIC RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, WOOD PLANT ID, AND OTHER TOPICS AS IDENTIFIED. THE OUTCOME OF OUR EFFORTS IS TO SHARE QUALITY UP-TO-DATE INFORMATION WITH GEORGIA CITIZENS THAT HELP THEM MAKE INFORMED NATURAL RESOURCE RELATED DECISIONS. PARTNER COLLABORATION: OUR TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO NURTURE EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, EDUCATORS (K- 16), AND INDUSTRY. WE ANTICIPATE THE OUTCOME OF THESE PARTNERSHIPS TO BE SUSTAINED SUPPORT AND COLLABORATION. WE ARE VERY AWARE OF THE IMPORTANCE OF PARTNERSHIPS WHEN IT COMES TO LENDING VALIDITY TO OUR WORK. WEB-BASED PRODUCTS: OUR WEB DEVELOPMENT TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO UPDATE SMARTPHONE APPS AND WEBSITES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF OUR EFFORT WILL BE TO OFFER WEB-BASED TOOLS THAT INCREASE INFORMATION SHARING AND DATA COLLECTION AND PROVIDE EXPERIENCES THAT BUILD NEW SKILLS AND BENEFIT OUR TARGET AUDIENCES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS, PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, PRIVATE CONSULTANTS, COUNTY EXTENSION ANR AGENTS, CITY/COUNTY GOVERNMENT STAFF, K-12 TEACHERS AND STUDENTS, SPECIAL INTEREST GROUPS, ASSOCIATIONS, NGOS AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, AND ALL CITIZENS OF GEORGIA. THERE ARE NO SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES PLANNED AT  THE TIME OF THIS AWARD.

LANDOWNER EDUCATION AND CONTINUING EDUCATION FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS ARE KEY TO REDUCING THE IMPACTS OF INVASIVE PLANTS AND IMPROVING THE HEALTH OF ALABAMA FORESTS. OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO EXPAND AWARENESS OF INVASIVE SPECIES AND INCREASE KNOWLEDGE OF INVASIVE PLANT IDENTIFICATION, IMPACTS, AND CONTROL OPTIONS. A SECONDARY OBJECTIVE IS TO MAINTAIN STATE AND REGIONAL PARTNERSHIPS WITH RELEVANT PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ORGANIZATIONS ADDRESSING ISSUES RELATED TO ASSESSMENT, MAPPING, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL, RESEARCH, AND EDUCATION. INVASIVE PLANTS ARE OUR MAIN FOCUS, BUT EMERGING INVASIVE INSECT AND ANIMAL PESTS MAY ALSO BE ADDRESSED. THE PRIMARY TARGET AUDIENCES ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT STUDENTS. BECAUSE NON-NATIVE PLANTS USED IN LANDSCAPING ARE A MAJOR SOURCE OF THE INVASIVE PLANTS THAT INVADE FORESTS, A SECONDARY AUDIENCE IS HOMEOWNERS, MASTER GARDENERS, THE GENERAL PUBLIC, AND K-12 EDUCATORS. PRIMARY COMMUNICATION PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS ADDRESSING INVASIVE PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL; SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS, BLOGS, AND SHORT ARTICLES FOR THE PRESS AND NEWSLETTER; CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE ACES FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE WEBPAGE; AND HIGH-DEFINITION PHOTOGRAPHS OF INVASIVE PLANTS FOR USE IN EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS. OUTREACH EVENTS WILL INCLUDE CO-CHAIRING THE ANNUAL ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL CONFERENCE, ORGANIZING AND JOINING ACES PROGRAMMING, AND OFFERING SEMINARS AND WEBINARS FOR THE FOREST INDUSTRY, FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AGENCIES, MASTER GARDENERS, CIVIC GROUPS, AND OTHERS. OVER ONE HUNDRED QUESTIONS FROM LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, EXTENSION AGENTS, AND THE PUBLIC ARE FIELDED EACH YEAR, INVOLVING PLANT ID AND INVASIVE PLANT TREATMENT OPTIONS. TEACH A SECTION ON INVASIVE PLANTS TO AUBURN UNIVERSITY FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE STUDENTS. LEAD THE EFFORT TO UPDATE THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL INVASIVE PLANT LIST AND PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE. SERVING ON STATE-WIDE INVASIVE PLANT TASK FORCES AND COMMITTEES AND MAINTAINING A LEADERSHIP ROLE WITHIN THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL. REGIONAL PUBLICATIONS AND EVENTS ARE THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH SOUTHERN REGION EXTENSION FORESTRY AND OTHER COLLEAGUES IN THE REGION. ONE REGIONAL EFFORT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN INVASIVE PLANT ASSESSMENT TOOL TO STANDARDIZE PLANT LISTS ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST. THE NATIONAL EARLY DETECTION AND DISTRIBUTION MAPPING SYSTEM SERVES AS A STATE VERIFIER FOR INVASIVE PLANT SUBMISSIONS. EDDMAPS IS AN IMPORTANT TOOL FOR MAPPING AND MONITORING THE SPREAD OF INVASIVE PLANTS. BEING ACTIVE IN THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF INVASIVE PLANT COUNCILS AND NORTH AMERICAN INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION IS IMPORTANT FOR MAINTAINING REGIONAL AND NATIONAL TIES. THE DIRECT BENEFITS OF THESE EFFORTS ARE INCREASED ABILITY TO IDENTIFY AND MONITOR INVASIVE SPECIES, EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF I NVASIVE SPECIES, REDUCED USE OF INVASIVE SPECIES IN LANDSCAPING, AND PROVIDING CECS FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS. THE ULTIMATE BENEFIT IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH THROUGH REDUCED SPREAD AND IMPACTS OF INVASIVE PLANTS. A CHANGE IN KNOWLEDGE WILL BE REFLECTED TH ROUGH AN INCREASED NUMBER OF LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS WHO KNOW HOW TO IDENTIFY INVASIVE PLANTS AND KNOW WHERE TO ACCESS SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION AND RESOURCES; INCREASED NUMBER OF LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS WITH KNOWLEDGE OF EFFECTIVE OPTIONS FOR INVASIVE PLANT PREVENTION AND CONTROL; AND AWARENESS OF EDDMAPS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH AND RESILIENCY THROUGH REDUCED USE OF NON-NATIVE PLANTS IN LANDSCAPING AND WILDLIFE PLANTINGS, REDUCED BEHAVIORS THAT SPREAD INVASIVE PLANTS, AND EARLIER AND EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OF INVASIVE PLANTS. EFFORTS TO IMPROVE INVASIVE PLANT LISTING AND MAPPING WILL IMPROVE THE ACCURACY OF DISTRIBUTION MAPS THAT REFLECT INVASIVE PLANT POPULATIONS ACROSS THE STATE, BETTER INFORMING MANAGEMENT DECISIONS.

THROUGH INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, NC STATE IS SOLVING CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF BOTH LARGE- AND SMALL-SCALE FARMS. RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE LANDSCAPING AND GARDENING. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND METHODS FOR ANIMAL BREEDING, REPRODUCTION, NUTRITION, GENETICS AND GENOMICS, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. THESE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS ALSO AIM TO TACKLE THE CRITICAL ISSUES IMPACTING THE QUALITY OF OUR SOIL, WATER AND AIR BY PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC SOLUTIONS FOR ANIMAL WASTE MANAGEMENT, WASTEWATER TREATMENT, NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, SOIL PROPERTIES, AND FISHERY AND POND MANAGEMENT. NC STATE'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH AND TO KEEP AMERICAN'S HEALTHY AND FREE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESS NECESSITATE A FOCUS ON PREVENTING FOOD SAFETY PROBLEMS RATHER THAN TAKING A REACTIONARY APPROACH. NC STATE'S INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS FOCUS ON PROTECTING THE SAFETY OF FOODS ALONG THE ENTIRE SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM PRODUCTION TO CONSUMPTION. TO MEET THE GROWING  NEED FOR HEALTHY FOOD, RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS THAT PROMOTE HEALTH AND PREVENT DISEASE. AT THE SAME TIME, EXTENSION PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO ENSURE THAT INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE THEY NEED TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES ABOUT FOOD AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSS-CUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGRO ECONOMICS. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITS WORK WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, PLACING SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON LIMITED RESOURCES, SMALL- SCALE MINORITY FARMERS. THE FARM PAVILION WILL FOCUS ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND LOCAL AND COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, HOUSING ITS APPLIED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROGRAMS' STAFF AND PROVIDING SPACE FOR MEETINGS, FORUMS AND CONFERENCES.

MSU RREA ABSTRACT MISSISSIPPI CONTAINS OVER 19.5 MILLION ACRES OF FOREST LAND, WHICH ACCOUNTS FOR 65% OF THE STATE'S TOTAL LAND AREA, AND 81% OF MISSISSIPPI'S FOREST LAND IS PRIVATELY OWNED BY NONINDUSTRIAL LANDOWNERS. OVER 80% OF PRIVATE FOREST OWNERSHIP IS IN PARCELS OF 100 ACRES OR LESS. EDUCATING PRIVATE FAMILY FOREST OWNERS ABOUT FOREST MANAGEMENT, HARVESTING, AND MARKETING PRACTICES AND TECHNIQUES IS ESSENTIAL TO THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE FOREST RESOURCE. THESE FAMILY FOREST LANDS ARE NOT ALWAYS MANAGED IN A WAY THAT MAXIMIZES PRIVATE AND ASSOCIATED PUBLIC BENEFITS THAT CAN INCLUDE TIMBER PRODUCTS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES, RECREATION AND WATER QUALITY BENEFITS. MANY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS DO NOT HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE OR SKILLS TO MANAGE FORESTS TO MEET THEIR OWN OBJECTIVES. THE RREA PROGRAM ALLOWS MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SERVICE TO GIVE SPECIAL ATTENTION TO HELPING FAMILY FOREST OWNERS MANAGE THEIR FORESTLANDS FOR MAXIMUM BENEFIT. THUS, THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INCREASE AND IMPROVE THE LEVELS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES BEING CONDUCTED ON MISSISSIPPI FORESTLAND SO AS TO ENHANCE ALL THE BENEFITS SOCIETY RECEIVES FROM WELL MANAGED FORESTS. THE CORE GOALS OF THE FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAM AS SUPPORTED BY RREA ARE TO INCREASE THE PRODUCTIVITY, EFFECTIVENESS, EFFICIENCY, AND PROFITABILITY OF OUR CLIENTELE, AS WELL AS AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE MANY VALUES OF THEIR FORESTS. NEW RESEARCH AND TECHNOLOGIES ARE DISSEMINATED TO CLIENTELE STATEWIDE THROUGH FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAMS AND MATERIALS.

MUCH OF OREGON IS FORESTLAND AND RANGELAND, AND MUCH OF THIS ACREAGE IS MANAGED BY PRIVATE OWNERS OF NON-INDUSTRIAL OPERATIONS. RREA FUNDS PROVIDED TO OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY (OSU) ARE USED TO SUPPORT EFFORTS OF OSU EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF TO ASSIST THESE LANDOWNERS IN THEIR RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS, AND TO ASSIST OTHERS IN UNDERSTANDING HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE ECONOMIC AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES THESE LANDS PROVIDE. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION TO OREGONIANS THAT ASSISTS THEM IN UNDERSTANDING HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE HEALTH, PRODUCTIVITY, AND RESILIENCY OF THESE LANDS. OUR AIM IS TO ENSURE HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS, INCREASE ECONOMIC BENEFITS, BUILD CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS, AND IN THE LONG TERM ENSURE SUSTAINABLE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THIS PROJECT HAS SEVERAL OBJECTIVES. OBJECTIVE ONE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF OWNERS AND MANAGERS OF PRIVATE NON-INDUSTRIAL FOREST AND RANGELAND OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES SO AS TO ENABLE THEM TO MEET THEIR MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES WHILE ENSURING HEALTHY FOREST AND RANGELANDS. OBJECTIVE TWO IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW LAND USE AND LAND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS INFLUENCE HABITAT FOR A VARIETY OF FISH, WILDLIFE, INSECTS, AND PATHOGENS TO ENSURE HIGH LEVELS OF BIODIVERSITY WHILE KEEPING IN CHECK INVASIVE SPECIES ACROSS ECOSYSTEMS. OBJECTIVE THREE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW CHANGING CLIMATIC CONDITIONS IS LIKELY TO INFLUENCE FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES (E.G., INCREASED SUMMER TEMPERATURES, PROLONGED DROUGHT, WIDESPREAD INSECT AND DISEASE OUTBREAKS, LARGER WILDFIRES), TO FOSTER EFFORTS THAT ENHANCE RESILIENCE IN THE FACE OF THREATS IMPOSED BY THESE CHANGES. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS; NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS SUCH AS FORESTERS, FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE BIOLOGISTS, RESTORATION SPECIALISTS, AND RANGELAND MANAGERS; FOREST WORKERS SUCH AS LOGGERS, TREE PLANTERS, FIREFIGHTERS; RANCHERS AND FARMERS; FORMAL AND INFORMAL EDUCATORS; POLICYMAKERS; AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. EDUCATIONAL EFFORTS SUPPORTED BY RREA FUNDS ARE GUIDED BY NEEDS ASSESSMENTS AND ARE TAILORED TO BEST MEET THE NEEDS OF THE SPECIFIC AUDIENCES AND SITUATIONS THEY ARE INTENDED TO ADDRESS. STANDARDIZED CURRICULUM AND EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS ARE DEVELOPED AND DELIVERED TO IMPROVE FOREST AND RANGELAND HEALTH, ENSURE HABITAT FOR A VARIETY OF FISH AND WILDLIFE, REDUCE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH CHANGING CLIMATE, AND EDUCATE COMMUNITIES AND POLICYMAKERS OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC CONTRIBUTIONS AND VALUE OF OUR WORKING FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES. EDUCATION EFFORTS ENCOMPASS A WIDE VARIETY OF MODALITIES. WRITTEN MATERIALS INCLUDE PUBLICATIONS AND NEWSLETTERS. ONLINE MATERIALS INCLUDE WEBSITES, BLOGS, WEBINARS, VIDEOS, AND PRE-RECORDED LEARNING MODULES. IN-PERSON EVENTS INCLUDE SITE VISITS, FIELD DAYS, TOURS, SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND SHORT-COURSES. OTHER DELIVERY METHODS INCLUDE HYBRID (PARTIALLY ONLINE AND PARTIALLY IN-PERSON) AND PODCASTS. EXTENSION PERSONNEL FROM FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES, RANGELAND RESOURCES ECOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT, AND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES RECEIVE BASE PROGRAM SUPPORT THROUGH RREA FUNDING. IN ADDITION, ALLOCATIONS ARE PROVIDED TO SUB-PROJECTS THAT ADDRESS A VARIETY OF STAKEHOLDER NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELANDS ACROSS THE STATE. RREA FUNDS ARE LEVERAGED WITH BOTH EXTERNAL GRANT FUNDS AND UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SUPPORT. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A WIDE VARIETY OF EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS AND TRAININGS THAT RESULT IN GAINS IN AWARENESS, GAINS IN KNOWLEDGE, INCREASES IN ACREAGE OVER WHICH RECOMMENDED PRACTICES ARE IMPLEMENTED, AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. ALL EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF REPORT ON THE ACTIVITIES PERFORMED AND OUTCOMES ACHIEVED ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

ACHIEVING FUNCTIONAL AND PRODUCTIVE WOODLANDS-THE CONSERVATION OF NY'S FORESTED NATURAL RESOURCES, AND THEIR ROLE IN MULTIPLE SOCIETAL GOALS, DEPENDS ON MANY WOODLAND OWNERS MAKING INFORMED DECISIONS THAT SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE OUTCOMES. RREA AT CORNELL WILL FOCUS ON THREE PRIMARY ISSUES: FOREST MANAGEMENT FOR DIVERSE OUTPUTS, WILDLIFE RESOURCES, AND FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY OF AGROFORESTRY ENTERPRISES IN FOREST FARMING AND SILVOPASTURE. ACHIEVING FUNCTIONAL AND PRODUCTIVE WOODLANDS IN NY DEPENDS ON INCREASING THE NUMBER OF WOODLAND OWNERS WHO HAVE AWARENESS AND KNOWLEDGE OF SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES, AND INCREASED CAPACITY FOR CCE EDUCATORS AND PARTNERS TO SUPPORT THOSE OWNERS. FOREST MANAGEMENT GOAL: ENSURE THAT FORESTS ARE SUSTAINABLY MANAGED FOR OPTIMAL OUTPUTS OF DESIRED GOODS AND SERVICES. OBJECTIVE: INCREASE OWNER AWARENESS OF INFORMATION, GAIN ACCESS TO TECHNICAL SPECIALISTS THAT SUPPORT THEIR INFORMED DECISION MAKING, AND PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO TECHNICAL SPECIALISTS AND PRACTITIONERS BASED ON APPLIED RESEARCH. WILDLIFE RESOURCES GOAL: SUSTAIN AND ENHANCE THE BIODIVERSITY AND HEALTH OF NATIVE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS. OBJECTIVE: INFORM THE DECISION MAKING CAPACITY OF WOODLAND OWNERS, WILDLIFE SPECIALISTS AND PRACTITIONERS. FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY GOAL: EXPAND THE AVAILABILITY OF LOCALLY PRODUCED FOREST-BASED FOODS, AND ENSURE THAT THE PRODUCERS ARE FINANCIALLY AND ECOLOGICALLY SUSTAINABLE. OBJECTIVE: DEMONSTRATE BEST PRACTICES, ACCESS APPLIED RESEARCH ON PRIMARY FOODS (E.G., MAPLE SYRUP, SUSTAINABLY GRAZED LIVESTOCK) AND RELATED FOOD DERIVATIVES, AND PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THAT SUPPORT NEW AND ESTABLISHED ENTERPRISES. METHODOLOGY ^ONLINE: A VARIETY OF ONLINE MEDIA WILL BE USED. WEBINARS WILL BE OFFERED MONTHLY, WITH ADDITIONAL SPECIAL FEATURE WEBINARS ON AN AS NEEDED BASIS. THE BASE PAGE FOR THE PROGRAM, WWW.FORESTCONNECT.INFO WILL INCLUDE ALL PROGRAMRELEVANT EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS. SOCIAL MEDIA WILL ARCHIVE AND SUPPORT PROGRAMMING RREA FUNDS WILL BE USED AS NECESSARY WILL ENSURE ADEQUATE COMPUTER HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE. ^PEERVOLUNTEERS: MASTER FOREST OWNER VOLUNTEERS WILL CONTINUE TO CONNECT WITH PRIVATE WOODLAND OWNERS. MASTER NATURALISTS WILL WORK IN THEIR COMMUNITIES THROUGH A VARIETY OF NETWORKS. ANNUAL TRAINING WILL ENGAGE AND RETAIN VOLUNTEERS. SELECT CCE EDUCATORS WILL SERVE AS REGIONAL DIRECTORS, AND THEY WILL ASSIST WITH PROGRAM MANAGEMENT. ^DEMONSTRATION SITES: UNIVERSITY AND PRIVATE WOODLANDS WILL BE USED, AND MAY DEMONSTRATE A VARIETY OF PRACTICES AND SUPPORT FIELD TOURS. ^APPLIED RESEARCH: APPLIED RESEARCH WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF DIRECT SUPPORT OF EXTENSION EDUCATION WILL ADDRESS ISSUES AND QUESTIONS THAT LACK AN ADEQUATE RESEARCH BASIS. RREA FUNDS WILL AT MOST PROVIDE A MINIMAL SUPPLEMENT TO APPLIED RESEARCH FUNDS. ^WORKSHOPS, TOURS AND FIELD DAYS: FIELD-BASED EVENTS WILL BE HELD WITH CCE EDUCATORS ON CORNELL AND PRIVATE LANDS TO DESCRIBE, DEMONSTRATE AND ILLUSTRATE SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES. ^CONFERENCES AND SEMINARS: INDOOR EVENTS WILL PROVIDE AUDIENCES WITH SEMINAR STYLE LEARNING ON A VARIETY OF TOPICS. ^MASS MEDIA: A MARKETING CAMPAIGN WILL DRAW ATTENTION TO EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM RESOURCES. ^EDUCATOR INSERVICE: AN ANNUAL FORESTRY-MAPLE TRAINING FOR CCE EDUCATORS WILL PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY TO SHARE PROGRAM TACTICS, AND INTERACT WITH CAMPUS SPECIALISTS. ^WRITTEN MATERIALS: STAFF AND SPECIALISTS, WITH COLLEAGUES, WILL DEVELOP FACT SHEETS, BULLETINS, AND FIELD GUIDES ON RREA TOPICS. WRITTEN MATERIALS WILL TYPICALLY BE AVAILABLE ONLINE. ^ORGANIZATIONAL SUPPORT: STAFF WILL WORK WITH PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, FOR EXAMPLE THE NEW YORK FOREST OWNERS ASSOCIATION AND THE STATE FORESTRY AGENCY, ON PROJECTS OF MUTUAL INTEREST AND THAT ENHANCE WORKING FOREST CONDITIONS. ^EVALUATION OF PROGRAM ACTIVITIES WILL HAPPEN THROUGH INFORMAL EXIT SURVEYS, DOCUMENTATION OF PARTICIPATION AT EVENTS, WEB-BASED ANALYTICAL SOFTWARE, AND CALCULATIONS THAT PROJECT BEHAVIOR CHANGES.

VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (VCE), A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN VIRGINIA POLYTECHNIC INSTITUTE AND STATE UNIVERSITY (VT) AND VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY (VSU), THE VIRGINIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (VAES) AND THE VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATION (VSUARS), ENABLES PEOPLE TO IMPROVE THEIR LIVES THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION USING SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE FOCUSED ON THE ISSUES AND NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF VIRGINIA. AUDIENCES ARE INVOLVED IN DESIGNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING NEEDSDRIVEN PROGRAMS. VCE, VAES AND VSUARS ARE DYNAMIC ORGANIZATIONS WHICH STIMULATE POSITIVE PERSONAL AND SOCIETAL CHANGE LEADING TO MORE PRODUCTIVE LIVES, FAMILIES, FARMS, AND FORESTS, AS WELL AS A BETTER ENVIRONMENT IN URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES. VCE'S GOALS ARE TO: 1) DEVELOP AND TRANSFER NEW KNOWLEDGE IN APPLIED AND BASIC LIFE SCIENCES, 2) PERFORM RELEVANT, OBJECTIVE, AND TIMELY RESEARCH 3) IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR COMMUNITIES AND CITIZENS IN THE COMMONWEALTH, 4) USE A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO PROGRAMMING, WITH TASK-ORIENTED WORK TEAMS THAT RESPOND TO THE NEEDS OF INDIVIDUALS, GROUPS, AND ORGANIZATIONS, 5) WORK WITH AT-RISK, UNDERSERVED, AND UNDERREPRESENTED AUDIENCES WHO NEED FOCUSED AND SPECIALIZED ATTENTION, 6) FULLY INTEGRATE A CULTURALLY DIVERSE PAID AND VOLUNTEER STAFF IN PLANNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING PROGRAMS, AND 7) RECRUIT AND COLLABORATE WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE PARTNERS TO BETTER UTILIZE RESOURCES, HEIGHTEN IMPACT, AND REACH A MORE DIVERSE AUDIENCE. WE WILL USE SCIENCE-BASED RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL STRATEGIES TO ADDRESS 1) CRITICAL AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY 2)OUR BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY PROGRAMS FOCUS ON ESTABLISHIN G REGIONAL COMMUNITY AND INDUSTRY NETWORKS TO IDENTIFY, RESEARCH AND EDUCATE ON UTILIZATION OF BACTERIA, WATER, PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND FORESTS PRODUCTS TO PRODUCE GOODS FOR HUMAN, INDUSTRIAL, AND AGRICULTURAL NEEDS FOR ALL VIRGINIANS 3) COMMUNITY VIABILITY PROGRAMMING WILL PROMOTE CONTINUING PROSPERITY AND FINANCIAL SECURITY FOR ALL VIRGINIANS 4) WE WILL ADDRESS FOOD SECURITY AND SAFETY, NUTRITION CHALLENGES AND HEALTH ISSUES FOR ALL VIRGINIANS; 5) WE WILL ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES OF NATURAL RESOURCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL ENHANCEMENT, PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION; 6) WE WILL SUPPORT STRONG, HEALTHY FAMILY DEVELOPMENT AND WELL-BEING LEADING TO STRONGER VIRGINIA COMMUNITIES; 7) 4-H PROGRAMS FOCUS ON DEVELOPING POSITIVE, HEALTHY, SKILLED, PRODUCTIVE YOUTH TO BE TOMORROW'S LEADERS.

UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA LEVERAGES RREA FUNDS WITH OTHER SOURCES OF FUNDING, PRIMARILY SALARY AND PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (UF/IFAS), TO PROVIDE EXTENSION SUPPORT TO TWELVE EXTENSION FACULTY AND THREE TECHNICAL STAFF IN THE SCHOOL OF FOREST, FISHERIES AND GEOMATICS SCIENCES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF WILDLIFE ECOLOGY AND CONSERVATION. THE PURPOSE OF THESE EXTENSION PROGRAMS IS TO ADDRESS MULTIPLE STAKEHOLDERS NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES IN FLORIDA; PROMOTE INFORMATION TRANSFER REGARDING THE ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES; AND PROVIDE INFORMATION ON LAND USE OPTIONS AND STRATEGIES FOR WORKING LANDSCAPES AND URBAN FORESTS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE FORMAL EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS SUCH AS COURSES, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS; INFORMAL INTERACTIONS TOA ADDRESS INDIVIDUAL PROBLEMS THROUGH PHONE CALLS, EMAIL CORRESPONDENCE, AND SITE VISITS; AND PASSIVE EDUCATION SUCH AS ONLINE WEBSITES AND EXTENSION FACT SHEETS THROUGH THE UF/IFD EDIS (ELECTRONIC DATA INFORMATION SOURCE) SYSTEM. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL DELIVER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS BOTH IN-PERSON VIA WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING PROGRAMS THAT INCLUDE CLASSROOM, LAB, AND/OR FIELD EXPERIENCES; ONLINE TOOLS INCLUDING WEBINARS, WEBSITES, AND VIDEOS; AND SOCIAL MEDIA SUCH AS TWITTER, BLOGS, AND APPS. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE EVENTS AND PRODUCTS. EVENTS WILL INCLUDE FACILITATION AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL RESOURCES LEADERSHIP INSTITUTE (NRLI), EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS ADDRESSING FOREST AND RANGELAND MANAGEMENT, NATURAL HISTORY, AND CONSERVATION THROUGH FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS SUCH AS THE FLORIDA FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND THE MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAMS; FOREST AND RANGE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL AREAS TRAINING ACADEMY (NATA); WORKSHOPS ON THE MANAGEMENT OF INVASIVE PLATS AND ANIMALS, FOREST INSECT PESTS, AND RANGELAND WEEDS VIA WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DAYS THROUGH REGIONAL WORKSHOPS AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS INCLUDING THE FOREST STEWARDSHIP PROGRAM, BARK BEETLE ACADEMY, AND THE INVASIVE SPECIES COUNCIL AND THE COOPERATIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AREAS TEAMS. PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION FACT SHEETS, PUBLISHED ONLINE IN THE UF/IFAS EDIS SYSTEM ON MULTIPLE TOPICS INCLUDING FOREST AND RANGELAND WILDLIFE, FOREST AND RANGELAND HEALTH AND MANAGEMENT, INVASIVE SPECIES AND THEIR CONTROL, AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL MAINTAIN, UPDATE, AND EXPAND (E.G., INVASIVE SPECIES WEBSITE PORTAL) WEBSITES IN FORESTRY, WILDLIFE, INVASIVE SPECIES, AND RELATED EXTENSION PROGRAMS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE CHANGE IN KNOWLEDGE, CHANGE IN ACTION, AND CHANGE IN CONDITION. WE EXPECT OUR TRAINING PROGRAMS, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS TO INCREASE PARTICIPANT KNOWLEDGE. WE EXPECT THAT PARTICIPANTS IN TRAINING PROGRAMS AND WORKSHOPS/FIELD DAYS WILL INDICATE THE INTENTION OF IMPLEMENTING AT LEAST ONE MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATION OR OTHER ACTION. WE ALSO EXPECT THAT PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT OR OTHER ACTIONS THAT WILL AFFECT 25% OF THE FLORIDA ACREAGE MANAGEMENT BY PARTICIPANTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF OUR ACTIVITIES AND DELIVERABLES INCLUDE FLORIDA PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, FOREST, AND RANGELAND MANAGERS; PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, BIOLOGISTS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTANTS; EDUCATORS; ELECTED OFFICIALS AND STAFF, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND INTERESTED CITIZENS; AND ECO/AGRITOURISM AND OTHER SMALL BUSINESS/RECREATIONAL OPERATIONS ON PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LANDS.

FEDERAL PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF OUR RREA PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE EXTENSION PROGRAMMING DESIGNED TO ASSIST FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS AND MANAGERS MAKE SCIENCE-BASED MANAGEMENT DECISIONS TO MEET HEALTH, SAFETY, PRODUCTION, PROTECTION, AND SUSTAINABILITY NEEDS OF THE OWNER AND SOCIETY. TOPICAL ISSUES INCLUDE: LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT; PUBLIC AWARENESS; RESOURCE MANAGEMENT; WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND PROTECTION; SUCCESSION AND ESTATE PLANNING; FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT; AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. WSUS RREA PROGRAM ALIGNS USDA STRATEGIC GOAL #1, TO COMBAT CLIMATE CHANGE TO SUPPORT AMERICA'S WORKING LANDS, NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMUNITIES. WE FOCUS ON RREA GOAL ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. OUR ISSUES AREAS ARE 1) FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH, AND 2) RANGELAND STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH. OUR FOCUS IS WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF FOREST AND RANGE FIRES, AND THE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOREST AND RANGE RESOURCES. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THE WSU EXTENSION FORESTRY <(>&<)> RANGE T EAM WILL PROVIDE UNBIASED, RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES TO MEET LANDOWNER AND MANAGER NEEDS. THROUGH FACE-TO-FACE AND DISTANCE DELIVERIES OF CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, SEMINARS, CONFERENCES, PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, SHORTCOURSES, CONSULTATIONS, MEDIA WORK, PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPROVE LEARNING AND APPLICATION OF NEW IDEAS LEADING TO DESIRABLE FUTURE CONDITIONS. PROGRAMS WILL BE LIVE AND PRE-RECORDED TO SUIT USE PREFERENCE FOR ACCESSING INFORMATION. AS APPROPRIATE, INFORMATION WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN SPANISH FOR THOSE WITH ENGLISH AS A SECOND LANGUAGE.PHYSICAL ACCESS AND DISABILITIES WILL BE ACCOMMODATED FOLLOWING ADA ACCESSIBILITY STANDARDS, INCLUDING WEB DESIGN. DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES: WSU EXPECTS TO DELIVER 100 ACTIVITIES REACHING 10,000 OWNERS AND MANAGERS AND POSITIVELY IMPACTING 0.5-MILLION ACRES. COMPREHENSIVE ACHIEVEMENTS WILL 1) ENHANCE FOREST AND RANGE SUSTAINABILITY BY DEVELOPING OWNER/ MANAGER CAPACITY FOR IMPROVING HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY; 2) PROMOTE LAND RESILIENCE BY PREPARING OWNER/ MANAGER CAPACITY FOR RESPONDING TO HARMFUL IMPACTS CAUSED BY WILDFIRE, DROUGHT, WILDLIFE DAMAGE, INVASIVE SPECIES, INSECTS PESTS AND DISEASE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS PERPETUATED BY CLIMATE CHANGE; AND 3) DIVERSIFY STEWARDSHIP OPPORTUNITIES THAT LEAD TO MULTIPLE-USE BENEFITS. WE BASE THESE EXPECTATIONS ON ACCOMPLISHMENTS DERIVED BY THE PAST 16 YEARS OF PROGRAM EVALUATION DATA. NOTEWORTHY IMPACTS EXPECTED: 1) IMPROVED FOREST <(>&<)> RANGELAND HEALTH; 2) DECREASED RISK OF WILDFIRE; 3) IMPROVE HABITAT; 4) DECREASED INSECT, DISEASE, AND INVASIVE SPECIES RISK; 5) IMPROVED PRODUCTIVITY OF TREES AND FORAGE; 6) DECREASED EROSION; 7) IMPROVED WOOD QUALITY AND PRODUCTS; 8) IMPROVED INCOME OPPORTUNITY; 9) IMPROVED PROTECTION OF CULTURAL RESOURCES AND SPECIAL SITES; AND 10) IMPROVED RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES. LIMITED LEARNING CHANGES WILL BE SOUGHT, AND WE WILL FOCUS EVALUATION ON MEASURING CHANGES IN BEHAVIORS, PRACTICES, AND WHEN APPROPRIATE, DECISIONS (FOR EXAMPLE, ASKING FOR A FORESTER VISIT). WE WILL COLLABORATE AND LEVERAGE OUR OUTREACH BY UTILIZING PARTNERSHIPS SUCH AS THE US FOREST SERVICE, WA DEPT. NATURAL RESOURCES, WA ASSOC. OF CONSERVATION DISTRICTS, WA FARM FORESTRY ASSOC., SOC. OF AMERICAN FORESTERS, ASSOC. OF CONSULTING FORESTERS, FORESTRY COLLABORATIVES, AND COUNTY PARTNERSHIPS. WE WILL CONTRIBUTE TO NGO PURPOSES THAT HOLD COMMON CONSERVATION GOALS FOR INFORMING THEIR MEMBERSHIP AND THE PUBLIC, SUCH AS THE NATURE CONSERVANCY, AMERICAN TREE FARM SYSTEM, AMERICAN FOREST FOUNDATIONS, ROCKY MOUNTAIN ELK FOUNDATION, AND VARIOUS LAND TRUSTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: NON-INDUSTRIAL PRIVATE FOREST (NIPF) AND RANGELAND OWNERS, AND MANAGERS (PRACTICING FORESTERS, LOGGERS, RANCHERS, SILVICULTURAL CONTRACTORS, AND TRIBAL NATURAL RESOURCE EMPLOYEES). INVITED PRESENTATIONS FOR YOUTH OR SERVICE ORGANIZATIONS ARE POSSIBLE BUT NOT TARGET BENEFICIARIES.

ARKANSAS FOREST AND NATURAL RESOURCES ARE CRITICAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY AND TO THE WELL-BEING OF ITS CITIZENS: WE ARE KNOWN AS THE NATURAL STATE. MORE THAN HALF OF THE STATE (55%) IS FORESTED, WITH ALMOST HALF OF THE FOREST COMPRISED OF OAK AND HICKORY FOREST TYPES AND NEARLY A THIRD COMPRISED OF LOBLOLLY AND SHORTLEAF PINE. THESE DIVERSE FORESTS PROVIDE HABITAT TO A HOST OF WILDLIFE SPECIES. THESE RANGE FROM GAME SPECIES, SUCH AS DEER, TURKEY, AND DUCKS, TO SONGBIRDS FOR WILDLIFE VIEWING, AND MANY REPTILES AND AMPHIBIANS. ARKANSAS FORESTS ALSO PROVIDE CLEAN DRINKING WATER TO METROPOLITAN AREAS AND PROTECT OTHER IMPORTANT WATERSHEDS. RAW MATERIALS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS SUPPORT A VIBRANT FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. FOREST RESOURCE COMPANIES OWN OR LEASE 23% OF THE STATE'S TIMBERLAND AND PROVIDED JOBS DIRECTLY TO 28,057 EMPLOYEES, REPRESENTING A LABOR INCOME OF $1.6 BILLION, IN 2014. MORE THAN HALF OF THE STATE'S 18.5 MILLION ACRES OF FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY PRIVATE NON-INDUSTRIAL FOREST LANDOWNERS. THIS IMPORTANT LANDOWNER GROUP IS EXTREMELY DIVERSE AND INCLUDES FARMERS, RANCHERS, HOMEOWNERS, TEACHERS, FACTORY WORKERS, PROFESSIONALS, AND RETIREES. THE DEMAND FOR BENEFITS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS, INCLUDING WILDLIFE HABITAT AND FOREST PRODUCTS, MUST INCREASINGLY BE MET BY THESE PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS. HOWEVER, MANY OF THESE LANDOWNERS ARE UNFAMILIAR WITH SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, TIMBER MARKETING, HABITAT RESTORATION, REFORESTATION INCENTIVES, AND OTHER VITAL INFORMATION CRITICAL TO SUSTAINING FOREST LANDS. MOST OF THEM ALSO HOLD THEIR FOREST LANDS FOR REASONS OTHER THAN TIMBER MANAGEMENT. THE FUTURE SUPPLY OF TIMBER, THEREFORE, MIGHT NOT BE SECURE UNLESS HARVESTING FOREST PRODUCTS FULFILLS THE LANDOWNER'S OBJECTIVES AND NEEDS. SEVERAL ISSUES ARE THREATENING ARKANSAS FORESTS, HOWEVER. INVASIVE PESTS INCLUDING FERAL HOGS, EMERALD ASH BORER, AND THE RECENTLY DISCOVERED LAUREL WILT DISEASE ARE BUT A FEW OF THE DIRECT FACTORS AFFECTING FOREST HEALTH IN RURAL AND URBAN FORESTS. FORESTERS ARE ALSO CONCERNED ABOUT A POTENTIAL INCREASE IN PINE BARK BEETLES INCLUDING SOUTHERN PINE BEETLE RESULTING FROM STRESS FROM OVER-CROWDING AND DROUGHT. OTHER LESS DIRECT FACTORS ARE FOREST FRAGMENTATION, FOREST DENSIFICATION, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND A WEAK FOREST PRODUCTS MARKET. THE WEAK MARKET CREATES CONSTRAINTS TO SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. NEW FOREST-BASED PRODUCTS, INCLUDING BIOENERGY, WOOD PELLETS, ARE STILL IN THE DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE BUT WILL HOPEFULLY AUGMENT AND INCREASE DEMAND FOR WOOD PRODUCTS. OUR GOAL THEN, IS TO INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO MANAGE AND TO SUSTAIN HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS THAT MEET BOTH HUMAN AND ECOLOGICAL NEEDS. ASSOCIATED WITH THIS GOAL, OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO IMPROVE FORESTRY STAKEHOLDER AWARENESS OF FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES BY: (1) HOSTING IN-PERSON EVENTS (WORKSHOPS, FIELD TOURS), (2) HOSTING VIRTUAL EVENTS (WEBINARS), (3) CONDUCTING DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS, (4) DEVELOPING WEB-BASED MANAGEMENT TOOLS AND (5) PUBLISHING RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION THROUGH DIVERSE MEDIA (BULLETINS, POPULAR PRESS, MEDIA RELEASES, INTERNET ARTICLES).

positiveFlows.title: PURPOSE: THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AT PENN STATE WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT TO PENNSYLVANIA RESIDENTS THROUGH THE PENNSYLVANIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND PENN STATE EXTENSION (PSE) ACTIVITIES. WE WILL BE RESPONSIVE TO STAKEHOLDER NEEDS THROUGH TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH AND DELIVERY OF SCIENCE-BASED PROGRAMS TO CLIENTELE. WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT INTERNATIONALLY RELEVANT FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH THAT GENERATES BASELINE DATA TO SOLVE FUTURE PROBLEMS AND ACTIVELY SEEK NEW AND BETTER WAYS TO COMMUNICATE OUR PROGRAMS TO NEW AUDIENCES. OUR FACULTY AND STAFF, SUPPORTED BY FEDERAL BASE FUNDING, WILL EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE THIS INVESTMENT AGAINST MANY OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO CONDUCT PROGRAMS OF THE HIGHEST CALIBER. WE ARE COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE IN RESEARCH, EDUCATING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS AND CITIZENS, AND PROMOTING LIFE-LONG LEARNING AMONG THE CITIZENS OF PENNSYLVANIA. OUR COLLEGE'S MISSION IS CLEAR: THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES IS TO DISCOVER, INTEGRATE, TRANSLATE, AND DISSEMINATE KNOWLEDGE TO ENHANCE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM, NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP, AND ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL WELLBEING, THEREBY IMPROVING THE LIVES OF PEOPLE IN PENNSYLVANIA, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. AGRICULTURE FACES CHALLENGES OF RISING ENERGY COSTS, WEATHER EXTREMES, AN EXPANDING HUMAN POPULATION, ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, AND LABOR SHORTAGES. THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ADDED TO THE CHALLENGES: DISRUPTIONS TO FOOD CHAINS, WORKFORCE CHALLENGES, IMPACTS ON YOUTH EDUCATION, AND BUSINESS INTERRUPTIONS. WE MUST ADDRESS THESE ISSUES TO MITIGATE FUTURE WIDESPREAD DISRUPTIONS THAT IMPACT ALL OF SOCIETY. ACTIVITIES: TO HELP MEET THESE CHALLENGES, WE ARE DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK BASED ON THE SCIENCE OF AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY-DEFINED AS THE INTEGRATION OF NATURAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO INFORM PRACTICE AND POLICY FOR PRODUCTIVE, WORKING LANDSCAPES, HEALTHY WATERSHEDS, AND RESILIENT ECONOMIES. THIS INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH, ENGAGEMENT, AND EDUCATION CENTERS ON THE IMPACTS AND SYNERGIES OF CONTIGUOUS RURAL AND URBAN LANDSCAPES. PENN STATE EXTENSION PROVIDES ACCESS TO FACE-TO-FACE AND ONLINE SCIENCE-BASED EDUCATION TO OUR CUSTOMERS TO HELP THEM ADDRESS PROBLEMS AND TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVEMENT AND INNOVATION. WE MAKE A DIFFERENCE LOCALLY THROUGH FOCUSED ENGAGEMENT AND, MORE WIDELY, TO CUSTOMERS CONNECTING IN THE DIGITAL LANDSCAPE. INITIATIVES ENSURE THE STABILITY OF THE FOOD SYSTEM IN THE COMMONWEALTH AND OUR EFFORTS TO PROVIDE A BROAD-BASED ONLINE LEARNING PLATFORM FOR NONCREDIT PROGRAMMING AND DIGITAL EDUCATION. WITH RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM (RREA) FUNDING, MSU EXTENSION FOSTERS ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE, A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, AND A PLENTIFUL AND SECURE FOOD SUPPLY FOR MICHIGAN RESIDENTS. OUR NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS IMPROVE PUBLIC UNDERSTANDING, HELP LANDOWNERS AND COMMUNITIES USE THOSE ASSETS FOR SUSTAINABLE LONG-TERM SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. WISCONSIN IS A LARGELY FORESTED LANDSCAPE COVERING 16 MILLION ACRES, ABOUT 46% OF THE STATE'S LAND AREA. OVERALL, 57% OF THE FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES, TOTALING 360,000 OWNERS. THIS INDUSTRY RELIES HEAVILY ON FAMILY?OWNED FORESTLAND. THE WDNR ESTIMATES THAT 10% OF THE 9.1 MILLION FORESTED ACRES, HELD BY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS, WILL BE SOLD, SUBDIVIDED OR CONVERTED TO NON?FOREST USE IN THE NEXT 5 YEARS. IN A SIMILAR STUDY, THE SUSTAINING FAMILY FORESTS INITIATIVE (SFFI) FOUND THE HIGHEST CONCERN REPORTED BY 56% OF ALL LANDOWNERS WAS KEEPING LAND INTACT FOR CHILDREN/HEIRS. INCIDENTALLY, THE SECOND HIGHEST CONCERN WAS HIGH PROPERTY TAXES. A THIRD STUDY, BY GOBSTER AND RICKENBACH (2004) LOOKED AT PERCEPTIONS OF PARCELIZATION. OUR COMPREHENSIVE FORESTRY OUTREACH PROGRAM ZEROES IN ON THESE CONCERNS. GOAL 1? ENSURING HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND GOAL 3 ? ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THE PRIMARY CROSS?CUTTING ISSUES WE WILL FOCUS ON INCLUDE FISH AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND INTERGENERATIONAL LAND AND OTHER LAND OWNERSHIP CHANGES. THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO HELP LANDOWNERS DEVELOP FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AROUND WOODLAND ECOLOGY, HEALTHY FORESTS, TIMBER HARVEST PRACTICES AND SALES, HABITAT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT BENEFIT WILDLIFE, STRATEGIES FOR THREATS SUCH AS INVASIVE SPECIES AND CLIMATE VARIABILITY, LAND OWNERSHIP AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRANSFERS, AND TO IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT PLAN PRACTICES TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINABLE FOREST RESOURCES AND TO MEET PERSONAL MANAGEMENT GOALS. THROUGH IN?PERSON CLASSES, VIRTUAL CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WE ARE EXPECTING TO INCREASE LANDOWNERS' AND RESOURCES PROFESSIONALS' SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE TO AFFECT LONG?TERM CHANGES IN ACTIVE MANAGEMENT BY WOODLAND OWNERS THAT WILL SUPPORT SUCCESSION TO FAMILY MEMBERS, REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF PARCELIZATION THROUGH STABLE LAND OWNERSHIP, AND RETAIN FOREST COVER AND CONTRIBUTE SUSTAINABLY TO THE WOOD FUEL CYCLE THROUGH REGULAR PLANNED TIMBER SALES GUIDED BY FOREST MANAGEMENT PLANS.

WHILE 94 PERCENT OF THE STATE'S LAND BASE (41+MILLION ACRES) IS PRIVATELY OWNED, LESS THAN 10 PERCENT OF THESE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AC TIVELY MANAGE THEIR FORESTS, WOODLANDS, AND NON-AGRICULTURAL FIELDS. THIS TRANSLATES DIRECTLY INTO LOST, VALUE-ADDED FOREST PRODUCTS AND INDIRECTLY INTO DIMINISHED ABILITY OF OUR FOREST AND WOODLANDS IN PROVIDING VALUABLE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, SUCH AS CLEAN AIR AND WATER. THIS LACK OF MANAGEMENT IS ALSO RESULTING IN LOST WILDLIFE HABITAT IN OUR WOODLANDS, ON OUR FARMS, AND IN OUR COMMUNITIES. THUS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR EXPANDED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT WILL ENABLE ALL MISSOURI CITIZENS TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS REGARDING THE WISE STEWARDSHIP AND CONSERVATION OF THE STATE'S FORESTS AND WOODLANDS, GRASSLANDS AND FIELDS, AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AND THE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS WHICH DEPEND UPON THESE ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS. THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS SO THAT A GREATER NUMBER OF CLIENTELE WILL RECONNECT WITH MISSOURI'S NATURAL RESOURCES, INCLUDING THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESOURCE, BECOME ACTIVE LAND STEWARDS SUPPORTING CONSERVATION GOALS AND OBJECTIVES. PROJECT GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: A. INCREASE AND ENHANCE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING ON PRIVATE LANDS FEATURING WORKING FORESTS, WOODLANDS, NATIVE GRASSLANDS AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION WITHIN MISSOURI AND B. BUILDING CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS. ACTIONS TAKEN WILL FEATURE THE DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY OF EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE FOREST AND WOODLAND MANAGEMENT BY MISSOURI'S FAMILY FOREST LANDOWNERS AND DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT SERVE TO INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES CONDUCTED BY MISSOURI'S PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. CREATING AND/OR REVISING 5 PEER-REVIEWED MU EXTENSION FOREST AND WOODLAND MANAGEMENT GUIDES AND 12 NATURAL RESOURCE NEWSLETTERS DISSEMINATED FOR STATE-WIDE USE; C. CREATING 8 NEW MISSOURI MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAM VOLUNTEER COHORTS EITHER THROUGH EXISTING CHAPTERS OR THE CREATION OF NEW CHAPTERS WITH OVER 200 NEW MU EXTENSION MASTER NATURALIST VOLUNTEERS BEING TRAINED AND CERTIFIED TO CONDUCT VOLUNTEER SERVICE PROJECTS IN THEIR COMMUNITY FEATURING THE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES; D. CONDUCTING 12 WILDLIFE HABITAT MANAGEMENT EDUCATIONAL EVENTS FOCUSED ON ENHANCING HABITATS FOR BOTH WOODLAND AND EARLY SUCCESSIONAL SPECIES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO GRASSLAND BIRDS AND BOBWHITE QUAIL; AND CONDUCTING 2 MASTER POLLINATOR STEWARD PROGRAMS THAT FEATURES THE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF NATIVE HABITATS THAT BENEFIT POLLINATORS; E. TARGET AUDIENCES AND INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS IN BOTH URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES WISHING TO IMPROVE THE NATURAL RESOURCE BASE ON THEIR PROPERTY; EDUCATORS WISHING TO IN CORPORATE SCIENCE-BASED FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES INTO THEIR CURRICULUM AND ONGOING PROGRAM ACTIVITIES AND; NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS REPRESENTING STATE, FEDERAL AND NON-PROFIT CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS WISHING TO COLLABORATE IN DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS.

TENNESSEE'S TWO LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS COMPRISE THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SYSTEM. THEY WORK INDEPENDENTLY AND COLLABORATIVELY TO CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ALL 95 COUNTIES AND TO SERVE THE STATE'S 6.9 MILLION PEOPLE. TENNESSEE'S LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS CONDUCT RESEARCH AND PROVIDE OUTREACH IN FIVE KEY AREAS TO ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES AFFECTING THE STATE: SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS; ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY; ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY; DEVELOPING OUR WORKFORCE; AND STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE PROGRAMS TO ADDRESS THE ONGOING NEEDS OF CITIZENS AND AGRICULTURE PRODUCERS ACROSS THE STATE. HEALTH ISSUES ARE A TOP CONCERN FOR RESIDENTS. EXTENSION WILL STRENGTHEN HEALTH PROGRAMMING BY OFFERING THE HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAMS AND PROVIDE RESOURCES FOR IMPROVING DIETARY AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY FOR LIMITED-RESOURCE TENNESSEANS. EXTENSION LIVESTOCK AND FORAGE PROGRAMS STRENGTHEN THE STATE'S LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS THOUGH RESEARCH AND OUTREACH IN HAY SCHOOLS, LATE GESTATION NUTRITION, MARKETING, AND FORAGES. TENNESSEE EXTENSION HAS DEVELOPED PROGRAMS TO STRENGTHEN AND PROVIDE VALUE-ADDED OPPORTUNITIES AND PROGRAMS ON FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT. THE CONSUMER ECONOMICS PROGRAM HELPS FAMILIES INCREASE SAVINGS, DECREASE DEBT, AND FINANCIALLY PLAN. 4-H WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED FOR YOUTH TO PROVIDE NEEDED SKILLS, TRAINING, AND EXPERIENCES TO PARTICIPANTS. EXTENSION CONTINUES TO DEVELOP PROGRAMS TO ENCOURAGE AND PROVIDE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES. UT AGRESEARCH CONDUCTS RESEARCH WITHIN EIGHT ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS AND SEVEN PHYSICAL CENTERS, AND AT TEN AGRESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS (REC) LOCATED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. IN ADDITION TO A DECADE OF EXCELLENCE: TEN-YEAR STRATEGIC PLAN FOR UTIA, 2018-2028, AGRESEARCH OPERATES UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF ITS 2021-2024 AGRESEARCH STRATEGIC ACTION PLAN (ASAP) WITH THE OBJECTIVES TO BALANCE A PORTFOLIO OF INTEGRATED, INTER-DISCIPLINARY PROGRAMS, CULTIVATE TEAMS TO APPROACH COMPLEX PROBLEMS, ADVANCE CONCEPTS WITH STRUCTURED SUPPORT, AND TO ENSURE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CAPACITY WITH TARGETED INVESTMENT. AGRESEARCH IS EMPHASIZING FOUR PROGRAMMATIC THEMES TO ESTABLISH INTEGRATED PROGRAMS THAT CONTRIBUTE SOLUTIONS TO COMPLEX PROBLEMS. THE UT ONE HEALTH INITIATIVE, A UT SYSTEM-WIDE APPROACH HOUSED WITHIN AGRESEARCH, IS WORKING TO PRESERVE AND PROMOTE HUMAN, ANIMAL, PLANT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH TO ADVANCE ECONOMIC GROWTH, AND CONSERVE BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL, NATIONAL, AND GLOBAL SCALES. SCHOLARS FROM ACROSS AGRESEARCH ARE CONTRIBUTING TO STUDIES THAT DEFINE THE FACTORS THREATENING HUMAN AND ANIMAL HEALTH, AND THE HEALTH OF OUR ENVIRONMENT. THE EMERGING DIGITAL AGRICULTURE PROGRAM DRAWS ON THE SKILLS OF RESEARCHERS ACROSS UT TO CREATE A TRANSDISCIPLINARY PATH TO CARBONSMART AGRICULTURE AND BENEFITS FROM ONGOING INVESTMENT TO BUILD CAPACITY IN PRECISION LIVESTOCK FARMING (PLF). THE PROGRAM INCORPORATES BOTH PLANT AND ANIMAL MANAGEMENT PROJECTS THAT ULTIMATELY WILL CONTRIBUTE INFORMATION TO REFINE STRATEGIES THAT OFFER CARBON REDUCTIONS OVER TODAY'S AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS. AGRESEARCH IS REALIGNING THE CAPABILITIES AT ITS REC'S TO SUPPORT THE PLF INITIATIVE, INCLUDING THE INSTALLATION OF A ROBOTIC MILKING SYSTEM. THE TRANSFORMATIONAL AGRICULTURAL GENOMICS AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY PROGRAM WILL ADVANCE ANIMAL AND PLANT-BASED PRODUCTIVITY AND RESILIENCE. ALTHOUGH EARLY IN ITS DEVELOPMENT, THE INITIATIVE ALREADY ENGAGES FACULTY ACROSS UT TO ADVANCE STATE-OF-THE-ART SCIENCE TO DESIGN CROPS THAT ARE RESILIENT TO CLIMATE CHANGE. THE BIOECONOMY ADVANCEMENT INITIATIVE IS AN ESTABLISHED INTERDISCIPLINARY, MULTIDEPARTMENTAL PROGRAM FOCUSED ON SUSTAINABLE FUELS, CHEMICALS, AND MATERIALS FROM STRANDED RESOURCES. THE INITIATIVE IS EMBRACING THE CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK OF THE CIRCULAR BIOECONOMY, SEEKING TO EXTEND THE LIFETIME OF RENEWABLE CARBON IN THE MARKETPLACE.

IT IS ESTIMATED THAT OVER 75% OF FAMILY FOREST LAND IS OWNED BY PEOPLE OVER THE AGE OF 55 AND NEARLY 50% IS OWNED BY PEOPLE OVER THE AGE OF 65 (BUTLER, ET AL. 2016). TIMBER PRODUCTION, IN THE U.S., RELIES HEAVILY ON PRIVATE LANDS, WHERE CLOSE TO 90% OF TIMBER PRODUCT OUTPUT COMES FROM THESE PROPERTIES (MORGAN, 2009). ALSO, WE WILL FOSTER NETWORKING BETWEEN EXTENSIONPROFESSIONALS AND PBA LEADERS TO REINFORCE CONCEPTS RELATED TO WILDLAND FIRE AND FACILITATEESTABLISHMENT OF SUCCESSFUL PBAS. positiveFlows.title: SUMMARYPRESCRIBED BURNING ASSOCIATIONS (PBAS) PLAY A VITAL ROLE IN BUILDING A NETWORK OF PRIVATE LANDOWNERS COMMITTED TO THE SAFE AND EFFECTIVE USE OF PRESCRIBED FIRE. WHILE TEXAS HAS AN EXISTING FRAMEWORK THROUGH THE PRESCRIBED BURN ALLIANCE OF TEXAS, THERE IS NO STATEWIDE LEADERSHIP TO COORDINATE, STRENGTHEN, AND EXPAND THIS NETWORK. THIS PROJECT PROPOSES A MULTI-AGENCY INITIATIVE TO INCREASE PRESCRIBED FIRE CAPACITY AND FOSTER A SUSTAINABLE FIRE CULTURE IN TEXAS. KEY ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: (1) FUNDING A DEDICATED PBA FACILITATOR TO PROVIDE LEADERSHIP AND COORDINATION; (2) DEVELOPING IN-PERSON RESOURCES, FIELD DAYS, AND WORKSHOPS THAT COMPLEMENT EXISTING ONLINE TRAINING; (3) CREATING AN ENHANCED COMMUNICATION NETWORK WITH REGULAR MEETINGS, SHARED RESOURCES, AND UPDATED ONLINE TOOLS; AND (4) DELIVERING TARGETED, HANDS-ON TRAINING SUCH AS FIRE FIELD DAYS, PRESCRIBED BURN SCHOOLS, AND BRUSH PILE BURNING WORKSHOPS TAILORED TO THE NEEDS OF LOCAL PBAS. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE NEW LANDOWNERS, AGENCY PERSONNEL, COUNTY EXTENSION AGENTS, AND PBAS ACROSS THE STATE. THIS COORDINATED APPROACH MIRRORS SUCCESSFUL MODELS IN OTHER STATES AND WILL HELP ENSURE SAFE, EFFECTIVE, AND LOCALLY ADAPTED PRESCRIBED FIRE PRACTICES IN TEXAS.

WATER SCARCITY, RESOURCE LIMITATIONS, AND GLOBAL ECONOMIC COMPETITION ARE DRIVING INNOVATIONS IN CALIFORNIA'S AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY, RESOURCE EFFICIENCY, AND LONG-TERM LAND STEWARDSHIP. RANGELAND MANAGEMENT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO DELIVER SIGNIFICANT SOIL HEALTH, WATER CONSERVATION, AND PRODUCTIVITY BENEFITS, THEREBY ENHANCING THE LONG-TERM VIABILITY AND PROFITABILITY OF THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR. MANAGEMENT PRACTICE FOR RANGELANDS SUCH AS PASTURE SEEDING, GRAZING, AND RIPARIAN ZONE MANAGEMENT OFFER OPPORTUNITIES FOR STEWARDSHIP OF WORKING LANDS. HOWEVER, ADOPTION OF THESE PRACTICES REMAINS LIMITED DUE TO UNCERTAINTY ABOUT ECONOMIC RETURNS, LACK OF PRACTICAL DEMONSTRATION MODELS, AND SHORT-TERM PROGRAM TIMELINES OF INCENTIVE PROGRAMS THAT MASK LONG-TERM BENEFITS. ADDITIONAL TARGETED OUTREACH IS NEEDED TO ADAPT EXISTING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND GRANT PROGRAMS FOR RANGELANDS AND PASTURES, ALONG WITH MORE PEER-TO-PEER CASE STUDIES DEMONSTRATING REDUCED MANAGEMENT COSTS AND IMPROVED OPERATIONAL OUTCOMES.THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EXPAND ADOPTION OF RANGELAND MANAGEMENT PRACTICES BY CLEARLY DEMONSTRATING AND COMMUNICATING THEIR ECONOMIC BENEFITS TO RANCHERS THROUGH INNOVATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAMMING AND HANDS-ON DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS. THIS RENEWABLE RESOURCE EXTENSION ACTION (RREA) NATIONAL FOCUS FUND PROJECT WILL ADDRESS EDUCATION AND EXTENSION NEEDS BY PRODUCING SCALABLE AND REPLICABLE RESOURCES FOR RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS. PLANNED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE WORKSHOPS, WEBINARS, AND ONLINE MATERIALS TO SHARE METHODS, RESULTS, AND PROVEN APPROACHES, THEREBY ENHANCING REPRODUCIBILITY AND ADOPTION. THE PROJECT WILL BUILD UPON AND COMPLEMENT ONGOING LARGE-SCALE EFFORTS IN CALIFORNIA THAT FOCUS ON RANGELAND MANAGEMENT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS.
