UNCHECKED GROWTH LEADS TO DIFFICULTIES FOR LOCAL ECONOMIES, OPEN-SPACE LANDS, WILDLIFE, AND WATER. OUR OBJECTIVES CENTER ON HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND PUBLIC BENEFIT OF PRIVATE LAND STEWARDSHIP FOR FOOD AND FIBER PRODUCTION AND ENHANCEMENT OF OUR NATURAL RESOURCES. WE WORK IN PRIORITY AREAS TO ADDRESS: 1) FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT, 2) GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION, 3) WILDFIRE PREVENTION, 4) LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT, AND 5) PUBLIC AWARENESS/YOUTH ENGAGEMENT. EXTENSION SPECIALISTS DEVELOP FLAGSHIP PROGRAMS IN THEIR AREA OF EXPERTISE TO MAXIMIZE REACH AND IMPACT FOR EACH. PROGRAMS LIKE PLANT PARTY, GENERATION NEXT, OUR TURN TO RANCH, PRESCRIBED BURN SCHOOL, TEXAS LAND TRENDS, AND LEOPOLD LIVE!, SHOW OUR ATTENTION TO EACH OF THESE PRIORITIES, RESPECTIVELY. OUR METHODS BLEND TRADITIONAL FACE-TO-FACE PROGRAMS, BUT WE ALSO DEVELOP ELECTRONIC RESOURCES, LIKE ON-LINE COURSES THAT ALLOW FOR EDUCATIONAL EXPLORATION, RATHER THAN JUST LINEAR LESSONS, ALLOWING FOR AN EDUCATIONAL JOURNEY. WE MAXIMIZE THE REACH OF OUR EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THROUGH IN-HOUSE SOCIAL MEDIA OUTLETS AND DEVELOP RELATIONSHIPS WITH CONSERVATION PARTNERS TO AMPLIFY THEIR DISTRIBUTION. WE STRUCTURE OUR MATERIALS IN A WAY THAT CURIOUS PEOPLE CAN FIND THEM ON THE INTERNET AND WE ACTIVELY TARGET TEACHING AND TRAINING TO SPECIFIC GROUPS LIKE LANDOWNERS, COUNTY OFFICIALS, STATE, AND FEDERAL AGENCY EMPLOYEES. COLLECTIVELY, OUR WORK KEEPS WORKING LANDS INTACT, AND WE KEEP THE NATION'S MOST IMPORTANT INFRASTRUCTURE - LAND - IN THE CENTER OF OUR THINKING.

FY25 RREA EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: ALASKA'S FORESTS ARE IMPORTANT FOR THEIR TIMBER, BIOMASS, SUBSISTENCE, FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT AND ECOSYSTEMS SERVICES RESOURCES. APPROXIMATELY 126 MILLION ACRES IN ALASKA ARE FORESTED, AND MOST ALASKANS LIVE IN OR NEXT TO A FOREST. CLIMATE VARIABILITY IMPACTS, CONTINUED DEMAND FOR TIMBER AND BIOMASS RESOURCES AND INCREASED USE FROM CONSUMPTIVE AND NON-CONSUMPTIVE USER GROUPS ARE PLACING MORE PRESSURES ON ALASKA'S FORESTS AND THE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND PROFESSIONALS MANAGING THOSE RESOURCES. IN ORDER TO SUSTAIN PRODUCTIVE FOREST RESOURCES AND FUNCTIONS ACROSS MULTIPLE LAND OWNERSHIP, INCLUDING FEDERAL, STATE, LOCAL, NATIVE AND PRIVATE, LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, USER GROUPS AND THE PUBLIC NEED ACCESS TO SCIENTIFICALLY SOUND AND RELEVANT INFORMATION ABOUT HOW FORESTS FUNCTION AND THE ROLE OF FOREST MANAGEMENT. PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS ARE UNDER INCREASING PRESSURE TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO FOREST RESOURCES WHILE MAINTAINING PUBLIC BENEFITS SUCH AS FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT, WATER AND WETLAND RESOURCES AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES BUT OFTEN LACK OPPORTUNITIES TO ACCESS THE MOST CURRENT INFORMATION. THIS PROJECT WILL USE A VARIETY OF METHODS, INCLUDING WEB-BASED PLATFORMS, PRINTED MATERIALS, SHORT WORKSHOPS AND PRESENTATIONS TO PROVIDE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS (INCLUDING NATIVE LANDOWNERS) AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS THE RESOURCES ALLOWING THEM TO MAKE GOOD MANAGEMENT DECISIONS FOR THEIR LANDS. THE GENERAL PUBLIC IS ALSO AN IMPORTANT AUDIENCE BECAUSE THEY CAN INFLUENCE POLICIES AFFECTING FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND MANAGEMENT ON PRIVATE AND PUBLIC FORESTED LANDS. THE GROWTH OF BIOMASS MARKETS OR OTHER WOOD USES IS ALSO INFLUENCED THROUGH PUBLIC OPINION IN THEIR LOCAL COMMUNITIES. EFFECTIVE AUDIENCE OUTREACH WILL INCLUDE EDUCATOR AND YOUTH PROGRAMMING ALONG WITH SOCIAL AND TRADITIONAL MEDIA RELEASES, WEB-BASED APPLICATIONS AND RADIO PROGRAMMING. THIS PROJECT WILL ENABLE PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS TO MAKE SOUND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS BASED ON THE LATEST AND MOST RELEVANT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH ON ALASKA'S FOREST RESOURCES AND IT WILL SUPPORT THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF ALASKA'S PUBLIC FORESTS LANDS BY INCREASING THE AWARENESS OF HOW FORESTS FUNCTION AND THE ROLE OF FOREST MANAGEMENT.

UC ANR RREA PROGRAM ABSTRACT DESCRIPTION <(>&<)> BENEFICIARIES THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT OF 1978 (RREA) SUPPORTS AN EXPANDED AND COMPREHENSIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM FOR FOREST AND RANGELAND RENEWABLE RESOURCES. RREA SUPPORTS FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS IN THE SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF WOOD PRODUCTS, FORAGE AND LIVESTOCK, FISH AND WILDLIFE POPULATIONS AND DEVELOPING OUTDOOR RECREATION OPPORTUNITIES. UC AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES OVERSEES THE UC RREA PROGRAM WHICH FOCUSES ON EIGHT ISSUE AREAS. PUBLIC AWARENESS AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT: ENGAGING YOUTH AND ADULTS ABOUT THE IMPORTANCE OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES, PARTICULARLY HOW FOREST LANDS AND RANGELANDS AFFECT RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES AND THE NEED TO USE SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION WHEN MAKING DECISIONS ABOUT THESE RESOURCES. ECOSYSTEM SERVICES: ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS IN ACTIVELY MANAGING THEIR LANDS WITH KNOWLEDGE OF FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM PROCESSES AND HOW SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES PRODUCE DIFFERENT COMBINATIONS OF ECO SYSTEM SERVICES; AND ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND USERS IN UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE DIFFERENT ECOSYSTEM SERVICES HAVE ON COMMUNITY WELL-BEING. FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT: ENSURING THAT PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS HAVE THE BEST AVAILABLE INFORMATION ABOUT FISH AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT HABITAT MANAGEMENT IN FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS. GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION AND OTHER LANDOWNERSHIP CHANGES: ENHANCING THE DECISION-MAKING ABILITY OF RANCH AND FOREST LANDOWNER FAMILIES FOR GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION BY PROVIDING INFORMATION ON AND FACILITATING COMMUNICATION ABOUT SUCH PLANNING OPTIONS AS CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, COMMUNITY-BASED NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT OR OTHER NON-TRADITIONAL SUCCESSION MODELS; TRAINING AND LINKING INTERESTED PARTIES IN COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS THAT WILL AUGMENT GENERATIONAL TRANSFER OF FOREST AND RANGELAND ENTERPRISES. INVASIVE SPECIES: INCREASING THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO ASSESS THE THREAT OF INVASIVE SPECIES; DEVELOPING INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT PLANS; IMPLEMENTING EFFECTIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL STRATEGIES TO PROTECT FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS; PROVIDING MEANS FOR THE GENERAL PUBLIC (INCLUDING ABSENTEE LANDOWNERS), YOUTH, AND COMMUNITY GROUPS FOR THEIR INTERACTION AND PARTICIPATION IN MONITORING AND CONTROLLING INVASIVE SPECIES. RURAL COMMUNITIES: WORKING WITH RURAL COMMUNITIES TO ASSESS NEEDS AND DETERMINE HOW TO SUSTAINABLY ENHANCE LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT THROUGH A FOCUS ON FOREST AND RANGELAND INDUSTRIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, AND EXPERTISE; CREATING A STRONGER RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HEALTHY FORESTS AND RANGELANDS AND THE SOCIAL AND SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC BASES OF RURAL COMMUNITIES; ASSESSING NEEDS AND DETERMINING HOW TO ENHANCE LOCAL LANDSCAPE ECONOMICS. WATER AND WETLANDS: ENCOURAGING MANAGEMENT OF FORESTS AND RANGELANDS TO IMPROVE WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY. WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT: ENGAGING FOREST AND RANGELAND COMMUNITIES WITH RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION ON WILDFIRE RISK-MANAGEMENT AND POST-FIRE RECOVERY STRATEGIES; INCREASING T HE CAPACITY OF COMMUNITY, COUNTY, AND STATE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS/CIVIL DEFENSE AUTHORITIES TO COMMUNICATE COMMUNITY NEEDS AND INFORM COMMUNITY-DEVELOPMENT POLICIES, CODES, AND ORDINANCES THAT PROTECT COMMUNITIES FROM WILDFIRE; DEVELOPING OUTREACH EFFORTS THAT IN CLUDE CURRENT AND EMERGING RESEARCH ON IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE ON FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOLOGY AND ECONOMICS, FUELS MANAGEMENT, AND PRESCRIBED FIRE TO CREATE APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES; INCREASING CAPACITY FOR COMMUNITY ACTION, EMPOWER LANDOWNERS TO ENGAGE IN P RESCRIBED FIRE, AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR TRAINING AND CAPACITY IN FUELS REDUCTION.

positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT FUNDING RECEIVED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA WARNELL SCHOOL OF FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES IS TO SUPPORT THE OUTREACH EFFORTS OF OUR EXTENSION FACULTY AND BRING SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION TO OUR TARGET AUDIENCES, SUCH AS GEORGIA FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, TO HELP THEM MAKE CRITICAL MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. WE EDUCATE GEORGIA CITIZENS ABOUT HOW AND WHY NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES ARE PRESCRIBED AND CONDUCTED. WE PROVIDE CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDIT COURSES REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN PROFESSIONAL CREDENTIALS. THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED IN THE COMING YEAR INCLUDE: 1) WORKSHOPS; 2) APPLIED RESEARCH; 3) PEER REVIEWED AND EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS; 4) PRESENTATIONS; AND 5) FOSTER PARTNER COLLABORATIONS. THE DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE: WORKSHOPS: THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM WILL PLAN, ORGANIZE AND DELIVER WORKSHOPS COVERING TOPICS THAT INCLUDE THE IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES, TIMBER TAXATION, INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT, FOREST HEALTH, URBAN WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION CERTIFICATION, AND AQUATIC RESOURCE MANAGEMENT. WORKSHOPS WILL BE PLANNED TO BE BOTH PROACTIVE AND REACTIVE. OUR ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION SPECIALISTS WILL OFFER EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EVENTS FOR STUDENTS AND TEACHERS USING INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED CURRICULA (PROJECT LEARNING TREE, PROJECT WILD, AND PROJECT WET). APPLIED RESEARCH: ACTIVITIES WILL INVOLVE MAINTAINING EXISTING AND DEVELOPING NEW SITES TO EVALUATE AND SERVE AS DEMONSTRATIONS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF APPLIED RESEARCH EFFORTS IS TO STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION WITH STATE/FEDERAL AGENCY PARTNERS AND PRIVATE INDUSTRY SPONSORS, AND AS DATA CONTINUES TO BE GATHERED AND ANALYZED, AN INCREASED USE OF THESE SITES AS EFFECTIVE DEMONSTRATION SITES FOR FIELD DAYS AND WORKSHOPS. PUBLICATIONS: TOPICS TO BE COVERED INCLUDE FIRESCAPING, WILD HARVESTING PRACTICES, WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, AND INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES (HERBICIDE APPLICATION AND SITE PREPARATION). ALL PUBLICATIONS WILL BE PRODUCED WITH THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF SPREADING TRUSTED INFORMATION AND INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PUBLICATIONS POSTED ON OUR WARNELL OUTREACH WEBSITE WHERE WE CAN TRACK THE NUMBER OF VIEWS AND DOWNLOADS. INNOVATIVE EDUCATIONAL VIDEOS WILL ALSO BE PRODUCED TO ALLOW CLIENTELE TO ACCESS INFORMATION CONVENIENTLY USING SMART PHONE TECHNOLOGY. PRESENTATIONS: WE HAVE PLANS TO COVER MANY TOPICS INCLUDING URBAN WILDLIFE ISSUES, FIRESCAPING, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, FOREST MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, AQUATIC RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, WOODY PLANT ID, AND OTHER TOPICS AS IDENTIFIED. THE OUTCOME OF OUR EFFORTS IS TO SHARE QUALITY UP-TO-DATE INFORMATION WITH GEORGIA CITIZENS THAT HELP THEM MAKE INFORMED NATURAL RESOURCE RELATED DECISIONS. PARTNER COLLABORATION: OUR TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO NURTURE EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, EDUCATORS (K- 16), AND INDUSTRY. WE ANTICIPATE THE OUTCOME OF THESE PARTNERSHIPS TO BE SUSTAINED SUPPORT AND COLLABORATION. WEB-BASED PRODUCTS: OUR WEB DEVELOPMENT TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO UPDATE SMARTPHONE APPS AND WEBSITES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF OUR EFFORTS WILL BE TO OFFER WEB-BASED TOOLS THAT INCREASE INFORMATION SHARING AND DATA COLLECTION AND PROVIDE EXPERIENCES THAT BUILD NEW SKILLS AND BENEFIT OUR TARGET AUDIENCES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS, PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, PRIVATE CONSULTANTS, COUNTY EXTENSION ANR AGENTS, CITY/COUNTY GOVERNMENT STAFF, K-12 TEACHERS AND STUDENTS, SPECIAL INTEREST GROUPS, ASSOCIATIONS, NGOS AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, AND ALL CITIZENS OF GEORGIA. THERE ARE NO SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES PLANNED AT THE TIME OF THIS AWARD.

FOREST HEALTH IN THE SOUTHEAST IS THREATENED BY INVASIVE SPECIES, EXACERBATED BY CLIMATE CHANGE. IT'S CRUCIAL TO EMPOWER LANDOWNERS AND RESOURCE MANAGERS TO MITIGATE THESE IMPACTS. OUR MAIN GOAL IS TO RAISE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF INVASIVE SPECIES, MAINTAIN PARTNERSHIPS WITH RELEVANT ORGANIZATIONS, AND IDENTIFY EMERGING INVASIVE INSECT AND ANIMAL PESTS. THE PRIMARY TARGET AUDIENCES ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS (E.G., FORESTERS, LOGGERS, WILDLIFE BIOLOGISTS) AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT STUDENTS. BECAUSE NON-NATIVE PLANTS USED IN LANDSCAPING ARE A MAJOR SOURCE OF THE INVASIVE PLANTS THAT INVADE FORESTS, A SECONDARY AUDIENCE IS HOMEOWNERS, MASTER GARDENERS, THE GENERAL PUBLIC, AND K-12 EDUCATORS. PRIMARY COMMUNICATION PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS ON INVASIVE PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL, SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS, BLOGS, AND ARTICLES FOR THE POPULAR PRESS AND TEAM NEWSLETTER, CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE ACES FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE WEBPAGE, AND HIGH-DEFINITION PHOTOGRAPHS OF INVASIVE PLANTS FOR EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS AND OUTREACH. OUTREACH EVENTS WILL INCLUDE CO-CHAIRING THE STATE-WIDE ANNUAL ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL CONFERENCE; ORGANIZING AND PARTICIPATING IN ACES WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DAYS; PROVIDING SEMINARS AND WEBINARS FOR FOREST INDUSTRY, FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AGENCIES, MASTER GARDENERS, CIVIC GROUPS, AND OTHERS AS REQUESTED (TYPICALLY ABOUT 20 EVENTS A YEAR.) MANY OF THESE EVENTS PROVIDE CECS FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS. EACH YEAR, WE RECEIVE OVER A HUNDRED QUESTIONS ABOUT PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND TREATMENT OPTIONS FOR INVASIVE PLANTS FROM STAKEHOLDERS. THESE ARE ADDRESSED VIA PHONE, EMAIL, TEXT, AND SOCIAL MEDIA. ADDITIONALLY, WE TEACH AUBURN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS ABOUT INVASIVE PLANTS, LEAD EFFORTS TO UPDATE THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL (ALIPC) INVASIVE PLANT LIST, AND PROVIDE EXPERTISE TO LOCAL INVASIVE PLANT CONTROL EFFORTS. BUILDING CAPACITY BY COLLABORATING WITH STATE AND LOCAL AGENCIES, SERVING ON STATEWIDE INVASIVE PLANT TASK FORCES, AND MAINTAINING A LEADERSHIP ROLE WITHIN THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL. WE ENCOURAGE THE USE OF THE NATIONAL EARLY DETECTION AND DISTRIBUTION MAPPING SYSTEM (EDDMAPS) FOR MAPPING AND MONITORING THE SPREAD OF INVASIVE PLANTS. REMAINING ACTIVE IN NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS LIKE THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF INVASIVE PLANT COUNCILS (NAIPC) AND NORTH AMERICAN INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION (NAISMA) HELPS MAINTAIN REGIONAL AND NATIONAL CONNECTIONS AND AWARENESS OF INVASIVE PLANT ISSUES AND POLICIES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMMEDIATE BENEFITS SUCH AS INCREASED ABILITY TO IDENTIFY AND MONITOR INVASIVE SPECIES, MORE EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES, REDUCED USE OF INVASIVE SPECIES IN LANDSCAPING, AND PROVIDING CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDITS FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS. THE ULTIMATE BENEFIT IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH THROUGH REDUCED SPREAD AND IMPACTS OF INVASIVE PLANTS. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH INCREASED KNOWLEDGE AND ACTION AMONG LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS WHO KNOW HOW TO IDENTIFY INVASIVE PLANTS, WHERE TO ACCESS SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION AND RESOURCES, AND INCREASED AWARENESS OF EDDMAPS. A CHANGE IN ACTION WILL BE INCREASED MONITORING AND CONTROL EFFORTS BY LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS, LEADING TO MORE ACRES BEING TREATED AND FEWER BEHAVIORS SPREADING INVASIVE PLANTS. THIS WILL ALSO RESULT IN FEWER HOMEOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS USING RISKY NON-NATIVE PLANTS AND AN INCREASE IN THE USE OF EDDMAPS TO REPORT INVASIVE PLANTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH AND RESILIENCY THROUGH REDUCED USE OF NON-NATIVE PLANTS IN LANDSCAPING AND WILDLIFE PLANTINGS, REDUCED BEHAVIORS THAT SPREAD INVASIVE PLANTS, AND EARLIER AND MORE EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OF INVASIVE PLANTS. IMPROVING INVASIVE PLANT LISTING AND MAPPING WILL PROVIDE MORE ACCURATE DISTRIBUTION MAPS AND BETTER INFORM MANAGEMENT DECISIONS.

THROUGH INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, NC STATE IS SOLVING CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF BOTH LARGE- AND SMALL-SCALE FARMS. RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE LANDSCAPING AND GARDENING. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND METHODS FOR ANIMAL BREEDING, REPRODUCTION, NUTRITION, GENETICS AND GENOMICS, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. THESE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS ALSO AIM TO TACKLE THE CRITICAL ISSUES IMPACTING THE QUALITY OF OUR SOIL, WATER AND AIR BY PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC SOLUTIONS FOR ANIMAL WASTE MANAGEMENT, WASTEWATER TREATMENT, NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, SOIL PROPERTIES, AND FISHERY AND POND MANAGEMENT. NC STATE'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH AND TO KEEP AMERICAN'S HEALTHY AND FREE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESS NECESSITATE A FOCUS ON PREVENTING FOOD SAFETY PROBLEMS RATHER THAN TAKING A REACTIONARY APPROACH. NC STATE'S INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS FOCUS ON PROTECTING THE SAFETY OF FOODS ALONG THE ENTIRE SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM PRODUCTION TO CONSUMPTION. TO MEET THE GROWING  NEED FOR HEALTHY FOOD, RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS THAT PROMOTE HEALTH AND PREVENT DISEASE. AT THE SAME TIME, EXTENSION PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO ENSURE THAT INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE THEY NEED TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES ABOUT FOOD AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSS-CUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGRO ECONOMICS. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITS WORK WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, PLACING SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON LIMITED RESOURCES, SMALL- SCALE MINORITY FARMERS. THE FARM PAVILION WILL FOCUS ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND LOCAL AND COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, HOUSING ITS APPLIED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROGRAMS' STAFF AND PROVIDING SPACE FOR MEETINGS, FORUMS AND CONFERENCES.

MUCH OF OREGON IS FORESTLAND AND RANGELAND, AND MUCH OF THIS ACREAGE IS MANAGED BY PRIVATE LANDOWNERS WITH NONINDUSTRIAL OPERATIONS. RREA FUNDS PROVIDED TO OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY (OSU) ARE USED TO SUPPORT EFFORTS OF EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF TO PROVIDE GUIDANCE TO THESE LANDOWNERS SO THEY CAN MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT THE MANAGEMENT OF THEIR NATURAL RESOURCES, AND TO PROMOTE UNDERSTANDING AMONG OTHERS ON HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE ECONOMIC AND ECOLOGICAL SERVICES THESE LANDS PROVIDE. THE PRIMARY AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION TO THE PEOPLE OF OREGON THAT ASSISTS THEM IN UNDERSTANDING HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE HEALTH, PRODUCTIVITY, AND RESILIENCY OF THESE LANDS. OUR GOAL IS TO ENSURE HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS, INCREASE ECONOMIC BENEFITS, BUILD CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS, AND IN THE LONG TERM ENSURE SUSTAINABLE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THIS PROJECT HAS SEVERAL OBJECTIVES. OBJECTIVE ONE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF OWNERS AND MANAGERS OF PRIVATE NON-INDUSTRIAL FOREST AND RANGELAND OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES SO AS TO ENABLE THEM TO MEET THEIR MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES WHILE ENSURING HEALTHY FOREST AND RANGELANDS. OBJECTIVE TWO IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW LAND USE AND LAND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS INFLUENCE HABITAT FOR A VARIETY OF FISH AND WILDLIFE SPECIES TO ENSURE PRODUCTIVE POPULATIONS AND HIGH LEVELS OF BIODIVERSITY ACROSS ECOSYSTEMS. OBJECTIVE THREE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW CHANGING CLIMATIC CONDITIONS ARE LIKELY TO INFLUENCE FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES (E.G., INCREASED SUMMER TEMPERATURES, PROLONGED DROUGHT, WIDESPREAD INSECT AND DISEASE OUTBREAKS, LARGER WILDFIRES OF HIGH INTENSITY), TO FOSTER EFFORTS THAT REDUCE THE THREATS IMPOSED BY THESE CHANGES. EDUCATION EFFORTS ENCOMPASS A WIDE VARIETY OF MODALITIES. WRITTEN MATERIALS INCLUDE PUBLICATIONS AND NEWSLETTERS. ONLINE MATERIALS INCLUDE WEBSITES, BLOGS, WEBINARS, VIDEOS, AND PRE-RECORDED LEARNING MODULES. IN-PERSON EVENTS INCLUDE SITE VISITS, FIELD DAYS, TOURS, SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND SHORT-COURSES. OTHER DELIVERY METHODS INCLUDE HYBRID (PARTIALLY ONLINE AND PARTIALLY IN-PERSON) AND PODCASTS. EXTENSION PERSONNEL FROM FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES, RANGELAND RES OURCES ECOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT, AND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES RECEIVE BASE PROGRAM SUPPORT THROUGH RREA FUNDING. IN ADDITION, ALLOCATIONS ARE PROVIDED TO SUB-PROJECTS THAT ADDRESS A VARIETY OF STAKEHOLDER NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELANDS ACROSS THE STATE. RREA FUNDS ARE LEVERAGED WITH BOTH EXTERNAL GRANT FUNDS AND UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SUPPORT. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A WIDE VARIETY OF EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS AND TRAININGS THAT RESULT IN GAINS IN AWARENESS AND IN KNOWLEDGE, INCREASES IN ACREAGE OVER WHICH RECOMMENDED PRACTICES ARE IMPLEMENTED, AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. ALL EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF REPORT ON THE ACTIVITIES PERFORMED AND OUTCOMES ACHIEVED ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

MISSISSIPPI CONTAINS OVER 19.5 MILLION ACRES OF FOREST LAND, WHICH ACCOUNTS FOR 65% OF THE STATE'S TOTAL LAND AREA, AND 81% OF MISSI SSIPPI'S FOREST LAND IS PRIVATELY OWNED BY NONINDUSTRIAL LANDOWNERS. OVER 80% OF PRIVATE FOREST OWNERSHIP IS IN PARCELS OF 100 ACRES OR LESS. EDUCATING PRIVATE FAMILY FOREST OWNERS ABOUT FOREST MANAGEMENT, HARVESTING, AND MARKETING PRACTICES AND TECHNIQUES IS ESSE NTIAL TO THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE FOREST RESOURCE. THESE FAMILY FOREST LANDS ARE NOT ALWAYS MANAGED IN A WAY THAT MAXIMIZES PRIVATE AND ASSOCIATED PUBLIC BENEFITS THAT CAN INCLUDE TIMBER PRODUCTS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES, RECREATION AND WATER QUALITY BENEFITS. MANY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS DO NOT HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE OR SKILLS TO MANAGE FORESTS TO MEET THEIR OWN OBJECTIVES. THE RREA PROGRAM ALLOWS MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SERVICE TO GIVE SPECIAL ATTENTION TO HELPING FAMILY FOREST OWNERS MANAGE THEIR FORESTLANDS FOR MAXIMUM BENEFIT. THUS, THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INCREASE AND IMPROVE THE LEVELS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES BEING CONDUCTED ON MISSISSIPPI FORESTLAND SO AS TO ENHANCE ALL THE BENEFITS SOCIETY RECEIVES FROM WELL MANAGED FORESTS. THE CORE GOALS OF THE FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAM AS SUPPORTED BY RREA ARE TO INCREASE THE PRODUCTIVITY, EFFECTIVENESS, EFFICIENCY, AND PROFITABILITY OF OUR CLIENTELE, AS WELL AS AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE MANY VALUES OF THEIR FORESTS. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, NEW RESEARCH AND TECHNOLOGIES  WILL BE DISSEMINATED TO CLIENTELE STATEWIDE THROUGH FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAMS AND MATERIALS. THESE PROGRAMS WILL INCLUDE THEMATIC WORKSHOPS, SHORT COURSES, AND STAND-ALONE PRESENTATIONS TARGETING CLIENTELE NEEDS. IN ADDITION, NEW EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS WILL BE PRODUCED AND DISSEMINATED VIA TRADITIONAL AND ELECTRONIC MEDIUMS.

RREA FY2025 ABSTRACT - SUSTAINING THE PRODUCTIVITY OF NY'S PRIVATE WOODLANDS RREA AT CORNELL HAS SUFFICIENT STAFF AND RESOURCES TO FOCUS ON THREE PRIMARY ISSUES: FOREST MANAGEMENT FOR DIVERSE OUTPUTS, WILDLIFE RESOURCES, AND FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY PARTICULARLY AS RELATES TO AGROFORESTRY ENTERPRISES OF FOREST FARMING AND SILVOPASTURE. THE DECISIONS ARE MADE ON SMALL PARCELS BUT AGGREGATE FOR AN ACCUMULATED IMPACT. PRIVATE OWNERS LACK AWARENESS AND KNOWLEDGE TO INTEGRATE BEST PRACTICES. SPECIALISTS AND PRACTITIONERS IDENTIFY KNOWLEDGE GAPS OR SEEK TECHNICAL SUPPORT. EXTENSION EDUCATORS SEEK SUPPORT WITH COMPLEX PROBLEMS AT COUNTY AND MULTI-COUNTY SCALES. THE GOAL FOR THE FOREST ISSUE IS TO ENSURE THAT FORESTS ARE SUSTAINABLY MANAGED FOR OPTIMAL OUTPUTS OF DESIRED GOODS AND SERVICES. THE GOAL FOR WILDLIFE RESOURCES IS TO SUSTAIN AND ENHANCE THE BIODIVERSITY AND HEALTH OF NATIVE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS IN BALANCE WITH THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE IN THEIR ECOSYSTEMS. THE GOAL FOR FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY IS TO EXPAND THE AVAILABILITY OF LOCALLY PRODUCED FOREST-BASED FOODS, AND TO ENSURE THAT THE PRODUCERS ARE FINANCIALLY AND ECOLOGICALLY SUSTAINABLE. THE ACTIVITIES DESCRIBED IN THE METHODS SECTION REFLECT A STRATEGY THAT RECOGNIZES STAKEHOLDERS ARRIVE AT DIFFERENT LEVELS OF AWARENESS, HAVE PREFERRED AND SOMETIMES ESSENTIAL MODES OF LEARNING, AND BENEFIT FROM MULTIPLE EXPOSURES TO SIMILAR INFORMATION, OPTIMALLY DEMONSTRATED TO ALLOW THEM TO VISUALIZE THE OUTCOME. IN RESPONSE TO DIFFERENT LEVELS OF AWARENESS, OUR PROGRAM MATERIALS RANGE FROM INTRODUCTORY TO MODERATELY COMPLEX. HIGHLY COMPLEX MATERIAL IS PROVIDED AS PEER REVIEWED SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS OR TECHNICAL REPORTS AND LARGELY OUTSIDE THE SCOPE OF RREA. WE ADDRESS PREFERRED LEARNING MODES BY CREATING MULTIPLE OUTLETS AND FORMATS THAT RANGE FROM SOCIAL MEDIA TO FACT SHEETS TO YOUTUBE TO FIELD TOURS AND DEMONSTRATION SITES. THE POWER OF VISUALIZATION IS REMARKABLE IN ITS CAPACITY TO CONVEY THE OPPORTUNITIES OF A PARTICULAR ACTION. THAT POWER, HOWEVER, CARRIES THE OBLIGATION TO ENSURE THAT THE ASSUMPTIONS OF WHAT'S DEMONSTRATED ARE CLEARLY DEFINED RELATIVE TO FACTORS THAT MIGHT BE DIFFERENT ELSEWHERE AND RESULT IN A DIFFERENT OUTCOME. DEMONSTRATIONS ARE CREATED TO ALLOW FOR DIRECT ENGAGEMENT, BUT ALSO THROUGH VIDEO, PICTURES, AND ILLUSTRATIONS. SPECIFIC METHODS INCLUDE: ONLINE RESOURCES,  PEER-VOLUNTEERS, DEMONSTRATION SITES, APPLIED RESEARCH, WORKSHOPS AND FIELD TOURS, CONFERENCES AND SEMINARS, MASS MEDIA, EDUCATOR IN-SERVICE TRAININGS, WRITTEN MATERIALS, ORGANIZATIONAL SUPPORT, AND PROGRAM EVALUATION

OVERVIEW  VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (VCE), A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN VIRGINIA POLYTECHNIC  INSTITUTE AND STATE UNIVERSITY (VT) AND VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY (VSU), THE VIRGINIA  AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (VAES) AND THE VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL  RESEARCH STATION (VSUARS), ENABLES PEOPLE TO IMPROVE THEIR LIVES THROUGH RESEARCH AND  EDUCATION USING SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE FOCUSED ON THE ISSUES AND NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF  VIRGINIA. AUDIENCES ARE INVOLVED IN DESIGNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING NEEDS-DRIVEN  PROGRAMS. VCE, VAES AND VSUARS ARE DYNAMIC ORGANIZATIONS WHICH STIMULATE  POSITIVE PERSONAL AND SOCIETAL CHANGE LEADING TO MORE PRODUCTIVE LIVES, FAMILIES, FARMS,  AND FORESTS, AS WELL AS A BETTER ENVIRONMENT IN URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES. VCE'S  GOALS ARE TO: 1) DEVELOP AND TRANSFER NEW KNOWLEDGE IN APPLIED AND BASIC LIFE SCIENCES,  2) PERFORM RELEVANT, OBJECTIVE, AND TIMELY RESEARCH 3) IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR  COMMUNITIES AND CITIZENS IN THE COMMONWEALTH, 4) USE A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO  PROGRAMMING, WITH TASK -ORIENTED WORK TEAMS THAT RESPOND TO THE NEEDS OF INDIVIDUALS,  GROUPS, AND ORGANIZATIONS, 5) WORK WITH AT-RISK, UNDERSERVED, AND UNDERREPRESENTED  AUDIENCES WHO NEED FOCUSED AND SPECIALIZED ATTENTION, 6) FULLY INTEGRATE A CULTURALLY  DIVERSE PAID AND VOLUNTEER STAFF IN PLANNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING PROGRAMS, AND  7) RECRUIT AND COLLABORATE WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE PARTNERS TO BETTER UTILIZE RESOURCES,  HEIGHTEN IMPACT, AND REACH A MORE DIVERSE AUDIENCE. WE WILL USE SCIENCE-BASED RESEARCH  AND EDUCATIONAL STRATEGIES TO ADDRESS 1) CRITICAL AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY AND  SUSTAINABILITY 2)OUR BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY PROGRAMS FOCUS ON  ESTABLISHING REGIONAL COMMUNITY AND INDUSTRY NETWORKS TO IDENTIFY, RESEARCH AND EDUCATE  ON UTILIZATION OF BACTERIA, WATER, PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND FORESTS PRODUCTS TO PRODUCE GOODS FOR  HUMAN, INDUSTRIAL, AND AGRICULTURAL NEEDS FOR ALL VIRGINIANS 3) COMMUNITY VIABILITY  PROGRAMMING WILL PROMOTE CONTINUING PROSPERITY AND FINANCIAL SECURITY FOR ALL VIRGINIANS  4) WE WILL ADDRESS FOOD SECURITY AND SAFETY, NUTRITION CHALLENGES AND HEALTH ISSUES FOR ALL  VIRGINIANS; 5) WE WILL ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES OF NATURAL RESOURCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL  ENHANCEMENT, PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION; 6) WE WILL SUPPORT STRONG, HEALTHY FAMILY  DEVELOPMENT AND WELL-BEING LEADING TO STRONGER VIRGINIA COMMUNITIES; 7) 4-H PROGRAMS  FOCUS ON DEVELOPING POSITIVE, HEALTHY, SKILLED, PRODUCTIVE YOUTH TO BE TOMORROW'S LEADERS.

UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA LEVERAGES RREA FUNDS WITH OTHER SOURCES OF FUNDING, PRIMARILY SALARY AND PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (UF/IFAS), TO PROVIDE EXTENSION SUPPORT TO TWELVE EXTENSION FACULTY AND THREE TECHNICAL STAFF IN THE SCHOOL OF FOREST, FISHERIES AND GEOMATICS SCIENCES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF WILDLIFE ECOLOGY AND CONSERVATION. THE PURPOSE OF THESE EXTENSION PROGRAMS IS TO ADDRESS MULTIPLE STAKEHOLDERS NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES IN FLORIDA; PROMOTE INFORMATION TRANSFER REGARDING THE ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES; AND PROVIDE INFORMATION ON LAND USE OPTIONS AND STRATEGIES FOR WORKING LANDSCAPES AND URBAN FORESTS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE FORMAL EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS SUCH AS COURSES, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS; INFORMAL INTERACTIONS TOA ADDRESS INDIVIDUAL PROBLEMS THROUGH PHONE CALLS, EMAIL CORRESPONDENCE, AND SITE VISITS; AND PASSIVE EDUCATION SUCH AS ONLINE WEBSITES AND EXTENSION FACT SHEETS THROUGH THE UF/IFD EDIS (ELECTRONIC DATA INFORMATION SOURCE) SYSTEM. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL DELIVER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS BOTH IN-PERSON VIA WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING PROGRAMS THAT INCLUDE CLASSROOM, LAB, AND/OR FIELD EXPERIENCES; ONLINE TOOLS INCLUDING WEBINARS, WEBSITES, AND VIDEOS; AND SOCIAL MEDIA SUCH AS TWITTER, BLOGS, AND APPS. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE EVENTS AND PRODUCTS. EVENTS WILL INCLUDE FACILITATION AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL RESOURCES LEADERSHIP INSTITUTE (NRLI), EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS ADDRESSING FOREST AND RANGELAND MANAGEMENT, NATURAL HISTORY, AND CONSERVATION THROUGH FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS SUCH AS THE FLORIDA FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND THE MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAMS; FOREST AND RANGE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL AREAS TRAINING ACADEMY (NATA); WORKSHOPS ON THE MANAGEMENT OF INVASIVE PLANTS AND ANIMALS, FOREST INSECT PESTS, AND RANGELAND WEEDS VIA WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DAYS THROUGH REGIONAL WORKSHOPS AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS INCLUDING THE FOREST STEWARDSHIP PROGRAM, BARK BEETLE ACADEMY, AND THE INVASIVE SPECIES COUNCIL AND THE COOPERATIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AREAS TEAMS. PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION FACT SHEETS, PUBLISHED ONLINE IN THE UF/IFAS EDIS SYSTEM ON MULTIPLE TOPICS INCLUDING FOREST AND RANGELAND WILDLIFE, FOREST AND RANGELAND HEALTH AND MANAGEMENT, INVASIVE SPECIES AND THEIR CONTROL, AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL MAINTAIN, UPDATE, AND EXPAND (E.G., INVASIVE SPECIES WEBSITE PORTAL) WEBSITES IN FORESTRY, WILDLIFE, INVASIVE SPECIES, AND RELATED EXTENSION PROGRAMS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE CHANGE IN KNOWLEDGE, CHANGE IN ACTION, AND CHANGE IN CONDITION. WE EXPECT OUR TRAINING PROGRAMS, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS TO INCREASE PARTICIPANT KNOWLEDGE. WE EXPECT THAT PARTICIPANTS IN TRAINING PROGRAMS AND WORKSHOPS/FIELD DAYS WILL INDICATE THE INTENTION OF IMPLEMENTING AT LEAST ONE MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATION OR OTHER ACTION. WE ALSO EXPECT THAT PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT OR OTHER ACTIONS THAT WILL AFFECT 25% OF THE FLORIDA ACREAGE MANAGEMENT BY PARTICIPANTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF OUR ACTIVITIES AND DELIVERABLES INCLUDE FLORIDA PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, FOREST, AND RANGELAND MANAGERS; PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, BIOLOGISTS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTANTS; EDUCATORS; ELECTED OFFICIALS AND STAFF, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND INTERESTED CITIZENS; AND ECO/AGRITOURISM AND OTHER SMALL BUSINESS/RECREATIONAL OPERATIONS ON PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LANDS.

FEDERAL PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF OUR RREA PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE EXTENSION PROGRAMMING DESIGNED TO ASSIST FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS AND MANAGERS MAKE SCIENCE-BASED MANAGEMENT DECISIONS TO MEET HEALTH, SAFETY, PRODUCTION, PROTECTION, AND SUSTAINABILITY NEEDS OF THE OWNER AND SOCIETY. TOPICAL ISSUES INCLUDE: LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT; PUBLIC AWARENESS; RESOURCE MANAGEMENT; WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND PROTECTION; SUCCESSION AND ESTATE PLANNING; FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT; AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. WSUS RREA PROGRAM ALIGNS USDA STRATEGIC GOAL #1, TO 'COMBAT CLIMATE CHANGE TO SUPPORT AMERICA'S WORKING LANDS, NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMUNITIES.' WE FOCUS ON RREA GOAL 'ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS.' OUR ISSUES AREAS ARE 1) FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH, AND 2) RANGELAND STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH. OUR FOCUS IS WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF FOREST AND RANGE FIRES, AND THE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOREST AND RANGE RESOURCES. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THE WSU EXTENSION FORESTRY <(>&<)> RANGE TEAM WILL PROVIDE UNBIASED, RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES TO MEET LANDOWNER AND MANAGER NEEDS. THROUGH FACE-TO-FACE AND DISTANCE DELIVERIES OF CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, SEMINARS, CONFERENCES, PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, SHORTCOURSES, CONSULTATIONS, MEDIA WORK, PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPROVE LEARNING AND APPLICATION OF NEW IDEAS LEADING TO DESIRABLE FUTURE CONDITIONS. PROGRAMS WILL BE LIVE AND PRE-RECORDED TO SUIT USE PREFERENCE FOR ACCESSING INFORMATION. AS APPROPRIATE, INFORMATION WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN SPANISH FOR THOSE WITH ENGLISH AS A SECOND LANGUAGE.PHYSICAL ACCESS AND DISABILITIES WILL BE ACCOMMODATED FOLLOWING ADA ACCESSIBILITY STANDARDS, INCLUDING WEB DESIGN. DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES: WSU EXPECTS TO DELIVER 100 ACTIVITIES REACHING 10,000 OWNERS AND MANAGERS AND POSITIVELY IMPACTING 0.5-MILLION ACRES. COMPREHENSIVE ACHIEVEMENTS WILL 1) ENHANCE FOREST AND RANGE SUSTAINABILITY BY DEVELOPING OWNER/ MANAGER CAPACITY FOR IMPROVING HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY; 2) PROMOTE LAND RESILIENCE BY PREPARING OWNER/ MANAGER CAPACITY FOR RESPONDING TO HARMFUL IMPACTS CAUSED BY WILDFIRE, DROUGHT, WILDLIFE DAMAGE, INVASIVE SPECIES, INSECTS PESTS AND DISEASE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS PERPETUATED BY CLIMATE CHANGE; AND 3) DIVERSIFY STEWARDSHIP OPPORTUNITIES THAT LEAD TO MULTIPLE-USE BENEFITS. WE BASE THESE EXPECTATIONS ON ACCOMPLISHMENTS DERIVED BY THE PAST 17 YEARS OF PROGRAM EVALUATION DATA. NOTEWORTHY IMPACTS EXPECTED: 1) IMPROVED FOREST <(>&<)> RANGELAND HEALTH; 2) DECREASED RISK OF WILDFIRE; 3) IMPROVE HABITAT; 4) DECREASED INSECT, DISEASE, AND INVASIVE SPECIES RISK; 5) IMPROVED PRODUCTIVITY OF TREES AND FORAGE; 6) DECREASED EROSION; 7) IMPROVED WOOD QUALITY AND PRODUCTS; 8) IMPROVED INCOME OPPORTUNITY; 9) IMPROVED PROTECTION OF CULTURAL RESOURCES AND SPECIAL SITES; AND 10) IMPROVED RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES. LIMITED LEARNING CHANGES WILL BE SOUGHT, AND WE WILL FOCUS EVALUATION ON MEASURING CHANGES IN BEHAVIORS, PRACTICES, AND WHEN APPROPRIATE, DECISIONS (FOR EXAMPLE, ASKING FOR A FORESTER VISIT). WE WILL COLLABORATE AND LEVERAGE OUR OUTREACH BY UTILIZING PARTNERSHIPS SUCH AS THE US FOREST SERVICE, WA DEPT. NATURAL RESOURCES, WA ASSOC. OF CONSERVATION DISTRICTS, WA FARM FORESTRY ASSOC., SOC. OF AMERICAN FORESTERS, ASSOC. OF CONSULTING FORESTERS, FORESTRY COLLABORATIVES, AND COUNTY PARTNERSHIPS. WE WILL CONTRIBUTE TO NGO PURPOSES THAT HOLD COMMON CONSERVATION GOALS FOR INFORMING THEIR MEMBERSHIP AND THE PUBLIC, SUCH AS THE NATURE CONSERVANCY, AMERICAN TREE FARM SYSTEM, AMERICAN FOREST FOUNDATIONS, ROCKY MOUNTAIN ELK FOUNDATION, AND VARIOUS LAND TRUSTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: NON-INDUSTRIAL PRIVATE FOREST (NIPF) AND RANGELAND OWNERS, AND MANAGERS (PRACTICING FORESTERS, LOGGERS, RANCHERS, SILVICULTURAL CONTRACTORS, AND TRIBAL NATURAL RESOURCE EMPLOYEES). INVITED PRESENTATIONS FOR YOUTH OR SERVICE ORGANIZATIONS ARE POSSIBLE BUT NOT TARGET BENEFICIARIES.

ARKANSAS FOREST AND NATURAL RESOURCES ARE CRITICAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY AND TO THE WELL-BEING OF ITS CITIZENS: WE ARE KNOWN AS 'THE NATURAL STATE'. MORE THAN HALF OF THE STATE (55%) IS FORESTED, WITH ALMOST HALF OF THE FOREST COMPRISED OF OAK AND HICKORY FOREST TYPES AND NEARLY A THIRD COMPRISED OF LOBLOLLY AND SHORTLEAF PINE. THESE DIVERSE FORESTS PROVIDE HABITAT TO A HOST OF WILDLIFE SPECIES. THESE RANGE FROM GAME SPECIES, SUCH AS DEER, TURKEY, AND DUCKS, TO SONGBIRDS FOR WILDLIFE VIEWING, AND MANY REPTILES AND AMPHIBIANS. ARKANSAS FORESTS ALSO PROVIDE CLEAN DRINKING WATER TO METROPOLITAN AREAS AND PROTECT OTHER IMPORTANT WATERSHEDS. RAW MATERIALS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS SUPPORT A VIBRANT FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. FOREST RESOURCE COMPANIES OWN OR LEASE 23% OF THE STATE'S TIMBERLAND AND PROVIDED JOBS DIRECTLY TO 28,057 EMPLOYEES, REPRESENTING A LABOR INCOME OF $1.6 BILLION, IN 2014. MORE THAN HALF OF THE STATE'S 18.5 MILLION ACRES OF FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY PRIVATE NON-INDUSTRIAL FOREST LANDOWNERS. THIS IMPORTANT LANDOWNER GROUP IS EXTR EMELY DIVERSE AND INCLUDES FARMERS, RANCHERS, HOMEOWNERS, TEACHERS, FACTORY WORKERS, PROFESSIONALS, AND RETIREES. THE DEMAND FOR BENEFITS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS, INCLUDING WILDLIFE HABITAT AND FOREST PRODUCTS, MUST INCREASINGLY BE MET BY THESE PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS. HOWEVER, MANY OF THESE LANDOWNERS ARE UNFAMILIAR WITH SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, TIMBER MARKETING, HABITAT RESTORATION, REFORESTATION INCENTIVES, AND OTHER VITAL INFORMATION CRITICAL TO SUSTAINING FOREST LANDS. MOST OF THEM ALSO HOLD THEIR FOREST LANDS FOR REASONS OTHER THAN TIMBER MANAGEMENT. THE FUTURE SUPPLY OF TIMBER, THEREFORE, MIGHT NOT BE SECURE UNLESS HARVESTING FOREST PRODUCTS FULFILLS THE LANDOWNER'S OBJECTIVES AND NEEDS. SEVERAL ISSUES ARE THREATENING ARKANSAS FORESTS, HOWEVER. INVASIVE PESTS INCLUDING FERAL HOGS, EMERALD ASH BORER, AND THE RECENTLY DISCOVERED LAUREL WILT DISEASE ARE BUT A FEW OF THE DIRECT FACTORS AFFECTING FOREST HEALTH IN RURAL AND URBAN FORESTS. FORESTERS ARE ALSO CONCERNED ABOUT A POTENTIAL INCREASE IN PINE BARK BEETLES INCLUDING SOUTHERN PINE BEETLE RESULTING FROM STRESS FROM OVER-CROWDING AND DROUGHT. OTHER LESS DIRECT FACTORS ARE FOREST FRAGMENTATION, FOREST DENSIFICATION, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND A WEAK FOREST PRODUCTS MARKET. THE WEAK MARKET CREATES CONSTRAINTS TO SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. NEW FOREST-BASED PRODUCTS, INCLUDING BIOENERGY, WOOD PELLETS, ARE STILL IN THE DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE BUT WILL HOPEFULLY AUGMENT AND INCREASE DEMAND FOR WOOD PRODUCTS. OUR GOAL THEN, IS TO INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO MANAGE AND TO SUSTAIN HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS THAT MEET BOTH HUMAN AND ECOLOGICAL NEEDS. ASSOCIATED WITH T HIS GOAL, OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO IMPROVE FORESTRY STAKEHOLDER AWARENESS OF FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES BY: (1) HOSTING IN-PERSON EVENTS (WORKSHOPS, FIELD TOURS), (2) HOSTING VIRTUAL EVENTS (WEBINARS), (3) CONDUCTING DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS, (4) DEVELOPING WEB-BASED MANAGEMENT TOOLS AND (5) PUBLISHING RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION THROUGH DIVERSE MEDIA (BULLETINS, POPULAR PRESS, MEDIA RELEASES, INTERNET ARTICLES).

positiveFlows.title: PROJECT ABSTRACT - MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY: RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM: MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION HELPS IMPROVE PEOPLE'S LIVES THROUGH AN EDUCATIONAL PROCESS THAT APPLIES KNOWLEDGE TO CRITICAL ISSUES, NEEDS, AND OPPORTUNITIES. FOR MORE THAN 100 YEARS, MSU EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF MEMBERS HAVE BEEN ACTIVELY REACHING PEOPLE WHERE THEY ARE - IN THEIR HOMES, FARMS, BUSINESSES, AND COMMUNITIES - WITH RESEARCH DRIVEN EDUCATION. WE HELP PEOPLE PERFORM THEIR JOBS BETTER, RAISE HEALTHY AND SAFE FAMILIES, BUILD STRONGER COMMUNITIES, AND EMPOWER CHILDREN TO DREAM OF BRIGHTER FUTURES. WITH RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM (RREA) FUNDING, MSU EXTENSION FOSTERS ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE, A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, AND A PLENTIFUL AND SECURE FOOD SUPPLY FOR MICHIGAN RESIDENTS. MICHIGAN'S NATURAL RESOURCES ARE A FUNDAMENTAL ASSET FOR THE STATE'S FUTURE ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES. CHALLENGES CONCERN HOW RESIDENTS OF THE STATE CAN BEST BENEFIT FROM ITS RICH NATURAL HERITAGE WITHOUT OVERBURDENING THE CARRYING CAPACITY OF ITS NATURAL SYSTEMS AND REDUCING OPPORTUNITIES FOR RESIDENTS AND VISITORS ALIKE. OUR NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS IMPROVE PUBLIC UNDERSTANDING, HELP LANDOWNERS AND COMMUNITIES USE THOSE ASSETS FOR SUSTAINABLE LONG-TERM SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. WE WILL DEVELOP TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY TO HELP MICHIGAN'S NATURAL RESOURCE-BASED TOURISM INDUSTRY GROW BY MEETING CONSUMER DEMANDS AND DETERMINE HOW WILDLIFE, FISHERIES, FOREST AND NATURAL RESOURCES AREAS RESPOND TO HABITAT MANAGEMENT TO ENCOURAGE MANAGEMENT FOR SUSTAINABLE BENEFITS.

PURPOSE: THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AT PENN STATE WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT TO PENNSYLVANIA RESIDENTS THROUGH THE PENNSYLVANIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND PENN STATE EXTENSION (PSE) ACTIVITIES. WE WILL BE RESPONSIVE TO STAKEHOLDER NEEDS THROUGH TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH AND DELIVERY OF SCIENCE-BASED PROGRAMS TO CLIENTELE. WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT INTERNATIONALLY RELEVANT FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH THAT GENERATES BASELINE DATA TO SOLVE FUTURE PROBLEMS AND ACTIVELY SEEK NEW AND BETTER WAYS TO COMMUNICATE OUR PROGRAMS TO NEW AUDIENCES. OUR FACULTY AND STAFF, SUPPORTED BY FEDERAL BASE FUNDING, WILL EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE THIS INVESTMENT AGAINST MANY OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO CONDUCT PROGRAMS OF THE HIGHEST CALIBER. WE ARE COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE IN RESEARCH, EDUCATING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS AND CITIZENS, AND PROMOTING LIFE-LONG LEARNING AMONG THE CITIZENS OF PENNSYLVANIA. OUR COLLEGE'S MISSION IS CLEAR: 'THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES IS TO DISCOVER, INTEGRATE, TRANSLATE, AND DISSEMINATE KNOWLEDGE TO ENHANCE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM, NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP, AND ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL WELLBEING, THEREBY IMPROVING THE LIVES OF PEOPLE IN PENNSYLVANIA, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD.' AGRICULTURE FACES CHALLENGES OF RISING ENERGY COSTS, WEATHER EXTREMES, AN EXPANDING HUMAN POPULATION, ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, AND LABOR SHORTAGES. THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ADDED TO THE CHALLENGES: DISRUPTIONS TO FOOD CHAINS, WORKFORCE CHALLENGES, IMPACTS ON YOUTH EDUCATION, AND BUSINESS INTERRUPTIONS. WE MUST ADDRESS THESE ISSUES TO MITIGATE FUTURE WIDESPREAD DISRUPTIONS THAT IMPACT ALL OF SOCIETY. ACTIVITIES: TO HELP MEET THESE CHALLENGES, WE ARE DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK BASED ON THE SCIENCE OF AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY--DEFINED AS THE INTEGRATION OF NATURAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO INFORM PRACTICE AND POLICY FOR PRODUCTIVE, WORKING LANDSCAPES, HEALTHY WATERSHEDS, AND RESILIENT ECONOMIES. THIS INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH, ENGAGEMENT, AND EDUCATION CENTERS ON THE IMPACTS AND SYNERGIES OF CONTIGUOUS RURAL AND URBAN LANDSCAPES. PENN STATE EXTENSION PROVIDES ACCESS TO FACE-TO-FACE AND ONLINE SCIENCE-BASED EDUCATION TO OUR CUSTOMERS TO HELP THEM ADDRESS PROBLEMS AND TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVEMENT AND INNOVATION. WE MAKE A DIFFERENCE LOCALLY THROUGH FOCUSED ENGAGEMENT AND, MORE WIDELY, TO CUSTOMERS CONNECTING IN THE DIGITAL LANDSCAPE. INITIATIVES ENSURE THE STABILITY OF THE FOOD SYSTEM IN THE COMMONWEALTH AND OUR EFFORTS TO PROVIDE A BROAD-BASED ONLINE LEARNING PLATFORM FOR NONCREDIT PROGRAMMING AND DIGITAL EDUCATION. THE WORK OF AES AND PSE IN OUR COLLEGE IS BUILT ON THE THREE INTEGRATED PILLARS OF INTENSIFICATION, RESILIENCE, AND REGENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AS SOLUTIONS TO SOME OF THE MOST VEXING PROBLEMS CONFRONTING PENNSYLVANIA AND SIMILAR MOSAIC LANDSCAPES WORLDWIDE. OUR CRITICAL ISSUES CAPTURE THE SYSTEMS APPROACH WE IDENTIFIED AS ESSENTIAL FOR GENERATING IMPACT. THEY CUT ACROSS DISCIPLINES, UNITING OUR RESEARCH EFFORTS WITH OUR EXTENSION EDUCATION CAPACITY. THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY PHILOSOPHY HAS REINFORCED THE NATURAL TENDENCY OF OUR FACULTY AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS TO WORK COOPERATIVELY TO SOLVE PROBLEMS. COUPLED WITH THE JOINT RESEARCH-EXTENSION APPOINTMENTS OF MANY OF OUR COLLEGE FACULTY, OUR WORK, AS REPRESENTED IN OUR PLAN OF WORK, WILL EFFECTIVELY UNITE FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE WITH PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS DELIVERED TO STAKEHOLDERS, EMPOWERING THEM TO ADDRESS IMPORTANT AND EMERGING ISSUES USING RELEVANT SCIENCE-BASED RESOURCES. THE NET RESULT WILL BE A TANGIBLE BENEFIT IN ECONOMIC PROSPERITY AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR PENNSYLVANIA CITIZENS.

WISCONSIN IS A LARGELY FORESTED LANDSCAPE COVERING 16 MILLION ACRES, ABOUT 46% OF THE STATE'S LAND AREA. OVERALL, 57% OF THE FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES, TOTALING 360,000 OWNERS. FOREST INDUSTRY IS VITAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY; THE STATE CONTINUES TO BE THE NUMBER ONE PAPER PRODUCING STATE IN THE COUNTRY, AND FOREST PRODUCT INDUSTRIES ARE SCATTERED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. THIS INDUSTRY RELIES HEAVILY ON FAMILY-OWNED FORESTLAND. THE WDNR ESTIMATES THAT 10% OF THE 9.1 MILLION FORESTED ACRES, HELD BY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS, WILL BE SOLD, SUBDIVIDED OR CONVERTED TO NON-FOREST USE IN THE NEXT 5 YEARS. IN A SIMILAR STUDY, THE SUSTAINING FAMILY FORESTS INITIATIVE (SFFI) FOUND THE HIGHEST CONCERN REPORTED BY 56% OF ALL LANDOWNERS WAS 'KEEPING LAND INTACT FOR CHILDREN/HEIRS'. INCIDENTALLY, THE SECOND HIGHEST CONCERN WAS 'HIGH PROPERTY TAXES'. A THIRD STUDY, BY GOBSTER AND RICKENBACH (2004) LOOKED AT PERCEPTIONS OF PARCELIZATION. THE PRIMARY DRIVERS INCLUDED ECONOMIC, DEMOGRAPHIC, VALUES <(>&<)> MOTIVATIONS, GLOBALIZATION <(>&<)> TECHNOLOGY, NATURAL CAPITAL, AND POLICIES. THUS, OUR EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON EDUCATING LANDOWNERS CAN RECOGNIZE THE BEST ECONOMIC RETURN ON TIMBER HARVESTS, UNDERSTAND HOW DIVIDING PROPERTY AFFECTS THE ECOSYSTEM, AND HOW MANAGEMENT PLANS CAN ADDRESS THESE ISSUES. OUR COMPREHENSIVE FORESTRY OUTREACH PROGRAM ZEROES IN ON THESE CONCERNS. DURING FFY2025, WISCONSIN RREA PROGRAMMING WILL ADDRESS RENEWABLE RESOURCES IN A VARIETY OF PROGRAMS AND PARTNERSHIPS TO ADDRESS STRATEGIC AND CROSS-CUTTING NATIONAL ISSUES RELATING TO GOALS IDENTIFIED IN THE NIFA RREA STRATEGIC PLAN. GOAL 1- ENSURING HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND GOAL 3 - ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THE PRIMARY CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES WE WILL FOCUS ON INCLUDE FISH AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND INTERGENERATIONAL LAND AND OTHER LAND OWNERSHIP CHANGES. THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO HELP LANDOWNERS DEVELOP FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AROUND WOODLAND ECOLOGY, HEALTHY FORESTS, TIMBER HARVEST PRACTICES AND SALES, HABITAT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT BENEFIT WILDLIFE, STRATEGIES FOR THREATS SUCH AS INVASIVE SPECIES AND CLIMATE VARIABILITY, LAND OWNERSHIP AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRANSFERS, AND TO IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT PLAN PRACTICES TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINABLE FOREST RESOURCES AND TO MEET PERSONAL MANAGEMENT GOALS. THROUGH IN-PERSON CLASSES, VIRTUAL CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WE ARE EXPECTING TO INCREASE LANDOWNERS' AND RESOURCES PROFESSIONALS' SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE TO AFFECT LONG-TERM CHANGES IN ACTIVE MANAGEMENT BY WOODLAND OWNERS THAT WILL SUPPORT SUCCESSION TO FAM ILY MEMBERS, REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF PARCELIZATION THROUGH STABLE LAND OWNERSHIP, AND RETAIN FOREST COVER AND CONTRIBUTE SUSTAINABLY TO THE WOOD FUEL CYCLE THROUGH REGULAR PLANNED TIMBER SALES GUIDED BY FOREST MANAGEMENT PLANS.

FY25 RREA PROJECT ABSTRACT - MISSOURI WHILE 94 PERCENT OF THE STATE'S LAND BASE (41+MILLION ACRES) IS PRIVATELY OWNED, LESS THAN 10 PERCENT OF THESE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS ACTIVELY MANAGE THEIR FORESTS, WOODLANDS, AND NON-AGRICULTURAL FIELDS. THIS TRANSLATES DIRECTLY INTO LOST, VALUE-ADDED FOREST PRODUCTS AND INDIRECTLY INTO DIMINISHED ABILITY OF OUR FOREST AND WOODLANDS IN PROVIDING VALUABLE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, SUCH AS CLEAN AIR AND WATER. THIS LACK OF MANAGEMENT IS ALSO RESULTING IN LOST WILDLIFE HABITAT IN OUR WOODLANDS, ON OUR FARMS, AND IN OUR COMMUNITIES. THUS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR EXPANDED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT WILL ENABLE ALL MISSOURI CITIZENS TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS REGARDING THE WISE STEWARDSHIP AND CONSERVATION OF THE STATE'S FORESTS AND WOODLANDS, GRASSLANDS AND FIELDS, AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AND THE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS WHICH DEPEND UPON THESE ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS. THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS SO THAT A GREATER NUMBER OF CLIENTELE WILL RECONNECT WITH MISSOURI'S NATURAL RE SOURCES, INCLUDING THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESOURCE, BECOME ACTIVE LAND STEWARDS SUPPORTING CONSERVATION GOALS AND OBJECTIVES. PROJECT GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: A. INCREASE AND ENHANCE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING ON PRIVATE LANDS FEATURING WORKING FORESTS, WOODLANDS, NATIVE GRASSLANDS AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION WITHIN MISSOURI AND B. BUILDING CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS. ACTIONS TAKEN WILL FEATURE THE DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY OF EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE FOREST AND WOODLAND MANAGEMENT BY MISSOURI'S FAMILY FOREST LANDOWNERS AND DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT SERVE TO INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES CONDUCTED BY MISSOURI'S PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. TO ACHIEVE THESE OBJECTIVES OUR PLAN OF ACTION INCLUDES A. CONDUCTING 10 FOREST-RELATED EDUCATIONAL EVENTS UNDER THE MISSOURI WOODLAND STEWARD PROGRAM THEME; B. CREATING AND/OR REVISING 5 PEER-REVIEWED MU EXTENSION FOREST AND WOODLAND MANAGEMENT GUIDES AND 12 NATURAL RESOURCE NEWSLETTERS DISSEMINATED FOR STATE-WIDE USE; C. CREATING 10 NEW MISSOURI MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAM VOLUNTEER COHORTS EITHER THROUGH EXISTING CHAPTERS OR THE CREATION OF NEW CHAPTERS RESULTING IN OVER 250 MU EXTENSION MASTER NATURALIST VOLUNTEERS BEING TRAINED AND CERTIFIED TO CONDUCT VOLUNTEER SERVICE PROJECTS IN THEIR COMMUNITY THAT FEATURE THE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES; D. CONDUCTING 8 WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT EDUCATIONAL EVENTS FOCUSED ON ENHANCING HABITATS FOR BOTH WOODLAND AND EARLY SUCCESSIONAL SPECIES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO GRASSLAND BIRDS, WHITE-TAILED DEER, BOBWHITE QUAIL AND WILD TURKEY; AND CONDUCTING 1 MASTER POLLINATOR STEWARD PROGRAM THAT FEATURES THE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF NATIVE HABITATS THAT BENEFIT POLLINATORS; E. CREATING AND DEVELOPING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS FEATURING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF NATIVE GRASSES FOR GRAZING AND CONSERVATION BENEFITS AND F. CREATING OR REVISING 6 PEER-REVIEWED MU EXTENSION GUIDES FEATURING WILDLIFE AND HABITAT MANAGEMENT THEMES, TARGETING PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. THESE PROJECTS AND ACTIONS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH EXPANDED PROGRAM COLLABORATIONS AND PARTNERSHIPS. TARGET AUDIENCES AND INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS IN BOTH URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES WISHING TO IMPROVE THE NATURAL RESOURCE BASE ON THEIR PROPERTY; EDUCATORS WISHING TO INCORPORATE SCIENCE-BASED FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES INTO THEIR CURRICULUM AND ONGOING PROGRAM ACTIVITIES AND; NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS REPRESENTING STATE, FEDERAL AND NON-PROFIT CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS WISHING TO COLLABORATE IN DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS.

TENNESSEE'S TWO LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS COMPRISE THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SYSTEM. THEY WORK INDEPENDENTLY AND COLLABORATIVELY TO CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ALL 95 COUNTIES AND TO SERVE THE STATE'S 6.9 MILLION PEOPLE. TENNESSEE'S LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS CONDUCT RESEARCH AND PROVIDE OUTREACH IN FIVE KEY AREAS TO ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES AFFECTING THE STATE: SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS; ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY; ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY; DEVELOPING OUR WORKFORCE; AND STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE PROGRAMS TO ADDRESS THE ONGOING NEEDS OF CITIZENS AND AGRICULTURE PRODUCERS ACROSS THE STATE. HEALTH ISSUES ARE A TOP CONCERN FOR RESIDENTS. EXTENSION WILL STRENGTHEN HEALTH PROGRAMMING BY OFFERING THE HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAMS AND PROVIDE RESOURCES FOR IMPROVING DIETARY AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY FOR LIMITED-RESOURCE TENNESSEANS. EXTENSION LIVESTOCK AND FORAGE PROGRAMS STRENGTHEN THE STATE'S LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS THOUGH RESEARCH AND OUTREACH IN HAY SCHOOLS, LATE GESTATION NUTRITION, MARKETING, AND FORAGES. TENNESSEE EXTENSION HAS DEVELOPED PROGRAMS TO STRENGTHEN AND PROVIDE VALUE-ADDED OPPORTUNITIES AND PROGRAMS ON FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT. THE CONSUMER ECONOMICS PROGRAM HELPS FAMILIES INCREASE SAVINGS, DECREASE DEBT, AND FINANCIALLY PLAN. 4-H WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED FOR YOUTH TO PROVIDE NEEDED SKILLS, TRAINING, AND EXPERIENCES TO PARTICIPANTS. EXTENSION CONTINUES TO DEVELOP PROGRAMS TO ENCOURAGE AND PROVIDE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES. UT AGRESEARCH CONDUCTS RESEARCH WITHIN EIGHT ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS AND SEVEN PHYSICAL CENTERS, AND AT TEN AGRESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS (REC) LOCATED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. IN ADDITION TO 'A DECADE OF EXCELLENCE: TEN-YEAR STRATEGIC PLAN FOR UTIA, 2018-2028,' AGRESEARCH OPERATES UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF ITS '2021-2024 AGRESEARCH STRATEGIC ACTION PLAN' (ASAP) WITH THE OBJECTIVES TO BALANCE A PORTFOLIO OF INTEGRATED, INTER-DISCIPLINARY PROGRAMS, CULTIVATE TEAMS TO APPROACH COMPLEX PROBLEMS, ADVANCE CONCEPTS WITH STRUCTURED SUPPORT, AND TO ENSURE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CAPACITY WITH TARGETED INVESTMENT. AGRESEARCH IS EMPHASIZING FOUR PROGRAMMATIC THEMES TO ESTABLISH INTEGRATED PROGRAMS THAT CONTRIBUTE SOLUTIONS TO COMPLEX PROBLEMS. THE UT ONE HEALTH INITIATIVE, A UT SYSTEM-WIDE APPROACH HOUSED WITHIN AGRESEARCH, IS WORKING TO PRESERVE AND PROMOTE HUMAN, ANIMAL, PLANT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH TO ADVANCE ECONOMIC GROWTH, AND CONSERVE BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL, NATIONAL, AND GLOBAL SCALES. SCHOLARS FROM ACROSS AGRESEARCH ARE CONTRIBUTING TO STUDIES THAT DEFINE THE FACTORS THREATENING HUMAN AND ANIMAL HEALTH, AND THE HEALTH OF OUR ENVIRONMENT. THE EMERGING DIGITAL AGRICULTURE PROGRAM DRAWS ON THE SKILLS OF RESEARCHERS ACROSS UT TO CREATE A TRANSDISCIPLINARY PATH TO CARBONSMART AGRICULTURE AND BENEFITS FROM ONGOING INVESTMENT TO BUILD CAPACITY IN PRECISION LIVESTOCK FARMING (PLF). THE PROGRAM INCORPORATES BOTH PLANT AND ANIMAL MANAGEMENT PROJECTS THAT ULTIMATELY WILL CONTRIBUTE INFORMATION TO REFINE STRATEGIES THAT OFFER CARBON REDUCTIONS OVER TODAY'S AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS. AGRESEARCH IS REALIGNING THE CAPABILITIES AT ITS REC'S TO SUPPORT THE PLF INITIATIVE, INCLUDING THE INSTALLATION OF A ROBOTIC MILKING SYSTEM. THE TRANSFORMATIONAL AGRICULTURAL GENOMICS AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY PROGRAM WILL ADVANCE ANIMAL AND PLANT-BASED PRODUCTIVITY AND RESILIENCE. ALTHOUGH EARLY IN ITS DEVELOPMENT, THE INITIATIVE ALREADY ENGAGES FACULTY ACROSS UT TO ADVANCE STATE-OF-THE-ART SCIENCE TO DESIGN CROPS THAT ARE RESILIENT TO CLIMATE CHANGE. THE BIOECONOMY ADVANCEMENT INITIATIVE IS AN ESTABLISHED INTERDISCIPLINARY, MULTI-DEPARTMENTAL PROGRAM FOCUSED ON SUSTAINABLE FUELS, CHEMICALS, AND MATERIALS FROM STRANDED RESOURCES. THE INITIATIVE IS EMBRACING THE CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK OF THE CIRCULAR BIOECONOMY, SEEKING TO EXTEND THE LIFETIME OF RENEWABLE CARBON IN THE MARKETPLACE.

negativeFlows.title: TO MEET THE CHALLENGE OF DELIVERING ACCURATE, RELEVANT, TIMELY, AND PRACTICAL INFORMATION TO EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS AND OTHER ADVISORS AND STAKEHOLDERS, A NEW APPROACH IS NEEDED FOR EFFICIENTLY DISCOVERING, LOCATING, AND SAVING SPECIFIC INFORMATION LOCATED IN HANDBOOKS, TECHNICAL NOTES, AND OTHER REFERENCE MATERIALS.THIS PROJECT WILL BUILD ON A PREVIOUS PROJECT FUNDED BY NRCS BY PROVIDING DIRECT ACCESS TO LOCALLY- AND REGIONALLY-PRODUCED RANGELAND SCIENCE WITHIN EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS FOR EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS, AND PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAND MANAGERS. SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS ARE OFTEN LONG AND DENSE AND CAN TAKE CONSIDERABLE TIME TO REVIEW AND SYNTHESIZE. GIVEN THE PLETHORA OF ELECTRONIC INFORMATION AVAILABLE, THIS CAN BE AN OVERWHELMING PROCESS. A NEW AND INNOVATED SEARCH TOOL HAS BEEN CREATED TO ADDRESS THIS PERSISTENT ISSUE THROUGH A NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION SERVICE (NRCS) CONSERVATION INNOVATION GRANT. RANGEDOCS (HTTPS://DOCS.RANGELANDSGATEWAY.ORG/) ALLOWS EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS AND OTHER LAND MANAGERS TO SEARCH RANGELAND TERMS AND PINPOINT PARAGRAPHS OF APPLICABLE INFORMATION FROM KEY NATIONAL RANGELAND RESOURCES (I.E. NRCS TECHNICAL REFERENCES, INTERAGENCY TECHNICAL REFERENCES, AND NATIONALLY-FOCUSED OPEN ACCESS PUBLICATIONS AND EXPERIMENTAL STATION BULLETINS). ALL RESOURCES IN RANGEDOCS HAVE BEEN ANNOTATED BY RANGELAND EXPERTS SO THAT SEARCH RESULTS ARE EFFICIENT AND POINT TO HIGHLY RELEVANT INFORMATION. ADDITIONALLY, RANGEDOCS FEATURES CURATED THEME COLLECTIONS (E.G. MONITORING, TARGETED GRAZING) TO DELIVER SELECTED PASSAGES OF RANGELAND LITERATURE AS WELL AS ALLOWS USERS TO SAVE CRUCIAL EXCERPTS IN PRIVATE THEME COLLECTIONS BASED ON GEOGRAPHIC REGIONS, TOPICS, OR AUDIENCES. THUS, RANGEDOCS OFFERS THE OPPORTUNITY TO IDENTIFY RELEVANT, HIGHLY CUSTOMIZABLE INFORMATION ON EACH CRITICAL ISSUE QUICKLY AND EFFICIENTLY AND TO ORGANIZE IT FOR INDIVIDUAL NEEDS.

VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY PROJECT ABSTRACT THE AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCE EXTENSION PROGRAMS THROUGH VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY (VSU) HAVE TRADITIONALLY FOCUSED ON LIMITED-RESOURCE LANDOWNERS. THE VSU RREA 2023 PROGRAM WILL BUILD ON THIS APPROACH BY CONTINUING SUPPORT FOR PROGRAMS, WORKSHOPS, AND DEMONSTRATIONS ABOUT PRODUCTION OF NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS, AS IN THE PAST, AND ALSO INCLUDING DISSEMINATION OF INFORMATION ABOUT MANAGEMENT FOR TIMBER ON SMALL WOODLOTS AND ABOUT AGROFORESTRY AND NON-TIMBER SYSTEMS. SMALL WOODLOT MANAGEMENT AND MARKETING PROGRAMS WILL LARGELY FOCUS ON FORESTRY BASICS, INCLUDING PLANNING, SELLING TIMBER, AND BASIC SILVICULTURE. WITH REGARDS TO ALTERNATIVE FOREST PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, EMPHASIS WILL BE PLACED ON GETTING LANDOWNERS THE MOST RELEVANT INFORMATION, AND ENCOURAGING THEM TO INNOVATE AND EXPLORE. GOALS / OBJECTIVES THE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO ENHANCE ECONOMIC BENEFITS AND ENHANCE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT THAT WILL ADDRESS THE CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, FOREST FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY AND URBANIZATION. THE RREA-SUPPORTED PROGRAM WILL ALSO BUILD ON INTEREST IN LONGLEAF AND SHORTLEAF PINE BY HELPING LANDOWNERS EXPLORE THE POSSIBILITY OF GOOD TIMBER QUALITY AND NTFPS. IN ADDITION, THERE WILL BE COLLABORATION WITH OTHER AREAS OF EXTENSION, SUCH AS HELPING LANDOWNERS DEVELOP MARKETING PLANS, FINANCIAL LITERACY TRAINING FOR FOREST LANDOWNERS, AND ESTATE PLANNING. THESE AREAS IMPACT THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF FORESTLANDS. COMPONENTS 1 - MARKETING AND ALTERNATIVE FOREST PRODUCTION SYSTEMS: A SIGNIFICANT ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCE IS STANDING IN SMALL AREAS ON THE PROPERTIES OF PRIVATE LANDHOLDERS IN VIRGINIA (ROSE 2009). ALSO, 58% OF LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS OWN WOODLOTS, WITH AN AVERAGE SIZE OF 55 ACRES (USDA 2007). IF THESE FORESTLANDS CANNOT PROVIDE ECONOMIC BENEFITS, LANDOWNERS WILL BE ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED, AND SOCIETY AS A WHOLE MAY LOSE AN IMPORTANT RENEWABLE RESOURCE IF FORESTS ARE CONVERTED TO OTHER LAND USES. PRODUCTION AND SALE OF TIMBER IS AN ECONOMIC BENEFIT FOR LANDOWNERS; HOWEVER, SMALL AND LIMITED-RESOURCE LANDOWNERS ARE AT A DISADVANTAGE: (1) TIMBER DOES NOT HELP SMALL AND LIMITED-RESOURCE LANDOWNERS MEET YEARLY CASH NEEDS; (2) THERE IS A LARGE INFORMATION GAP BETWEEN MOST LANDOWNERS AND FOREST INDUSTRY WORKERS; AND (3) ECONOMIES OF SCALE CAN MAKE LOGGING FOR SOME TIMBER PRODUCTS ON SMALL TRACTS UNECONOMICAL. COMPONENT 2 - URBAN FORESTRY: A MAJOR NEW EMPHASIS IN VSU’S RREA PROGRAM WILL BE URBAN FORESTRY. URBAN FOREST MANAGEMENT CAN HELP MEET URGENT NEEDS IN THE US, AND THE COMMONWEALTH OF VIRGINIA. FOR INSTANCE, WELL-SELECTED AND WELL-PLACED TREES AND OTHER PERENNIAL VEGETATION CAN: REDUCE ENERGY CONSUMPTION AND COSTS FROM HEATING AND COOLING BUILDINGS, THEREBY PROMOTING ENERGY INDEPENDENCE AND A REDUCED CARBON FOOTPRINT; ENCOURAGE HEALTHY OUTDOOR LIVING HABITS; IMPROVE STORMWATER MANAGEMENT THEREBY REDUCING COSTS OF STORMWATER ENGINEERING AND POTENTIALLY IMPROVING WATER QUALITY IN THE IMPAIRED CHESAPEAKE BAY; PROVIDE BIOREMEDIATION OF CONTAMINATED SOILS/GROUNDWATER IN URBAN BROWNFIELD SITES; AND CAPTURE CARBON DIOXIDE FROM THE ATMOSPHERE (BOLUND AND HUNHAMMAR 1999). THE VSU RREA PROGRAM WILL COMPLEMENT THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESEARCH AND TEACHING PROGRAMS IN URBAN FORESTRY AT VSU. THE PURPOSE OF THE EXTENSION COMPONENT WILL BE TO PROVIDE SUPPORT TO COMMUNITIES TO MAXIMIZE THE BENEFITS OF TREES. VSU OUTCOMES: COMPONENT 1. ALTERNATIVE FOREST PRODUCTION SYSTEMS: DEMONSTRATE THE POTENTIAL FOR ECONOMIC RETURNS FROM NON-TRADITIONAL FOREST-BASED SYSTEMS, SUCH AS AGROFORESTRY SYSTEMS (INCLUDING SI LVOPASTURE AND FOREST FARMING OF NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS). SUPPORT NIPF LANDOWNERS TO INNOVATE NON-TRADITIONAL FOREST-BASED SYSTEMS. OUTCOME TARGET 2.1: DEMONSTRATION PRODUCTS AT RESEARCH STATION AND PRIVATE LANDHOLDINGS ARE SHOWN TO BE FINANCIALLY VIABLE, THROUGH MEASUREMENT OF REAL-WORLD COSTS AND REVENUES. OUTCOME TARGET 2.2: AT LEAST 100 LANDOWNERS IN VIRGINIA ESTABLISH AT LEAST ONE NEW ALTERNATIVE FOREST PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE. OUTCOME TARGET 2.3: AT LEAST 20 LANDOWNERS EXPERIMENT WITH INNOVATIVE PRACTICES AS A RESULT OF CONCEPTS LEARNED AND CONTACTS MADE. COMPONENT 2. URBAN FOREST MANAGEMENT: INCREASE PUBLIC AWARENESS OF ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES PROVIDED BY TREES. AID COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPMENT OF URBAN/COMMUNITY FOREST MANAGEMENT PLANS. OUTCOME TARGET 3.1: PARTICIPANTS IN RREA-SUPPORTED EVENTS INCREASE AWARENESS OF ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES RELATIVE TO THEIR BASELINE KN OWLEDGE. OUTCOME TARGET 3.2: AT LEAST TWO COMMUNITIES ADOPT OR IMPROVE URBAN/COMMUNITY FOREST MANAGEMENT PLANS. PROJECT DELIVERY METHOD VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY IS ACTIVELY BUILDING AND STRENGTHENING ITS PROGRAM FOR FORESTRY EXTENSION. THIS PROGRAM BUILDS ON TRADITIONAL (E.G., NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS; SERVING SMALL AND LIMITED-RESOURCE LANDOWNERS) AND EMERGING (E.G., URBAN HORTICULTURE AND AGRICULTURE) AREAS OF FOCUS FOR VSU. VSU’S AND RREA-SUPPORTED PROGRAMS WILL PRIMARILY BE MARKETED TO UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS - SMALL AND LIMITED-RESOURCE LANDOWNERS, AS WELL AS MINORITY AND ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES. VSU TRADITIONALLY HAS HAD THE LARGEST IMPACT BY DIRECTLY TARGETING THOSE COMMUNITIES. VSU FORESTRY EXTENSION WILL WORK IN COORDINATION WITH THE VSU SMALL FARM OUTREACH PROGRAM TO REACH OUT TO THESE STAKEHOLDERS. FURTHERMORE, AN ONGOING SURVEY FUNDED BY MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS WILL HELP IDENTIFY STAKEHOLDERS WHO HAVE NEVER HAD CONTACT WITH VCE IN THE PAST. WHILE VSU CAN HELP THE EXISTING FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAMS TO REACH NEW AUDIENCES, IT IS NOT THE INTENT OF VCE/VSU TO EXCLUDE OTHER INTERESTED STAKEHOLDERS. VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION IS A SINGLE INSTITUTION, AND VSU AND VIRGINIA TECH WILL CONTINUE TO WORK TOGETHER TO IDENTIFY WAYS TO COMPLEMENT EFFORTS TO CREATE SYNERGIES. FURTHERMORE, VSU WILL WORK WITH OTHER ORGANIZATIONS TO IDENTIFY COMMON FOCUS AREAS AND NEEDS IN VIRGINIA. AREAS THAT ARE CURRENTLY RECEIVING ATTENTION FROM NUMEROUS VIRGINIA ORGANIZATIONS INCLUDE RESTORATION OF SHORTLEAF AND LONGLEAF PINE, AND WATER QUALITY IN THE CHESAPEAKE BAY. EMERGING THEMES OF INTEREST IN VIRGINIA INCLUDE BIOENERGY AND MARKETS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES. IT WILL BE IMPORTANT FOR VSU TO STAY ABREAST OF THESE THEMES AND INTEGRATE THEM INTO THE THREE COMPONENTS DESCRIBED ABOVE BECAUSE THEY CAN HELP VSU COOPERATE WITH OTHER INSTITUTIONS, AND CAPTURE GREATER PUBLIC INTEREST. MONITORING AND EVALUATION: MONITORING AND EVALUATION ARE CRUCIAL ELEMENTS TO BE ABLE TO ADAPT AND IMPROVE PROGRAMS AND TO ENSURE LONG-TERM SUCCESS. WE INTEND TO MEASURE AND MONITOR THE OUTPUT AND OUTCOME TARGETS DESCRIBED ABOVE. OUTPUTS ARE MOST EASILY MEASURED: THEY CAN BE QUANTIFIED IN TERMS OF NUMBER OF WORKSHOP PARTICIPANTS, NUMBER OF PUBLICATIONS, ETC. OUTCOMES, HOWEVER, IMPLY A CHANGE IN BEHAVIOR BY THE AUDIENCE, AND CAN BE SOMEWHAT MORE DIFFICULT TO MEASURE. EACH DELIVERY METHOD NECESSITATES DIFFERENT OUTCOME MONITORING AND EVALUATIONTOOLS, SOME OF WHICH REQUIRE SPECIFIC FUNDING. (A) DEM ONSTRATION SITES WILL HAVE LOGBOOKS FOR VISITOR INFORMATION AND SUGGESTIONS (COUNTS OF VISITORS MEASURE OUTPUT). (B) COSTS AND REVENUES OF DEMONSTRATION SITES WILL BE LOGGED TO ESTIMATE FINANCIAL RETURNS. (C) IN-EVENT QUESTIONNAIRES AND OCCASIONAL POST-EVENT SURVEYS. (D) REVIEW OF CONTINUANCE OF PRACTICES AFTER SUPPORT IS ENDED THROUGH FORMAL OR INFORMAL SURVEYS.

THIS IS A PROJECT WITH LEADERSHIP FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA EXTENSION, DEPARTMENT OF FOREST RESOURCES, AND CLOQUETFORESTRY CENTER (UMN).IT IS A STRATEGIC AND EFFICIENT PROJECT INCLUDING MULTIPLE EXTENSION ACTIVITIES THAT ARE HIGHLY REPLICABLE IN OTHER REGIONS. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL ALL SYNERGISTICALLY FOSTER ENGAGED LEARNING THROUGH THE MULTI-DIRECTIONAL EXCHANGE OF KNOWLEDGE TO FOREST AND RANGE OWNERS AND MANAGERS. THE PROJECT INCLUDES NEW CITIZEN SCIENCE CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY, CRUCIAL IMPROVEMENTS TO AN INNOVATIVE, PROVEN LEARNING PLATFORM AND KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE PROCESS, CAPACITY TO SUPPORT NEW KNOWLEDGE GENERATION AND EXCHANGE, AND NEW USER-GENERATED CONTENT DEVELOPMENT FOCUSED ON INCREASING ACCESSIBILITY. ADDITIONALLY, WE LEVERAGE THE LIMITED RREA BUDGET WITH A COMMITMENT TO GENERATE EXTERNAL FUNDING TO SUPPORT PROJECT-RELATED EXTENSION PROGRAM DELIVERY.THE PROJECT'S MODEL OF COMMUNITY-GENERATED KNOWLEDGE ADDRESSES SEVERAL RREA STRATEGIC PLAN PRIORITIES AND THE FOCUS ON INCREASING THE SALIENCE, CREDIBILITY AND LEGITIMACY OF EXTENSION PROGRAM CONTENT. AT LEAST SINCE THE NOVEMBER 2015 NATIONAL EXTENSION FORESTRY AND WOOD PRODUCTS CONFERENCE IN COCODRIE, LA, A KEY STRATEGIC OBJECTIVE FOR THE EXTENSION FORESTRY SYSTEM, INCLUDING RREA FOCUS FUNDS, HAS BEEN IMPROVING THE EFFICIENCY AND IMPACT OF OUR PROGRAM DELIVERY MODELS. THIS PROPOSAL DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THAT OBJECTIVE, WHICH IS FOCUSED ON NOT JUST TRANSFERRING KNOWLEDGE TO FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS, BUT ENGAGING THEM IN ACTIVELY BUILDING NEW KNOWLEDGE AND EXCHANGING IT THROUGH AN INNOVATIVE YET WELL-ESTABLISHED PLATFORM.CONTENT GENERATED BY PEERS AND PRACTITIONERS TENDS TO BE SEEN AS HIGHLY CREDIBLE. THIS IS A CORE TENET OF DIFFUSION OF INNOVATIONS THEORY (ROGERS 2003), SUPPORTED BY MORE RECENT WOODLAND OWNER RESEARCH (KUEPER ET AL 2013). IN THE LANGUAGE OF THE REQUEST FOR APPLICATIONS, EXTENSION PROGRAM MODELS THAT INVOLVE COMMUNITY-GENERATED KNOWLEDGE CAN HELP SOLVE THE CHALLENGE THATSCIENTISTS OFTEN DO NOT FULLY UNDERSTAND THE CONTEXTS IN WHICH DECISIONS ARE BEING MADE. THESE PROGRAM MODELS POSITION PRACTITIONERS, LANDOWNERS, AND OTHER CITIZENS AS THE SOURCES OF KNOWLEDGE, WITH OPPORTUNITIES FOR THAT CONTENT TO BE REVIEWED, VALIDATED, AND USED BY OTHERSTHE ISSUE THAT THIS PROPOSAL IS INTENDED TO ADDRESS IS INCREASING THE SALIENCE, CREDIBILITY AND LEGITIMACY OF EXTENSION PROGRAM CONTENT. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO LEVERAGE AN INNOVATIVE MODEL OF TECHNOLOGY-ENHANCED EXTENSION PROGRAM DELIVERY TO PROMOTE THE ADOPTION OF SOUND SILVICULTURAL TECHNIQUES TO ADVANCE CLIMATE ADAPTATION AND RESILIENCE THROUGHOUT FORESTS IN THE LAKE STATES AND BEYOND. THE DELIVERABLES SUPPORTING THIS GOAL ARE AS FOLLOWS:EVALUATE THE VALUE, USES, AND PERCEPTIONS OF END-USERS OF THE SILVICULTURE LIBRARY. (COMPLETE, WITH REPORT CURRENTLY IN-PREP, SO NO PROJECT FUNDS NEEDED.)DEVELOP AND DELIVER NEW PILOT-TESTED CURRICULUM ABOUT ON-THE-JOB AND ON-THE-WOODLOT EXPERIMENTATION. THIS WILL BE A NEW OFFERING IN THE UMN EXTENSION'S DIVERSE AND HIGHLY SUCCESSFUL CITIZEN SCIENCE PROGRAM PORTFOLIO. IT WILL MOBILIZE CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO GENERATE NEW KNOWLEDGE AND IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF CITIZEN SCIENCE OUTPUTS;USE DATA FROM THE END-USER EVALUATION TO DESIGN, TEST, AND EVALUATE MORE STREAMLINED CASE STUDY SUBMISSION PROCESSES. THIS WILL DIRECTLY ADDRESS THE GREATEST BARRIER IDENTIFIED BY END-USERS, THE DIFFICULTY OF ENTERING NEW CASE STUDY CONTENT;PUBLISH A MINIMUM OF 20 NEW CASE STUDIES FOCUSED ON FOREST MANAGEMENT TO PROMOTE WILDLIFE HABITAT FOR SPECIES OF PRIORITY INTEREST TO LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS;DEVELOP THE GREAT LAKES SILVICULTURE LIBRARY 2.0 PLATFORM TO ENSURE THAT PUBLISHED CASE STUDY DATA ARE SECURE, PROPERLY ARCHIVED, WIDELY ACCESSIBLE, AND WELL DESIGNED FOR AN OPTIMIZED USER EXPERIENCE. IMPORTANTLY, THE NEW LIBRARY PLATFORM WILL ALSO SUPPORT REGIONAL EXPANSION, WHICH HAS BEEN REQUESTED BY PARTNERS IN MULTIPLE STATES INCLUDING THE MID-ATLANTIC, NORTHEAST, AND PACIFIC NORTHWEST REGIONS.
