negativeFlows.title: RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM TUSKEGEE UNIVERSITY HOLDS A HISTORIC CONNECTION TO LANDOWNERS IN THE BLACK BELT OF ALABAMA, AS WELL AS ACROSS THE STATE FOR PROVIDING SUPPORT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR LAND MANAGEMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY. WITH GROWING CONCERNS IN CLIMATE CHANGE, AND GROWING NEEDS TO ACQUIRE AND RETAIN LAND IT IS THE FOCUS OF TUCE’S RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT CAPACITY FUNDING TO SUPPORT PROGRAMS THAT EDUCATE LANDOWNERS IN SOME OF THESE MORE PERTINENT AREAS OF RESEARCH. THROUGH PROGRAMS DELIVERED AS WORKSHOPS, FIELD DAYS, HANDS ON DEMONSTRATIONS, WEBINARS, INTERNSHIPS, AND CONFERENCES IT IS THE INTENTION FOR THE FOCUS OF THIS YEAR’S WORK TO FOCUS ON 1) HEIR PROPERTY; 2) CLIMATE CHANGE <(>&<)> FORESTRY MANAGEMENT (SOCIAL SCIENCE); 3) AGRITOURISM -RECREATION; 4) FERAL HOGS <(>&<)> FORESTRY MANAGEMENT; AND 5) POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICE MARKETS. ALL PLANNED PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS CONTAINED IN THE TUCE INTEGRATED EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PLAN OF WORK WERE DEVELOPED WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF RESEARCH AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT OF RELEVANCE TO ALL RESIDENTS OF ALABAMA WHO MAY BENEFIT FROM THE LOCAL KNOWLEDGE BASE OR SERVICE. THIS COMMITMENT IS WITHOUT REGARD TO ANY PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS, TO INCLUDE AGE, ETHNIC ORIGIN, GENDER, RELIGION, SEXUAL ORIENTATION, OR GEOGRAPHIC LOCATION. ALABAMA POPULATIONS ARE INCLUDED, AS APPROPRIATE, IN THE PROJECT AND PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT PROCESS. AS A PART OF THE DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, EACH PROJECT OR PROGRAM THAT WAS IDENTIFIED AND DEVELOPED FOR GRASSROOTS PROGRAM DELIVERY, DETAILS THE INTENDED AUDIENCE(S) TO BE SERVED. AS A PART OF THE REVIEW PROCESS, THE RESPECTIVE ASSISTANT/ASSOCIATE DIRECTORS AND ADMINISTRATORS ARE CHARGED WITH ENSURING THAT THE INTENDED AUDIENCE(S) FOR EACH PROJECT OR PROGRAM INCLUDES THE SPECTRUM OF POTENTIAL RECIPIENTS OF THE ALABAMA POPULATION.

SUSTAINING FOREST RESOURCES IN THE U.S. VIRGIN ISLANDS THE ECONOMY OF THE U.S. VIRGIN ISLANDS IS PREDOMINANTLY DEPENDENT UPON THE TOURISM INDUSTRY. OUR NATURAL RESOURCES ARE CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF THE ECONOMY AND ARE ALSO IMPORTANT FOR OUR QUALITY OF LIFE. THE NEED EXISTS, THEREFORE, TO DEVELOP AND MAINTAIN A SUSTAINABLE ECOSYSTEM THAT CAN PROVIDE BENEFITS FOR RESIDENTS AND VISITORS. THERE ARE MANY COMPETING DEMANDS FOR OUR LIMITED LAND RESOURCES. POLICYMAKERS ARE FACED WITH TOUGH DECISIONS AS THEY TRY TO FIND A DELICATE BALANCE BETWEEN THE INCREASED NEEDS AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS RELATED TO LAND FOR ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND HOUSING. THIS USUALLY RESULTS IN FURTHER FOREST FRAGMENTATION AND THE ASSOCIATED NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES. PRIVATE LANDOWNERS ARE FORCED TO MAKE FINANCIAL DECISIONS REGARDING THE USE AND MANAGEMENT OF THEIR PROPERTIES. MANY OF THESE LANDOWNERS ARE NOT FAMILIAR WITH PROPER MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR TREES AND FORESTS. THEY MUST BECOME AWARE OF THE BENEFITS OF PROPER LAND STEWARDSHIP AND HOW IT SUPPORTS OUR NATURAL RESOURCES. THEY ALSO NEED TO BE MADE AWARE OF THE VALUE OF TREES/FORESTS AND WHAT THEY PROVIDE TO LOCAL ECONOMIES - INCLUDING THE VALUABLE CONTRIBUTIONS MADE TO THE TOURISM INDUSTRY AND THE QUALITY OF LIFE OF RESIDENTS. TREES/FORESTS MUST BE APPRECIATED FOR ENCOURAGING BIODIVERSITY, PROVIDING OPEN SPACES AND RECREATIONAL OPPO RTUNITIES. PROPER TREE ESTABLISHMENT, CARE AND MAINTENANCE ARE SOME OF THE TOPICS THAT WILL BE EMPHASIZED. PARTNERSHIPS WITH OTHER GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS WILL ASSIST IN GETTING INFORMATION TO OUR STAKEHOLDERS. THIS WILL HELP TO IMPROVE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS. THE INFORMATION WILL BE PRIMARILY PROVIDED THROUGH WORKSHOPS, SITE VISITS, DEMONSTRATIONS, WEBPAGES AND SEMINARS. STAKEHOLDERS WILL ALSO BE MADE AWARE OF THE NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON WEATHER, ESPECIALLY DROUGHTS, FLOODING, THE SEVERITY OF TROPICAL STORMS/HURRICANES AND HOW BEST TO MITIGATE THESE EFFECTS. THE HURRICANE SEASON LASTS FOR SIX MONTHS EACH YEAR. DURING THIS TIME OUR TREES/URBAN FORESTS ARE VULNERABLE TO DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE PASSAGE OF STORMS OF VARYING INTENSITIES. WE WILL FOCUS ON STRATEGIES THAT PREPARE OUR URBAN FORESTS TO WITHSTAND DIVERSE/EXTREME WEATHER CONDITIONS AND HOW TO RECOVER FROM SUCH EVENTS. THE RECYCLING OF FALLEN TREES AND PARTS OF TREES INTO VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS WILL ALSO BE INCLUDED. THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT HAS INITIATED A PROGRAM TO RECYCLE GREEN WASTE INTO COMPOST AND MULCH, WE WILL PARTNER WITH THIS PROGRAM IN THE EDUCATIONAL ASPECT. THE PROGRAM WILL FOCUS ON THE CRITICAL ISSUES OF PUBLIC AWARENESS AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON FORESTS AND PROVIDING INCREASED ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES. THE CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES WILL BE CLIMATE VARIABILITY, URBANIZATION AND INVASIVE SPECIES. THE MAIN OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1) COMMUNICATE THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS AND OPPORTUNITIES THAT CAN BE DERIVED FROM TREE POPULATIONS AND ASSOCIATED NATURAL RESOURCES; 2) DEVELOP PARTNERSHIPS WITH COOPERATING STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, ORGANIZATIONS, BUSINESSES, AND LANDOWNERS TO REACH AND ENGAGE S TAKEHOLDERS MORE EFFECTIVELY; 3) EDUCATE LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE EXTENSION AND OTHER PROFESSIONALS, AND YOUTH ABOUT THE BENEFITS OF APPLYING PRACTICES THAT S USTAIN TREE POPULATIONS; 4) DELIVER RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THAT WILL HELP GUIDE DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES THAT ENHANCE WORKING LANDSCAPES. THE TARGET AUDIENCE FOR THE PROJECT CONSISTS OF LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS, OTHER EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS, URBAN FORESTERS, FORESTRY PROFESSIONALS, POLICYMAKERS, GOVERNMENTAL AGENCY PERSONNEL, NGOS, YOUTH AND YOUTH GROUPS, FORESTRY COUNCIL MEMBERS, AGRICULTURE ADVISORY GROUPS, LANDSCAPERS, WOODWORKERS/WOOD ARTISANS AND RESIDENTS. THE PROJECT WILL UTILIZE THE FOLLOWING OUTPUTS AS EDUCATIONAL STRATEGIES TO ACHIEVE THE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: WORKSHOPS; SITE VISITS; CONSULTATIONS; TRAINING SESSIONS; SEMINARS AND COUNSELING. THESE WILL BE TARGETED TO: LANDOWNERS; NATURAL RESOURCES AND OTHER PROFESSIONALS; URBAN AND OTHER FORESTERS. THEY WILL BE CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES ALONG WITH NONGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES AND OTHER GROUPS, ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE AN INCREASE IN: PARTICIPATION OF LANDOWNERS IN EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES; THE NUMBER OF LANDOWNERS AND PROPERTY MANAGERS WITH IMPROVED DECISIONS MAKING SKILLS; KNOWLEDGE OF LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS ABOUT PROPERLY MANAGING TREE POPULATIONS; KNOWLEDGE OF LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS ABOUT THE BENEFITS OF TREE POPULATIONS; KNOWLEDGE OF LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS ABOUT NATIVE, NATURALIZED AND INVASIVE TREE SPECIES AND INCOME OF WOODWORKERS RECYCLING TREE PARTS INTO VALUE-ADDED ITEMS. FOR EACH OBJECTIVE, THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING, PROMOTING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS IN VARIOUS FORMATS INCLUDING: WORKSHOPS; HANDS-ON DEMONSTRATIONS; SHORT COURSES; INFORMAL CLASSROOM INSTRUCTION; EDUCATIONAL DISPLAYS; INTERNET WEBPAGES; TOURS; AND SEMINARS ALONG WITH WEBINARS, ONLINE TRAINING AND VIDEOS. EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AND DISSEMINATED TO THE TARGET AUDIENCE. PARTNERSHIPS WILL BE DEVELOPED AND MAINTAINED WITH STAKEHOLDER GROUPS AND ORGANIZATIONS INCLUDING GOVERNMENTAL DEPARTMENTS/AGENCIES AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS. COMMUNITY DECISION-MAKING WILL BE PROMOTED THROUGH INCREASING THE PUBLIC'S UNDERSTANDING AND INVOLVEMENT. THIS WILL ALLOW STAKEHOLDERS TO RECOGNIZE PROBLEMS AND BECOME INVOLVED IN THE PROCESS TO RESOLVE THEM. THE MEDIA WILL BE UTILIZED TO PROMOTE THE ACTIVITIES OF THE PROGRAM. SPECIAL EMPHASIS WILL BE PLACED ON THE PARTICIPATION OF YOUTH IN THE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS. EXTENSION STAFF AND OTHER PROFESSIONALS WILL BE THE FOCUS OF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES. THE OUTCOME OF THE PROJECT WILL BE MEASURED THROUGH THE NUMBER OF PERSONS WHO: GAINED AWARENESS, KNOWLEDGE AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS; INCREASED THEIR UNDERSTANDING; AND CHANGED THEIR ASSUMPTIONS, HABITS AND PRACTICES BASEDUPON THEIR INCREASED KNOWLEDGE. THIS WILL BE DONE THROUGH EVALUATIONS CONSISTING PRIMARILY OF PRE AND POST-TESTS. OTHER METHODS THAT WILL BE USED INCLUDE: OBSERVATIONS; VISUAL EVIDENCE; ANECDOTAL EVIDENCE; SURVEYS; GROUP DISCUSSIONS; TESTIMONIALS; END-OF-EVENT ANALYSIS; AND QUESTIONNAIRES.

RREA PROJECT ABSTRACT UAPB THE RREA PROGRAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT PINE BLUFF (UAPB) IS DESIGNED TO EDUCATE HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED PRODUCERS (HUPS) ABOUT FORESTRY MANAGEMENT AND NAVIGATING THROUGH THE FORESTRY NETWORK. THIS NETWORK INCLUDES TREE PLANTERS, LOGGERS, TREE THINNERS, CONSULTING FORESTERS, COUNTY FORESTERS WITH THE ARKANSAS DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY DIVISION: AND THE NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION SERVICES (NRCS) ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY INCENTIVE PROGRAM (EQIP). THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROGRAM IS: TO PROVIDE FORESTRY MANAGEMENT EDUCATION TO HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED PRODUCERS. TO EDUCATE PRODUCERS ABOUT USDA CONSERVATION PROGRAMS USED TO IMPROVE FORESTLAND. TO ASSIST HUPS IN NAVIGATION THROUGH THE FORESTRY NETWORK TO MANAGE THEIR FORESTLAND. TO IMPLEMENT THE PROGRAM, UAPB PROVIDES FORESTRY EDUCATIONAL MEETINGS THAT INCLUDE COUNTY FORESTERS AND A UAPB FORESTER (PART-TIME) WHO CONDUCTS FORESTRY EDUCATIONAL MEETINGS FOR HUPS. IN ADDITION, AN NRCS EMPLOYEE ALONG WITH A UAPB CONSERVATION CONSULTANT PROVIDES INFORMATION ABOUT THE EQIP CONSERVATION PROGRAM, ITS PRACTICES, AND ITS FINANCIAL INCENTIVES USED TO HELP FORESTLAND OWNERS INSTALL IMPROVEMENT PRACTICES ON THEIR LAND. TO ASSIST THE FOREST LANDOWNERS, UAPB HAS A FORESTRY TEAM (CONSERVATION CONSULTANT AND PART TIME FORESTER). THE TEAM MAKES SITE VISITS TO FORESTRY LANDOWNERS TO PROVIDE FORESTRY AND CONSERVATION RECOMMENDATIONS. LANDOWNERS ARE ASSISTED IN APPLYING FOR THE EQIP PRO GRAM TO INSTALL LAND IMPROVEMENT PRACTICES AND IN THE SELECTION OF VENDORS TO INSTALL CONSERVATION PRACTICES IF FUNDED THROUGH THE EQIP PROGRAM.

RREA KSU NON-TECHNICAL SUMMARY IN 2020 THE KENTUCKY FOREST SECTOR PROVIDED “AN ESTIMATED $9.55 BILLION IN DIRECT CONTRIBUTION AND A TOTAL ECONOMIC CONTRIBUTION OF $13.97 BILLION” ACCORDING TO THE 2020 KENTUCKY FORESTRY ECONOMIC IMPACT REPORT (AS ESTIMATED BY IMPLAN DATA FOR KENTUCKY AND THE KENTUCKY FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY DIRECTORY). MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT PROMOTE HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS FOR KENTUCKY'S SMALL WOODLAND OWNERS ARE CRITICAL TO THE CONTINUED PROTECTION AND UTILIZATION OF KENTUCKY'S FORESTS. COMPLEX ECOSYSTEMS WITH BIOTIC INTERACTIONS AMONG PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND MICROORGANISMS AS WELL AS ABIOTIC, PHYSICAL, AND CHEMICAL INTERACTIONS CAN GREATLY AFFECT THE HEALTH OF FORESTS, WATERSHEDS, AND AGRICULTURAL ECOSYSTEMS. FOREST HEALTH, IN TERMS OF FUNCTION OF RIPARIAN/WETLAND VEGETATION, CAN BE ENHANCED THROUGH SILVICULTURE AND AGROFORESTRY APPROACHES THAT SUPPORT NATIVE PLANT POPULATIONS, REDUCE INVASIVE SPECIES, PROMOTE THE HEALTH OF RIPARIAN ZONES, AND INCREASE WATER QUALITY. ALMOST HALF (48%) OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY’S LAND IS COVERED IN FOREST. THERE ARE 467,000 SMALL PRIVATE WOODLAND OWNERS. MUCH OF THE STATE’S REMAINING LAND IS OCCUPIED BY 12.9 MILLION ACRES OF FARMLAND, WITH NEARLY 75,000 FARMS, MOST BEING SMALL-SCALE, FAMILY OPERATIONS. WITH SUCH FRAGMENTED OWNERSHIP, ECOSYSTEM HEALTH AND ADEQUATE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT CAN BE DIFFICULT TO ACHIEVE. THEREFORE, PROGRAMS THAT HELP LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS UNDERSTAND AND IMPLEMENT HEALTHY FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ARE ESSENTIAL FOR THE IMPROVEMENT AND PROTECTION OF KENTUCKY’S LANDS, WATERS, WILDLIFE, AND ECONOMIC RESOURCES. KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY (KSU) WILL PROVIDE ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS, FOREST LANDOWNER AND PROFESSIONAL TRAINING WORKSHOPS, AND PRESENTATIONS FOCUSING ON: RREA GOAL 1: ENSURING HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS 1. INVASIVE SPECIES (KA 213 WEEDS AFFECTING PLANTS) 2. WETLAND RESOURCES (KA 112 WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT) 3. CLIMATE VARIABILITY (KA 132 WEATHER AND CLIMATE) RREA GOAL 2: ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS 1. FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH (KA 112 WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, KA 123 MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOREST RESOURCES, KA 213 WEEDS AFFECTING PLANTS). 2. WILDLIFE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES (KA 112 WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, KA 135 AQUATIC AND TERRESTRIAL WILDLIFE, AND KA 136 CONSERVATION OF BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY). RREA GOAL 3: BUILDING CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS 1. COMMUNICATION, EDUCATION, AND INFORMATION DELIVERY (KA 903 COMMUNICATION, EDUCATION, AND INFORMATION DELIVERY). THIS EXTENSION PROJECT WILL CONTRIBUTE TOWARD A NUMBER OF RREA GOALS USING PROGRAMING THAT PROMOTES HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS THROUGH INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, FOREST STEWARDSHIP, WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, AND ENHANCING CONNECTIONS TO THE NATURAL RESOURCES AND LANDOWNER COMMUNITIES. THE STAFF OF THE CENTER WILL EMPLOY THEIR EXPERTISE AS WELL AS THAT OF OTHER EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS TO PROVIDE IMPACTFUL EXPERIENCES FOR VISITORS SEEKING CONSERVATION INFORMATION AND TRAINING. THESE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO K-16 STUDENTS, EDUCATORS, NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS, LANDOWNERS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC TO ENCOURAGE THEM TO UNDERSTAND AND ADOPT CONSERVATION PRACTICES AND TO ENGAGE IN CONSERVATION. THE FIELD-BASED, HANDS-ON NATURE OF THE PROGRAMMING PROVIDED BY THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO EMPOWER INDIVIDUALS WITH THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS TO POSITIVELY IMPACT THE MILLIONS OF ACRES OF THE COMMONWEALTH THAT IS CURRENTLY FORESTED. THE OVERALL EXPECTATION IS THAT KSU AFFECTS THE CONSERVATION AWARENESS, KNOWLEDGE, AND FUTURE BEHAVIORS OF AT LEAST 80% OF PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS. ADDITIONALLY, AT LEAST 55 ACRES OF LAND PER YEAR WILL BE POSITIVELY IMPACTED THROUGH PROGRAMS AND PRESENTATIONS RELATED TO THIS INITIATIVE. PROJECT INFORMATION METHODOLOGY THE KSU ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH CENTER (EERC) IS ON 307 ACRES OF LAND, APPROXIMATELY 15 MILES NORTH OF THE KSU CAMPUS IN HENRY COUNTY, KENTUCKY. THE EERC IS LOCATED AT THE WESTERN END OF THE APPALACHIAN MOUNTAIN REGION, LARGELY DOMINATED BY HARDWOOD FOREST TREES WELL ADAPTED TO HILLY TERRAIN. MANY STREAMS AND CREEKS THAT DRAIN MULTIPLE RURAL AREAS CAN BE FOUND IN THESE FORESTED ACRES AND ARE PART OF THE KENTUCKY RIVER WATERSHED. THE EERC HAS A 1.25-ACRE POND, 6.5 MILES OF WALKING TRAILS, AND SITES THAT ARE USED FOR TEACHING PURPOSES AND FOR CONDUCTING RESEARCH PROJECTS IN A WIDE VARIETY OF DISCIPLINES INCLUDING AQUATIC SCIENCES, FORESTRY, BIOLOGY, AND SCIENCE EDUCATION. MANY KSU UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS CONDUCT A WIDE VARIETY OF APPLIED RESEARCH AND PARTICIPATE IN CLASSES HOSTED BY THE EERC, MAKING THIS CENTER A HIGH PRIORITY FOR FACILITY IMPROVEMENT AND LONG-TERM COMMITMENT. THE EERC IS MANAGED WITH DEMONSTRABLE ENVIRONMENTALLY-SOUND STEWARDSHIP PRACTICES AND PROVIDES A UNIQUE PERSPECTIVE ON LAND USE AND IMPACTS ON WATER QUALITY. KSU WILL ACCOMPLISH THE PROJECT GOALS USING THE EERC AS THE PLATFORM FOR THIS PROJECT. THE EERC WILL FACILITATE K-16 AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT LEARNING WITH ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS AND PRESENTATIONS. ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION THAT PROVIDES HANDS-ON LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES IN THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT PROVIDES STUDENTS OF ALL AGES THE TOOLS TO DEVELOP BONDS WITH THE ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH THEY LIVE WHILE REINFORCING THE BONDS AMONG COMMUNITIES WHICH THEY CALL HOME. IT IS A PLACE FOR LEARNERS OF ALL BACKGROUNDS TO GAIN A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND WHAT CAN BE DONE TO IMPROVE AND MAINTAIN IT. THESE EVENTS WILL PREDOMINANTLY INCORPORATE EXPERIENTIAL, FIELD-BASED TRAINING AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION TOPICS DESIGNED FOR LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS, EDUCATORS, STUDENTS, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC WITH INTEREST IN THESE TOPICS. PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WHO ARE NOT LANDOWNERS WILL BE INTRODUCED TO COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES TO ENGAGE IN COMMUNITY CLEANUPS, PLANTINGS, AND INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT. KSU WILL HOST MONTHLY NATURE HIKES AT THE EERC (MAR-NOV, WEATHER PERMITTING) FOCUSING ON NATIVE FLORA. SEASONAL PUBLIC EDUCATIONAL EVENTS WILL BE HOSTED FOCUSING ON OTHER ASPECTS OF NATIVE ECOLOGY. KSU WILL IMPLEMENT UP TO FOUR PROGRAMS OR FIELD DAYS PER YEAR AT THE EERC THAT INCLUDE EDUCATION ON CLIMATE VARIABILITY AND MITIGATION STRATEGIES FOR STUDENTS AND LANDOWNERS. KSU WILL ALSO CONDUCT ONE TRAINING SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS ON HOW TO TEACH ABOUT CLIMATE VARIABILITY, PROJECTED IMPACTS, AND ADAPTATION STRATEGIES. KSU WILL PROVIDE ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS FOR FOREST LANDOWNERS THROUGH PROFESSIONAL TRAINING WORKSHOPS, AND PRESENTATIONS. ADDITIONALLY, UP TO SIX TRAINING WORKSHOPS OR FIELD DAYS WILL FOCUS ON THE IMPLEMENTATION AND UNDERSTANDING OF HABITAT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. KSU INTENDS TO REACH A MINIMUM OF 100 STUDENTS, CITIZENS, NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS, AND FOREST LANDOWNERS. KSU WILL ALSO HOST A COMMUNITY DELIBERATION AND DIALOGUE SESSION FOCUSING ON WATER STEWARDSHIP IN THE COMMONWEALTH. THE CONFERENCE CENTER AT THE KSU HAROLD R. BENSON RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION FARM WILL BE USED TO DELIVER UP TO TWO PROGRAMS PER YEAR ON CONTENT AND ACTIVITIES OCCURRING AT THE EERC. TO MEASURE PROGRESS TOWARD THE ACHIEVEMENT OF GOALS AND OBJECTIVES, PROGRAM AND PRESENTATION PARTICIPANTS ARE ASKED TO COMPLETE EVALUATION FORMS. THE FORMS COLLECT DEMOGRAPHIC INFORMATION, EVALUATE THE FACILITY AND THE PROGRAMMING OFFERED, AS WELL AS TRACK SHORT-TERM KNOWLEDGE AND BEHAVIORAL AND LIFE STYLE CHANGES RESULTING FROM THE PROGRAMS.

PROJECT SUMMARY RENEWABLE RESOURCE EXTENSION ACT URBAN FORESTRY EXTENSION PROVIDES VALUABLE, EXPERT INFORMATION ON TREE AND URBAN LANDSCAPE CARE AND MAINTENANCE FOR PRIVATE CITIZENS, MUNICIPALITIES, AND INDUSTRY. NORTHWEST FLORIDAS URBAN FORESTS IS ONE OF ITS GREATEST ASSETS AND THE CITIZENS HOLD THEM IN HIGH REGARD. TREES PROVIDE MUCH TO ITS CITIZENS INCLUDING ENERGY CONSERVATION, IMPROVED AIR QUALITY, STORM WATER RETENTION, WILDLIFE HABITAT, AESTHETICS, REAL ESTATE VALUE AND A SINCE OF COMMUNITY. TREES CAN ALSO HELP REDUCE WIND DAMAGE DURING STORMS AND UNFORTUNATELY CAN CAUSE DAMAGE IF THEY FALL ON PROPERTY. IT IS THE GOAL OF THIS PROGRAM TO HELP PEOPLE GET THE GREATEST BENEFIT AND THE LEAST LIABILITY FROM THIS TREE RESOURCE. ADDITIONALLY, AND AS A SECOND GOAL, PROPER LANDSCAPE TRAINING CAN HELP THE PUBLIC TO DEVELOP A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR LANDSCAPING OPTIONS IN ORDER TO UTILIZE THE BEST QUALITY OF MATERIALS, PROPER INSTALLATION AND MAINTENANCE TECHNIQUES TO ASSURE HEALTHIER PLANTS, AND TO HELP THEM DETERMINE WHAT THE RIGHT PLANT IN THE RIGHT PLACE MEANS. THE GREEN INDUSTRY  BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ARE A SCIENCEBASED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT TEACH ENVIRONMENTALLY SAFE TREE MANAGEMENT AND LANDSCAPING PRACTICES THAT HELP CONSERVE AND PROTECT FLORIDAS GROUND AND SURFACE WATERS. THEY CAN ALSO SAVE THE FLORIDA HOMEOWNER MONEY, TIME, AND EFFORT; INCREASE THE BEAUTY OF THE HOME LANDSCAPE; AND PROTECT THE HEALTH OF YOUR FAMILY, PETS, AND THE ENVIRONMENT. FAMUS RREA FIVEYEAR PLAN WILL LOOK AT EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS DESIGNED TO PROVIDE HOMEOWNERS, CORPORATE, GOVERNMENTAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERSONNEL THE BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR TREES AND LANDSCAPE.

UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM ABSTRACT THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT (RREA) PROGRAM PROVIDED FUNDS FOR EXTENSION ACTIVITIES DESIGNED TO: (1) PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT ENABLE INDIVIDUALS TO RECOGNIZE, ANALYZE, AND RESOLVE PROBLEMS DEALING WITH RENEWABLE RESOURCES, INCLUDING FOREST- AND RANGE-BASED OUTDOOR RECREATION OPPORTUNITIES, TREES, AND FORESTS IN URBAN AREAS, AND TREES AND SHRUBS IN SHELTERBELTS; (2) USE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TO DISSEMINATE THE RESULTS OF RESEARCH ON RENEWABLE RESOURCES; (3) CONDUCT EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT TRANSFER THE BEST AVAILABLE TECHNOLOGY TO THOSE INVOLVED IN THE MANAGEMENT AND PROTECTION OF FORESTS AND RANGELANDS AND THE PROCESSING AND USE OF THEIR ASSOCIATED RENEWABLE RESOURCES; (4) DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT GIVE SPECIAL ATTENTION TO THE EDUCATIONAL NEEDS OF SMALL, PRIVATE NON-INDUSTRIAL FOREST LANDOWNERS; (5) DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS IN RANGE AND FISH AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT; (6) ASSIST IN PROVIDING CONTINUING EDUCATION PROGRAMS FOR PROFESSIONALLY TRAINED INDIVIDUALS IN FISH AND WILDLIFE, FOREST, RANGE, WATERSHED MANAGEMENT AND RELATED FIELDS; (7) HELP FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS IN SECURING TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO BRING APPROPRIATE EXPERTISE TO BEAR ON THEIR PROBLEMS; AND (8) HELP IDENTIFY AREAS OF NEEDED RESEARCH REGARDING RENEWABLE RESOURCE. THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT (UCONN), COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, HEALTH, AND NATURAL RECOURSES (CAHNR) RREA PROGRAM SUPPORTS EXTENSION ACTIVITIES THAT PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS AND OUTREACH RELATING TO TREE EQUITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL/CLIMATE JUSTICE FOR FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS, MUNICIPAL TREE WARDENS, AND OTHER PUBLIC OFFICIALS IN MAKING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. IN ADDITION, OUR PROGRAM SUPPORTS COMMUNITY FORESTRY VOLUNTEERS AND MANAGERS. OUTPUTS FROM OUR PROGRAM INCLUDE PEER REVIEW PUBLICATIONS, RESEARCH PRESENTATIONS, AND TREE WARDEN WORKSHOPS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME INCLUDES THE KNOWLEDGE OUR TARGET AUDIENCE WILL GAIN FROM RESEARCH-BASED EXTENSION OUTREACH PROGRAMS TO HELP THEM MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS THAT SUPPORT THE SUSTAINABILITY OF RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCE AND ADOPT BEHAVIORS THAT LEAD TO SAFER, HEALTHIER AND GREENER COMMUNITIES. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES FOR OUR RREA PROGRAM INCLUDE WOODLAND OWNERS, FORESTRY PROFESSIONALS, LOCAL AND REGIONAL FORESTRY ORGANIZATIONS, STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, TREE WARDENS, MUNICIPAL ENGINEERS, COMMUNITY FORESTRY VOLUNTEERS AND PLANNING/ZONING BOARDS, ALONG WITH UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. WE ARE EXPANDING OUR AUDIENCE BECAUSE (1) FORESTRY PROFESSIONALS ARE NOT A VERY DIVERSE DEMOGRAPHIC, (2) FORESTRY TODAY REQUIRES TRANSDISCIPLINARY PARTNERSHIPS TO ENSURE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF OUR PROGRAMS, AND (3) WE WANT TO SUPPORT UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES BY AMPLIFYING THEIR VOICES IN THE TREE CANOPY EXPANSION/MANAGEMENT PROCESS.

negativeFlows.title: 2022 DELAWARE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION PROGRAM ABSTRACT DELAWARE HAS AN INCREASING NUMBER OF FOREST ACREAGE THAT IS BEING CONVERTED TO HOUSES AND PARKING LOTS. THE STATE IS ALSO LOSING MANY OF ITS NATURAL RESOURCE-BASED BUSINESSES, WHICH HAS A NEGATIVE IMPACT ON LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND FAMILIES. THE LAND CONVERSION PROBLEM CAN BE RESOLVED THROUGH EDUCATION AND AWARENESS OF THE PUBLIC THROUGH TOURS, WORKSHOPS, AND DEMONSTRATIONS IMPLEMENTED BY DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY. OUR STAFF WILL ALSO HELP TO EDUCATE CURRENT AND FUTURE NATURAL RESOURCE ENTREPRENEURS ABOUT THE EXISTING OR POTENTIAL NEW FORESTRY BUSINESSES AND PRACTICES IN AN ATTEMPT TO REVERSE THE CURRENT LOSS OF OPPORTUNITIES IN THIS HISTORIC INDUSTRY. THE MAIN OBJECTIVE OF THE RREA PROGRAM WILL BE TO FACILITATE FORESTRY-BASED ENTERPRISES “INCLUDING WOOD PRODUCTS AND NON-TIMBER FORE ST PRODUCTS” IN DELAWARE. DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (DSU) WILL ADDRESS THIS OBJECTIVE BY PRESENTING WORKSHOPS, WHICH WILL GIVE OVER 150 PEOPLE IN THE STATE OF DELAWARE AWARENESS OF THE NEW AND EXISTING FORESTRY BUSINESS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO INCREASE IN GENERAL KNOWLEDGE AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY IN DELAWARE BY DEVELOPING EDUCATIONAL AWARENESS PROGRAMS FOR YOUTH. TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, WE WILL DESIGN ON OUTDOOR TOURS TO REACH A DIVERSE AUDIENCE OF APPROXIMATELY 400 ADULTS AND SCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN IN ORDER TO STRENGTHEN THEIR KNOWLEDGE OF LAND AND FOREST CONSERVATION. THE RREA PROJECT IN DELAWARE WITH INCREASE THE NUMBER OF ACRES UNDER NEW MANAGEMENT PRACTICES BY 15% IN DELAWARE. DSU STAFF WILL WORK WITH 75 PROPERTY OWNERS THROUGH SITE VISITS TO INCREASE BOTH KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS OF THE OWNERS. THE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP SOME NEW PLANS FOR ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY PRACTICES IN DELAWARE. THE APPROACH WILL HAVE DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (DSU) CONDUCTING THREE WORKSHOPS TO EDUCATE LANDOWNERS AND ENTREPRENEURS ABOUT OPPORTUNITIES THAT EXIST WITHIN THE FORESTRY INDUSTRY. DSU WILL ALSO DELIVER OUTDOOR ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION TOURS TO GIVE YOUTH AND ADULTS HANDS-ON LEARNING ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT AND OUR NATURAL RESOURCES. WORKSHOPS, EDUCATIONAL TOURS AND DEMONSTRATIONS WILL BE ASSESSED BY MEASURING PARTICIPANT NUMBERS FOR EACH EVENT AND THROUGH WRITTEN EVALUATION FORMS. EXTENSION AGENTS WILL BE PROVIDING PROPERTY OWNERS WITH ONE-ON-ONE STYLE EDUCATION ON FOREST HEALTH, WATER QUALITY, AND WILDLIFE HABITAT. THE QUALITY OF WORK PERFORMED BY DSU STAFF WILL BE MEASURED BY THE IMPACT OF CONSERVATION PLANS DEVELOPED ON EACH PROPERTY, THE NUMBER OF PERSONAL CONTACTS MADE, AND BY THE NUMBER OF ACRES ENHANCED THROUGH GOOD CONSERVATION PRACTICES.

PROJECT ABSTRACT WISCONSIN IS A LARGELY FORESTED LANDSCAPE COVERING 16 MILLION ACRES, ABOUT 46% OF THE STATE'S LAND AREA. OVERALL, 57% OF THE FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES, TOTALING 360,000 OWNERS. FOREST INDUSTRY IS VITAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY; THE STATE CONTINUES TO BE THE NUMBER ONE PAPER PRODUCING STATE IN THE COUNTRY, AND FOREST PRODUCT INDUSTRIES ARE SCATTERED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. THIS INDUSTRY RELIES HEAVILY ON FAMILY OWNED FORESTLAND. THE WDNR ESTIMATES THAT 10% OF THE 9.1 MILLION FORESTED ACRES, HELD BY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS, WILL BE SOLD, SUBDIVIDED OR CONVERTED TO NON‐FOREST USE IN THE NEXT 5 YEARS. IN A SIMILAR STUDY, THE SUSTAINING FAMILY FORESTS INITIATIVE (SFFI) FOUND THE HIGHEST CONCERN REPORTED BY 56% OF ALL LANDOWNERS WAS "KEEPING LAND INTACT FOR CHILDREN/HEIRS". INCIDENTALLY, THE SECOND HIGHEST CONCERN WAS "HIGH PROPERTY TAXES". A THIRD STUDY, BY GOBSTER AND RICKENBACH (2004) LOOKED AT PERCEPTIONS OF PARCELIZATION. THE PRIMARY DRIVERS INCLUDED ECONOMIC, DEMOGRAPHIC, VALUES <(>&<)> MOTIVATIONS, GLOBALIZATION <(>&<)> TECHNOLOGY, NATURAL CAPITAL, AND POLICIES. THUS EDUCATING LANDOWNERS ON RECOGNIZING THE BEST ECONOMIC RETURN ON TIMBER HARVESTS, UNDERSTANDING HOW DIVIDING PROPERTY AFFECTS THE ECOSYSTEM, AND WHAT POLICIES EXISTS TO ASSIST WITH MANAGEMENT WILL ASSIST WITH THESE ISSUES. OUR COMPREHENSIVE FORESTRY OUTREACH PROGRAM ZEROS IN ON THESE CONCERNS. DURING FFY2023, WISCONSIN RREA PROGRAMMING WILL ADDRESS RENEWABLE RESOURCES IN A VARIETY OF PROGRAMS AND PARTNERSHIPS TO ADDRESS STRATEGIC AND CROSS‐CUTTING NATIONAL ISSUES RELATING TO GOALS IDENTIFIED IN THE NIFA RREA STRATEGIC PLAN. GOAL 1‐ ENSURING HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND GOAL 3 ‐ ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THE PRIMARY CROSS‐CUTTING ISSUES WE WILL FOCUS ON INCLUDE FISH AND WILDLIFE R ESOURCES, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND INTERGENERATIONAL LAND AND OTHER LAND OWNERSHIP CHANGES. THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO HELP LANDOWNERS DEVELOP FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AROUND WOODLAND ECOLOGY, HEALTHY FORESTS, TIMBER HARVEST PRACTICES AND SALES, HABITAT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT BENEFIT WILDLIFE, STRATEGIES FOR THREATS SUCH AS INVASIVE SPECIES AND CLIMATE VARIABILITY, LAND OWNERSHIP AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRANSFERS, AND TO IMPLEMENT PRACTICES TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINABLE FOREST RESOURCES AND TO MEET PERSONAL MANAGEMENT GOALS. THROUGH IN‐PERSON CLASSES, DISTANCE CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WE ARE EXPECTING TO INCREASE LANDOWNERS' AND RESOURCES PROFESSIONALS' SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE TO AFFECT LONG‐TERM CHANGES IN ACTIVE MANAGEMENT BY WOODLAND OWNERS THAT WILL SUPPORT SUCCESSION TO FAMILY MEMBERS, REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF PARCELIZATION THROUGH STABLE LAND OWNERSHIP, AND RETAIN FOREST COVER AND CONTRIBUTE SUSTAINABLY TO THE WOOD FUEL CYCLE THROUGH REGULAR PLANNED TIMBER SALES.

CARING FOR PUERTO RICO’S URBAN TREES THE ISLAND OF PUERTO RICO IS LOCATED IN THE CARIBBEAN AREA. ITS CLIMATE VARIABILITY PRINCIPALLY DEPENDS ON ITS TOPOGRAPHY AND THE NORTHEASTERLY TRADE WINDS THAT RECEIVES YEARLY (USGS, 2016). THROUGH EACH YEAR IS SUBJECT TO “VAGUADAS”, WHICH ARE HEAVY RAIN EVENTS, BUT DURING JUNE 1ST TO NOVEMBER 30TH, WE HAVE TO BE PREPARED BECAUSE IT IS THE HURRICANE SEASON (NMEAD, 2022). THIS NATURAL EVENTS IMPACT THE ISLAND, INCLUDING THE FORESTS AND URBAN FORESTS. IN SEPTEMBER OF 2017, CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE MARÍA HIT THE ISLAND, WITH SUSTAINED WINDS OF 155 MILES PER HOUR (THE WEATHER CHANNEL, 2017), THAT DESTROYED AND UPROOTED TREES AND, THOSE THAT STILL STANDING, WERE WITHOUT ANY LEAVES, AND ITS 15-20 INCHES OF RAIN, CAUSED FLOODS AND LANDSLIDES THAT ALSO AFFECTED THE TREES (SCOTT, 2018). ON SEPTEMBER OF 2022, THE ISLAND WAS IMPACTED AGAIN BY HURRICANE FIONA, WITH 85 MILES PER HOUR WINDS AND 30-60 INCHES OF RAIN. AGAIN, THE FORESTS AND URBAN FORESTS TREES WERE DAMAGED BY THE WINDS OR BY THE LANDSLIDES. THESE EVENTS ALSO CREATE ANOTHER PROBLEM, WHICH IS THE DAMAGE FALLING TREES CAN CAUSE TO INFRASTRUCTURE, LIKE ELECTRICITY AND COMMUNICATIONS LINES, TO BUILDINGS AND TO HOUSES AND CARS. AND, AS CLIMATE CHANGE AFFECTS THE PLANET, FOR PUERTO RICO THE EFFECTS INCLUDE AN INCREASE IN THE FREQUENCY OF EXTREME EVENTS AND, THOSE WILL HAVE AN INCREASE IN THE AMOUNT OF RAIN (WATER ENVIRONMENT FEDERATION, 2021). FOR THIS, IT IS NECESSARY TO EDUCATE THE PUERTO RICO AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION SERVICE (PRAES) AGRICULTURAL AGENTS IN TOPICS RELATED TO GREEN SPACES EMERGENCY PLAN PREPARATION, DAMAGE EVALUATION, TREES PRUNING AND PROTECTION, AND CONSIDERATIONS FOR TREE SELECTION IN URBAN AREAS. THIS CAN BE DELIVERED AS A SHORT COURSE, THAT THEY CAN THEN OFFER TO THE COMMUNITY LEADERS. WE EXPECT THAT THIS WILL HELP REDUCE THE IMPACT OF EXTREME EVENTS IN, AT LEAST, THE URBAN TREES AND THE STRUCTURES AROUND THEM. REFERENCES: NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION (NASA). FY 2023 RREA GRANT PROPOSAL WITH BUDGET NARRATIVE PROJECT TITLE: SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT FOR SMALL-SCALE FARMERS AND WOODLAND OWNERS IN NORTH CAROLINA AND THE SOUTHERN USA ABSTRACT: CURRENT TRENDS SHOW THAT SMALL-SCALE FARMS AND LIMITED RESOURCE FARMS CARRY CRITICAL AND ESSENTIAL FAMILY ECONOMIC ASSETS TO NORTH CAROLINA AND IN THE SOUTHERN UNITED STATES REGION. THESE LANDOWNERS (HAVING LANDHOLDING OF ~20 ACRES AND BELOW) GENERALLY DO NOT REALIZE THE FULL BENEFIT OF THEIR LANDS AND THEREFORE ARE UNABLE TO COMPETE WITH LARGE-SCALE FARMS AND WOOD LANDOWNERS. USING OUR CURRENT FIVE-YEAR STRATEGIC PLAN BY AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCE UNIT AT NCAT (I.E. MISSION POSSIBLE), OUR PROGRAM IS GEARED AT PROVIDING EDUCATIONAL AND OUTREACH PROGRAMS TO GUIDE AND MOTIVATE THESE SMALL-SCALE, LIMITED RESOURCES AND SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS AND WOODLAND OWNERS TO MAKE MORE SUSTAINABLE DECISIONS. IT WILL NOT ONLY IMPROVE THEIR ECONOMIC CONDITIONS BUT ALSO IMPROVE OVERALL LIFESTYLE WHILE GENERATING LONG-TERM STEWARDS OF THE ENVIRONMENT. OUR PROGRAM WILL IMPLEMENT THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES: I) BUILD A VERY STRONG PARTNERSHIP WITH FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER NOT-FOR-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS TO IDENTIFY CLUSTERS OF LANDOWNERS (YOUTH, ADULT, NEW, BEGINNING, AND VETERANS) INTERESTED IN REALIZING THE FULL BENEFIT OF THEIR LANDS; II) CONDUCT IN- SERVICE TRAINING (~TRAIN THE TRAINER TYPE) WITH OUR COUNTY AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES EXTENSION AGENTS AND OTHER PARAPROFESSIONALS INTERESTED IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES-RELATED OPERATIONS (I.E. SOI, WATER AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY) AND ALSO, LAND-LOSS ISSUES; AND III) ASSIST SMALL-SCALE GROWERS AND LANDOWNERS TO APPLY AND COMPLETE COST-SHARE APPLICATIONS FROM THE USDA AND ALSO, APPLY FOR EXISTING GOVERNMENT LOANS AND GRANTS RELATEDTO SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP. USING THE EXISTING EDUCATIONAL TRAINING MATERIALS THROUGH THE TRAIN-THE-TRAINER MODEL, THIS PROJECT INTENDS TO TRAIN COUNTY EXTENSION AGENTS, SMALL-SCALE FARMERS, WOODLAND, AND OTHER LANDOWNERS WITH AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND AGROFORESTRY SKILLS AND THEIR PROPERTY BASICS TO STEM THE LAND LOSS. FOR SMALL-SCALE FARMERS AND WOODLAND OWNERS IN NORTH CAROLINA AND THE SOUTHERN UNITED STATES REGION, AGROFORESTRY CAN CONTRIBUTE TOWARDS SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE BY MINIMIZING INPUTS AND COSTS, REDUCING ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS, AND PROVIDING ADDITIONAL ECONOMIC BENEFITS TO THE FARMERS AND WOODLAND OWNERS.

THESE FIGURES REFLECT LIVELIHOODS, RURAL RESILIENCE, AND CULTURAL HERITAGE TIED TO THE LAND. THIS ECONOMY DEPENDS ON HEALTHY PRIVATE LANDS AND LANDOWNER STEWARDSHIP. TEXAS IS EXPERIENCING ITS LARGEST INTERGENERATIONAL LAND TRANSFER-56M ACRES ARE SET TO CHANGE HANDS. MANY NEW LANDOWNERS, ESPECIALLY THOSE WITH SMALLER PARCELS, LACK ACCESS TO SCIENCE-BASED LAND MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE. THE TEXAS A<(>&<)>M NATURAL RESOURCES INSTITUTE IDENTIFIED AN ACREAGE THRESHOLD WHERE PROFITABILITY SHIFTS FOR THOSE RELYING ON FARMING, RANCHING, OR TIMBER. TEXAS'S POPULATION IS PROJECTED TO GROW FROM 30M TO 42M BY 2045. AS LAND SUSTAINS LIFE THROUGH AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL PROCESSES, THE LOSS OR CONVERSION OF AGRICULTURAL LAND IS A GROWING CONCERN. AGING LANDOWNERS WILL PASS WORKING LANDS TO YOUNGER, OFTEN INEXPERIENCED HEIRS WHO MAY LACK AGRICULTURAL KNOWLEDGE OR FINANCIAL RESOURCES, ACCELERATING LAND SALES AND CONVERSION. THIS THREATENS FOOD AND WATER SECURITY AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. TO ADDRESS THIS, TEXAS A<(>&<)>M AGRILIFE EXTENSION SERVICE WILL INVEST RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT FUNDS TO CREATE OR ENHANCE PROGRAMS THAT GUIDE LANDOWNERS TOWARD PROFITABILITY THROUGH NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT. THE DEPARTMENT OF RANGELANDS, WILDLIFE AND FISHERIES MANAGEMENT HAS A STRONG TEAM OF EXTENSION SPECIALISTS EMBEDDED IN RURAL COMMUNITIES, WITH LONG-STANDING RELATIONSHIPS THAT WILL SUPPORT OUTREACH. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE NEW LANDOWNERS, EARLY-CAREER PROFESSIONALS, CITIZEN SCIENTISTS (E.G., TEXAS MASTER NATURALISTS), AND POLICYMAKERS. PROGRAMS WILL PROMOTE STEWARDSHIP KNOWLEDGE, SMART LAND PRACTICES-WHERE STACKING CONSERVATION PRACTICES ON THE SAME ACREAGE YIELDS FINANCIAL BENEFITS OR URBAN SAVINGS (E.G., CREATING RANGELAND SPONGES TO REDUCE CATASTROPHIC URBAN FLOODING). PRESCRIBED FIRE WILL BE EMPHASIZED FOR WILDFIRE DEFENSE AND LANDSCAPE REJUVENATION. THE 2024 SMOKEHOUSE CREEK FIRE BURNED 1.2M ACRES AND CAUSED $123M IN AGRICULTURAL LOSSES. PRESCRIBED BURNING COULD HAVE MITIGATED THESE IMPACTS. LANDOWNERS MUST UNDERSTAND PLANT COMMUNITIES TO MANAGE WILDFIRES EFFECTIVELY. TRAINING WILL ALSO ADDRESS PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND LAND PRACTICES TO SUPPORT LIVESTOCK AND WILDLIFE. INVASIVE SPECIES-WHETHER INTRODUCED UNINTENTIONALLY OR MALICIOUSLY-REQUIRE FOCUSED SOLUTIONS. PROGRAMS WILL TACKLE ISSUES LIKE INVASIVE WILD SWINE, BRUSH, AND EXOTIC GRASSES. WE EXPECT TO SAVE MILLIONS BY DELIVERING SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION THROUGH VISITS, PRESENTATIONS, DEMONSTRATIONS, AND A ROBUST ONLINE PRESENCE WITH EDUCATIONAL MODULES FOR INDIVIDUALS, RURAL COMMUNITIES, AND SUBURBAN RESIDENTS. AS CONSERVATION AND SUSTAINABLE LAND USE GROW AMONG TEXAS LANDOWNERS, PRIVATE STEWARDS-WHO MANAGE MILLIONS OF ACRES-REMAIN CENTRAL TO THE STATE'S ECOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SECURITY FUTURE. RREASUPPORTED PROGRAMMING WILL UNLOCK CONSERVATION VALUE, STRENGTHEN RURAL ECONOMIES, AND PREPARE THE NEXT GENERATION TO CARRY FORWARD TEXAS'S LEGACY OF STEWARDSHIP. PROJECT ABSTRACT

APPROXIMATELY 35% OF ALASKA'S LAND AREA (126 MILLION ACRES) IS FORESTED. MOST ALASKANS LIVE IN OR NEAR A FOREST, WITH FORESTS BEING UNIQUELY INTEGRAL TO THE LIVES AND LIVELIHOODS OF THE MAJORITY OF THOSE WHO RESIDE IN THIS STATE. FORESTS PROVIDE A MULTITUDE OF RESOURCES INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: TIMBER AND OTHER WOOD PRODUCTS, HARVESTING FOOD AND HUNTING, ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, WILDLIFE HABITAT, AND RECREATION. FORESTED LAND IN ALASKA IS OWNED AND MANAGED BY MULTIPLE ENTITIES: FEDERAL, STATE, LOCAL, NATIVE AND PRIVATE. VARYING INTERESTS OF LAND OWNERS, EXTREME WEATHER, WILDFIRES, AND LIMITED ACCESSIBLE INFORMATION POSE CHALLENGES FOR MAKING INFORMED DECISIONS REGARDING FOREST MANAGEMENT. INCREASED ACCESS TO RESEARCH-BASED AND RELEVANT FORESTRY INFORMATION IS FUNDAMENTAL FOR DECISION-MAKING AND MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT SUSTAIN PRODUCTIVE FORESTS ACROSS ALL LAND OWNERSHIP AND USE. THIS PROJECT WILL PRODUCE ACCESSIBLE AND VARIED RESOURCES INTENDED FOR PRIVATE LAND OWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS THAT COMMUNICATE RELEVANT FORESTRY RESEARCH. THE PROJECT WILL CONTINUE TO PARTNER WITH COMMUNITIES AND ORGANIZATIONS STATEWIDE IN ORDER TO INCREASE THE IMPACT OF FORESTRY EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION AND EXPAND INNOVATION OF FOREST USE AND PRODUCTIVITY. THIS PROGRAM WILL UTILIZE VARIOUS OUTREACH MATERIALS DEPENDING ON THE NEEDS OF THE INTENDED AUDIENCE INCLUDING WEB-BASED RESOURCES, PRINTED PUBLICATIONS, PODCASTS, AND EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS AND PROGRAMMING. PERTINENT MATERIALS WILL BE CREATED TO CONVEY THE RESEARCH AND OUTREACH CONDUCTED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS, SPECIFICALLY THE FOREST SOILS LAB AND ONETREE ALASKA. EMPHASIS WILL BE PLACED ON TOPICS SUCH AS THE MANAGEMENT OF SPRUCE BARK BEETLE IMPACTS, HARVESTING FIREWOOD FOR EFFICIENT DRYING TIMES, MANAGING LAND FOR WATER RETENTION AND FOREST FIRE PROTECTION, AND COLLECTING AND UTILIZING BIRCH SAP. STATE-WIDE COLLABORATION WILL FOCUS ON WORKSHOPS THAT DEVELOP KNOWLEDGE OF FORESTRY PRACTICES AND FACILITATE FORESTRY WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL WORK WITH THE STATE OF ALASKA DIVISION OF FORESTRY AND FIRE PROTECTION AND THE ALASKA FIRE SCIENCE CONSORTIUM TO EXPAND ON THE INFORMATION AVAILABLE FOR EDUCATING HOMEOWNERS ABOUT PREPARING FOR AND RESPONDING TO WILDFIRE EVENTS. THE MEANINGFUL DISTRIBUTION OF ACCURATE, RELEVANT AND ENGAGING FORESTRY INFORMATION IS CRUCIAL FOR SUSTAINING HEALTHY FORESTS ACROSS ALASKA. HEALTHY FORESTS BENEFIT ALL LIVELIHOODS IN THE STATE, ESPECIALLY AS PR ODUCTIVE FORESTS ENCOURAGE LOCAL RESOURCE USE, IN TURN REDUCING LIVING COSTS AND INCREASING SUPPORT OF DOMESTIC MARKETS.

UC ANR RREA PROGRAM ABSTRACT DESCRIPTION <(>&<)> BENEFICIARIES THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT OF 1978 (RREA) SUPPORTS AN EXPANDED AND COMPREHENSIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM FOR FOREST AND RANGELAND RENEWABLE RESOURCES. RREA SUPPORTS FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS IN THE SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF WOOD PRODUCTS, FORAGE AND LIVESTOCK, FISH AND WILDLIFE POPULATIONS AND DEVELOPING OUTDOOR RECREATION OPPORTUNITIES. UC AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES OVERSEES THE UC RREA PROGRAM WHICH FOCUSES ON EIGHT ISSUE AREAS. PUBLIC AWARENESS AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT: ENGAGING YOUTH AND ADULTS ABOUT THE IMPORTANCE OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES, PARTICULARLY HOW FOREST LANDS AND RANGELANDS AFFECT RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES AND THE NEED TO USE SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION WHEN MAKING DECISIONS ABOUT THESE RESOURCES. ECOSYSTEM SERVICES: ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS AND MANAGERS IN ACTIVELY MANAGING THEIR LANDS WITH KNOWLEDGE OF FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM PROCESSES AND HOW SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES PRODUCE DIFFERENT COMBINATIONS OF ECO SYSTEM SERVICES; AND ASSISTING FOREST AND RANGELAND USERS IN UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE DIFFERENT ECOSYSTEM SERVICES HAVE ON COMMUNITY WELL-BEING. FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT: ENSURING THAT PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS HAVE THE BEST AVAILABLE INFORMATION ABOUT FISH AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT HABITAT MANAGEMENT IN FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS. GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION AND OTHER LANDOWNERSHIP CHANGES: ENHANCING THE DECISION-MAKING ABILITY OF RANCH AND FOREST LANDOWNER FAMILIES FOR GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION BY PROVIDING INFORMATION ON AND FACILITATING COMMUNICATION ABOUT SUCH PLANNING OPTIONS AS CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, COMMUNITY-BASED NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT OR OTHER NON-TRADITIONAL SUCCESSION MODELS; TRAINING AND LINKING INTERESTED PARTIES IN COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS THAT WILL AUGMENT GENERATIONAL TRANSFER OF FOREST AND RANGELAND ENTERPRISES. INVASIVE SPECIES: INCREASING THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO ASSESS THE THREAT OF INVASIVE SPECIES; DEVELOPING INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT PLANS; IMPLEMENTING EFFECTIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL STRATEGIES TO PROTECT FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEMS; PROVIDING MEANS FOR THE GENERAL PUBLIC (INCLUDING ABSENTEE LANDOWNERS), YOUTH, AND COMMUNITY GROUPS FOR THEIR INTERACTION AND PARTICIPATION IN MONITORING AND CONTROLLING INVASIVE SPECIES. RURAL COMMUNITIES: WORKING WITH RURAL COMMUNITIES TO ASSESS NEEDS AND DETERMINE HOW TO SUSTAINABLY ENHANCE LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT THROUGH A FOCUS ON FOREST AND RANGELAND INDUSTRIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, AND EXPERTISE; CREATING A STRONGER RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HEALTHY FORESTS AND RANGELANDS AND THE SOCIAL AND SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC BASES OF RURAL COMMUNITIES; ASSESSING NEEDS AND DETERMINING HOW TO ENHANCE LOCAL LANDSCAPE ECONOMICS. WATER AND WETLANDS: ENCOURAGING MANAGEMENT OF FORESTS AND RANGELANDS TO IMPROVE WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY. WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT: ENGAGING FOREST AND RANGELAND COMMUNITIES WITH RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION ON WILDFIRE RISK-MANAGEMENT AND POST-FIRE RECOVERY STRATEGIES; INCREASING T HE CAPACITY OF COMMUNITY, COUNTY, AND STATE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS/CIVIL DEFENSE AUTHORITIES TO COMMUNICATE COMMUNITY NEEDS AND INFORM COMMUNITY-DEVELOPMENT POLICIES, CODES, AND ORDINANCES THAT PROTECT COMMUNITIES FROM WILDFIRE; DEVELOPING OUTREACH EFFORTS THAT IN CLUDE CURRENT AND EMERGING RESEARCH ON IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE ON FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOLOGY AND ECONOMICS, FUELS MANAGEMENT, AND PRESCRIBED FIRE TO CREATE APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES; INCREASING CAPACITY FOR COMMUNITY ACTION, EMPOWER LANDOWNERS TO ENGAGE IN P RESCRIBED FIRE, AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR TRAINING AND CAPACITY IN FUELS REDUCTION.

positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT FUNDING RECEIVED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA WARNELL SCHOOL OF FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES IS TO SUPPORT THE OUTREACH EFFORTS OF OUR EXTENSION FACULTY AND BRING SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION TO OUR TARGET AUDIENCES, SUCH AS GEORGIA FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, TO HELP THEM MAKE CRITICAL MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. WE EDUCATE GEORGIA CITIZENS ABOUT HOW AND WHY NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES ARE PRESCRIBED AND CONDUCTED. WE PROVIDE CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDIT COURSES REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN PROFESSIONAL CREDENTIALS. THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED IN THE COMING YEAR INCLUDE: 1) WORKSHOPS; 2) APPLIED RESEARCH; 3) PEER REVIEWED AND EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS; 4) PRESENTATIONS; AND 5) FOSTER PARTNER COLLABORATIONS. THE DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE: WORKSHOPS: THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM WILL PLAN, ORGANIZE AND DELIVER WORKSHOPS COVERING TOPICS THAT INCLUDE THE IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES, TIMBER TAXATION, INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT, FOREST HEALTH, URBAN WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION CERTIFICATION, AND AQUATIC RESOURCE MANAGEMENT. WORKSHOPS WILL BE PLANNED TO BE BOTH PROACTIVE AND REACTIVE. OUR ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION SPECIALISTS WILL OFFER EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EVENTS FOR STUDENTS AND TEACHERS USING INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED CURRICULA (PROJECT LEARNING TREE, PROJECT WILD, AND PROJECT WET). APPLIED RESEARCH: ACTIVITIES WILL INVOLVE MAINTAINING EXISTING AND DEVELOPING NEW SITES TO EVALUATE AND SERVE AS DEMONSTRATIONS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF APPLIED RESEARCH EFFORTS IS TO STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION WITH STATE/FEDERAL AGENCY PARTNERS AND PRIVATE INDUSTRY SPONSORS, AND AS DATA CONTINUES TO BE GATHERED AND ANALYZED, AN INCREASED USE OF THESE SITES AS EFFECTIVE DEMONSTRATION SITES FOR FIELD DAYS AND WORKSHOPS. PUBLICATIONS: TOPICS TO BE COVERED INCLUDE FIRESCAPING, WILD HARVESTING PRACTICES, WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, AND INTENSIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES (HERBICIDE APPLICATION AND SITE PREPARATION). ALL PUBLICATIONS WILL BE PRODUCED WITH THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOME OF SPREADING TRUSTED INFORMATION AND INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PUBLICATIONS POSTED ON OUR WARNELL OUTREACH WEBSITE WHERE WE CAN TRACK THE NUMBER OF VIEWS AND DOWNLOADS. INNOVATIVE EDUCATIONAL VIDEOS WILL ALSO BE PRODUCED TO ALLOW CLIENTELE TO ACCESS INFORMATION CONVENIENTLY USING SMART PHONE TECHNOLOGY. PRESENTATIONS: WE HAVE PLANS TO COVER MANY TOPICS INCLUDING URBAN WILDLIFE ISSUES, FIRESCAPING, COMMUNITY FORESTRY, FOREST MANAGEMENT, EXTENSION TEACHING ACADEMY, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, AQUATIC RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, WOODY PLANT ID, AND OTHER TOPICS AS IDENTIFIED. THE OUTCOME OF OUR EFFORTS IS TO SHARE QUALITY UP-TO-DATE INFORMATION WITH GEORGIA CITIZENS THAT HELP THEM MAKE INFORMED NATURAL RESOURCE RELATED DECISIONS. PARTNER COLLABORATION: OUR TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO NURTURE EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, EDUCATORS (K- 16), AND INDUSTRY. WE ANTICIPATE THE OUTCOME OF THESE PARTNERSHIPS TO BE SUSTAINED SUPPORT AND COLLABORATION. WEB-BASED PRODUCTS: OUR WEB DEVELOPMENT TEAM WILL CONTINUE TO UPDATE SMARTPHONE APPS AND WEBSITES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF OUR EFFORTS WILL BE TO OFFER WEB-BASED TOOLS THAT INCREASE INFORMATION SHARING AND DATA COLLECTION AND PROVIDE EXPERIENCES THAT BUILD NEW SKILLS AND BENEFIT OUR TARGET AUDIENCES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE WARNELL OUTREACH TEAM ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS, PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, PRIVATE CONSULTANTS, COUNTY EXTENSION ANR AGENTS, CITY/COUNTY GOVERNMENT STAFF, K-12 TEACHERS AND STUDENTS, SPECIAL INTEREST GROUPS, ASSOCIATIONS, NGOS AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, AND ALL CITIZENS OF GEORGIA. THERE ARE NO SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES PLANNED AT THE TIME OF THIS AWARD

FOREST HEALTH IN THE SOUTHEAST IS THREATENED BY NUMEROUS INVASIVE PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND PATHOGENS. IT'S CRUCIAL TO EMPOWER LANDOWNERS AND RESOURCE MANAGERS TO MITIGATE THESE IMPACTS. OUR MAIN GOAL IS TO RAISE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF INVASIVE SPECIES, MAINTAIN PARTNERSHIPS WITH RELEVANT ORGANIZATIONS, AND IDENTIFY EMERGING INVASIVE PLANT, INSECT, AND ANIMAL PESTS. THE PRIMARY TARGET AUDIENCES ARE FOREST LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS (E.G., FORESTERS, LOGGERS, WILDLIFE BIOLOGISTS) AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT STUDENTS. BECAUSE NON-NATIVE PLANTS USED IN LANDSCAPING ARE A MAJOR SOURCE OF THE INVASIVE PLANTS THAT INVADE FORESTS, A SECONDARY AUDIENCE IS HOMEOWNERS, MASTER GARDENERS, THE GENERAL PUBLIC, AND K-12 EDUCATORS. PRIMARY COMMUNICATION PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS ON INVASIVE PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL, SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS, BLOGS, AND ARTICLES FOR THE POPULAR PRESS AND TEAM NEWSLETTER, CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE ACES FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE WEBPAGE, AND HIGHDEFINITION PHOTOGRAPHS OF INVASIVE PLANTS AND ANIMALS FOR EDUCATIONAL PRODUCTS AND OUTREACH. OUTREACH EVENTS WILL INCLUDE CO-CHAIRING THE STATE-WIDE ANNUAL ALABAMA I NVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL CONFERENCE; ORGANIZING AND PARTICIPATING IN ACES WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DAYS; PROVIDING SEMINARS AND WEBINARS FOR FOREST INDUSTRY, FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AGENCIES, MASTER GARDENERS, CIVIC GROUPS, AND OTHERS AS REQUESTED (TYPICALLY ABOUT 20 EVENTS A YEAR.) MANY OF THESE EVENTS PROVIDE CECS FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS. EACH YEAR, WE RECEIVE OVER A HUNDRED QUESTIONS ABOUT PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND TREATMENT OPTIONS FOR INVASIVE PLANTS FROM STAKEHOLDERS. THESE ARE ADDRESSED VIA PHONE, EMAIL, TEXT, AND SOCIAL MEDIA. ADDITIONALLY, WE TEACH AUBURN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS ABOUT INVASIVE PLANTS, LEAD EFFORTS TO UPDATE THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL (ALIPC) INVASIVE PLANT LIST, AND PROVIDE EXPERTISE TO LOCAL INVASIVE PLANT CONTROL EFFORTS. BUILDING CAPACITY BY COLLABORATING WITH STATE AND LOCAL AGENCIES, SERVING ON STATEWIDE INVASIVE PLANT TASK FORCES, AND MAINTAINING A LEADERSHIP ROLE WITHIN THE ALABAMA INVASIVE PLANT COUNCIL. WE ENCOURAGE THE USE OF THE NATIONAL EARLY DETECTION AND DISTRIBUTION MAPPING SYSTEM (EDDMAPS) FOR MAPPING AND MONITORING THE SPREAD OF INVASIVE PLANTS. REMAINING ACTIVE IN NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS LIKE THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF INVASIVE PLANT COUNCILS (NAIPC) AND NORTH AMERICAN INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION (NAISMA) HELPS MAINTAIN REGIONAL AND NATIONAL CONNECTIONS AND AWARENESS OF INVASIVE PLANT ISSUES AND POLICIES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMMEDIATE BENEFITS SUCH AS INCREASED ABILITY TO IDENTIFY AND MONITOR INVASIVE SPECIES, MORE EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES, REDUCED USE OF INVASIVE SPECIES IN LANDSCAPING, AND PROVIDING CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDITS FOR NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS. THE ULTIMATE BENEFIT IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH THROUGH REDUCED SPREAD AND IMPACTS OF INVASIVE PLANTS. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH INCREASED KNOWLEDGE AND ACTION AMONG LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS WHO KNOW HOW TO IDENTIFY INVASIVE PLANTS, WHERE TO ACCESS SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION AND RESOURCES, AND INCREASED AWARENESS OF EDDMAPS. A CHANGE IN ACTION WILL BE INCREASED MONITORING AND CONTROL EFFORTS BY LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS, LEADING TO MORE ACRES BEING TREATED AND FEWER BEHAVIORS SPREADING INVASIVE PLANTS. THIS WILL ALSO RESULT IN FEWER HOMEOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS USING RISKY NON-NATIVE PLANTS AND AN INCREASE IN THE USE OF EDDMAPS TO REPORT INVASIVE PLANTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS IMPROVED FOREST HEALTH AND RESILIENCY THROUGH REDUCED USE OF NON-NATIVE PLANTS IN LANDSCAPING AND WILDLIFE PLANTINGS, REDUCED BEHAVIORS THAT SPREAD INVASIVE PLANTS, AND EARLIER AND MORE EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OF INVASIVE PLANTS. IMPROVING INVASIVE PLANT LISTING AND MAPPING WILL PROVIDE MORE ACCURATE DISTRIBUTION MAPS AND BETTER INFORM MANAGEMENT DECISIONS.

THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROVIDES FUNDING FOR EXTENSION ACTIVITIES RELATED TO FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES AT LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITIES. THE USDA RENEWABLE RESOURCE EXTENSION ACT (RREA), PASSED BY CONGRESS IN 1978, PROVIDES FUNDING TO EXPAND THE REACH OF FOREST AND RANGELAND EXTENSION PROGRAMS AT 73 LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITIES THROUGH BETTER COORDINATION AND DELIVERY, USE OF INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES, AND DEVELOPMENT OF EASILY REPLICABLE PROGRAM MODELS. THE RREA AUTHORIZED ANNUAL FUNDING LEVEL IS $30,000,000; HOWEVER, ONLY ABOUT $4,000,000 IS APPROPRIATED EACH YEAR. (I) 92% APPORTIONED TO STATES THROUGH A FORMULA AND (II) 8% APPLIED TO NATIONAL FOCUSED FUND PROJECTS VIA A COMPETITIVE GRANT PROCESS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS FUNDING IS TO ASSIST STATES IN CARRYING OUT AN EXTENSION PROGRAM DESIGNED TO ASSIST FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS AND MANAGERS IN MAKING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS BASED ON RESEARCH FINDINGS. FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INCLUDE VEGETATION, WATER, FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE, SOIL, AND RECREATION. IN SOUTH CAROLINA, OUR SCSU-1890 RESEARCH AND EXTENSION RREA PROGRAM IS TARGETING FARMERS AND LANDOWNERS WHO OWN SMALL - TRACTS TO MID-SIZE HOLDINGS AND INCLUDE YOUTHS, BEGINNING FARMERS, RANCHERS, AND VETERANS ACROSS SOUTH CAROLINA GROUPS. A TEAM OF REGIONAL EXTENSION AGENTS WORKING FOR SCSU-1890 EXTENSION AND CLEMSON UNIVERSITY ARE ENGAGING IN CONDUCING EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS AND HANDS-ON DEMONSTRATIONS ACROSS THE STATE. THE SCSU-1890 RESEARCH AND EXTENSION RREA PROGRAM IS INTRODUCING LAND CONVERSION AND FRAGMENTATION PROJECT BY ESTABLISHING A SILVOPASTURE DEMONSTRATION PLOT AT THE UNIVERSITY FARM IN OLAR, SC. SILVOPASTURE COMBINES TREES WITH FORAGE AND LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION. THE TREES ARE MANAGED FOR HIGH-VALUE SAWLOGS, PROVIDE SHADE AND SHELTER FOR LIVESTOCK AND FORAGE, REDUCING STRESS AND SOMETIMES INCREASING FORAGE PRODUCTION. WE WILL USE THIS KNOWLEDGE TO DESIGN AN INTEGRATED TIMBER/GRAZING PRACTICE USING TWO CONIFER SPECIES (LOBLOLLY AND LONGLEAF PINES) THAT WILL ALLOW HIGH VALUE SAW LOGS TO BE GROWN AS A LONG-TERM PRODUCT, WHILE ON THE SAME ACREAGE ANNUAL INCOME CAN BE GENERATED FROM GRAZING LIVESTOCK. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF SILVOPASTURE INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: (I) ECONOMIC RISK IS R EDUCED BECAUSE THE SYSTEM PRODUCES MULTIPLE PRODUCTS; (II) WELL MANAGED FORAGE PRODUCTION PROVIDES IMPROVED NUTRITION FOR LIVESTOCK AND ENHANCE CARBON SEQUESTRATION OPPORTUNITIES; (III) IN AREAS IN THE BOUNDARIES WHERE WEED COMPETITION FOR MOISTURE, NUTRIENTS AND SUNLIGHT IS EMINENT, BROWSING CAN BE USED TO CONTROL THE WEED AND ENHANCE THE GROWTH OF TREES; (IV) WELL MANAGED BROWSING PROVIDES ECONOMICAL CONTROL OF WEEDS AND BRUSH WITHOUT HERBICIDES, MAINTAINS FIRE BREAKS AND REDUCES HABITAT FOR GROWING RODENTS; (V) FERTILIZER APPLIED FOR FORAGE IS ALSO USED BY TREES, AND IN ADDITION, LIVESTOCK MANURE RECYCLES NUTRIENTS TO TREES AND FORAGE; (VI) SOME FORAGES CONTAIN CONDENSED TANNIN THAT INHIBIT THE GROWTH OF PARASITES; (VII) TREES THAT PROVIDE SHADE OR WIND PROTECTION CAN HAVE A CLIMATE STABILIZING EFFECT TO REDUCE HEAT STRESS AND WIND-CHILL OF LIVESTOCK; (VIII) THE FORAGE PROTECTS THE SOIL FROM WATER AND WIND EROSION, WHILE ADDING ORGANIC MATTER TO IMPROVE SOIL PROPERTIES AND ENHANCING ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE; AND (X) IN CONTRAST TO CONCENTRATED LIVESTOCK OPERATIONS, THIS AGROFORESTRY PRACTICE IS LESS LIKELY TO RAISE ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS RELATED TO WATER QUALITY, ODORS, DUST, NOISE, DISEASE PROBLEMS AND ANIMAL TREATMENT. TO MEET THE STRATEGIES IN THE 2018-2022 RREA STRATEGIC PLAN, OTHER PROFESSIONALS AND PARAPROFESSIONALS FROM SOUTH CAROLINA DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, USDA-NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION SERVICES AND FARM SERVICES AGENCY WILL BRING THE SYNERGY TO INTEGRATE OUR EFFORTS ON CONSERVATION AND SUSTAINABILITY GOING FORWARD..

MISSISSIPPI CONTAINS OVER 19.5 MILLION ACRES OF FOREST LAND, WHICH ACCOUNTS FOR 65% OF THE STATE'S TOTAL LAND AREA, AND 81% OF MISSI SSIPPI'S FOREST LAND IS PRIVATELY OWNED BY NONINDUSTRIAL LANDOWNERS. OVER 80% OF PRIVATE FOREST OWNERSHIP IS IN PARCELS OF 100 ACRES OR LESS. EDUCATING PRIVATE FAMILY FOREST OWNERS ABOUT FOREST MANAGEMENT, HARVESTING, AND MARKETING PRACTICES AND TECHNIQUES IS ESSE NTIAL TO THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE FOREST RESOURCE. THESE FAMILY FOREST LANDS ARE NOT ALWAYS MANAGED IN A WAY THAT MAXIMIZES PRIVATE AND ASSOCIATED PUBLIC BENEFITS THAT CAN INCLUDE TIMBER PRODUCTS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES, RECREATION AND WATER QUALITY BENEFITS. MANY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS DO NOT HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE OR SKILLS TO MANAGE FORESTS TO MEET THEIR OWN OBJECTIVES. THE RREA PROGRAM ALLOWS MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SERVICE TO GIVE SPECIAL ATTENTION TO HELPING FAMILY FOREST OWNERS MANAGE THEIR FORESTLANDS FOR MAXIMUM BENEFIT. THUS, THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INCREASE AND IMPROVE THE LEVELS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES BEING CONDUCTED ON MISSISSIPPI FORESTLAND SO AS TO ENHANCE ALL THE BENEFITS SOCIETY RECEIVES FROM WELL MANAGED FORESTS. THE CORE GOALS OF THE FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAM AS SUPPORTED BY RREA ARE TO INCREASE THE PRODUCTIVITY, EFFECTIVENESS, EFFICIENCY, AND PROFITABILITY OF OUR CLIENTELE, AS WELL AS AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE MANY VALUES OF THEIR FORESTS. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, NEW RESEARCH AND TECHNOLOGIES WILL BE DISSEMINATED TO CLIENTELE STATEWIDE THROUGH FORESTRY EXTENSION PROGRAMS AND MATERIALS. THESE PROGRAMS WILL INCLUDE THEMATIC WORKSHOPS, SHORT COURSES, AND STAND-ALONE PRESENTATIONS TARGETING CLIENTELE NEEDS. IN ADDITION, NEW EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS WILL BE PRODUCED AND DISSEMINATED VIA TRADITIONAL AND ELECTRONIC MEDIUMS.

MUCH OF OREGON IS FORESTLAND AND RANGELAND, AND MUCH OF THIS ACREAGE IS MANAGED BY PRIVATE LANDOWNERS WITH NONINDUSTRIAL OPERATIONS. RREA FUNDS PROVIDED TO OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY (OSU) ARE USED TO SUPPORT EFFORTS OF EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF TO PROVIDE GUIDANCE TO THESE LANDOWNERS SO THEY CAN MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT THE MANAGEMENT OF THEIR NATURAL RESOURCES, AND TO PROMOTE UNDERSTANDING AMONG OTHERS ON HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE ECONOMIC AND ECOLOGICAL SERVICES THESE LANDS PROVIDE. THE PRIMARY AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION TO THE PEOPLE OF OREGON THAT HELPS THEM UNDERSTAND HOW DECISIONS REGARDING MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES INFLUENCE THE HEALTH, PRODUCTIVITY, AND RESILIENCY OF THESE LANDS. OUR GOAL IS TO ENSURE HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS, ENHANCE ECONOMIC BENEFITS, STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY THROUGH IMPROVED CONNECTIONS, AND IN THE LONG TERM ENSURE SUSTAINABLE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THIS PROJECT HAS SEVERAL OBJECTIVES. OBJECT IVE ONE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF OWNERS AND MANAGERS OF PRIVATE NONINDUSTRIAL FOREST AND RANGELAND OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES SO AS TO ENABLE THEM TO MEET THEIR MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES WHILE ENSURING HEALTHY FOREST AND RANGELANDS. OBJECTIVE TWO IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW LAND USE AND LAND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS INFLUENCE HABITAT FOR A VARIETY OF FISH AND WILDLIFE SPECIES TO ENSURE PRODUCTIVE POPULATIONS AND HIGH LEVELS OF BIODIVERSITY ACROSS ECOSYSTEMS. OBJECTIVE THREE IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF HOW CHANGING CLIMATIC CONDITIONS ARE LIKELY TO INFLUENCE FOREST AND RANGELAND RESOURCES (E.G., INCREASED SUMMER TEMPERATURES, PROLONGED DROUGHT, WIDESPREAD INSECT AND DISEASE OUTBREAKS, LARGER WILDFIRES OF HIGH INTENSITY), TO FOSTER EFFORTS THAT REDUCE THE THREATS IMPOSED BY THESE CHANGES. EDUCATION EFFORTS ENCOMPASS A WIDE VARIETY OF MODALITIES. WRITTEN MATERIALS INCLUDE PUBLICATIONS AND NEWSLETTERS. ONLINE MATERIALS INCLUDE WEBSITES, BLOGS, WEBINARS, VIDEOS, AND PRE-RECORDED LEARNING MODULES. IN-PERSON EVENTS INCLUDE SITE VISITS, FIELD DAYS, TOURS, SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND SHORT-COURSES. OTHER DELIVERY METHODS INCLUDE HYBRID (PARTIALLY ONLINE AND PARTIALLY IN-PERSON) AND PODCASTS. EXTENSION PERSONNEL FROM FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE CONSERVATION SCIENCES RECEIVE BASE PROGRAM SUPPORT THROUGH RREA FUNDING. IN ADDITION, ALLOCATIONS ARE PROVIDED TO SUB-PROJECTS THAT ADDRESS A VARIETY OF STAKEHOLDER NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FORE ST AND RANGELANDS ACROSS THE STATE. RREA FUNDS ARE LEVERAGED WITH BOTH EXTERNAL GRANT FUNDS AND UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SUPPORT. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A WIDE VARIETY OF EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS AND TRAININGS DESIGNED TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND KNOWLEDGE, EXPAND THE ACREAGE OVER WHICH RECOMMENDED PRACTICES ARE APPLIED, AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. ALL EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF RE PORT ON THE ACTIVITIES PERFORMED AND OUTCOMES ACHIEVED ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

VIRGINIA POLYTECHNIC INSTITUTE AND STATE UNIVERSITY NIFA PROJECT ABSTRACT - EXTENSION OVERVIEW VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (VCE), A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN VIRGINIA POLYTECHNIC INSTITUTE AND STATE UNIVERSITY (VT) AND VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY (VSU), THE VIRGINIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (VAES) AND THE VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATION (VSUARS), ENABLES PEOPLE TO IMPROVE THEIR LIVES THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION USING SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE FOCUSED ON THE ISSUES AND NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF VIRGINIA. AUDIENCES ARE INVOLVED IN DESIGNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING NEEDS DRIVEN PROGRAMS. VCE, VAES AND VSUARS ARE DYNAMIC ORGANIZATIONS WHICH STIMULATE POSITIVE PERSONAL AND SOCIETAL CHANGE LEADING TO MORE PRODUCTIVE LIVES, FAMILIES, FARMS, AND FORESTS, AS WELL AS A BETTER ENVIRONMENT IN URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES. VCE'S GOALS ARE TO: 1) DEVELOP AND TRANSFER NEW KNOWLEDGE IN APPLIED AND BASIC LIFE SCIENCES, 2) PERFORM RELEVANT, OBJECTIVE, AND TIMELY RESEARCH 3) IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR COMMUNITIES AND CITIZENS IN THE COMMONWEALTH, 4) USE A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO PROGRAMMING, WITH TASK-ORIENTED WORK TEAMS THAT RESPOND TO THE NEEDS OF INDIVIDUALS, GROUPS, AND ORGANIZATIONS, 5) WORK WITH AT-RISK, UNDERSERVED, AND UNDERREPRESENTED AUDIENCES WHO NEED FOCUSED AND SPECIALIZED ATTENTION, 6) FULLY INTEGRATE A CULTURALLY DIVERSE PAID AND VOLUNTEER STAFF IN PLANNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING PROGRAMS, AND 7) RECRUIT AND COLLABORATE WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE PARTNERS TO BETTER UTILIZE RESOURCES, HEIGHTEN IMPACT, AND REACH A MORE DIVERSE AUDIENCE. WE WILL USE SCIENCE-BASED RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL STRATEGIES TO ADDRESS 1) CRITICAL AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY 2)OUR BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY PROGRAMS FOCUS ON ESTABLISHING REGIONAL COMMUNITY AND INDUSTRY NETWORKS TO IDENTIFY, RESEARCH AND EDUCATE ON UTILIZATION OF BACTERIA, WATER, PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND FORESTS PRODUCTS TO PRODUCE GOODS FOR HUMAN, INDUSTRIAL, AND AGRICULTURAL NEEDS FOR ALL VIRGINIANS 3) COMMUNITY VIABILITY PROGRAMMING WILL PROMOTE CONTINUING PROSPERITY AND FINANCIAL SECURITY FOR ALL VIRGINIANS 4) WE WILL ADDRESS FOOD SECURITY AND SAFETY, NUTRITION CHALLENGES AND HEALTH ISSUES FOR ALL VIRGINIANS; 5) WE WILL ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES OF NATURAL RESOURCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL ENHANCEMENT, PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION; 6) WE WILL SUPPORT STRONG, HEALTHY FAMILY DEVELOPMENT AND WELL-BEING LEADING TO STRONGER VIRGINIA COMMUNITIES; 7) 4-H PROGRAMS FOCUS ON DEVELOPING POSITIVE, HEALTHY, SKILLED, PRODUCTIVE YOUTH TO BE TOMORROW'S LEADERS.

RREA FY2026 ABSTRACT - SUSTAINING THE PRODUCTIVITY OF NY'S PRIVATE WOODLANDS: RREA AT CORNELL FOCUSES ON OWNER AND OPERATOR DECISION MAKING RELATED TO FORESTS, WILDLIFE, AND FOOD SYSTEMS. WE HAVE SUFFICIENT STAFF AND RESOURCES TO FOCUS ON THREE PRIMARY ISSUES: FOREST MANAGEMENT FOR DIVERSE OUTPUTS, WILDLIFE RESOURCES, AND FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY PARTICULARLY RELATED TO AGROFORESTRY ENTERPRISES OF FOREST FARMING AND SILVOPASTURE. THE DECISIONS MADE BY OWNERS AND OPERATORS OCCUR ON SMALL PARCELS BUT AGGREGATE FOR AN ACCUMULATED IMPACT. PRIVATE OWNERS LACK AWARENESS AND KNOWLEDGE TO INTEGRATE BEST PRACTICES. SPECIALISTS AND PRACTITIONERS IDENTIFY KNOWLEDGE GAPS OR SEEK TECHNICAL SUPPORT. EXTENSION EDUCATORS SEEK SUPPORT WITH COMPLEX PROBLEMS AT COUNTY AND MULTI-COUNTY SCALES. THE GOAL FOR THE FOREST ISSUE IS TO ENSURE THAT FORESTS ARE SUSTAINABLY MANAGED FOR OPTIMAL OUTPUTS OF DESIRED GOODS AND SERVICES. THE GOAL FOR WILDLIFE RESOURCES IS TO SUSTAIN AND ENHANCE THE BIODIVERSITY AND HEALTH OF NATIVE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS IN BALANCE WITH THE AVAILABILITY OF LOCALLY PRODUCED FOREST-BASED FOODS, AND TO ENSURE THAT THE PRODUCERS ARE FINANCIALLY AND ECOLOGICALLY SUSTAINABLE. THE ACTIVITIES DESCRIBED IN THE METHODS SECTION REFLECT A STRATEGY THAT RECOGNIZES STAKEHOLDERS ARRIVE AT DIFFERENT LEVELS OF AWARENESS, HAVE PREFERRED AND SOMETIMES ESSENTIAL MODES OF LEARNING, AND BENEFIT FROM MULTIPLE EXPOSURES TO SIMILAR INFORMATION, OPTIMALLY DEMONSTRATED TO ALLOW THEM TO VISUALIZE THE OUTCOME. IN RESPONSE TO DIFFERENT LEVELS OF AWARENESS, OUR PROGRAM MATERIALS RANGE FROM INTRODUCTORY TO MODERATELY COMPLEX. HIGHLY COMPLEX MATERIAL IS PROVIDED AS PEER REVIEWED SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS OR TECHNICAL REPORTS AND LARGELY OUTSIDE THE SCOPE OF RREA. WE ADDRESS PREFERRED LEARNING MODES BY CREATING MULTIPLE OUTLETS AND FORMATS THAT RANGE FROM SOCIAL MEDIA TO FACT SHEETS TO YOUTUBE TO FIELD TOURS AND DEMONSTRATION SITES. THE POWER OF VISUALIZATION IS REMARKABLE IN ITS CAPACITY TO CONVEY THE OPPORTUNITIES OF A PARTICULAR ACTION. THAT POWER, HOWEVER, CARRIES THE OBLIGATION TO ENSURE THAT THE ASSUMPTIONS OF WHAT'S DEMONSTRATED ARE CLEARLY DEFINED RELATIVE TO FACTORS THAT MIGHT BE DIFFERENT, AND THUS RESULT IN A DIFFERENT OUTCOME. DEMONSTRATIONS ARE CREATED TO ALLOW FOR DIRECT ENGAGEMENT, BUT ALSO THROUGH VIDEO, PICTURES, AND ILLUSTRATIONS. SPECIFIC METHODS INCLUDE: ONLINE RESOURCES, PEER-VOLUNTEERS, DEMONSTRATION SITES, APPLIED RESEARCH, WORKSHOPS AND FIELD TOURS, CONFERENCES AND SEMINARS, MASS MEDIA, EDUCATOR IN-SERVICE TRAININGS, WRITTEN MATERIALS, ORGANIZATIONAL SUPPORT, AND PROGRAM EVALUATION.

UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA LEVERAGES RREA FUNDS WITH OTHER SOURCES OF FUNDING, PRIMARILY SALARY AND PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (UF/IFAS), TO PROVIDE EXTENSION SUPPORT TO TWELVE EXTENSION FACULTY AND THREE TECHNICAL STAFF IN THE SCHOOL OF FOREST, FISHERIES AND GEOMATICS SCIENCES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF WILDLIFE ECOLOGY AND CONSERVATION. THE PURPOSE OF THESE EXTENSION PROGRAMS IS TO ADDRESS MULTIPLE STAKEHOLDERS NEEDS AND PROMOTE BOTH THE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES IN FLORIDA; PROMOTE INFORMATION TRANSFER REGARDING THE ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES BENEFITS OF FOREST AND RANGELAND LANDSCAPES; AND PROVIDE INFORMATION ON LAND USE OPTIONS AND STRATEGIES FOR WORKING LANDSCAPES AND URBAN FORESTS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE FORMAL EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS SUCH AS COURSES, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS; INFORMAL INTERACTIONS TO ADDRESS INDIVIDUAL PROBLEMS THROUGH PHONE CALLS, EMAIL CORRESPONDENCE, AND SITE VISITS; AND PASSIVE EDUCATION SUCH AS ONLINE WEBSITES AND EXTENSION FACT SHEETS THROUGH THE UF/IFD EDIS (ELECTRONIC DATA INFORMATION SOURCE) SYSTEM. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL DELIVER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS BOTH IN-PERSON VIA WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING PROGRAMS THAT INCLUDE CLASSROOM, LAB, AND/OR FIELD EXPERIENCES; ONLINE TOOLS INCLUDING WEBINARS, WEBSITES, AND VIDEOS; AND SOCIAL MEDIA SUCH AS TWITTER, BLOGS, AND APPS. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE EVENTS AND PRODUCTS. EVENTS WILL INCLUDE FACILITATION AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL RESOURCES LEADERSHIP INSTITUTE (NRLI), EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS ADDRESSING FOREST AND RANGELAND MANAGEMENT, NATURAL HISTORY, AND CONSERVATION THROUGH FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS SUCH AS THE FLORIDA FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND THE MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAMS; FOREST AND RANGE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TRAINING THROUGH THE NATURAL AREAS TRAINING ACADEMY (NATA); WORKSHOPS ON THE MANAGEMENT OF INVASIVE PLANTS AND ANIMALS, FOREST INSECT PESTS, AND RANGELAND WEEDS VIA WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DAYS THROUGH REGIONAL WORKSHOPS AND ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS INCLUDING THE FOREST STEWARDSHIP PROGRAM, BARK BEETLE ACADEMY, AND THE INVASIVE SPECIES COUNCIL AND THE COOPERATIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT AREAS TEAMS. PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE EXTENSION FACT SHEETS, PUBLISHED ONLINE IN THE UF/IFAS EDIS SYSTEM ON MULTIPLE TOPICS INCLUDING FOREST AND RANGELAND WILDLIFE, FOREST AND RANGELAND HEALTH AND MANAGEMENT, INVASIVE SPECIES AND THEIR CONTROL, AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. FACULTY AND STAFF WILL MAINTAIN, UPDATE, AND EXPAND (E.G., INVASIVE SPECIES WEBSITE PORTAL) WEBSITES IN FORESTRY, WILDLIFE, INVASIVE SPECIES, AND RELATED EXTENSION PROGRAMS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE CHANGE IN KNOWLEDGE, CHANGE IN ACTION, AND CHANGE IN CONDITION. WE EXPECT OUR TRAINING PROGRAMS, WORKSHOPS, AND FIELD DAYS TO INCREASE PARTICIPANT KNOWLEDGE. WE EXPECT THAT PARTICIPANTS IN TRAINING PROGRAMS AND WORKSHOPS/FIELD DAYS WILL INDICATE THE INTENTION OF IMPLEMENTING AT LEAST ONE MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATION OR OTHER ACTION. WE ALSO EXPECT THAT PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT OR OTHER ACTIONS THAT WILL AFFECT 25% OF THE FLORIDA ACREAGE MANAGEMENT BY PARTICIPANTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF OUR ACTIVITIES AND DELIVERABLES INCLUDE FLORIDA PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, FOREST, AND RANGELAND MANAGERS; PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, BIOLOGISTS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTANTS; EDUCATORS; ELECTED OFFICIALS AND STAFF, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND INTERESTED CITIZENS; AND ECO/AGRITOURISM AND OTHER SMALL BUSINESS/RECREATIONAL OPERATIONS ON PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LANDS.

ARKANSAS FORESTS AND NATURAL RESOURCES ARE CRITICAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY AND WELL-BEING OF ITS CITIZENS; THE STATE IS KNOWN AS  'THE NATURAL STATE '. MUCH OF THE STATE (54%) IS FORESTED, WITH THE MOST PREVALENT FOREST TYPES BEING OAK-HICKORY (40%) AND LOBLOLLY AND SHORTLEAF PINE (32%). THESE DIVERSE FORESTS PROVIDE HABITAT TO DIVERSE WILDLIFE SPECIES. THESE RANGE FROM GAME SPECIES, SUCH AS DEER, TURKEY, AND DUCKS, TO SONGBIRDS FOR WILDLIFE VIEWING, AND MANY REPTILES AND AMPHIBIANS. ARKANSAS FORESTS ALSO PROVIDE CLEAN DRINKING WATER TO METROPOLITAN AREAS AND PROTECT OTHER IMPORTANT WATERSHEDS. RAW MATERIALS FROM ARKANSAS FORESTS SUPPORT A VIBRANT FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY THAT CONTRIBUTED $13 BILLION TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY IN 2024. NON-INDUSTRIAL PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS OWN 69% OF ARKANSAS'S FORESTLANDS. THIS LANDOWNER GROUP IS EXTREMELY DIVERSE AND INCLUDES FARMERS, RANCHERS, HOMEOWNERS, TEACHERS, FACTORY WORKERS, PROFESSIONALS, AND RETIREES. THE DEMAND FOR BENEFITS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS, INCLUDING WILDLIFE HABITAT AND FOREST PRODUCTS, MUST INCREASINGLY BE MET BY THESE PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS. HOWEVER, MANY OF THESE LANDOWNERS ARE UNFAMILIAR WITH SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, TIMBER MARKETING, HABITAT RESTORATION, REFORESTATION INCENTIVES, AND OTHER VITAL INFORMATION CRITICAL TO SUSTAINING FORESTLANDS. MOST OF THEM ALSO HOLD THEIR FORESTLANDS FOR REASONS OTHER THAN TIMBER MANAGEMENT. THE SECURITY OF FUTURE TIMBER SUPPLIES, FOREST ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND FOREST HEALTH IS THUS COMPROMISED BY LACK OF LANDOWNER KNOWLEDGE OF THESE ISSUES. SEVERAL ISSUES ARE THREATENING ARKANSAS FORESTS. INVASIVE PESTS INCLUDING FERAL HOGS, EMERALD ASH BORER, AND LAUREL WILT DISEASE ARE BUT A FEW OF THE DIRECT FACTORS AFFECTING FOREST HEALTH IN RURAL AND URBAN FORESTS. FORESTERS ARE ALSO CONCERNED ABOUT A POTENTIAL INCREASE IN PINE BARK BEETLES AND SUDDENLY LETHAL BEHAVIOR OF BROWN SPOT NEEDLE BLIGHT IN LOBLOLLY PINE, RESULTING FROM STRESS OF OVERSTOCKED CONDITIONS AND PRECIPITATION EXTREMES. OTHER LESS-DIRECT FACTORS ARE FOREST FRAGMENTATION, FOREST DENSIFICATION, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND WEAK FOREST PRODUCTS MARKETS, PARTICULARLY FOR SMALL-DIAMETER TREES. WEAK MARKETS CREATE CONSTRAINTS TO SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. NEW FOREST-BASED PRODUCTS, INCLUDING BIO-ENERGY, WOOD PELLETS AND COMPOSITE DIMENSIONAL TIMBERS ARE STILL IN THE DEVELOPMENT BUT WILL HOPEFULLY AUGMENT AND INCREASE DEMAND FOR WOOD PRODUCTS. OUR GOAL THEN, IS TO INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO MANAGE AND SUSTAIN HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS THAT MEET HUMAN AND ECOLOGICAL NEEDS. ASSOCIATED WITH THIS GOAL, OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO IMPROVE FORESTRY STAKEHOLDER AWARENESS OF FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES BY: (1) HOSTING IN-PERSON EVENTS (WORKSHOPS, FIELD TOURS), (2) HOSTING VIRTUAL EVENTS (WEBINARS), (3) CONDUCTING DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS, (4) DEVELOPING WEB-BASED MANAGEMENT TOOLS AND (5) PUBLISHING RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION THROUGH DIVERSE MEDIA (BULLETINS, POPULAR PRESS, MEDIA RELEASES, INTERNET ARTICLES).
