positiveFlows.title: WISCONSIN IS A LARGELY FORESTED LANDSCAPE COVERING 16 MILLION ACRES, ABOUT 46% OF THE STATE'S LAND AREA. OVERALL, 57% OF THE FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES, TOTALING 360,000 OWNERS. FOREST INDUSTRY IS VITAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY; THE STATE CONTINUES TO BE THE NUMBER ONE PAPER PRODUCING STATE IN THE COUNTRY, AND FOREST PRODUCT INDUSTRIES ARE SCATTERED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. THIS INDUSTRY RELIES HEAVILY ON FAMILY-OWNED FORESTLAND. THE WDNR ESTIMATES THAT 10% OF THE 9.1 MILLION FORESTED ACRES, HELD BY FAMILY FOREST OWNERS, WILL BE SOLD, SUBDIVIDED OR CONVERTED TO NON-FOREST USE IN THE NEXT 5 YEARS. IN A SIMILAR STUDY, THE SUSTAINING FAMILY FORESTS INITIATIVE (SFFI) FOUND THE HIGHEST CONCERN REPORTED BY 56% OF ALL LANDOWNERS WAS 'KEEPING LAND INTACT FOR CHILDREN/HEIRS'. INCIDENTALLY, THE SECOND HIGHEST CONCERN WAS 'HIGH PROPERTY TAXES'. A THIRD STUDY, BY GOBSTER AND RICKENBACH (2004) LOOKED AT PERCEPTIONS OF PARCELIZATION. THE PRIMARY DRIVERS INCLUDED ECONOMIC, DEMOGRAPHIC, VALUES <(>&<)> MOTIVATIONS, GLOBALIZATION <(>&<)> TECHNOLOGY, NATURAL CAPITAL, AND POLICIES. THUS, OUR EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON EDUCATING LANDOWNERS TO RECOGNIZE THE BEST ECONOMIC RETURN ON TIMBER HARVESTS, UNDERSTAND HOW DIVIDING PROPERTY AFFECTS THE ECOSYSTEM, AND HOW MANAGEMENT PLANS CAN ADDRESS THESE ISSUES. OUR COMPREHENSIVE FORESTRY OUTREACH PROGRAM ZEROES IN ON THESE CONCERNS. DURING FFY2026, WISCONSIN RREA PROGRAMMING WILL ADDRESS RENEWABLE RESOURCES IN A VARIETY OF PROGRAMS AND PARTNERSHIPS TO ADDRESS STRATEGIC AND CROSS-CUTTING NATIONAL ISSUES RELATING TO GOALS IDENTIFIED IN THE NIFA RREA STRATEGIC PLAN. GOAL 1- ENSURING HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND GOAL 3 - ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS. THE PRIMARY CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES WE WILL FOCUS ON INCLUDE FISH AND WILDLIFE RESOURCES, RISK MANAGEMENT, AND INTERGENERATIONAL LAND AND OTHER LANDOWNERSHIP CHANGES. THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO HELP LANDOWNERS DEVELOP FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AROUND WOODLAND ECOLOGY, HEALTHY FORESTS, TIMBER HARVEST PRACTICES AND SALES, HABITAT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT BENEFIT WILDLIFE, STRATEGIES FOR THREATS SUCH AS INVASIVE SPECIES AND OTHER FOREST HEALTH CONCERNS, LAND OWNERSHIP AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRANSFERS, AND TO IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT PLAN PRACTICES TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINABLE FOREST RESOURCES AND TO MEET PERSONAL MANAGEMENT GOALS. THROUGH IN-PERSON CLASSES, VIRTUAL CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WE ARE EXPECTING TO INCREASE LANDOWNERS' AND RESOURCES PROFESSIONALS' SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE TO AFFECT LONG-TERM CHANGES IN ACTIVE MANAGEMENT BY WOODLAND OWNERS THAT WILL SUPPORT SUCCESSION TO FAMILY MEMBERS, REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF PARCELIZATION THROUGH STABLE LAND OWNERSHIP, AND RETAIN FOREST COVER AND CONTRIBUTE SUSTAINABLY TO THE WOOD FUEL CYCLE THROUGH REGULAR PLANNED TIMBER SALES GUIDED BY FOREST MANAGEMENT PLANS.

PURPOSE: THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AT PENN STATE WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT TO PENNSYLVANIA RESIDENTS THROUGH THE PENNSYLVANIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND PENN STATE EXTENSION (PSE) ACTIVITIES. WE WILL BE RESPONSIVE TO STAKEHOLDER NEEDS THROUGH TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH AND DELIVERY OF SCIENCE-BASED PROGRAMS TO CLIENTELE. WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT INTERNATIONALLY RELEVANT FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH THAT GENERATES BASELINE DATA TO SOLVE FUTURE PROBLEMS AND ACTIVELY SEEK NEW AND BETTER WAYS TO COMMUNICATE OUR PROGRAMS TO NEW AUDIENCES. OUR FACULTY AND STAFF, SUPPORTED BY FEDERAL BASE FUNDING, WILL EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE THIS INVESTMENT AGAINST MANY OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO CONDUCT PROGRAMS OF THE HIGHEST CALIBER. WE ARE COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE IN RESEARCH, EDUCATING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS AND CITIZENS, AND PROMOTING LIFE-LONG LEARNING AMONG THE CITIZENS OF PENNSYLVANIA. OUR COLLEGES MISSION IS CLEAR: 'THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES IS TO DISCOVER, INTEGRATE, TRANSLATE, AND DISSEMINATE KNOWLEDGE TO ENHANCE THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM, NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP, AND ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL WELLBEING, THEREBY IMPROVING THE LIVES OF PEOPLE IN PENNSYLVANIA, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD.' AGRICULTURE FACES CHALLENGES OF RISING ENERGY COSTS, WEATHER EXTREMES, AN EXPANDING HUMAN POPULATION, ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, AND LABOR SHORTAGES. THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ADDED TO THE CHALLENGES: DISRUPTIONS TO FOOD CHAINS, WORKFORCE CHALLENGES, IMPACTS ON YOUTH EDUCATION, AND BUSINESS INTERRUPTIONS. WE MUST ADDRESS THESE ISSUES TO MITIGATE FUTURE WIDESPREAD DISRUPTIONS THAT IMPACT ALL OF SOCIETY. ACTIVITIES: TO HELP MEET THESE CHALLENGES, WE ARE DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK BASED ON THE SCIENCE OF AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY--DEFINED AS THE INTEGRATION OF NATURAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO INFORM PRACTICE AND POLICY FOR PRODUCTIVE, WORKING LANDSCAPES, HEALTHY WATERSHEDS, AND RESILIENT ECONOMIES. THIS INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH, ENGAGEMENT, AND EDUCATION CENTERS ON THE IMPACTS AND SYNERGIES OF CONTIGUOUS RURAL AND URBAN LANDSCAPES. PENN STATE EXTENSION PROVIDES ACCESS TO FACE-TO-FACE AND ONLINE SCIENCE-BASED EDUCATION TO OUR CUSTOMERS TO HELP THEM ADDRESS PROBLEMS AND TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVEMENT AND INNOVATION. WE MAKE A DIFFERENCE LOCALLY THROUGH FOCUSED ENGAGEMENT AND, MORE WIDELY, TO CUSTOMERS CONNECTING IN THE DIGITAL LANDSCAPE. INITIATIVES ENSURE THE STABILITY OF THE FOOD SYSTEM IN THE COMMONWEALTH AND OUR EFFORTS TO PROVIDE A BROAD-BASED ONLINE LEARNING PLATFORM FOR NONCREDIT PROGRAMMING AND DIGITAL EDUCATION. THE WORK OF AES AND PSE IN OUR COLLEGE IS BUILT ON THE THREE INTEGRATED PILLARS OF INTENSIFICATION, RESILIENCE, AND REGENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AS SOLUTIONS TO SOME OF THE MOST VEXING PROBLEMS CONFRONTING PENNSYLVANIA AND SIMILAR MOSAIC LANDSCAPES WORLDWIDE. OUR CRITICAL ISSUES CAPTURE THE SYSTEMS APPROACH WE IDENTIFIED AS ESSENTIAL FOR GENERATING IMPACT. THEY CUT ACROSS DISCIPLINES, UNITING OUR RESEARCH EFFORTS WITH OUR EXTENSION EDUCATION CAPACITY. THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY PHILOSOPHY HAS REINFORCED THE NATURAL TENDENCY OF OUR FACULTY AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS TO WORK COOPERATIVELY TO SOLVE PROBLEMS. COUPLED WITH THE JOINT RESEARCH-EXTENSION APPOINTMENTS OF MANY OF OUR COLLEGE FACULTY, OUR WORK, AS REPRESENTED IN OUR PLAN OF WORK, WILL EFFECTIVELY UNITE FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE WITH PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS DELIVERED TO STAKEHOLDERS, EMPOWERING THEM TO ADDRESS I MPORTANT AND EMERGING ISSUES USING RELEVANT SCIENCE-BASED RESOURCES. THE NET RESULT WILL BE A TANGIBLE BENEFIT IN ECONOMIC PROSPERITY AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR PENNSYLVANIA CITIZENS.

PROJECT ABSTRACT - MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY: RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM: MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION HELPS IMPROVE PEOPLE'S LIVES THROUGH AN EDUCATIONAL PROCESS THAT APPLIES KNOWLEDGE TO CRITICAL ISSUES, NEEDS, AND OPPORTUNITIES. FOR MORE THAN 100 YEARS, MSU EXTENSION FACULTY AND STAFF MEMBERS HAVE BEEN ACTIVELY REACHING PEOPLE WHERE THEY ARE - IN THEIR HOMES, FARMS, BUSINESSES, AND COMMUNITIES - WITH RESEARCH DRIVEN EDUCATION. WE HELP PEOPLE PERFORM THEIR JOBS BETTER, RAISE HEALTHY AND SAFE FAMILIES, BUILD STRONGER COMMUNITIES, AND EMPOWER CHILDREN TO DREAM OF BRIGHTER FUTURES. WITH RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM (RREA) FUNDING, MSU EXTENSION FOSTERS ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE, A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, AND A PLENTIFUL AND SECURE FOOD SUPPLY FOR MICHIGAN RESIDENTS. MICHIGAN'S NATURAL RESOURCES ARE A FUNDAMENTAL ASSET FOR THE STATE'S FUTURE ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES. CHALLENGES CONCERN HOW RESIDENTS OF THE STATE CAN BEST BENEFIT FROM ITS RICH NATURAL HERITAGE WITHOUT OVERBURDENING THE CARRYING CAPACITY OF ITS NATURAL SYSTEMS AND REDUCING OPPORTUNITIES FOR RESIDENTS AND VISITORS ALIKE. OUR NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS IMPROVE PUBLIC UNDERSTANDING, HELP LANDOWNERS AND COMMUNITIES USE THOSE ASSETS FOR SUSTAINABLE LONG-TERM SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. WE WILL DEVELOP TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY TO HELP MICHIGAN'S NATURAL RESOURCE-BASED TOURISM INDUSTRY GROW BY MEETING CONSUMER DEMANDS AND DETERMINE HOW WILDLIFE, FISHERIES, FOREST AND NATURAL RESOURCES AREAS RESPOND TO HABITAT MANAGEMENT TO ENCOURAGE MANAGEMENT FOR SUSTAINABLE BENEFITS.

THE PRIMARY INDUSTRY IN SC IS AGRICULTURE, WITH 25,000 FARMS ACROSS 4.7 MILLION ACRES THAT CONTRIBUTES OVER $46 BILLION TO THE STATE'S ANNUAL ECONOMY AND PROVIDES OVER 247,000 JOBS. FORESTRY IS ALSO AN IMPORTANT ECONOMIC DRIVER IN SC, CONTRIBUTING OVER $21.2 BILLION ANNUALLY. WITH SUCH DIVERSE NATURAL RESOURCES ACROSS THE STATE, TOURISM IS ALSO A MAJOR ECONOMIC FORCE, ACCOUNTING FOR EXPENDITURES OF $24.4 BILLION IN 2019. THE 5.1 MILLION PEOPLE LIVING IN SC ARE CRUCIAL TO MAINTAINING THE QUALITY OF LIFE AND CONSERVATION OF THE NATURAL BEAUTY IN SC, PARTICULARLY YOUTH, SINCE THEY ARE OUR FUTURE STEWARDS OF THE STATE. THE LIVELIHOOD AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR SC RESIDENTS IS WHAT DRIVES THE PROGRAMMING AND RESEARCH FOCUSES FOR CLEMSON UNIVERSITY AND SOUTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY (SC STATE). THE PLAN OF WORK REFLECTS RESEARCH AND EXTENSION ACTIVITIES TO BENEFIT AGRIBUSINESS, COMMUNITIES, AND CITIZENS OF SC. FOCUS AREAS INCLUDE ADVANCING THE COMPETITIVENESS OF THE AGRICULTURE AND FORESTRY, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, SAFEGUARDING THE FOOD SUPPLY, PRESERVING NATURAL RESOURCES, AND PREPARING THE YOUNGER GENERATIONS TO BECOME PRODUCTIVE CITIZENS. THE MAJOR PROGRAM AREAS FOR CLEMSON EXTENSION INCLUDE: AGRISYSTEMS PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY, AGRIBUSINESS AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESO URCES CONSERVATION, FOOD SAFETY, SECURITY AND NUTRITION, AND YOUTH AND FAMILY DEVELOPMENT. CLEMSON EXTENSION ALSO PARTICIPATES IN MULTIPLE MULTISTATE EXTENSION ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING THE SOUTHERN REGION FRUIT CONSORTIUM, TOBACCO, APPLE AND STRAWBERRY RESEARCH WITH UGA AND NC STATE, THE REGIONAL PEACH INITIATIVE WITH UGA, THE ORCHARD FLOOR MANAGEMENT PROJECT, AND THE REGIONAL APPLE INITIATIVE.

SINCE 1882, THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE AGRESEARCH (FORMERLY THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION) HAS SERVED AS THE BACKBONE OF TENNESSEE'S AGRI-FORESTRY ECONOMY THROUGH RESEARCH, INNOVATION, AND APPLICATION. AS THE STATE'S TOP INDUSTRY, AGRI-FORESTRY CONTRIBUTES $103 BILLION ANNUALLY TO TENNESSEE'S ECONOMY. WORKING IN TANDEM WITH UT EXTENSION, MORE THAN 850 AGRESEARCH FACULTY, STAFF, AND GRADUATE STUDENTS ADDRESS CHALLENGES FACING AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES THROUGH SOLUTION-ORIENTED RESEARCH AND DISSEMINATION OF KNOWLEDGE TO FARMERS, ALLIED INDUSTRIES, AND CONSUMERS. UT AGRESEARCH OPERATES TEN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS (RECS) ACROSS TENNESSEE, COVERING DIVERSE GEOGRAPHIES, PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, CROPS, AND LIVESTOCK. THESE 40,000 ACRES OF FIELD LABORATORIES ALLOW RESEARCHERS TO CONDUCT TRIALS UNDER REALWORLD CONDITIONS AND SERVE AS PLATFORMS FOR OUTREACH THROUGH ROUGHLY 20 FIELD DAYS EACH YEAR, ATTRACTING TENS OF THOUSANDS OF PARTICIPANTS FROM ACROSS THE STATE, REGION, AND BEYOND. THE RECS ALSO PROVIDE HANDS-ON LEARNING FOR COLLEGE STUDENTS AND YOUTH. AGRESEARCH ENCOMPASSES SEVEN ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS AND ONE SCHOOL OF NATURAL RESOURCES, WITH ABOUT 150 FACULTY HOLDING RESEARCH APPOINTMENTS. GUIDED BY THE UT INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURE'S A DECADE OF EXCELLENCE (2018-2028) AND GROWING GREATNESS (2025-2030) STRATEGIC PLANS, UT AGRESEARCH HAS ESTABLISHED THE AGRESEARCH STRATEGIC ACTION PLAN (ASAP) AS A ROADMAP TO MEET STATE AND NATIONAL NEEDS. ASAP FOCUSES ON BALANCING A PORTFOLIO OF INTEGRATED, INTERDISCIPLINARY PROGRAMS; CULTIVATING COLLABORATIVE TEAMS; ADVANCING INNOVATIVE CONCEPTS WITH STRUCTURED SUPPORT; AND SUSTAINING RESEARCH CAPACITY THROUGH TARGETED INVESTMENTS. FOUR THEMATIC INTEGRATED PROGRAMS ADDRESS COMPLEX, EMERGING CHALLENGES: UT ONE HEALTH INITIATIVE - A UT SYSTEM-WIDE PROGRAM HOUSED WITHIN AGRESEARCH THAT ADVANCES HUMAN, ANIMAL, PLANT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH TO PROMOTE ECONOMIC GROWTH AND ECOSYSTEM RESILIENCE AT LOCAL, NATIONAL, AND GLOBAL LEVELS. PRECISION AND DIGITAL AGRICULTURE - A TRANSDISCIPLINARY EFFORT INCORPORATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, SENSING TECHNOLOGIES (E.G., DRONES AND ROBOTICS), AND DATA ANALYTICS TO ENHANCE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY, CONSERVE FINITE NATURAL RESOURCES, REDUCE LABOR DEMANDS, AND IMPROVE PROFITABILITY. PROJECTS SPAN PLANT AND ANIMAL SYSTEMS, ENABLING PRODUCERS TO MAKE INFORMED, DATADRIVEN DECISIONS. AGRICULTURAL GENOMICS AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY - A TRANSFORMATIONAL INITIATIVE ADVANCING PRODUCTIVITY AND RESILIENCE IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS THROUGH GENETIC INNOVATION. RESEARCH FOCUSES ON DISEASE AND DROUGHT RESISTANCE, WATER-USE EFFICIENCY, YIELD IMPROVEMENT, AND MITIGATION OF WILDLIFE DAMAGE, POSITIONING TENNESSEE AT THE FOREFRONT OF NEXT-GENERATION CROP AND LIVESTOCK DEVELOPMENT. BIOECONOMY ADVANCEMENT - AN INTERDISCIPLINARY PROGRAM CREATING SUSTAINABLE FUELS, CHEMICALS, AND MATERIALS FROM RENEWA BLE OR STRANDED BIOMASS RESOURCES. THE CIRCULAR BIOECONOMY SYSTEM (CBS), A CONVERGENT RESEARCH INITIATIVE BETWEEN UT/UTIA AND OAK RIDGE NATIONAL LABORATORY, DEVELOPS TECHNOLOGIES THAT CONVERT BIOMASS (E.G., MISCANTHUS GRASS) GROWN ON MARGINAL LANDS INTO MATERIALS FOR AUTOMOTIVE, PACKAGING, AND CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES-STIMULATING RURAL ECONOMIC GROWTH ACROSS TENNESSEE AND THE REGION. THROUGH THESE INTEGRATED INITIATIVES, UT AGRESEARCH ENHANCES THE SUSTAINABILITY, PROFITABILITY, AND RESILIENCE OF TENNESSEE'S AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL RESOURCE SECTORS, ENSURING THAT RESEARCH-BASED INNOVATION CONTINUES TO DRIVE THE STATE'S ECONOMIC VITALITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP INTO THE FUTURE.

FY26 RREA PROJECT ABSTRACT - MISSOURI WHILE 94 PERCENT OF THE STATE'S LAND BASE (41+MILLION ACRES) IS PRIVATELY OWNED, LESS THAN 10 PERCENT OF THESE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS ACTIVELY MANAGE THEIR FORESTS, WOODLANDS, AND NON-AGRICULTURAL FIELDS. THIS TRANSLATES DIRECTLY INTO LOST, VALUE-ADDED FOREST PRODUCTS AND INDIRECTLY INTO DIMINISHED ABILITY OF OUR FOREST AND WOODLANDS IN PROVIDING VALUABLE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, SUCH AS HABITATS FOR WILDLIFE AS WELL AS CLEAN AIR AND WATER. THUS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR EXPANDED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT WILL ENABLE ALL MISSOURI CITIZENS, LIVING IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN ENVIRONMENTS, TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS REGARDING THE WISE STEWARDSHIP AND CONSERVATION OF THE STATE'S FORESTS AND WOODLANDS, GRASSLANDS AND FIELDS, AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES AND THE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS WHICH DEPEND UPON THESE ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS. THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL P ROGRAMS SO THAT A GREATER NUMBER OF CLIENTELE WILL RECONNECT WITH MISSOURI'S NATURAL RESOURCES, INCLUDING THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESOURCE, AND BECOME ACTIVE LAND STEWARDS SUPPORTING CONSERVATION GOALS AND OBJECTIVES. PROJECT GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: A. INCREASE AND ENHANCE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING ON PRIVATE LANDS FEATURING WORKING FORESTS, WOODLANDS, NATIVE GRASSLANDS AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION WITHIN MISSOURI AND B. BUILDING CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS. ACTIONS TAKEN WILL FEATURE THE DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY OF EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE FOREST AND WOODLAND MANAGEMENT BY MISSOURI'S FAMILY FOREST LANDOWNERS AND DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT SERVE TO INCREASE THE LEVEL OF ACTIVE WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES CONDUCTED BY MISSOURI'S PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. TO ACHIEVE THESE OBJECTIVES OUR PLAN OF ACTION INCLUDES A. CONDUCTING 10 FOREST-AND WILDLIFE-RELATED EDUCATIONAL EVENTS UNDER THE BANNER OF THE MU EXTENSION FOREST ECOLOGY AND WILDLIFE ECOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS; B. CREATING AND/OR REVISING 15 PEER-REVIEWED MU EXTENSION FOREST AND WOODLAND MANAGEMENT AND WILDLIFE ECOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT GUIDES AND 12 NATURAL RESOURCE NEWSLETTERS DISSEMINATED FOR STATE-WIDE USE; C. CREATING 10 NEW MISSOURI  MASTER NATURALIST PROGRAM VOLUNTEER COHORTS EITHER THROUGH EXISTING CHAPTERS OR THE CREATION OF NEW CHAPTERS RESULTING IN OVER 250 MU EXTENSION MASTER NATURALIST VOLUNTEERS BEING TRAINED AND CERTIFIED TO CONDUCT VOLUNTEER SERVICE PROJECTS IN THEIR COMMUNITY THAT FEATURE THE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES; D. CONDUCTING 6 WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT EDUCATIONAL EVENTS FOCUSED ON ENHANCING HABITATS FOR BOTH WOODLAND AND EARLY SUCCESSIONAL SPECIES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO GRASSLAND BIRDS, WHITE-TAILED DEER, BOBWHITE QUAIL AND WILD TURKEY; AND CONDUCTING 1 MASTER POLLINATOR STEWARD PROGRAM THAT FEATURES THE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF NATIVE HABITATS THAT BENEFIT POLLINATORS; AND E. CREATING AND DEVELOPING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS FEATURING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF NATIVE GRASSES FOR GRAZING AND CONSERVATION BENEFITS TARGETING PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. THESE PROJECTS AND ACTIONS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH EXPANDED PROGRAM COLLABORATIONS AND PARTNERSHIPS. TARGET AUDIENCES AND INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS IN BOTH URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES WISHING TO IMPROVE THE NATURAL RESOURCE BASE ON THEIR PROPERTY; EDUCATORS WISHING TO INCORPORATE SCIENCEBASED FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES INTO THEIR CURRICULUM AND ONGOING PROGRAM ACTIVITIES AND; NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS REPRESENTING STATE, FEDERAL AND NON-PROFIT CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS WISHING TO COLLABORATE IN DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS.

CAPACITY GRANT OPPORTUNITY: RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT PROGRAM FUNDING OPPORTUNITY NUMBER: USDA-NIFA-10515-RREAFXXX-26-0001 FEDERAL PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF OUR RREA PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE EXTENSION PROGRAMMING DESIGNED TO ASSIST FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS AND MANAGERS MAKE SCIENCE-BASED MANAGEMENT DECISIONS TO MEET HEALTH, SAFETY, PRODUCTION, PROTECTION, AND SUSTAINABILITY NEEDS OF THE OWNER AND SOCIETY. TOPICAL ISSUES INCLUDE: LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT; PUBLIC AWARENESS; RESOURCE MANAGEMENT; WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND PROTECTION; SUCCESSION AND ESTATE PLANNING; FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT; AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. WSUS RREA PROGRAM ALIGNS WITH  RREA GOAL 'ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS.' OUR ISSUES AREAS ARE 1) FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH, AND 2) RANGELAND STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH. OUR FOCUS IS WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF FOREST AND RANGE FIRES, AND THE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOREST AND RANGE RESOURCES. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THE WSU EXTENSION FORESTRY <(>&<)> RANGE TEAM WILL PROVIDE UNBIASED, RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES TO MEET LANDOWNER AND MANAGER NEEDS. THROUGH FACE-TO-FACE AND DISTANCE DELIVERIES OF CLASSES, FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, SEMINARS, CONFERENCES, PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, SHORT COURSES, CONSULTATION S, MEDIA WORK, PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPROVE LEARNING AND APPLICATION OF NEW IDEAS LEADING TO DESIRABLE FUTURE CONDITIONS. PROGRAMS WILL BE LIVE AND PRE-RECORDED TO SUIT USE PREFERENCE FOR ACCESSING INFORMATION. PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL ACCESS WILL MEET ADA ACCESSIBILITY STANDARDS. DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES: WSU EXPECTS TO DELIVER 100 ACTIVITIES REACHING 10,000 OWNERS AND MANAGERS AND POSITIVELY IMPACTING 0.5-MILLION ACRES. COMPREHENSIVE ACHIEVEMENTS WILL 1) ENHANCE FOREST AND RANGE SUSTAINABILITY BY DEVELOPING OWNER/MANAGER CAPACITY FOR IMPROVING HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY; 2) PROMOTE LAND RESILIENCE BY PREPARING OWNER/MANAGER CAPACITY FOR RESPONDING TO HARMFUL IMPACTS CAUSED BY WILDFIRE, DROUGHT, WILDLIFE DAMAGE, INVASIVE SPECIES, DISEASES AND INSECT PESTS, AND CLIMATE STRESSORS; AND 3) DIVERSIFY STEWARDSHIP OPPORTUNITIES THAT LEAD TO MULTIPLE-USE BENEFITS. WE BASE THESE EXPECTATIONS ON ACCOMPLISHMENTS DOCUMENTED BY THE PAST 18 YEARS OF PROGRAM EVALUATION DATA. IMPACTS EXPECTED: 1) IMPROVED FOREST <(>&<)> RANGELAND HEALTH; 2) DECREASED WILDFIRE RISK; 3) IMPROVED HABITAT AND BIODIVERSITY; 4) DECREASED INSECT, DISEASE, AND INVASIVE SPECIES RISK; 5) IMPROVED TIMBER AND FORAGE PRODUCTIVITY; 6) DECREASED EROSION; 7) IMPROVED WOOD QUALITY AND PRODUCTS; 8) IMPROVED INCOME OPPORTUNITY; 9) IMPROVED CULTURAL RESOURCE AND SPECIAL SITE PROTECTION; 10) IMPROVED RECREATION OPPORTUNITIES; AND 11) IMPROVED WATER QUALITY. LIMITED LEARNING CHANGES WILL BE SOUGHT, AND WE WILL FOCUS EVALUATION ON MEASURING CHANGES IN KNOWLEDGE, BEHAVIORS, PRACTICES, AND ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC CONDITIONS. WE WILL COLLABORATE AND LEVERAGE OUR OUTREACH BY UTILIZING PARTNERSHIPS SUCH AS THE US FOREST SERVICE, WA DEPT. NAT URAL RESOURCES, WA ASSOC. OF CONSERVATION DISTRICTS, WA FARM FORESTRY ASSOC., SOC. OF AMERICAN FORESTERS, ASSOC. OF CONSULTING FORESTERS, LOCAL TRIBES, AND COUNTY PARTNERSHIPS. WE WILL CONTRIBUTE TO NGO PURPOSES THAT HOLD COMMON CONSERVATION GOALS FOR INFORMING THEIR MEMBERSHIP AND THE PUBLIC, SUCH AS THE NATURE CONSERVANCY, AMERICAN TREE FARM SYSTEM, AMERICAN FOREST FOUNDATION, ROCKY MOUNTAIN ELK FOUNDATION, AND LAND TRUSTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: NON-INDUSTRIAL PRIVATE FOREST (NIPF) OWNERS, RANGELAND OWNERS, AND LAND MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS (FORESTERS, LOGGERS, SILVICULTURAL CONTRACTORS, AND TRIBAL NATURAL RESOURCE EMPLOYEES). INVITED PRESENTATIONS FOR YOUTH OR SERVICE ORGANIZATIONS ARE POSSIBLE BUT NOT TARGET BENEFICIARIES.

FORESTS COVER 13.8 MILLION ACRES IN LOUISIANA (48% OF TOTAL LAND COVER) AND REPRESENT A CRITICALLY IMPORTANT ECONOMIC, ECOLOGICAL, AND CULTURAL RESOURCE TO THE STATE. FIFTY-NINE OF LOUISIANA'S 64 PARISHES CONTAIN LAND CAPABLE OF PRODUCING TIMBER TO SUPPORT THE FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY, AND ~87% OF FORESTLAND AND ~88% OF TIMBERLAND IS PRIVATELY OWNED. AS ONE OF THE TOP AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES, FORESTS SUPPORT MORE THAN 25,000 JOBS IN LOUISIANA. IN ADDITION, FOREST-BASED RECREATION CONTRIBUTES CONSIDERABLE INCOME TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY EACH YEAR (E.G. HUNTING LEASES, WILDLIFE VIEWING) AND ALL RESIDENTS BENEFIT FROM THE ECOLOGICAL SERVICES AND SCENIC BEAUTY OF LOUISIANA'S FORESTED SYSTEMS. THE RREA STRATEGIC PLAN FOR FY 2018-2022 IDENTIFIED NINE CRITICAL ISSUES FACED BY PRIVATE FOREST AND RANGELAND OWNERS/MANAGERS IN THE U.S., WHICH INCLUDED ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT, PUBLIC AWARENESS, INVASIVE SPECIES, WILDFIRE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT, RURAL COMMUNITIES, WATER AND WETLANDS, GENERATIONAL SUCCESSION AND LAND OWNERSHIP CHANGES, AND FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT. THESE CHALLENGES ARE ECHOED BY SURVEYS DISTRIBUTED TO LOUISIANA'S FOREST LANDOWNERS BY THE LSU AGCENTER AND IN THE 2020 FOREST ACTION PLAN DEVELOPED BY THE LOUISIANA DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FORESTRY. FURTHER, OUR CLIENTS CONSISTENTLY REQUEST MORE INFORMATION ON MARKET TRENDS, TAX AND INCENTIVE PROGRAMS, PUBLIC POLICY, TECHNOLOGY, CARBON MARKETS, AMONG OTHERS. THE LSU AGCENTER'S FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE EXTENSION TEAM WILL (1) PROVIDE FOREST LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGERS WITH RESOURCES THAT PROMOTE PROFIT AND RESOURCE SUSTAINABILITY, INCLUDING INFORMATION ON THE TOPICS IDENTIFIED ABOVE; AND (2) INFORM OUR DIVERSE CLIENTS (E.G., ADULTS AND YOUTH FROM RURAL AND URBAN AREAS) ABOUT THE IMPORTANCE OF FORESTS TO LOUISIANA AND BEYOND. WE WILL DISSEMINATE THIS CRITICAL INFORMATION TO OUR CLIENTS USING A COMBINATION OF TRADITIONAL (E.G., PRINTED AND ON-LINE FACT SHEETS AND PUBLICATIONS; FIELD DAYS; DEMONSTRATIONS; FORUMS, SITE VISITS) AND NON-TRADITIONAL (E.G., WEBINARS, SOCIAL MEDIA) TECHNIQUES. WE WILL USE IN-PERSON SURVEYS, ON-LINE QUESTIONNAIRES, AND WEB-BASED ANALYTICS TO ASSESS THE OUTCOMES OF OUR PROGRAMS (E.G., INCREASE IN KNOWLEDGE, VALUE OF INFORMATION, SOCIAL MEDIA ENGAGEMENT). WE WILL USE THIS INFORMATION TO QUANTIFY THE IMPACT OF OUR PROGRAMS AND TO ADJUST FUTURE PROGRAMMING AS NEEDED.

TUSKEGEE UNIVERSITY HOLDS A HISTORIC CONNECTION TO LANDOWNERS IN THE BLACK BELT OF ALABAMA, AS WELL AS ACROSS THE STATE FOR PROVIDING SUPPORT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR LAND MANAGEMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY. WITH GROWING CONCERNS IN CLIMATE CHANGE, AND GROWING NEEDS TO ACQUIRE AND RETAIN LAND IT IS THE FOCUS OF TUCE'S RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT CAPACITY FUNDING TO SUPPORT PROGRAMS THAT EDUCATE LANDOWNERS IN SOME OF THESE MORE PERTINENT AREAS OF RESEARCH. THROUGH PROGRAMS DELIVERED AS WORKSHOPS, FIELD DAYS, HANDS ON DEMONSTRATIONS, WEBINARS, INTERNSHIPS, AND CONFERENCES IT IS THE INTENTION FOR THE FOCUS OF THIS YEAR'S WORK TO FOCUS ON 1) HEIR PROPERTY; 2) CLIMATE CHANGE <(>&<)> FORESTRY MANAGEMENT (SOCIAL SCIENCE); 3) AGRITOURISM -RECREATION; 4) FERAL HOGS <(>&<)> FORESTRY MANAGEMENT; AND 5) POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICE MARKETS. PROJECT ABSTRACT - RREA PROPER TREE ESTABLISHMENT, CARE AND MAINTENANCE ARE SOME OF THE TOPICS THAT WILL BE EMPHASIZED. PARTNERSHIPS WITH OTHER GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS WILL ASSIST IN GETTING INFORMATION TO OUR STAKEHOLDERS. THIS WILL HELP TO IMPROVE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS. THE INFORMATION WILL BE PRIMARILY PROVIDED THROUGH WORKSHOPS, SITE VISITS, DEMONSTRATIONS, WEBPAGES, AND SEMINARS. STAKEHOLDERS WILL ALSO BE MADE AWARE OF THE NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON WEATHER, ESPECIALLY DROUGHTS, FLOODING, THE SEVERITY OF TROPICAL STORMS/HURRICANES AND HOW BEST TO MITIGATE THESE EFFECTS. THE HURRICANE SEASON LASTS FOR SIX MONTHS EACH YEAR. WE WILL FOCUS ON STRATEGIES THAT PREPARE OUR URBAN FORESTS TO WITHSTAND DIVERSE/EXTREME WEATHER CONDITIONS AND HOW TO RECOVER FROM SUCH EVENTS. THE RECYCLING OF FALLEN TREES AND PARTS OF TREES INTO VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS WILL ALSO BE INCLUDED. THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT HAS INITIATED A PROGRAM TO RECYCLE GREEN WASTE INTO COMPOST AND MULCH. WE WILL PARTNER WITH THIS PROGRAM IN CONDUCTING ACTIVITIES THAT WILL FOCUS ON THE CRITICAL ISSUES OF PUBLIC AWARENESS AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON FORESTS AND PROVIDING INCREASED ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES. THE CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES WILL BE CLIMATE VARIABILITY, URBANIZATION, AND INVASIVE SPECIES. THE MAIN OBJECTIVES ARE TO COMMUNICATE THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS AND OPPORTUNITIES THAT CAN BE DERIVED FROM TREE POPULATIONS AND ASSOCIATED NATURAL RESOURCES; DEVELOP PARTNERSHIPS WITH COOPERATING STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, ORGANIZATIONS, BUSINESSES, AND LANDOWNERS TO REACH AND ENGAGE STAKEHOLDERS MORE EFFECTIVELY; EDUCATE LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE EXTENSION AND OTHER PROFESSIONALS, AND YOUTH ABOUT THE BENEFITS OF APPLYING PRACTICES THAT SUSTAIN TREE POPULATIONS; DELIVER RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THAT WILL HELP GUIDE DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES THAT ENHANCE WORKING LANDSCAPES. THE TARGET AUDIENCE FOR THE PROJECT CONSISTS OF LANDOWNERS, NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS, OTHER EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS, URBAN FORESTERS, FORESTRY PROFESSIONALS, POLICYMAKERS, GOVERNMENTAL AGENCY PERSONNEL, NGOS, YOUTH AND YOUTH GROUPS, FORESTRY COUNCIL MEMBERS, AGRICULTURE ADVISORY GROUPS, LANDSCAPERS, WOODWORKERS/WOOD ARTISANS AND RESIDENTS. CES WILL UTILIZE WORKSHOPS, SITE VISITS, CONSULTATIONS, TRAINING SESSIONS, SEMINARS AND COUNSELLING. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE AN INCREASE IN PARTICIPATION OF LANDOWNERS IN EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES; THE NUMBER OF LANDOWNERS AND PROPERTY MANAGERS WITH IMPROVED DECISIONS MAKING SKILLS; KNOWLEDGE OF LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS ABOUT PROPERLY MANAGING TREE POPULATIONS; KNOWLEDGE OF LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS ABOUT THE BENEFITS OF TREE POPULATIONS; KNOWLEDGE OF LANDOWNERS AND RESIDENTS ABOUT NATIVE, NATURALIZED AND INVASIVE TREE SPECIES AND INCOME OF WOODWORKERS RECYCLING TREE PARTS INTO VALUE-ADDED ITEMS.

ARKANSAS FOREST AND NATURAL RESOURCES ARE CRITICAL TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY AND TO THE WELL-BEING OF ITS CITIZENS: WE ARE KNOWN AS THE NATURAL STATE. MORE THAN HALF OF THE STATE (55%) IS FORESTED, WITH ALMOST HALF OF THE FOREST COMPRISED OF OAK AND HICKORY FOREST TYPES AND NEARLY A THIRD COMPRISED OF LOBLOLLY AND SHORTLEAF PINE. THESE DIVERSE FORESTS PROVIDE HABITAT TO A HOST OF WILDLIFE SPECIES. THESE RANGE FROM GAME SPECIES, SUCH AS DEER, TURKEY, AND DUCKS, TO SONGBIRDS FOR WILDLIFE VIEWING, AND MANY REPTILES AND AMPHIBIANS. ARKANSAS FORESTS ALSO PROVIDE CLEAN DRINKING WATER TO METROPOLITAN AREAS AND PROTECT OTHER IMPORTANT WATERSHEDS. RAW MATERIALS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS SUPPORT A VIBRANT FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. FOREST RESOURCE COMPANIES OWN OR LEASE 23% OF THE STATE'S TIMBERLAND AND PROVIDED JOBS DIRECTLY TO 28,057 EMPLOYEES, REPRESENTING A LABOR INCOME OF $1.6 BILLION, IN 2014. MORE THAN HALF OF THE STATE'S 18.5 MILLION ACRES OF FORESTLAND IS OWNED BY PRIVATE NON-INDUSTRIAL FOREST LANDOWNERS. THIS IMPORTANT LANDOWNER GROUP IS EXTREMELY DIVERSE AND INCLUDES FARMERS, RANCHERS, HOMEOWNERS, TEACHERS, FACTORY WORKERS, PROFESSIONALS, AND RETIREES. THE DEMAND FOR BENEFITS FROM THE STATE'S FORESTS, INCLUDING WILDLIFE HABITAT AND FOREST PRODUCTS, MUST INCREASINGLY BE MET BY THESE PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS. HOWEVER, MANY OF THESE LANDOWNERS ARE UNFAMILIAR WITH SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, TIMBER MARKETING, HABITAT RESTORATION, REFORESTATION INCENTIVES, AND OTHER VITAL INFORMATION CRITICAL TO SUSTAINING FOREST LANDS. MOST OF THEM ALSO HOLD THEIR FOREST LANDS FOR REASONS OTHER THAN TIMBER MANAGEMENT. THE FUTURE SUPPLY OF TIMBER, THEREFORE, MIGHT NOT BE SECURE UNLESS HARVESTING FOREST PRODUCTS FULFILLS THE LANDOWNER'S OBJECTIVES AND NEEDS. SEVERAL ISSUES ARE THREATENING ARKANSAS FORESTS, HOWEVER. INVASIVE PESTS INCLUDING FERAL HOGS, EMERALD ASH BORER, AND THE RECENTLY DISCOVERED LAUREL WILT DISEASE ARE BUT A FEW OF THE DIRECT FACTORS AFFECTING FOREST HEALTH IN RURAL AND URBAN FORESTS. FORESTERS ARE ALSO CONCERNED ABOUT A POTENTIAL INCREASE IN PINE BARK BEETLES INCLUDING SOUTHERN PINE BEETLE RESULTING FROM STRESS FROM OVER-CROWDING AND DROUGHT. OTHER LESS DIRECT FACTORS ARE FOREST FRAGMENTATION, FOREST DENSIFICATION, CLIMATE VARIABILITY, AND A WEAK FOREST PRODUCTS MARKET. THE WEAK MARKET CREATES CONSTRAINTS TO SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT FOR PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. NEW FOREST-BASED PRODUCTS, INCLUDING BIOENERGY, WOOD PELLETS, ARE STILL IN THE DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE BUT WILL HOPEFULLY AUGMENT AND INCREASE DEMAND FOR WOOD PRODUCTS. OUR GOAL THEN, IS TO INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF LANDOWNERS, MANAGERS, AND PROFESSIONALS TO MANAGE AND TO SUSTAIN HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS THAT MEET BOTH HUMAN AND ECOLOGICAL NEEDS. ASSOCIATED WITH THIS GOAL, OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO IMPROVE FORESTRY STAKEHOLDER AWARENESS OF FOREST AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES BY: (1) HOSTING IN-PERSON EVENTS (WORKSHOPS, FIELD TOURS), (2) HOSTING VIRTUAL EVENTS (WEBINARS), (3) CONDUCTING DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS, (4) DEVELOPING WEB-BASED MANAGEMENT TOOLS AND (5) PUBLISHING RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION THROUGH DIVERSE MEDIA (BULLETINS, POPULAR PRESS, MEDIA RELEASES, INTERNET ARTICLES).

negativeFlows.title: THE RREA PROGRAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT PINE BLUFF (UAPB) IS DESIGNED TO EDUCATE HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED PRODUCERS (HUPS) ABOUT FORESTRY MANAGEMENT AND NAVIGATING THROUGH THE FORESTRY NETWORK. THIS NETWORK INCLUDES TREE PLANTERS, LOGGERS, TREE THINNERS, CONSULTING FORESTERS, COUNTY FORESTERS WITH THE ARKANSAS DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY DIVISION: AND THE NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION SERVICES (NRCS) ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY INCENTIVE PROGRAM (EQIP). THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE FORESTRY MANAGEMENT EDUCATION TO HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED PRODUCERS. TO EDUCATE PRODUCERS ABOUT USDA CONSERVATION PROGRAMS USED TO IMPROVE FORESTLAND. TO ASSIST HUPS IN NAVIGATION THROUGH THE FORESTRY NETWORK TO MANAGE THEIR FORESTLAND. TO IMPLEMENT THE PROGRAM, UAPB PROVIDES FORESTRY EDUCATIONAL MEETINGS THAT INCLUDE COUNTY FORESTERS AND A UAPB FORESTER (PART-TIME) WHO CONDUCTS FORESTRY EDUCATIONAL MEETINGS FOR HUPS. IN ADDITION, AN NRCS EMPLOYEE ALONG WITH A UAPB CONSERVATION CONSULTANT PROVIDES INFORMATION ABOUT THE EQIP CONSERVATION PROGRAM, ITS PRACTICES, AND ITS FINANCIAL INCENTIVES USED TO HELP FORESTLAND OWNERS INSTALL IMPROVEMENT PRACTICES ON THEIR LAND. TO ASSIST THE FOREST LANDOWNERS, UAPB HAS A FORESTRY TEAM (CONSERVATION CONSULTANT AND PARTTIME FORESTER). THE TEAM MAKES SITE VISITS TO FORESTRY LANDOWNERS TO PROVIDE FORESTRY AND CONSERVATION RECOMMENDATIONS. LANDOWNERS ARE ASSISTED IN APPLYING FOR THE EQIP PROGR AM TO INSTALL LAND IMPROVEMENT PRACTICES AND IN SELECTING VENDORS TO INSTALL CONSERVATION PRACTICES IF FUNDED THROUGH THE EQIP PROGRAM.

NEW MEXICO RANGELANDS HAVE EXPERIENCED A VARIETY OF PRECIPITATION LEVELS THROUGHOUT THE STATE. EXTREME DROUGHT IN SOME REGIONS WITH ABOVE AVERAGE PRECIPITATION LEVELS BEING EXPERIENCED IN OTHER REGIONS. THE DIVERSE IMPACTS OF THESE EVENTS HAS LED THE PROGRAMMATIC EFFORTS IN A MANNER THAT ADDRESSES PRODUCERS FACING THESE SITUATIONS. THE PROGRAMMATIC EFFORTS HAVE ENGAGED PRODUCERS IN THE REALM OF MANAGING RANGELAND RESOURCES IN A FORWARD THINKING MANNER, WITH AN EMPHASIS ON THE ABILITY TO REMAIN A SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION UNIT. THE ULTIMATE GOAL FOR EACH PROGRAMMATIC EFFORT IS TO PROVIDE GREATER INSIGHT FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS, LAND MANAGEMENT AGENCIES AND EDUCATIONAL FACULTY INTO THE IMPACT THAT FORWARD THINKING MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS WILL HAVE ON THE AGGREGATE RANGELAND HEALTH AND RESOURCES FOUND THROUGHOUT NEW MEXICO. THIS GAINED KNOWLEDGE WILL BENEFIT ALL RESOURCE MANAGERS IN A MANNER THAT WILL BROADEN THEIR ABILITIES TO UNDERSTAND, MANAGE, AND IMPLEMENT MANAGEMENT PLANS IN PERIODS OF EXTREME AND SUSTAINED DROUGHT. DETERMINING THE CONTENT AND VIABILITY OF A BROAD ARRAY OF FORAGES ACROSS THE STATE HAS BEEN AN OBJECTIVE AND GOAL OF THE PROGRAMMATIC EFFORTS EMPLOYED. THE ABILITY TO CONVEY THE PROTEIN CONTENT, DIGESTIBLE NUTRIENTS, AND THE AGGREGATE VALUE OF THE PLANT AT DIFFERENT STAGES OF GROWTH IS A VALUABLE TOOL FOR PRODUCERS AND RESOURCE MANAGERS ACROSS NEW MEXICO. EMPLOYING THE APPROPRIATE TIMING FOR THE OPTIMAL USE OF EACH RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM HELD IN THE STATE IS A BENEFICIAL PROCESS FOR LIVESTOCK, WILDLIFE, AND RESOURCE MANAGERS THAT ARE IN PLACE ON THESE LANDSCAPES. THESE PRINCIPLES ARE ESSENTIAL TO THE CONTINUED HEALTH AND MANAGEMENT OF NEW MEXICO RANGELANDS AND FOREST HEALTH ISSUES FACING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS AND RESOURCE MANAGERS ACROSS THE STATE IN TODAY'S VARYING CONDITIONS.

CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY (CSU) EXTENSION WORKS WITH WOODLAND OWNERS IN OHIO TO FACILITATE STEWARDSHIP, BUILD NETWORKS, AND PROMOTE LEGACY PLANNING. OHIO'S FOREST SECTOR GENERATES $26 BILLION AND SOUTHEAST OHIO REPRESENTS ALMOST 50 PERCENT OF THE STATE'S FOREST RESOURCES. HOWEVER, 76 PERCENT OF THE FORESTED LAND IN THE AREA IS PRIVATELY OWNED BY SMALL-SCALE WOODLAND OWNERS, MAKING EDUCATION AN IMPORTANT PART OF MANAGEMENT EFFORTS. AS PART OF THE APPALACHIAN REGION, THESE COUNTIES ALSO REPRESENT THE HIGHEST PERCAPITA POVERTY RATE IN THE STATE AND ARE A FOCUS FOR CSU EXTENSION. THE OAK DOMINATED FOREST ECOSYSTEMS IN THE REGION REMAIN LARGELY INTACT, BUT THEY ARE AT A TIPPING POINT AND REGENERATION OF OAK IS ABSENT FROM MANY STANDS AND BEING REPLACED BY SHADE TOLERANT SPECIES SUCH AS RED MAPLE AND TULIP POPLAR. WHITE OAK IS A PARTICULAR ECONOMIC BENEFIT TO THE APPALACHIAN REGION AND FOREST STEWARDSHIP TO PROMOTE FUTURE GROWTH OF THIS SPECIE AND OTHER OAK IS VITAL TO THE LOCAL ECONOMIC FUTURE. CSU EXTENSION WILL BE HIRING A FOREST OUTREACH COORDINATOR IN FISCAL YEAR 2024 TO WORK WITH THE OHIO INTERAGENCY FORESTRY TEAM, WHICH CONSISTS OF FEDERAL AND STATE AGENCIES IN THE APPALACHIAN REGION, TO PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. THE PROJECT OBJECTIVES FOR THE RREA ARE TO (1) CON DUCT PROGRAMMING FOR SMALL-SCALE WOODLAND OWNERS TO IDENTIFY BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR OAK REGENERATION TO IMPROVE ECONOMIC POTENTIAL, (2) PROVIDE LEADERSHIP AND PROGRAMMING GUIDANCE TO THE SOUTHEAST OHIO CHAPTER OF WOMEN OWNING WOODLANDS TO EMPOWER WOMEN TO T AKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN WOODLAND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS, AND (3) DEVELOP CURRICULUM AND PROGRAMMING FOR FOREST LEGACY PLANNING TO HELP SMALL WOODLAND OWNERS PASS THEIR LEGACY TO THE NEXT GENERATION WITH SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT AND ADDRESS HEIRS PROPERTY CHALLENGES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE THAT SMALL-SCALE WOODLAND OWNER PROGRAMS WILL GENERATE A 30 PERCENT INCREASE IN KNOWLEDGE OF SMALL-SCALE WOODLAND OWNER BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR OAK REGENERATION FOR PARTICIPANTS ATTENDING THE PROGRAMS. CSU EXTENSION WILL DEVELOP WORKSHOPS TO ADDRESS EQUITY ISSUES FOR WOMEN IN FOREST MANAGEMENT TO EMPOWER THEM TO BE ACTIVE IN MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. THE THIRD OUTCOME IS TO DEVELOP CURRICULUM FOR FOREST LEGACY PLANNING TO ADDRESS ISSUES AND CHALLENGES SUCH AS SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT, OAK REGENERATION, AND HEIRS' PROPERTY.

ENGAGING UNDERSERVED MISSISSIPPI SMALL-SCALE FARMERS AND WOODLAND OWNERS IN FOREST FARMING MISSISSIPPI IS AMONG THE TOP-TEN FOREST STATES IN THE UNITED STATES (US) WITH 65% OF ITS LAND IN FORESTS AND OVER 70% OF THIS LAND OWNED BY NON-INDUSTRY PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS. EVEN WITH THE RICH MIXED HARDWOOD FOREST RESOURCES, MUSHROOM PRODUCTION AMONG THE UNDERSERVED FARMERS AND FOREST LANDOWNERS (UFFLOS) IS SCARCELY CONSIDERED AS A SOURCE OF FRESH FOODS AND/OR AN ECONOMIC ENDEAVOR TO BOOST ADDITIONAL INCOME WHILE WAITING FOR TIMBER TO MATURE. THE CULTIVATION OF SPECIALTY CROPS SUCH AS SHIITAKE (LENTINULA EDODES) AND OYSTER (PLEUROTUS OSTREATUS) MUSHROOMS COULD BE A POTENTIAL SOURCE OF FRESH FOOD THAT CAN MINIMIZE THE IMPACT OF FOOD INSECURITY IN MISSISSIPPI. EDIBLE MUSHROOMS ARE GLOBALLY CONSIDERED AS HEALTHY FOOD, LOW IN CALORIES WITH EXCELLENT NUTRITIVE MEDICINAL PROPERTIES, AND ARE FUNDAMENTAL IN FOOD SECURITY MUSHROOMS ARE DESIRABLE IN AREAS WITH FOOD INSECURITY BECAUSE THEY CONVERT INFERIOR LIGNOCELLULOSIC WASTE LEFT IN FORESTS AFTER TIMBER HARVESTING INTO HIGHLY NUTRITIOUS AND HEALTHY FOOD. THE TECHNOLOGY OF MUSHROOM CULTIVATION IS ONE OF THE FEW MICROBIAL TECHNOLOGIES FOR BIOCONVERSION OF INFERIOR WASTE WOOD AND AGRICULTURAL RESIDUES TO FUNCTIONAL FOODS. THUS, THE ULTIMATE GOAL FOR THE PROJECT IS  TO EDUCATE OUR TARGET AUDIENCE ON THE ECONOMIES AND TECHNOLOGY REGARDING THE CULTIVATION OF VARIOUS OUTDOOR EDIBLE MUSHROOMS USING WASTE WOOD AND AGRICULTURAL RESIDUES. AMONG THE OUTDOOR MUSHROOMS EXPECTED TO BE PROMOTED IN THIS PROJECT INCLUDE LENTINULA EDODES, PHOLIOTA NAMEKO, STROPHARIA RUGOSO-ANNULATA, AGARICUS SUBRUFESCENS, CLITOCYBE NUDA, INCLUDING OYSTER SPECIES. ALL THESE EDIBLE MUSHROOMS HAVE MEDICINAL PROPERTIES FOR CHRONIC DISEASE, ARE NUTRITIOUS, WITH MANY VITAMINS, AND ALSO ARE EXCELLENT SOURCES OF FIBER AND MINERALS. BESIDES, UFFLOS WILL BE EDUCATED ON THE ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE/OPPORTUNITIES OF OTHER AGROFORESTRY COMPONENTS SUCH AS ALLEY CROPPING, SILVOPASTURE, RIPARIAN BUFFERS, AND WINDBREAKS INCLUDING SOIL QUALITY AMELIORATION AND FOREST HEALTH. WORKSHOPS WILL ALSO BE CONDUCTED ON USDA GOOD AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES HARMONIZED FOOD SAFETY STANDARDS AND POSTHARVEST AUDIT CERTIFICATION. THIS CERTIFICATION AFFORDS PARTICIPANTS THE OPPORTUNITY TO SELL THEIR PRODUCE TO RETAIL AND OTHER OUTLET MARKETS. THEREFORE, THIS PROJECT WILL 1. EDUCATE OUR TARGET AUDIENCES- THE UFFLOS ON THE ECONOMIES AND TECHNOLOGY REGARDING THE CULTIVATION OF VARIOUS OUTDOOR EDIBLE MUSHROOMS USING WASTE WOOD AND AGRICULTURAL RESIDUES, 2. EDUCATE UFFLOS ON THE ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE/OPPORTUNITIES OF OTHER AGROFORESTRY COMPONENTS SUCH AS ALLEY CROPPING, SILVOPASTURE, RIPARIAN BUFFERS, AND WINDBREAKS. THE TARGET AUDIENCE IS 1. EXTENSION AND OUTREACH PERSONNEL (IN-SERVICE TRAINING), 2. UNDERSERVED AND LIMITED RESOURCES FARMERS AND LANDOWNERS, 3. FORESTRY AND OTHER USDA PERSONNEL, AND 4. PUBLIC POLICY MAKERS. THE IMPACT/OUTCOME INDICATORS ARE 1. INCREASE NUMBER OF UNDERSERVED FARMERS AND LANDOWNERS ATTENDING FIELD DAYS AND WORKSHOPS IN AGROFORESTRY PRACTICES; 2. INCREASED NUMBER OF WOODLAND OWNERS WHO HAVE ADOPTED AGROFORESTRY SYSTEMS REGARDING THE CULTIVATION OF MUSHROOMS USING WASTE WOOD AND AGRICULTURAL RESIDUES; 3. INCREASE THE NUMBER OF UFFLOS WHO OBTAIN GAP AND POSTHARVEST AUDIT CERTIFICATION.

THE URI COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES (CELS) IS THE HOME OF RHODE ISLAND'S AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (EXTENSION). URI'S LAND GRANT PROGRAMS ADDRESS A WIDE RANGE OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ISSUES, WITH AN EMPHASIS ON THE NEEDS OF OUR STATE. OUR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS SEEK TO IMPROVE RHODE ISLANDERS' QUALITY OF LIFE, THEIR LIVELIHOODS, AND THE HEALTH OF OUR NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, WITH SPECIAL ATTENTION TO LOCAL PROBLEMS. LOCAL TO GLOBAL ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE - INCREASE OUR ABILITY TO RESPOND AND ADAPT TO LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND GLOBAL ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES. OUTCOMES/DELIVERABLES - RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION: ENSURE READY ACCESS TO ESSENTIAL GEOSPATIAL INFORMATION FOR DECISION MAKERS AND LANDOWNERS TO SUPPORT RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. MAXIMIZE THE CAPACITY OF MANAGED ENVIRONMENTS TO PROVIDE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES SUCH AS NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, WATER QUALITY AND HABITAT. UNDERSTAND HOW ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE MAY ALTER THE BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY OF COASTAL, FRESHWATER, MARINE AND TERRESTRIAL SPECIES, AND HABITATS ON LOCAL THROUGH GLOBAL SCALES. IMPROVE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HUMAN-NATURAL SYSTEMS (INCLUDING COASTAL, FRESHWATER, MARINE, AND TERRESTRIAL), HOW THEY ARE COUPLED, AND HOW TO ENHANCE THEIR RESILIENCE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE. FACILITATE TRANSITIONS TO RENEWABLE ENERGY TECHNOLOGIES BY BETTER UNDERSTANDING THEIR IMPACTS ON BOTH HUMANS AND THE ENVIRONMENT. INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS TO APPLY BEST STEWARDSHIP PRACTICES TO ACHIEVE COASTAL RESILIENCE, ECOSYSTEM RESILIENCE, AND INCREASED USE OF EFFECTIVE GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE. INCREASE PUBLIC AWARENESS OF HOW LAND-USE DECISION-MA KING AFFECTS ECONOMIC VIABILITY, QUALITY OF LIFE, ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH, AND FOOD SECURITY. BY WORKING WITH STAKEHOLDERS, WE WILL DEVELOP SOLUTIONS TO PROTECT AND RESTORE BIODIVERSITY AND THE ECOSYSTEMS THAT SUPPORT OUR PLANET. UNDERSTAND HOW THE COUPLING BETWEEN HUMAN AND NATURAL SYSTEMS CAN ENHANCE AND PRESERVE BIODIVERSITY, ENHANCE RESILIENCE, IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT OF AQUACULTURE, FISHERIES, AND WILDLIFE POPULATIONS AND HABITATS, AND PROMOTE A VIBRANT, SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENT. INCREASE RHODE ISLANDERS' AWARENESS OF CONTEMPORARY ENERGY CHALLENGES AND PROMOTE BEST PRACTICES THAT INCREASE SUSTAINABLE ENERGY CONSUMPTION AND PRODUCTION TO BRING ABOUT BEHAVIOR CHANGE. STRENGTHEN RHODE ISLAND'S GROWING ENERGY SECTOR BY PROVIDING KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT TO UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS THROUGH THE URI ENERGY FELLOWS PROGRAM.

URBAN FOREST SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT: BEST PRACTICES FOR PUERTO RICO'S URBAN FORESTS RESILIENT TO CLIMATE CHANGE THE PUERTO RICO EXPERTS AND ADVISORS COMMITTEE IN CLIMATE CHANGE REPORTED THAT FOR PUERTO RICO THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE INCLUDE HIGHER ATMOSPHERIC TEMPERATURES. THIS WILL AFFECT THE LAND BIODIVERSITY AND THE ISLAND'S ECONOMY. THE NGO PARA LA NATURALEZA INDICATED THAT RECENTLY, EVEN THOUGH ARE CONSIDERED PART OF OUR NORMAL LIFE, EVENTS LIKE HIGH HEAT SENSATION, SAHARA DUST DENSE CLOUDS AND THE REDUCTION IN RAIN EVENTS ARE GROWING IN MAGNITUDE AND FOR LONGER PERIODS OF TIME, ALTERING THE DAILY ACTIVITIES OF THE ISLAND RESIDENTS; THIS NEW REALTY HAVE TO BE MANAGE USING ADAPTIVE METHODS AND PROMOTING NEW BEHAVIORS THAT WILL HELP THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE COMMUNITIES. WE PROPOSE A NON-FORMAL COURSE TO BE OFFERED TO PRAES PERSONNEL IN WHOM THEY WILL LEARN ARBORICULTURE'S BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AS A TOOL TO MODULATE EXTREME HEAT CAUSED BY CLIMATE CHANGE. THEN, THEY WILL OFFER IT TO THEIR COMMUNITY LEADERS. IT WILL BE USED EDUCATIONAL MATERIAL ALREADY PREPARED AND WILL BE ADDED MATERIAL RELATED SPECIFICALLY TO HEAT WAVES AND CLIMATE CHANGE.

FY 2024 RREA PROJECT PROJECT TITLE: ENHANCE CLIMATE CHANGE RESILIENCY AND RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP THROUGH EDUCATION AND OUTREACH TO UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES ABSTRACT OVER 80% OF THE U.S. POPULATION LIVES IN URBAN AND SUBURBAN COMMUNITIES. CONSEQUENTLY, INTEREST IN THE PRESERVATION OF THE URBAN ENVIRONMENT IS ON THE RISE. URBAN RESIDENTS ARE INCREASINGLY CONCERNED ABOUT ISSUES RELATED TO URBAN SPRAWL AT THE URBAN - WILD LAND INTERFACE AND THEIR EFFECTS ON RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES. HOWEVER, IN MANY UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES THERE IS LITTLE OR NO KNOWLEDGE OF THE ECOLOGICAL AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF SUSTAINABLE URBAN FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH. LOCATED IN THE GULF COAST REGION, LOUISIANA IS EXTREMELY VENERABLE TO CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS, SUCH AS SEA LEVEL RISE, SALTWATER INTRUSION, INCREASE HURRICANE FREQUENCY, AND FLOODING. THE IMPACTS ARE DISPROPORTIONALLY HIGHER TO THE LOW-INCOME UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES ALONG THE COAST. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR EDUCATION AND OUTREACH TO HELP THESE COMMUNITIES IN CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP EDUCATION AND OUTREACH MATERIALS, AND DISSEMINATE TECHNOLOGICAL KNOWLEDGE ON FORESTRY, ENVIRONMENT, AND RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES TO DIVERSE AUDIENCES. THE MAJOR OBJECTIVES ARE: 1. OUTREACH AND EDUCATE THE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, ESPECIALLY YOUNG GENERATIONS ON HEALTHY URBAN FORESTS AND URBAN-WILDLAND ECOSYSTEMS, 2. OUTREACH AND EDUCATE THE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES ON CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS AND ADAPTATION STRATEGIES, AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICES, 3: DISSEMINATE TECHNOLOGICAL KNOWLEDGE TO UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES TO ENHANCE ENVIRONMENT AND RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, AND 4: BUILDING OUTREACH AND EXTENSION CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS. WE WILL UTILIZE VIRTUAL/ONLINE PLATFORMS TO CONDUCT OUTREACH AND EDUCATION ACTIVITIES, SUCH AS DISTRIBUTING ELECTRONIC FLYERS, HOSTING VIRTUAL INFORMATIONAL SESSIONS, WEBINARS, DISCUSSION FORUMS, ETC. WE WILL ALSO UTILIZE FACE-TO-FACE METHODS, SUCH AS CLASSROOM VISITS, COMMUNITY VISITS, TRAINING SESSIONS, MEETINGS, WORKSHOPS, ETC., TO ACCOMPLISH THE PROJECT GOAL AND OBJECTIVES. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES FOR STUDENTS THROUGH DIRECT PROJECT INVOLVEMENT. THE TARGET AUDIENCES COMPRISE OF THE LOUISIANA COMMUNITIES SUCH AS HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, COLLEGE STUDENTS, FACULTY, RESIDENTS, FARMERS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, GREEN ORGANIZATIONS, MUNICIPAL ORGANIZATIONS AND NONPROFITS WORKING ON URBAN AND COMMUNITY FORESTRY ISSUES, ARBORISTS, URBAN FORESTERS, ETC. ELECTRONIC EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS FOR URBAN FORESTRY, ENVIRONMENT, AND RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES, AND PRINTED MATERIALS TO ENHANCE STAKEHOLDERS' KNOWLEDGE, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, PAPER PUBLICATIONS, ETC. WE HOPE THAT OUR PROJECT WILL INCREASE THE COMMUNITIES' AWARENESS ON URBAN FORESTRY SUSTAINABILITY, ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, AND NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION; ENHANCE THE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITY'S ABILITY IN CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION; AND INCREASE YOUNG GENERATION'S INTERESTS AND THEIR DESIRE IN PLAYING AN ACTIVE ROLE IN ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP.

IN 2020 THE KENTUCKY FOREST SECTOR PROVIDED AN ESTIMATED $9.55 BILLION IN DIRECT CONTRIBUTION AND A TOTAL ECONOMIC CONTRIBUTION OF $13.97 BILLION ACCORDING TO THE 2020 KENTUCKY FORESTRY ECONOMIC IMPACT REPORT (AS ESTIMATED BY IMPLAN DATA FOR KENTUCKY AND THE KENTUCKY FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY DIRECTORY). MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT PROMOTE HEALTHY FOREST ECOSYSTEMS FOR KENTUCKY'S SMALL WOODLAND OWNERS ARE CRITICAL TO THE CONTINUED PROTECTION AND UTILIZATION OF KENTUCKY'S FORESTS. COMPLEX ECOSYSTEMS WITH BIOTIC INTERACTIONS AMONG PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND MICROORGANISMS AS WELL AS ABIOTIC, PHYSICAL, AND CHEMICAL INTERACTIONS CAN GREATLY AFFECT THE HEALTH OF FORESTS, WATERSHEDS, AND AGRICULTURAL ECOSYSTEMS. FOREST HEALTH, IN TERMS OF FUNCTION OF RIPARIAN/WETLAND VEGETATION, CAN BE ENHANCED THROUGH SILVICULTURE AND AGROFORESTRY APPROACHES THAT SUPPORT NATIVE PLANT POPULATIONS, REDUCE INVASIVE SPECIES, PROMOTE THE HEALTH OF RIPARIAN ZONES, AND INCREASE WATER QUALITY. ALMOST HALF (48%) OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY'S LAND IS COVERED IN FOREST. THERE ARE 467,000 SMALL PRIVATE WOODLAND OWNERS. MUCH OF THE STATE'S REMAINING LAND IS OCCUPIED BY 12.9 MILLION ACRES OF FARMLAND, WITH NEARLY 75,000 FARMS, MOST BEING SMALL-SCALE, FAMILY OPERATIONS. WITH SUCH FRAGMENTED OWNERSHIP, ECOSYSTEM HEALTH AND ADEQUATE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT CAN BE DIFFICULT TO ACHIEVE. THEREFORE, PROGRAMS THAT HELP LANDOWNERS AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS UNDERSTAND AND IMPLEMENT HEALTHY FOREST AND RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ARE ESSENTIAL FOR THE IMPROVEMENT AND PROTECTION OF KENTUCKY'S LANDS, WATERS, WILDLIFE, AND ECONOMIC RESOURCES. KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY (KSU) WILL PROVIDE ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS, FO REST LANDOWNER AND PROFESSIONAL TRAINING WORKSHOPS, AND PRESENTATIONS FOCUSING ON: 1. RREA GOAL 1: ENSURING HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS A. INVASIVE SPECIES (KA 213 WEEDS AFFECTING PLANTS) B. WETLAND RESOURCES (KA 112 WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT) C. CLIMATE VARIABILITY (KA 132 WEATHER AND CLIMATE) 2. RREA GOAL 2: ENHANCING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON WORKING FORESTS AND RANGELANDS A. FOREST STEWARDSHIP AND HEALTH (KA 112 WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, KA 123 MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOREST RESOURCES, KA 213 WEEDS AFFECTING PLANTS). B. WILDLIFE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES (KA 112 WATERSHED PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, KA 135 AQUATIC AND TERRESTRIAL WILDLIFE, AND KA 136 CONSERVATION OF BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY). 3. RREA GOAL 3: BUILDING CAPACITY THROUGH ENHANCED CONNECTIONS A. COMMUNICATION, EDUCATION, AND INFORMATION DELIVERY (KA 903 COMMUNICATION, EDUCATION, AND INFORMATION DELIVERY).

THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF ITS RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES ARE CRITICAL ISSUES. AS URBAN COMMUNITIES CONTINUE TO GROW, ISSUES LIKE WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, DEFORESTATION, AND NATURAL RESOURCE CONSERVATION ARE BECOMING PRIMARY CONCERNS FOR MANY COMMUNITIES. DRASTIC CHANGES IN CLIMATE AND WEATHER PATTERNS ONLY PERPETUATE THESE PROBLEMS, WARRANTING INCREASED OUTREACH BY EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS. NOTABLY, THE FUTURE LIES IN OUR CITIZENS' HANDS, SO THEIR ABILITY TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS IS VITAL. THE RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT (RREA) ASSISTS FOREST AND RANGE LANDOWNERS AND MANAGERS IN MAKING RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS BASED ON RESEARCH FINDINGS. LIKE RREA, ALABAMA EXTENSION SUPPORTS THE NOTION THAT CITIZENS SHOULD BE PREPARED TO PROTECT NATURAL RESOURCES WHENEVER POSSIBLE. MORE IMPORTANTLY, IT ALSO OFFERS IDEAL TOOLS FOR GARNERING SUCH IN-DEPTH INVOLVEMENT AND ENSURING INCREASED ADOPTION OF THE BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (BMPS) REQUIRED TO MANAGE AND PROTECT THESE RESOURCES. THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS THE CRITICAL SOCIAL, ECOLOGICAL, AND ECONOMIC ISSUES IDENTIFIED IN THE RREA STRATEGIC PLAN, ADDRESSING ISSUES SUCH AS FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITATS, INVASIVE SPECIES, LANDOWNER ENGAGEMENT, PUBLIC AWARENESS, AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT. THE MAIN PURPOSE OF TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY'S RENEWABLE RESOURCES EXTENSION ACT (RREA) PROJECT IS TO RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT THE BENEFITS OF URBAN AND COMMUNITY FORESTS IN TENNESSEE. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO, GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, URBAN FORESTS AND ARBORISTS, MINORITY COLLEGE GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, EXTENSION AGENTS, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. THEY WILL BENEFIT FROM THIS PROJECT BY BETTER UNDERSTANDING THE BENEFITS OF TREES IN URBAN AREAS AND THEY CAN ALSO USE THE INFORMATION AND MATERIALS TO MAKE BETTER-INFORMED DECISIONS WHEN IT COMES TO URBAN AND COMMUNITY FOREST MANAGEMENT OR OTHER RELATED ISSUES.
